She lived for 46 years, during the consulship of Severus and Iordanus. Rusticus made this according to his vow.
EDCS-08501205.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Stephania, her age, the date, and the maker of the monument, Rusticus, likely dating to the 3rd or 4th century CE.

EDCS-08501206.translation: Pyminius of good memory rests in peace. He lived 25 years, 3 months, and 27 days. He departed on the Kalends of June, after the consulship of Veri Venantius, a most distinguished consul. Peace be with you forever.
EDCS-08501206.summary: This epitaph commemorates Pyminius, recording his age at death and the date of his passing, likely from the 4th century CE.

EDCS-08501207.translation: This distinguished inscription, no less worthy than his ancestors, when Pantagathus left the fragile use of life, preferred to commit his body to his own land rather than seek a place through prayers, if rest is to be sought from great patrons. The most holy Vincentius, with his peers and companions, seeks these approaches and protects the house and master, providing light from the light of truth from darkness. If you should happen to ask what service he rendered, and what good he accomplished, when placed in the light above, you will find that he gave just laws and sanctioned them with his judgments. For he was called guardian and ruler of the homeland and ruled the homeland with the freedom of spirit, generous to friends and sparing of himself, and faithful to his lords. First, as the order of life demands, his fame transmits him to the eternal world. Envious death took him from worldly affairs in the tenth lustrum. For after laying down the symbols of a senator, he spent his life.
EDCS-08501207.summary: This complex funerary epitaph praises Pantagathus and Vincentius, highlighting their civic virtues, piety, and service, likely dating to the late Roman period (4th-5th century CE).

EDCS-08501208.translation: Eripius the presbyter of holy memory rests in peace here. He lived 27 years, 10 months, and 18 days. He died on the 8th day before the Kalends of February, after the second consulship of Agapitus, a most distinguished man.
EDCS-08501208.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Eripius, a presbyter, including his age and date of death, likely from the 4th century CE.

EDCS-08501209.translation: Amicus the deacon of good memory rests in peace here. He lived 30 years. He died on the 3rd day before the Ides of January, after the second consulship of Paulinus the Younger, in the fourteenth indiction.
EDCS-08501209.summary: This epitaph records the death of Amicus, a deacon, his age, and the date of his passing, likely from the 4th century CE.

EDCS-08501210.summary: A simple epitaph or dedicatory inscription for Florentiole, likely from the 4th-6th century CE.

EDCS-08501211.translation: Neglicia, a Christian woman, peace be with you.
EDCS-08501211.summary: A short epitaph for Neglicia, identifying her as Christian, likely from the 4th-6th century CE.

EDCS-08501212.translation: Papitus of good memory rests in peace here. He lived 50 years and 8 months. He died on the fourth day before the Kalends of August. NB BS CONI COSVC [This part is unclear and likely contains abbreviations or corruptions].
EDCS-08501212.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Papitus, noting his age and the date of his death, with unclear abbreviations, likely from the 4th-6th century CE.

EDCS-08501213.translation: Pelagius the presbyter rests in peace here. He lived [age missing] years. He died [date missing].
EDCS-08501213.summary: This fragmentary funerary inscription records the name and office of Pelagius, a presbyter, but lacks details of his lifespan or death date, likely from the 4th-6th century CE.

EDCS-08501214.translation: Stafili, peace be with you in God. Hail, farewell.
EDCS-08501214.summary: A brief epitaph or farewell message for Stafili, invoking God's peace, likely from the 4th-6th century CE.

EDCS-08501215.summary: This is a personal inscription, possibly funerary or a blessing, addressed to Susomine.

EDCS-08501216.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the age of Teto, associated with Concordia.

EDCS-08501218.translation: To Titulus, of two brothers, the genuine ones.
EDCS-08501218.summary: This is a dedicatory or funerary inscription honoring Titulus, described as genuine among two brothers.

EDCS-08501223.translation: To the divine shades of Titus Viriatius Temporinus, aedile of the Vocontii, and Viriatia Pia. Titus Viriatius Priscus, senator of the Vocontii, and Sextus Viriatius Sequens, the heirs.
EDCS-08501223.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by heirs for Titus Viriatius Temporinus, an aedile, and Viriatia Pia, likely his family members, from the Vocontii tribe.

EDCS-08501225.translation: To the divine shades of Viator, son of Sabinus, for Julia Maria, his dearest wife, set up by her husband.
EDCS-08501225.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by a husband for his beloved wife, Julia Maria.

EDCS-08501226.translation: Us Tacitus paid his vow willingly and deservedly with his own money.
EDCS-08501226.summary: This is a votive inscription where Tacitus fulfilled a vow made with his own funds.

EDCS-08501230.translation: To Silvanus, Gaius Julius Thallus, according to his vow.
EDCS-08501230.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the god Silvanus by Gaius Julius Thallus, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-08501231.translation: Publius Julius Gratus restored (this) according to his vow.
EDCS-08501231.summary: This is a votive inscription recording the restoration of something by Publius Julius Gratus, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-08501233.translation: Claudius Postumus Dardanus, a distinguished man of patrician rank, former consular governor of the province of Vienne, former master of the office of petitions, former quaestor, former praetorian prefect of the Gauls, and Nevia Galla, a most distinguished and illustrious woman, matron of the family, have provided for public use the roads by cutting the sides of both mountains, and they have given walls and gates, which they wanted to be established on their own land for the protection of all. With the assistance also of the distinguished Claudius Lepidus, count and brother of the aforementioned man, former consular governor of Germania Prima, former master of the memorial office, former count of the privy purse, so that their zeal for the safety of all and a public inscription of their devotion might be shown.
EDCS-08501233.summary: This is a monumental inscription recording the public works (roads, walls, gates) provided by Claudius Postumus Dardanus and Nevia Galla, with the help of Claudius Lepidus, to benefit the public, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-08501234.translation: To Fortuna, Hedone Marina, a freedwoman, paid her vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-08501234.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the goddess Fortuna by Hedone Marina, a freedwoman.

EDCS-08501235.translation: Sextus Marius Montanus gladly and deservedly paid his vow to Silvanus.
EDCS-08501235.summary: This is a votive inscription from Sextus Marius Montanus to the god Silvanus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501238.translation: To the departed spirits of Quinctus Caetronius, son of Quinctus, of the Voltinian tribe, Titullus the veteran of the VI praetorian cohort, former chief magistrate, pontiff of the colony of Ariminum, prefect of the pagus Epoti, flamen of Augustus, and curator of public works, his heirs, in accordance with his will, dedicated this to the August Goddess Vocontiorum.
EDCS-08501238.summary: This complex funerary inscription records the dedication by the heirs of Titullus, a prominent local official and veteran, to the August Goddess Vocontiorum.

EDCS-08501239.translation: Here rests in good memory John, a most distinguished man, who lived fifty years, in the second indiction.
EDCS-08501239.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and resting place of a distinguished man named John, likely from the Late Roman or Early Christian period.

EDCS-08501240.translation: Pompeia Lucilla gladly and deservedly paid her vow to Allobrogus.
EDCS-08501240.summary: This is a votive inscription from Pompeia Lucilla to the god Allobrogus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501241.translation: Cornelia Materna gladly and deservedly paid her vow to Isis.
EDCS-08501241.summary: This is a votive inscription from Cornelia Materna to the goddess Isis, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501243.translation: Sextus Marius Montanus paid his vow to Mars.
EDCS-08501243.summary: This is a votive inscription from Sextus Marius Montanus to the god Mars, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501244.translation: Marcus Iulius Maternianus [dedicated this] in accordance with his vow to the Unconquered Sun God.
EDCS-08501244.summary: This is a votive inscription from Marcus Iulius Maternianus to the Unconquered Sun God (Sol Invictus), likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501245.translation: Decimus Roccius Titullus paid his vow to Silvanus.
EDCS-08501245.summary: This is a votive inscription from Decimus Roccius Titullus to the god Silvanus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501246.translation: Victor Vitalis, son of Victor, gladly and deservedly gave this offering to Victory Augusta.
EDCS-08501246.summary: This is a dedication from Victor Vitalis to the goddess Victoria Augusta, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501247.translation: Caius Lucceius Apolaustus gladly and deservedly paid his vow to Novatianus, while he was safe.
EDCS-08501247.summary: This is a votive inscription from Caius Lucceius Apolaustus to Novatianus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501248.translation: Erus gladly fulfilled his vow, as was deserved.
EDCS-08501248.summary: This is a votive inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow by Erus, likely in thanks to a deity.

EDCS-08501255.translation: To the Divine Spirits: Attilia Verina and Vassata and Avita, parents.
EDCS-08501255.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Attilia Verina, Vassata, and Avita, set up by their parents.

EDCS-08501256.translation: To the Divine Spirits: Aelia Fortunata, mother, arranged for this to be set up for Baebia Gratiana.
EDCS-08501256.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Baebia Gratiana, erected by her mother Aelia Fortunata.

EDCS-08501257.translation: To the Divine Spirits: Titus Valentinius Messianus, alive, for Iulia Marcina.
EDCS-08501257.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Iulia Marcina, set up by Titus Valentinius Messianus during his lifetime.

EDCS-08501258.translation: To the Divine Spirits and for eternal memory: Servata, daughter of Catullus, for her most dutiful son Paternus Paulus, and for her husband Lucius Eppius Fortunatus, set up while alive.
EDCS-08501258.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Paternus Paulus and Lucius Eppius Fortunatus, set up by Servata, wife and mother.

EDCS-08501259.translation: Victorinus, son of Mogetus, and Marina, freedwoman, heir.
EDCS-08501259.summary: This inscription appears to record an inheritance or a funerary dedication involving Victorinus, his father Mogetus, and Marina.

EDCS-08501262.translation: Erus gladly fulfilled his vow to Mars Augustus, as was deserved.
EDCS-08501262.summary: This is a votive inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow by Erus to Mars Augustus.

EDCS-08501263.translation: To the Eternal Fires, Julius Placidianus, clarissimus vir, prefect of the praetorian guard, set this up in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-08501263.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument to the Eternal Fires by Julius Placidianus, a high-ranking official (praetorian prefect), in fulfillment of a vow, likely dating to the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-08501264.translation: Lucius Maternius Optatus, sacred to Vulcan Augustus.
EDCS-08501264.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription by Lucius Maternius Optatus to the god Vulcan Augustus.

EDCS-08501265.translation: In this tomb rests in peace, of good memory, Urbanicius the abbot, noble by birth, but blessed by deeds, chaste, sober, kind.
EDCS-08501265.summary: This is a funerary inscription praising the deceased Urbanicius, an abbot, highlighting his virtues.

EDCS-08501268.translation: To the August Goddess Andarta: Lucius Carisius Serenus, one of the six priests of Augustus, gladly fulfilled his vow, as was deserved.
EDCS-08501268.summary: This is a votive inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow by Lucius Carisius Serenus, a local magistrate, to the goddess Andarta.

EDCS-08501269.translation: To the August Goddess Andarta, Titus Dexius Zosimus.
EDCS-08501269.summary: An offering to the goddess Andarta by Titus Dexius Zosimus.

EDCS-08501270.translation: To the August Goddess Andarta, Quintus Iulius Antoninus; to the August Goddess Andarta, Marcus Iulius Theodorus.
EDCS-08501270.summary: Offerings to the goddess Andarta by Quintus Iulius Antoninus and Marcus Iulius Theodorus.

EDCS-08501271.translation: To the Goddess Andarta Augusta, Sextus Plutatius Paternus, in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-08501271.summary: A votive offering to the goddess Andarta Augusta by Sextus Plutatius Paternus.

EDCS-08501272.translation: To the August Goddess Andarta, Marcus Pompeius Primitivus, in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-08501272.summary: A votive offering to the goddess Andarta Augusta by Marcus Pompeius Primitivus.

EDCS-08501273.translation: To Bormanus and Bormana, Publius Sappinius Eusebes willingly fulfilled his vow as was fitting.
EDCS-08501273.summary: A vow fulfilled to the gods Bormanus and Bormana by Publius Sappinius Eusebes.

EDCS-08501274.translation: To Queen Isis, Birria Secundilla, in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-08501274.summary: A votive offering to the goddess Isis Regina by Birria Secundilla.

EDCS-08501275.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Epaphroditus, freedman of Caius Venaesius Hermagoras and Venaesia Attica, in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-08501275.summary: A votive offering to Jupiter Optimus Maximus made by Epaphroditus, a freedman.

EDCS-08501276.translation: Cinna, as aedile for the second time, gives from his own means to the Lares.
EDCS-08501276.summary: An offering to the Lares by Cinna, who was aedile for the second time.

EDCS-08501277.translation: Verri Albini Evecus set up this monument in fulfillment of his vow to Mars Masucicus.
EDCS-08501277.summary: A monument dedicated to Mars Masucicus by Verri Albini Evecus, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-08501278.translation: The curators erected (this) for the August God Mars.
EDCS-08501278.summary: An erection for the god Mars Augustus, commissioned by the curators.

EDCS-08501279.translation: To the Mother of the Gods Magna Idaea, sacred, they made a taurobolium with their beasts for sacrifice and all the paraphernalia: Lucius Dagidius Marius, perpetual pontiff of the city of Valentia, and Verullia Martina and Verullia Maria, their daughter, for the safety of the Emperors Philippus Augustus and Augustus, and of Otacilia Severa Augusta, mother of the emperor and the camp, with the priests officiating: Junius Titus, decemvir, of the people of Arausio, and Castricius Zosimon, of the people of Alba, and Blattius Paterno, of the people of Vocontii, and Fabricius Orfitus, of Liber Pater, and the other assisting priests, they fulfilled their vow willingly and deservedly in the place where it was founded, on the day before the Kalends of October, when Philippus Augustus and Titianus were consuls.
EDCS-08501279.summary: This extensive inscription records a taurobolium dedication to the Mother of the Gods Magna Idaea for the safety of the Emperor Philippus Arabs and his family, performed by civic and religious leaders from various cities, dating precisely to September 30, 244 CE.

EDCS-08501280.translation: For the safety of the Emperor, he made a taurobolium from his own resources: Attius, son of Attianus.
EDCS-08501280.summary: This inscription records a private taurobolium performed by Attius, son of Attianus, for the safety of the Emperor, likely dating to the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-08501281.translation: To the Mother of the Gods, for the safety of the Emperor, they made a taurobolium: Titus Helvius Marcellinus and Valeria Decumilla, in fulfillment of a vow, with Attius, son of Attianus, as priest.
EDCS-08501281.summary: This inscription records a taurobolium dedication to the Mother of the Gods for the Emperor's safety, performed by Titus Helvius Marcellinus and Valeria Decumilla, with Attius Attiani as priest, likely dating to the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-08501282.translation: Novellus Iovincati willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mercury.
EDCS-08501282.summary: This is a votive inscription to Mercury, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-08501283.translation: Masidia Ingenua willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow to Silvanus.
EDCS-08501283.summary: This is a votive inscription to Silvanus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-08501284.translation: Paternus' freedman, according to his vow, to Vulcan.
EDCS-08501284.summary: This is a votive inscription to Vulcan, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-08501285.summary: This is a dedication or identification of an individual, R. Pompeius Lucus, who served as a priest, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-08501286.summary: This inscription likely identifies Statilius Carpophorus, possibly in relation to the imperial cult, from the Imperial period.

EDCS-08501288.translation: To the Divine Shades. Aurelius Titus, beneficiary, made this for his friend Valentinius Fortunatus, soldier of the Ist Legion Minervia Pia Fidelis.
EDCS-08501288.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for a soldier of the Ist Legion Minervia, erected by a colleague, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-08501289.translation: To the Divine Shades. Ambidavus, flamen of the deified Augusti, made this for his family and himself while alive.
EDCS-08501289.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for a priest of the imperial cult, who set it up for himself and his family, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-08501290.summary: This inscription identifies Felix as the prefect of the Vocontii, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-08501292.translation: Lucius Iulius Iulianus made this for his dearest father, Lucius Iulius Cladaeus, Augustalis seviral, and for his mother, Iulia Carpima, while alive.
EDCS-08501292.summary: This is a tombstone inscription set up by a son for his parents, including an Augustalis seviral, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-08501293.translation: Marcus Iulius Regulus, freedman and heir, [made this] for his excellent patron, Marcus Iulius Theodorus, Augustalis seviral of the goddess Augusta of the Vocontii.
EDCS-08501293.summary: This is an epitaph honoring a patron who was an Augustalis seviral, set up by his freedman and heir, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-08501295.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Venaesia Euthychis, patroness and heir, made [this] for Caius Venaesius Fortunatus, one of the six priests of the Augustan cult.
EDCS-08501295.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Caius Venaesius Fortunatus, set up by Venaesia Euthychis.

EDCS-08501296.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, likely a funerary dedication or ownership mark.

EDCS-08501297.translation: For Sextus Vencius Iuventianus, priest of the deified Augustus, also priest and curator of the Villian gladiatorial games, who was appointed to the curia of the people of Lugudunum in the name of citizenship, by the most splendid order of that city, the order of the Vocontii, by common consent and petition of the people, on account of his exceptional generosity in presenting public shows.
EDCS-08501297.summary: This is an honorary inscription from the Vocontii people of Lugudunum honoring Sextus Vencius Iuventianus for his generosity in sponsoring gladiatorial games.

EDCS-08501304.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Valerianus the scribe made [this] for his dearest wife Marcellina and for himself while alive.
EDCS-08501304.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Marcellina, made by her husband Valerianus, who also provided for himself.

EDCS-08501305.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Camasius the butcher made [this] for his dearest wife Martina.
EDCS-08501305.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Martina, made by her husband Camasius.

EDCS-08501306.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Pompeia Iphigenia, perfumer, lived 9 years, 11 months, and 23 days, and [they] made [this] for themselves while alive.
EDCS-08501306.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Pompeia Iphigenia, a perfumer, who died young, and for whom her family provided the tomb.

EDCS-08501307.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Myron, slave of the Vocontii, and Verina for their dearest son Severus, who lived 1 year and 10 days.
EDCS-08501307.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Severus, the son of Myron (a slave of the Vocontii) and Verina.

EDCS-08501308.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Silvanus the secutor. By Valerius Proculus.
EDCS-08501308.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Silvanus, a secutor (type of gladiator), made by Valerius Proculus.

EDCS-08501309.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Verus Severianus, a banker, aged 29. Severinus and Iulia, most unhappy parents, made [this] for themselves while alive.
EDCS-08501309.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Verus Severianus, a 29-year-old banker, made by his grieving parents who also provided for themselves.

EDCS-08501310.translation: [---]us, slave of the Vocontii, made [this] for himself and his family.
EDCS-08501310.summary: This is a funerary dedication for a slave of the Vocontii and his family, likely made by himself.

EDCS-08501313.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Achilleus the slave.
EDCS-08501313.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to a slave named Achilleus.

EDCS-08501314.translation: Titus Admatius Verinus arranged for this to be made in accordance with his will.
EDCS-08501314.summary: A funerary inscription stating that Titus Admatius Verinus arranged for the monument to be built according to his will.

EDCS-08501315.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Alleticia Trophime made this, while alive, for her foster-daughter Alleticia Doridis and for herself.
EDCS-08501315.summary: A funerary inscription set up by Alleticia Trophime for her foster-daughter and herself.

EDCS-08501317.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Gaius Livius Docimus and Atilia Stasime, parents, for their most devoted son, Gaius Atilius Decuminus.
EDCS-08501317.summary: A funerary inscription from parents for their son, Gaius Atilius Decuminus.

EDCS-08501318.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Iulia Chrysis made this, while alive, for her dearest husband, Lucius Atilius Dionysus, and for herself.
EDCS-08501318.summary: A funerary inscription set up by Iulia Chrysis for her husband and herself.

EDCS-08501320.translation: Porcius Uderulus for his mother, Aventina, daughter of Carinus.
EDCS-08501320.summary: A funerary inscription set up by Porcius Uderulus for his mother, Aventina.

EDCS-08501322.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Acne made this, while alive, for his dearest son, Carinianus Valerianus, aged 15, and for himself.
EDCS-08501322.summary: A funerary inscription set up by Acne for his son, Carinianus Valerianus, and himself.

EDCS-08501323.translation: Coelia Marcellina for her son, Paternianus, aged 17.
EDCS-08501323.summary: A funerary inscription set up by Coelia Marcellina for her son, Paternianus.

EDCS-08501324.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Philumene for her dearest son, Charmides, freedman of Attia, aged 18.
EDCS-08501324.summary: A funerary inscription set up by Philumene for her son, Charmides.

EDCS-08501325.translation: Freedman of Gaius Laelius Atticus, tax collector of the hundredth tax.
EDCS-08501325.summary: An inscription identifying an individual as a freedman of Gaius Laelius Atticus, a tax collector.

EDCS-08501326.translation: Titus Coelius Asiaticus made this for himself while alive.
EDCS-08501326.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by Titus Coelius Asiaticus to himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-08501327.translation: Cuncius Cinnamus and his wife Baburia Fuscina made this for themselves while alive.
EDCS-08501327.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by Cuncius Cinnamus and his wife Baburia Fuscina to themselves during their lifetime.

EDCS-08501328.translation: To the Divine Spirits of Marcus Eutychius Sabinianus, Eutychia Sabina [dedicated this] to her most excellent father.
EDCS-08501328.summary: This funerary inscription records Eutychia Sabina's dedication to her father, Marcus Eutychius Sabinianus.

EDCS-08501329.translation: To the Divine Spirits of Faustinus Homuncio, his daughter Carilla dedicated [this] to her father.
EDCS-08501329.summary: This funerary inscription records Carilla's dedication to her father, Faustinus Homuncio.

EDCS-08501330.translation: [dedicated by] the son of Felicissimus to his brother.
EDCS-08501330.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication from a brother to his deceased brother.

EDCS-08501332.translation: Fortunia [dedicated this] to the most dutiful DR.
EDCS-08501332.summary: This inscription seems to be a dedication by Fortunia to a person referred to as DR.

EDCS-08501333.translation: Gratilla, daughter of Gratinus Mercator, [dedicated this] to her dearest brother.
EDCS-08501333.summary: This funerary inscription records Gratilla's dedication to her brother.

EDCS-08501335.translation: While alive, Iulianusolanus, a physician of the Vocontii, made this cinerary urn for himself.
EDCS-08501335.summary: This is a funerary monument, likely a cinerary urn, commissioned by Iulianusolanus, a physician, for himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-08501336.translation: [dedicated by] Vilius Ianuarius to his most excellent wife, Flamina.
EDCS-08501336.summary: This funerary inscription records Vilius Ianuarius' dedication to his wife, Flamina.

EDCS-08501337.translation: Iullus and Marcella [dedicated this] to their son Ianuarius.
EDCS-08501337.summary: This funerary inscription records Iullus and Marcella's dedication to their son, Ianuarius.

EDCS-08501338.translation: Ioventio, daughter of Adrumetus, Verecunda, daughter of Vercatus, his wife, made this while alive for herself.
EDCS-08501338.summary: This is a funerary monument made by a wife for herself and her husband, dating from the Imperial period.

EDCS-08501339.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Iulianus, son of Verina, and for his wife Glycera. Verina, their daughter, made this for her most excellent parents while alive.
EDCS-08501339.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by a daughter for her deceased parents, dating from the Imperial period.

EDCS-08501340.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Iulius and Iulianus.
EDCS-08501340.summary: This is a brief funerary inscription dedicated to two individuals, likely family members, dating from the Imperial period.

EDCS-08501341.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Lucius Iulius Onesimus. Iulia Secundina made this for her most excellent husband.
EDCS-08501341.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by a wife for her deceased husband, dating from the Imperial period.

EDCS-08501342.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Paternus and Iulia Pompeia. Iulius Paezon and Iulia Paternilla, their most dutiful children, made this for their dearest parents.
EDCS-08501342.summary: This funerary inscription records children setting up a monument for their parents, dating from the Imperial period.

EDCS-08501343.translation: For Quintus Iulius Quadratus, son of Quintus. Quintus Iulius Florus made this for his father.
EDCS-08501343.summary: This funerary inscription records a son setting up a monument for his deceased father, dating from the Imperial period.

EDCS-08501344.translation: For Julius Veinus. Iulius Verinus made this for his most dutiful father.
EDCS-08501344.summary: This funerary inscription records a son setting up a monument for his deceased father, dating from the Imperial period.

EDCS-08501346.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Iulia, daughter of Iullinus, and for Iullinus Victorinus, her son.
EDCS-08501346.summary: This funerary inscription dedicates the monument to a mother and son, dating from the Imperial period.

EDCS-08501347.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Iulia Acme, who lived 27 years. Caius Iulius Asclepiades made this for his deserving wife.
EDCS-08501347.summary: This funerary inscription records a husband setting up a monument for his wife, including her age at death, dating from the Imperial period.

EDCS-08501348.translation: ... and Iulia Carina, parents, made this for their children and for themselves while alive.
EDCS-08501348.summary: This is a funerary inscription fragment where parents are dedicating a monument for themselves and their children, dating from the Imperial period.

EDCS-08501349.translation: Gaius Venaesius Asclepiodorus made this for his incomparable wife Iulia Eutychia and for himself while alive.
EDCS-08501349.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Gaius Venaesius Asclepiodorus for his wife Iulia Eutychia and himself.

EDCS-08501351.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Sextus Pompeius Eutyches for his wife Iulia Philumene and Iulia Calinice for her most devoted freedwoman.
EDCS-08501351.summary: This inscription is a joint dedication to the spirits of the underworld by Sextus Pompeius Eutyches for his wife Iulia Philumene and Iulia Calinice for her freedwoman.

EDCS-08501352.translation: Titus Iulius Agathangelus for his dearest wife Iulia Servanda.
EDCS-08501352.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Titus Iulius Agathangelus for his wife Iulia Servanda.

EDCS-08501353.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: His mother made this for Marcella and for Secundinus, son of Papius.
EDCS-08501353.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a mother for her children, Marcella and Secundinus.

EDCS-08501355.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Verus and Severus for their father Caius Mellinius Secundinus.
EDCS-08501355.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the spirits of the underworld by Verus and Severus for their father, Caius Mellinius Secundinus.

EDCS-08501356.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Mellinius Alexander and Valeria Martina for their dearest son Mellinius Severianus.
EDCS-08501356.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the spirits of the underworld by Mellinius Alexander and Valeria Martina for their son, Mellinius Severianus.

EDCS-08501357.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Gratilla, daughter, for Mercator, son of Porcius.
EDCS-08501357.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the spirits of the underworld by Gratilla for Mercator.

EDCS-08501358.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Severia Vitalis for her husband Marcus Numisius Primus.
EDCS-08501358.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Severia Vitalis for her husband Marcus Numisius Primus.

EDCS-08501359.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: [DO] for Oporinus, her companion in barracks.
EDCS-08501359.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication to the spirits of the underworld by an unnamed individual for their companion in barracks, Oporinus.

EDCS-08501360.translation: Quintus Iulius Dioscorus for his companion in barracks.
EDCS-08501360.summary: This inscription records Quintus Iulius Dioscorus dedicating something for his companion in barracks.

EDCS-08501361.translation: To the Divine Manes. Marcellus Mercatoris, son of Marcellus, [erected this] to his mother and brother.
EDCS-08501361.summary: This funerary inscription records a son dedicating a monument to his mother and brother.

EDCS-08501362.translation: To the Divine Manes. Lucius Pompeius Hermeros, a devoted father, had lost his son Lucius Pompeius Faustinus, aged 20, after the death of his brother Severianus.
EDCS-08501362.summary: This funerary inscription records a father mourning his son who died after his brother.

EDCS-08501363.translation: Pompeia, daughter of Titus, aged 26. Pompeius V[erecundus?].
EDCS-08501363.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Pompeia, daughter of Titus, aged 26.

EDCS-08501365.translation: [This monument is for] Aemmius Pothinus, to his most holy wife.
EDCS-08501365.summary: This funerary inscription records a husband dedicating a monument to his wife.

EDCS-08501366.translation: To the Divine Manes. Euhemer and Philocyrius, sons of Primanius.
EDCS-08501366.summary: This funerary inscription records two sons dedicated to the Divine Manes.

EDCS-08501367.translation: To the Divine Manes. Atisia Paulina [erected this] to her most excellent husband, Marcus Primus Messoris.
EDCS-08501367.summary: This funerary inscription records a wife dedicating a monument to her husband.

EDCS-08501368.translation: Loes, Cnaeus, his freedman Zelus, and his freedwoman Prisca.
EDCS-08501368.summary: This inscription lists individuals, likely freedmen and freedwomen, possibly associated with a household or family.

EDCS-08501370.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus liberorum ac coniugibus Publici Callisti et ipsius consecratum cum besse vineae arepennis ex cuius reditu omnibus annis prolibari volo ne minus XV vini sextariis exactis hic tumulus heredem non sequetur\n
EDCS-08501370.translation: Consecrated to the Divine Shades, to his children and wives by Publius Callistus and to himself, together with three-quarters of an arpent of vineyard, the income from which I wish to be used each year to draw at least fifteen sextarii of wine; with this stipulated, this tomb will not pass to an heir.
EDCS-08501370.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Publius Callistus, establishing conditions for the upkeep of his tomb and vineyard income, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501371.translation: To the Divine Manes. Pusinna, wife of Publicus Nitoris.
EDCS-08501371.summary: This funerary inscription records a wife dedicated to the Divine Manes by her husband.

EDCS-08501372.translation: To the Divine Manes. Paternus, a father, [erected this] to his son Pupi Paternus.
EDCS-08501372.summary: This funerary inscription records a father dedicating a monument to his son.

EDCS-08501373.translation: To the Divine Manes. Quarti, daughter of Quartinus.
EDCS-08501373.summary: This funerary inscription records a daughter dedicated to the Divine Manes by her father.

EDCS-08501374.translation: Voltinia, daughter of Sextus, to her father, Quintilla, to her husband.
EDCS-08501374.summary: This epitaph records the dedication by Quintilla, daughter of Sextus and belonging to the Voltinian tribe, to her father and husband.

EDCS-08501375.translation: Decimus, of the Romani tribe, to Verulus, of the Romania tribe, a freedman, to his patron.
EDCS-08501375.summary: This inscription is a dedication from Decimus, a freedman belonging to the Romani tribe, to his patron Verulus, of the Romania tribe.

EDCS-08501376.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Mercatilla, daughter of Secundinus, to her dearest husband, Saturninus, son of Secundinus.
EDCS-08501376.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Mercatilla to her husband Saturninus, both children of a Secundinus.

EDCS-08501377.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Pompeia Servatilla to her dearest son, Servatus, son of Secundinus.
EDCS-08501377.summary: This funerary inscription records Pompeia Servatilla dedicating a monument to her son, Servatus.

EDCS-08501379.translation: Maturus, son of Solitus, and Temporina made this for their father.
EDCS-08501379.summary: This inscription records Maturus and Temporina dedicating a monument to their father.

EDCS-08501380.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Lucius Sollius Calendio, by nationality a Rei, dedicated this to his dearest wife Sollia Sabina, and consecrated it under the axe.
EDCS-08501380.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Lucius Sollius Calendio, of the Rei ethnicity, to his wife Sollia Sabina, with the special rite 'sub ascia'.

EDCS-08501381.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Vera to her excellent father, Successus Vitalis, son of Vitalis.
EDCS-08501381.summary: This funerary inscription records Vera dedicating a monument to her father, Successus Vitalis.

EDCS-08501382.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Mercator, son of Secundus, and Victorina, daughter of Temporinus, to their most dutiful son, Valerius.
EDCS-08501382.summary: This funerary inscription records Mercator and Victorina dedicating a monument to their son, Valerius.

EDCS-08501383.translation: Caius Pompeius Valerianus to his wife, Valeria.
EDCS-08501383.summary: This inscription records Caius Pompeius Valerianus dedicating a monument to his wife, Valeria.

EDCS-08501384.translation: Aventina Secundiae, daughter of Secundus, to her daughter, Valeria, daughter of Valentinus.
EDCS-08501384.summary: This inscription records Aventina Secundiae dedicating a monument to her daughter, Valeria.

EDCS-08501385.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Martinus, her brother, made this tomb for Valeria, daughter of Valerius, in accordance with her will.
EDCS-08501385.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by a brother for his sister, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-08501386.translation: For Valeria Vera, deceased at six years of age. Lucius Valerius Veratianus, for his incomparable daughter.
EDCS-08501386.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young girl, likely dating to the Imperial period, set up by her father.

EDCS-08501387.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Vera, her mother, for her most excellent son, Veratius Albinus.
EDCS-08501387.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by a mother for her son, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-08501388.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Veratius Verinus, son of Marcellus, most dutiful, and for himself, erected during his lifetime.
EDCS-08501388.summary: A funerary monument erected by a man for himself and his son, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-08501390.translation: For Aes, his most dutiful daughter, for Verinus, his dearest sister, and for himself, erected during his lifetime, deceased at twenty-two years of age.
EDCS-08501390.summary: A funerary monument dedicated to a daughter and sister, also for the dedicator and his sister, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-08501391.translation: For Verini Pupi, son of Pupi. Vera Pupi, daughter of Pupi, for her dearest brother.
EDCS-08501391.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by a sister for her brother, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-08501392.translation: To the spirits of the departed and for security. Quintus Verrius Bassus, during his lifetime, made this for himself and for his daughter Carilla.
EDCS-08501392.summary: A funerary monument erected by a man for himself and his daughter, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-08501393.translation: The ground of burial for Sextus Vervinius Lepidus, measuring sixty feet in length and sixty feet in width.
EDCS-08501393.summary: A boundary marker for a burial plot, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501395.translation: To Victoria, to Victorina, to Victor.
EDCS-08501395.summary: A dedication to three individuals, likely part of a larger funerary or honorary monument, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-08501396.translation: To the spirits of the departed and for the prosperity of Urbicilla. Iulius Asclepiades, for his dearest and most dutiful wife, and for himself, erected during his lifetime.
EDCS-08501396.summary: A funerary monument erected by a husband for his wife and himself, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-08501397.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Vrittia Primigenia.
EDCS-08501397.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Vrittia Primigenia.

EDCS-08501399.translation: To Gaius Julius Icarus, his father Gaius Julius Isidorus dedicated me, his young son, and this modest tomb; this house will forever cover us both. The father dedicated his child, fashioned a stone tomb for both.
EDCS-08501399.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by a father for his son, Gaius Julius Icarus, and himself, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-08501403.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Vana, to her most beloved husband Quintus Iulius Ic and to herself, made while alive.
EDCS-08501403.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Vana for her husband Quintus Iulius Ic and herself, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-08501415.translation: Here Dalmata, redeemed by Christ's death, rests in peace and joyfully awaits the day of future judgment, with the saints interceding.
EDCS-08501415.summary: This is a Christian epitaph recording the death and burial of Dalmata, a redeemed individual awaiting judgment.

EDCS-08501416.translation: Here rests in peace, of good memory, Desiderius the deacon, who lived 31 years, died on the 3rd day before the Ides of April, in the 12th indiction.
EDCS-08501416.summary: This is a Christian epitaph for Desiderius, a deacon, giving his age at death and the date of his passing.

EDCS-08501418.translation: An area 33 feet wide. Valeria Secundina, according to her vow. Place for a monument. ON.
EDCS-08501418.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a burial plot purchased by Valeria Secundina according to a vow, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-08501420.translation: Sabinus Coelius paid his vow to the Matres, gladly and deservedly.
EDCS-08501420.summary: This is a dedication recording Sabinus Coelius fulfilling a vow to the Matres, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-08501421.translation: To the spirits of the departed and eternal memory, for Severiola, incomparable wife, RAT placed this monument.
EDCS-08501421.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Severiola, placed by her husband RAT, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-08501423.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Gellius Paulina, Lucius Caresius Severianus made this for his most excellent wife and for himself while alive.
EDCS-08501423.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Lucius Caresius Severianus for his wife Gellius Paulina and himself, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-08501424.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Quintus Julius Quintianus, son of Quintilianus, deceased at the age of 2 years, 7 months, and 2 days, Julius Quintilianus and Attia Avita to their sweetest and most missed son at all hours.
EDCS-08501424.summary: This is a funerary dedication from parents Julius Quintilianus and Attia Avita for their young son Quintus Julius Quintianus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-08501425.translation: To the Divine Shades. Iulianus, son of Avitus, dedicated this to his dearest wife, Severinia Attica, beneath the measuring line.
EDCS-08501425.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Iulianus to his wife Severinia Attica, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501426.translation: To Diana Tifatina, Marcus Iccius Mumm(ius) dedicated this.
EDCS-08501426.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Diana Tifatina by Marcus Iccius Mumm(ius), likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501427.translation: Sacred to Mercury. Rufia, daughter of Suegius, daughter of Cai, paid her vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-08501427.summary: This inscription is a votive offering to Mercury by Rufia, daughter of Suegius.

EDCS-08501430.translation: To all the gods. Nonnus paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-08501430.summary: This inscription is a votive offering to all the gods by Nonnus.

EDCS-08501431.translation: To Mercury, Taurus Veratius willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-08501431.summary: This is a votive inscription to Mercury by Taurus Veratius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501432.translation: To Lucius Voturius Maximus, aedile of the Aletani district, son of Cai Voturius Avitus.
EDCS-08501432.summary: This inscription honors Lucius Voturius Maximus, an aedile of the Aletani district.

EDCS-08501433.translation: To the spirits of the dead. Catia Paternus, deceased, aged 5 years, 2 months, and 19 days. Sextus Pat[...]
EDCS-08501433.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Catia Paternus, who died at a young age.

EDCS-08501434.translation: To the Mother Goddess. Marcus Lusius Rhodon paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-08501434.summary: This inscription is a votive offering to the Mother Goddess by Marcus Lusius Rhodon.

EDCS-08501435.translation: Of Spartus, son of Cassilius, of Ritucai, wife.
EDCS-08501435.summary: This inscription likely designates ownership or burial place for Spartus and his wife.

EDCS-08501436.translation: To the spirits of the dead. Verilla set up and dedicated this monument, marked by an axe, for her husband Tertinius Maximianus.
EDCS-08501436.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Verilla to her husband, Tertinius Maximianus, with the monument marked by an axe.

EDCS-08501437.translation: Sextus Sergius Tiro returned his vow to the Mother Goddess willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-08501437.summary: This inscription is a votive offering returned to the Mother Goddess by Sextus Sergius Tiro.

EDCS-08501438.translation: To the spirits of the dead. Julius Felix for his dearest wife Verilla, daughter of Veratus Flavianus.
EDCS-08501438.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Julius Felix to his wife, Verilla.

EDCS-08501439.translation: To the spirits of the dead. Atticianus and Maternatius for their excellent father Atticinus, son of Aventinus.
EDCS-08501439.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Atticianus and Maternatius to their father, Atticinus.

EDCS-08501440.translation: To the Conservatrices, Volusius Valerianus, praetor of the Vocontii.
EDCS-08501440.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the 'Conservatrices' by Volusius Valerianus, who held the office of praetor for the Vocontii tribe.

EDCS-08501441.translation: To the Divine Shades and eternal rest of Marcus Primanius Iulianus, deceased at the age of 3 years, 11 months, and 10 days, Marcus Primanius and his mother Iulia Veratia [dedicated this].
EDCS-08501441.summary: This epitaph records the untimely death of a young child, Marcus Primanius Iulianus, and was dedicated by his father and mother.

EDCS-08501442.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Marcus Iulius Servatus [dedicated this].
EDCS-08501442.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Marcus Iulius Servatus.

EDCS-08501443.translation: Cnaeus Iulius made this for himself, alive, as a most dutiful son of Dionysius.
EDCS-08501443.summary: This is a self-funded funerary monument erected during the lifetime of Cnaeus Iulius, in honour of his father Dionysius.

EDCS-08501444.translation: Frontia Marciane, daughter [of...], and her son-in-law Claudius Primanus arranged for this to be set up and dedicated it under the axe for the Divine Shades and eternal rest of Segudia Maximilla.
EDCS-08501444.summary: This funerary monument, dedicated to Segudia Maximilla, was set up and consecrated by her daughter and son-in-law.

EDCS-08501446.translation: Here lie in good peace, Rodanics II. In this tomb lies Ferreola, who died in good peace.
EDCS-08501446.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating two individuals, Rodanics II and Ferreola, who are described as resting in peace.

EDCS-08501448.translation: Pupa, companion of Vitalis, son of Quartonis, made this for herself and her husband while alive.
EDCS-08501448.summary: This funerary epitaph was erected by Pupa, the companion of Vitalis, for herself and her husband.

EDCS-08501449.translation: To the Divine Shades, Cassius Severianus and Vettia Matronilla, parents [of this infant].
EDCS-08501449.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Divine Shades for an infant, set up by its parents Cassius Severianus and Vettia Matronilla.

EDCS-08501451.translation: Iulia Secunda gladly and deservedly fulfilled a vow to her mother.
EDCS-08501451.summary: This inscription records Iulia Secunda fulfilling a vow to her mother.

EDCS-08501453.translation: To the Divine Shades, Aemilia Exorata, daughter of Sextus and wife of Gaius Cornaiius Sedulus, [dedicated this] to her most excellent husband.
EDCS-08501453.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Gaius Cornaiius Sedulus, set up by his wife Aemilia Exorata.

EDCS-08501454.summary: This is a dedication from a mother to her daughter.

EDCS-08501455.summary: This is a dedication to the son of Primus.

EDCS-08501456.translation: To the Divine Shades. The heir arranged for the monument to be made for Rutilius Calvus, a veteran of the Third Legion.
EDCS-08501456.summary: This funerary monument was erected by the heir for Rutilius Calvus, a veteran of the Third Legion.

EDCS-08501458.translation: Baebia Eroe made this monument for her relatives.
EDCS-08501458.summary: This monument was made by Baebia Eroe for her own family members.

EDCS-08501459.summary: This marks a monument dedicated to Lucius Antonius.

EDCS-08501460.summary: This epitaph indicates that a veteran is buried here.

EDCS-08501461.translation: Gaius Julius Pastor made this while alive for his wife, Tertulla, daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-08501461.summary: This is a funerary monument built by Gaius Julius Pastor for his wife, Tertulla, during his lifetime.

EDCS-08501462.translation: To the Divine Shades. Gaius Severius Julianus [dedicated this] to his most dutiful mother, Suaduilia Iulianena.
EDCS-08501462.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Gaius Severius Julianus to his mother, Suaduilia Iulianena.

EDCS-08501464.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Marcus Aucius Macrinus.
EDCS-08501464.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Marcus Aucius Macrinus.

EDCS-08501466.translation: For the safety of the Emperors and for the divine house, Caius Valerius Urbanus(?), priest, and Caius Flavius Restitutus(?) performed a taurobolium and a criobolium of the Great Mother of the Gods Idaea.
EDCS-08501466.summary: This is a record of a taurobolium and criobolium ritual performed by two priests for the well-being of the Emperors and the imperial house, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-08501467.translation: To Mercury. Cassius and his companions willingly and deservedly fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-08501467.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Cassius and others to the god Mercury.

EDCS-08501470.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed and to the eternal memory of Petronius Castus, a veteran honorably discharged from the First Minervian Legion, formerly optio to a procurator of 200,000 sesterces, and of his wife Vitalinia Flora; they had this erected for themselves while alive and dedicated it beneath the axe.
EDCS-08501470.summary: This funerary epitaph honors a veteran and his wife, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501471.translation: For Tiberius Claudius Pius, son of Tiberius, of the Galeria tribe, a decurion of Lugudunum, honored with the rank of duumvir, who died at Rome while on a legation; Claudius Spendon and Cestia C, his parents, for their son Tiberius.
EDCS-08501471.summary: This funerary dedication is for Tiberius Claudius Pius, a local magistrate from Lugudunum, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501472.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed, for Quintus Julius Aper, a citizen of Lugudunum, a Sexvir [of the city], who lived 17 years, 9 months, and 29 days, his body rests here; the mausoleum was made by his mother Vindauscia Euvanelis for her dearest son and dedicated beneath the axe.
EDCS-08501472.summary: This epitaph records the death of a young man, Quintus Julius Aper, and was erected by his mother to form a mausoleum, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501474.translation: Marcus Junius Secundus, Caius Valerius Terentianus, Caius Valerius Decuminus, and Quarta Sextilla gave these steps from their own funds.
EDCS-08501474.summary: This inscription records a donation of steps by four individuals, likely for a public building or monument, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501475.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed, for Lucius Liberalinius Florentinus, a taster; Sergius Liberalinius Gallicanus erected this for his most dutiful father beneath the axe.
EDCS-08501475.summary: This funerary epitaph honors Lucius Liberalinius Florentinus, a 'taster', and was erected by his son, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501476.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed, for Valentinus VIBLIC[---], son of C. VA[---]nus and Attia Victorina, their most dutiful son, who lived 21 years, 5 months, and 8 days; they dedicated it beneath the axe.
EDCS-08501476.summary: This epitaph commemorates Valentinus, son of VIBLIC[---] and Attia Victorina, and was erected by his parents, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501477.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed, for Verulia Aventina Vocontia, to her incomparable wife.
EDCS-08501477.summary: This funerary dedication is from Marcus Barbarius Perpetuus to his wife Verulia Aventina Vocontia, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501478.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed, for Lucius Aelius Euelpistianus, who lived 21 years, 11 months; Aelius Euelpistus made this for his dearest son and for himself and his descendants, and dedicated it beneath the axe.
EDCS-08501478.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Lucius Aelius Euelpistianus and was erected by his father for him, himself, and descendants, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501480.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed and to the memory of Crescentina, aged 5 years and 7 days; Lucius Albanius Achillaeus [erected this] for his foster-child.
EDCS-08501480.summary: This funerary dedication commemorates a young child, Crescentina, and was erected by her foster-father, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501481.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed, for Sextus Decidius Hilarus, who lived 20 years, 5 months, and 10 days; his brothers Decidius Hilarianus and Hilarus, and his sister and heir Iulia Vitellia, made this according to his will and dedicated it beneath the axe.
EDCS-08501481.summary: This funerary epitaph was erected by the brothers and sister of Sextus Decidius Hilarus, honoring his memory and following his testamentary instructions, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501482.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Donnia Quintilla and her son Cassius Valentinus, who lived 16 years, 6 months, and 12 days. Cassius Valerius dedicated [this monument] to his dearest wife and most dutiful son, under the axe.
EDCS-08501482.summary: A funerary dedication by Cassius Valerius for his wife Donnia Quintilla and son Cassius Valentinus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501484.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Iulius Maternus.
EDCS-08501484.summary: A funerary dedication to Iulius Maternus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501485.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Lucius Iulius Maternus. Valeria Materna [dedicated this] for herself and Aelius Achillis.
EDCS-08501485.summary: A funerary dedication for Lucius Iulius Maternus, also mentioning Valeria Materna and Aelius Achillis, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501486.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Iulia Decumilla. Titus Iulius Paternus made [this monument] for his dearest wife and for himself, and dedicated it under the axe while alive.
EDCS-08501486.summary: A funerary dedication made by Titus Iulius Paternus for his wife Iulia Decumilla and himself, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501487.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Iulia Marcella. Lucius Severius Severianus [dedicated this] to his dearest wife. Tiberius Severius.
EDCS-08501487.summary: A funerary dedication by Lucius Severius Severianus for his wife Iulia Marcella, also mentioning Tiberius Severius, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501488.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Iulia Marullina. Quintus Saedius Athamallus dedicated [this monument] to his dearest wife under the axe.
EDCS-08501488.summary: A funerary dedication by Quintus Saedius Athamallus for his wife Iulia Marullina, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501489.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld and to the memory of Iulia Valeria. Mustius Iulianus took care to have [this monument] made for his excellent wife, and dedicated it under the axe.
EDCS-08501489.summary: A funerary dedication commissioned by Mustius Iulianus for his wife Iulia Valeria, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501490.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Iustina.
EDCS-08501490.summary: A funerary dedication to Iustina, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501491.translation: For Titus Pompeius Hilarus, freedman of Veriuccus. Titus Pompeius Bassus for his father and himself.
EDCS-08501491.summary: A funerary dedication by Titus Pompeius Bassus for his freedman Titus Pompeius Hilarus and himself, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501492.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Titus Pompeius Severus. Titus Pompeius Primitivus and Valeria Severina dedicated [this monument] to their sweetest son, under the axe.
EDCS-08501492.summary: A funerary dedication by Titus Pompeius Primitivus and Valeria Severina for their son Titus Pompeius Severus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501493.translation: To the spirits of the departed and for the eternal memory of Quintus Pontenius Bassianus, who lived 25 years, 8 months, and 4 days. Carisia Bassiana, a grieving mother, had this made for her most dutiful son and dedicated it under the axe.
EDCS-08501493.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Pontenius Bassianus, set up by his mother.

EDCS-08501494.translation: To Primo, son of Br, by the decision of Publius Cossutius S.
EDCS-08501494.summary: A funerary dedication for Primo, possibly by a relative or friend.

EDCS-08501496.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Decimus Lucanius ThrHeption to his most holy wife Severina, and their daughter Maximina to her incomparable mother, and for themselves, their descendants, while alive.
EDCS-08501496.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Decimus Lucanius ThrHeption and his daughter to his wife and their mother, Severina.

EDCS-08501497.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Tiberius to his dearest son, who lived [---] years. Dedicated under the axe.
EDCS-08501497.summary: A funerary epitaph for a son, set up by his father Tiberius.

EDCS-08501498.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Coelius Aelianus to his most holy wife, Vindauscia Petrusonia.
EDCS-08501498.summary: A funerary dedication by Coelius Aelianus to his wife, Vindauscia Petrusonia.

EDCS-08501499.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Gaius Volusius Apollinaris. Veratia Gellia, his wife.
EDCS-08501499.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gaius Volusius Apollinaris, set up by his wife Veratia Gellia.

EDCS-08501502.translation: [...] who lived 60 years, died peacefully on the 8th day before the Kalends of August, in the consulship of Maximinus, most illustrious man.
EDCS-08501502.summary: A funerary epitaph recording a death date and the consul Maximinus, likely from the 3rd century AD.

EDCS-08501503.translation: To the Great Mother of the Gods Idaea, for the safety of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Commodus Antoninus Augustus Pius and for the divine house of the colony Copia Claudia Augusta Lugudunensis, Quintus Aquius Antonianus, perpetual pontifex, performed a taurobolium, begun according to the prophecy of Pusanius Iulianus, archigallus, on the 12th day before the Kalends of May and completed on the 9th day before the Kalends of May, with Lucius Eggius Marullus and Gnaeus Papirius Aelianus as consuls, under the direction of Aelius Castrensis, priest, and with Albius Verinus as the tibicen.
EDCS-08501503.summary: This inscription records a taurobolium ritual dedicated to the Great Mother of the Gods Idaea in Lugudunum, performed by Quintus Aquius Antonianus for the safety of Emperor Commodus and the city, with specific dates and officials mentioned, dating to 185 AD.

EDCS-08501504.translation: To Quintus Valerius, son of Caius, of the Voltinian tribe, from Macedon, flamen of the youth, quaestor of the colony of Viennensium, duovir of the treasury, augur, a commissioner for public places. To this man, the divine Hadrian offered the broad stripe with the quaestorship and accepted his request for exemption. The villagers of Boxsanus and Noiomagenses [dedicate this] to their patron.
EDCS-08501504.summary: A dedication by villagers to their patron Quintus Valerius, listing his numerous civic and religious offices in the colony of Viennensium, and noting an honor from Emperor Hadrian.

EDCS-08501505.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Valeria Iulia and Sabina, daughter. Set up by herself while alive, and dedicated under the axe.
EDCS-08501505.summary: A funerary epitaph for Valeria Iulia and her daughter Sabina, set up by Valeria Iulia herself.

EDCS-08501508.translation: Here rests in peace, of good memory, Leubatena, who lived 45 years, died on the 14th day before the Kalends of February, in the consulship of Volusianus, most illustrious man.
EDCS-08501508.summary: A funerary epitaph for Leubatena, recording her age at death and the consul Volusianus, likely from the 3rd century AD.

EDCS-08501512.translation: Constantiola rests here in peace, who lived 20 years and 3 months. She departed on the 22nd of February, after the third consulship of Leo.
EDCS-08501512.summary: A funerary inscription for Constantiola, dating to the period after the third consulship of Leo (likely 470s AD), recording her lifespan and death date.

EDCS-08501513.translation: Here rests in peace the young man of good memory, Levanius, who lived 16 years and 6 months. He departed from this life on the 22nd of February, after the consulship of the most illustrious men, Florentius and Anthemis.
EDCS-08501513.summary: A funerary inscription for the young man Levanius, who died on February 22nd after the consulship of Florentius and Anthemis (455 AD), recording his age and death date.

EDCS-08501519.translation: To the departed spirits. Alcius Sabinianus dedicated this monument to his incomparable wife Selia Sexta, who lived with him for 23 years, 5 months, and 21 days. Her brother Sextinus also took care of its erection, and they dedicated it under the chisel.
EDCS-08501519.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to Selia Sexta by her husband Alcius Sabinianus and her brother Sextinus, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century AD, detailing her lifespan and the dedicators.

EDCS-08501521.translation: Receive, Placidia, appeased one, who served you with faith, piety, and power, filled with the fruits of her thirtieth widowhood, she attained the third place in martyrdom; she lived sixty years.
EDCS-08501521.summary: An epitaph likely for a Christian woman named Placidia, possibly a martyr, who lived to sixty years and had experienced thirty years of widowhood.

EDCS-08501526.translation: To the departed spirits. Trebellia Tyche to her patron Quintus Trebellius Macareus, who deserved well of her.
EDCS-08501526.summary: A funerary dedication from Trebellia Tyche to her patron Quintus Trebellius Macareus, likely from the 1st to 3rd century AD.

EDCS-08501527.translation: To Marcus Apronius Eutropus, physician, Augustalis decurion, and to his wife Clodia Apronia Clodilla, his best parents.
EDCS-08501527.summary: A funerary dedication to Marcus Apronius Eutropus and his wife Clodia Apronia Clodilla, honoring their roles as parents and his profession as a physician and Augustalis decurion, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-08501528.translation: To the departed spirits. For Contessia Martina, who died at 5 years and 3 months. Caius Titius Sedulus and Contessia Severina, patrons of their dearest foster-daughter, dedicated this.
EDCS-08501528.summary: A funerary inscription for a young child, Contessia Martina, who died at the age of five years and three months, dedicated by her patrons, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-08501531.translation: To Marcus Sextius Atticus, freedman of Primus.
EDCS-08501531.summary: A simple dedication or epitaph for Marcus Sextius Atticus, a freedman of Primus.

EDCS-08501532.translation: Sacred to Apollo, from a vow. Gaius Virius Victor and Lucius Virius Vitalis willingly and deservedly fulfilled (their vow).
EDCS-08501532.summary: This is a votive inscription to Apollo by Gaius Virius Victor and Lucius Virius Vitalis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501533.translation: Dedicated to Apollo Augustus by Nattia Severa, daughter of Soillus, in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-08501533.summary: A dedication to Apollo Augustus, made by Nattia Severa in fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-08501536.translation: To Fortuna, from a vow. Lucius Terentius Sabinus.
EDCS-08501536.summary: This is a votive inscription to Fortuna by Lucius Terentius Sabinus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501537.translation: A statue of the Genius. Namerius Euprepes, magister of the hastiferi, gave as a gift.
EDCS-08501537.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a statue of the Genius by Namerius Euprepes, an official of the hastiferi, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501538.translation: To the Genius and Honor of the 'utricularii' (boatmen/water carriers). Aurelius Eutyches and Antonius Pelagius, immunes (tax-exempt soldiers/officials), dedicated this from their own funds. Aurelius Marinus also granted the site by decree of the 'utricularii'.
EDCS-08501538.summary: A dedication to the Genius and Honor of the 'utricularii' by Aurelius Eutyches and Antonius Pelagius, with the site granted by Aurelius Marinus, likely from the 3rd century AD.

EDCS-08501539.translation: Sacred to Juno Regina Augusta. Titus Cassius Eros and his sons Cassius Priscus, Euphemus, and Secundus.
EDCS-08501539.summary: This is a sacred dedication to Juno Regina Augusta by Titus Cassius Eros and his sons, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501540.translation: To Jupiter, from a vow, Sentius Sabinus and Sentius Amabilis.
EDCS-08501540.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Jupiter by two individuals, Sentius Sabinus and Sentius Amabilis, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-08501541.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, from a vow, Lucius Crepereius Marinus.
EDCS-08501541.summary: This inscription records a vow made to Jupiter Best and Greatest by Lucius Crepereius Marinus.

EDCS-08501542.translation: Lucius Rufius Rufinus gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Jupiter Best and Greatest and to Augusta Venus.
EDCS-08501542.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow by Lucius Rufius Rufinus to Jupiter Best and Greatest and Venus Augusta.

EDCS-08501544.translation: To Mars. Sextus Contessius Verus, aedile.
EDCS-08501544.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the god Mars by Sextus Contessius Verus in his capacity as aedile.

EDCS-08501547.translation: Decimus Dimarius Messulus restored this to the August Mother from a vow.
EDCS-08501547.summary: This inscription records the restoration of something to the August Mother by Decimus Dimarius Messulus, in fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-08501548.translation: Gnaeus Pompeius Quartus gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the August Mother.
EDCS-08501548.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow by Gnaeus Pompeius Quartus to the August Mother.

EDCS-08501549.translation: To the August Mother, Caius Titius Sedulus from a vow.
EDCS-08501549.summary: This inscription records a vow made to the August Mother by Caius Titius Sedulus.

EDCS-08501551.translation: Sacred to Mercury, Lucius Taietius Chresimus, Augustalis *IIIIII vir*, from a vow.
EDCS-08501551.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Mercury by Lucius Taietius Chresimus, an Augustalis *IIIIII vir*, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-08501552.translation: Sacred to August Mercury, Publicius Avinis.
EDCS-08501552.summary: This inscription records a dedication to August Mercury by Publicius Avinis.

EDCS-08501553.translation: To August Mercury, having undertaken a vow, Titus Laetorius Duellus Antestianus and Laetorius Numida Antestianus, father and son, give.
EDCS-08501553.summary: This inscription records a dedication to August Mercury by Titus Laetorius Duellus Antestianus and his son Laetorius Numida Antestianus, fulfilling an undertaken vow.

EDCS-08501556.translation: To the Chthonic Gods, Pluto and Proserpina, Cornelia, daughter of Gaius, from a vow.
EDCS-08501556.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Pluto and Proserpina by Cornelia, daughter of Gaius, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-08501557.translation: To Silvanus Augustus Primigenius, the freedman of Victor, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-08501557.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Silvanus Augustus by a freedman, dated by the names of the deities and the honorific 'Augustus'.

EDCS-08501559.translation: Gellia Iucunda willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow to the god Sucellus.
EDCS-08501559.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the god Sucellus by Gellia Iucunda.

EDCS-08501561.translation: Sapavidus and Campana set these up for the Holy Virgins.
EDCS-08501561.summary: This is a dedication to the 'Holy Virgins' by Sapavidus and Campana.

EDCS-08501562.translation: In the second consulship of the Emperor Caesar Nerva Trajan Augustus Germanicus, from the temple offerings.
EDCS-08501562.summary: This inscription records the building of something under the consuls of Trajan's second year, possibly indicating a public work funded by temple offerings.

EDCS-08501564.translation: To Afer, in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-08501564.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made by someone named Afer.

EDCS-08501569.translation: To Germanicus Caesar, son of Emperor Tiberius Augustus, grandson of the deified Augustus, great-grandson of the deified Julius.
EDCS-08501569.summary: This inscription honors Germanicus Caesar, providing his full lineage up to Julius Caesar.

EDCS-08501570.translation: To Drusus Caesar, son of Emperor Tiberius Augustus, grandson of the deified Augustus, great-grandson of the deified Julius, holding the tribunician power for the second time, consul for the second time.
EDCS-08501570.summary: This inscription honors Drusus Caesar, detailing his imperial lineage and his consulships and tribunician power.

EDCS-08501571.translation: To Gaius Caesar, son of Germanicus, grandson of Emperor Tiberius Augustus, great-grandson of the deified Augustus, Germanicus, the pontifex, quaestor.
EDCS-08501571.summary: This inscription honors Gaius Caesar (Caligula), detailing his imperial lineage and his religious and administrative offices.

EDCS-08501572.translation: To Gaius Caesar, son of Germanicus, grandson of Emperor Tiberius Augustus, great-grandson of the deified Augustus, Germanicus, the pontifex, quaestor.
EDCS-08501572.summary: This inscription honors Gaius Caesar (Caligula), detailing his imperial lineage and his religious and administrative offices, similar to EDCS-08501571.

EDCS-08501575.translation: To our lord Flavius Constantinus, the greatest and invincible Augustus, by virtue most strong and piety most clement, Marcus Alfius Apronianus, vir perfectissimus, praeses of the province of Flavia Viennensis, devoted to his divine majesty.
EDCS-08501575.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Marcus Alfius Apronianus, a high-ranking official, to Emperor Constantine, likely from the 4th century CE.

EDCS-08501576.translation: To Gaius Bellicus Calpurnius Torquatus, most excellent consul, citizen, patron of the Viennenses.
EDCS-08501576.summary: This is a dedication to the consul Gaius Bellicus Calpurnius Torquatus, honoring him as patron by the people of Vienne.

EDCS-08501577.translation: To Marcus Julius Atticus, son of Gaius, of the Voltinian tribe, procurator of two provinces.
EDCS-08501577.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Julius Atticus, son of Gaius, who served as procurator of two provinces.

EDCS-08501579.text_edition: \n Caio Iulio Pacatiano viro egregio procuratori Augustorum nostrorum militiis equestribus perfuncto procuratori provinciae Osrhoenae praefecto legionis Parthicae procuratori Alpium Coritt<i>arum adlecto inter comites Augggustorum nnnostrorum procuratori pro legato provinciae Mauretaniae Tingitanae colonia Aelia Augusta Italica patrono merentissimo\n
EDCS-08501579.translation: To Gaius Julius Pacatianus, an outstanding man, procurator of our Emperors in equestrian military service, procurator of the province of Osrhoena, prefect of the Parthian legion, procurator of the Cottian Alps, enrolled among the companions of our Emperors, acting governor of the province of Mauretania Tingitana, a most deserving patron of the colonia Aelia Augusta Italica.
EDCS-08501579.summary: This extensive inscription details the distinguished career of Gaius Julius Pacatianus, listing his various procuratorial and prefectural appointments under the Roman Emperors, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-08501582.translation: To Quintus Valerius Lupercus, son of Quintus, of the Voltinian tribe, urban quaestor, tribune of the plebs, praetor-designate. Quintus Pullius Secundus with his wife Flavia Tertia and sons Pullius Secundus and Priscus and daughter Pullia Prisca. Pullius Gallus with his wife.
EDCS-08501582.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Valerius Lupercus, listing his career, and also mentions his family members and another family, Pullius Gallus and his wife.

EDCS-08501589.translation: To the most excellent patron, from the freedmen Bellinus and Ninnus.
EDCS-08501589.summary: This is an inscription from two freedmen, Bellinus and Ninnus, dedicated to their patron.

EDCS-08501590.translation: To Marcus Coelius Lectus, son of Cnaeus, of the Voltinian tribe, prefect of the engineers, tribune of the III Gallica legion, duovir of the treasury, pontiff, aedile.
EDCS-08501590.summary: This inscription details the career of Marcus Coelius Lectus, including military and civic positions.

EDCS-08501592.translation: To Decimus Julius Capito, son of Decimus, of the Voltinian tribe, flamen of the youth, duovir of public places, duovir of the treasury, augur, prefect of the engineers, tribune of the II Adiutrix legion, censor of the federated civitas of the Remi. The place was publicly granted at Remi by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-08501592.summary: This inscription records the public grant of a place to Decimus Julius Capito in the civitas of the Remi, listing his numerous civic and religious offices.

EDCS-08501594.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Minnius Vestinus, a retired centurion of the 13th Urban Cohort, a councilor of Lugudunum, erected and dedicated this under the axe for his dearest: his father Venustus, a councilor of the civitas of the Sogiontii, and his brother Sextus Minnius Valerianus, son of the same, and his cousin Sextus Minnius Quintilianus.
EDCS-08501594.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Minnius Vestinus to honor his father and other relatives, likely in the late Roman Empire.

EDCS-08501595.translation: Marcus Valerius Rufus, Publius Tincius Pacatus, Lucius Tincius Tertius, Lucius Tarius Rufus, Sextus Valerius Venator, Valerius Crispinus, and Sextus Calvisius Quietus, friends, [erected this] for Gaius Passierus Afro, son of Publius, of the Voltinia tribe, a military tribune of the 22nd Legion, a quaestor, a flamen of the deified Augustus, a flamen of Germanicus Caesar, and a prefect of the engineers.
EDCS-08501595.summary: This monument was dedicated by friends to Gaius Passierus Afro, a prominent local official and priest, likely in the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-08501598.translation: To Sextus, son of Sextus, Laetus, aedile, by the urban plebs (?).
EDCS-08501598.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Sextus Laetus, an aedile, possibly sponsored by the urban plebs, with a lacuna for the specific deity or purpose.

EDCS-08501600.translation: The carpenters of Vienna, for their patron Lucius Aquilius Severianus, son of Lucius, of the Voltinia tribe, aedile, duovir, treasurer, and master carpenter.
EDCS-08501600.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the carpenters' guild to their patron, Lucius Aquilius Severianus, a local magistrate, probably in the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-08501601.translation: Attia Priscilla for herself [and...] on account of whose dedication she gave sportulas (cash gifts) of two denarii for the dendrophori.
EDCS-08501601.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Attia Priscilla for herself and possibly others, involving a distribution of cash for the dendrophori on the occasion of a dedication.

EDCS-08501602.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Lucius Vibrius Eutyches for his most devoted wife, Aurelia Prima, a member of the Augustan priestly college.
EDCS-08501602.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Lucius Vibrius Eutyches for his wife Aurelia Prima, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-08501603.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Quintus Connius Sauria, a priest of the college of Six, an Augustalis. Quintus Connius Aper, to his most devoted father and his grandfather, a priest of the college of Six, an Augustalis.
EDCS-08501603.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Quintus Connius Aper for his father and grandfather, both priests of the college of Six and Augustales, dating to the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-08501604.translation: This place was granted by decree of the councilors to Domitius, son of Sextus, of the Voltinia tribe.
EDCS-08501604.summary: This inscription records the allocation of public space by local councilors to Domitius, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501613.summary: This brief inscription records a donation by someone named Justinus, without further context.

EDCS-08501614.translation: Lucius Litugius, son of Sextus, of the Laena family, quaestor of the colony of Viennenses.
EDCS-08501614.summary: This is a dedication or record of office for Lucius Litugius, a quaestor in the Roman colony of Viennenses, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501615.translation: For Aulus Lucilius Cantabrus, quaestor of the colony of Viennenses.
EDCS-08501615.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Aulus Lucilius Cantabrus, who held the office of quaestor in the colony of Viennenses, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08501617.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely records a dedication by the daughter of a prefect named Marcellus, the exact nature of which is lost.

EDCS-08501618.translation: To Sextus Marius Navus, aedile. Decimus Marius Martinus ordered this to be made by his will.
