EDCS-09201808.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Fabius Hermes, a dropacistes, set up for himself and his family.

EDCS-09201810.translation: To the Divine Shades: Vitalis, comrade of Primion, who worked in the iron mines.
EDCS-09201810.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the Divine Shades for Vitalis, comrade of Primion.

EDCS-09201811.translation: Gnaeus Pompius Maximus Fontanus, son of Gnaeus, [set this up] for himself and for Gnaeus Pompius Maximus, his grandfather, son of Gnaeus, and for Gaius Marius, his father, in accordance with his will.
EDCS-09201811.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gnaeus Pompius Maximus Fontanus, set up for himself, his grandfather, and his father.

EDCS-09201812.translation: Censor Iugarius, while alive, [set this up] for himself and...
EDCS-09201812.summary: This is a partial funerary epitaph for Censor Iugarius, set up for himself.

EDCS-09201813.translation: To the Divine Shades: For Quintus Valerius Virrilio, a student of law, and for his sister Valeria Quita. Annia, mother [dedicated this].
EDCS-09201813.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Valerius Virrilio and his sister Valeria Quita, dedicated by their mother Annia.

EDCS-09201814.translation: To the Shades: Of Reburrus, son of Virilis, a linen merchant.
EDCS-09201814.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Reburrus, son of Virilis, a linen merchant.

EDCS-09201815.translation: To the Divine Shades: For Caius Antistius Antus, the doctor. Syneros, freedman of Antistia Irena.
EDCS-09201815.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Antistius Antus, dedicated by his freedman Syneros.

EDCS-09201816.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, of Titus Caecilius Optatus, aedile of the colony.
EDCS-09201816.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Titus Caecilius Optatus, an aedile of a colony.

EDCS-09201817.translation: To Flavia Hedo, a doctor, by her will.
EDCS-09201817.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the doctor Flavia Hedo, according to her will.

EDCS-09201818.translation: To Lucius Avidius Secundus, a musician; his wife Festa.
EDCS-09201818.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the musician Lucius Avidius Secundus, set up by his wife Festa.

EDCS-09201819.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, to Lucius Trebonius Nicephorus Patillus, a tavern keeper; Maximius Epaphroditus, to his best friend.
EDCS-09201819.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Maximius Epaphroditus to his friend Lucius Trebonius Nicephorus Patillus, a tavern keeper.

EDCS-09201820.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, to Gaius Julius Albus, a food vendor; his wife Spuria Euplia.
EDCS-09201820.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Gaius Julius Albus, a food vendor, set up by his wife Spuria Euplia.

EDCS-09201821.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, to Afrodis Symmele of the troop of Galli from Memphis and Paris, pantomime performers, with Sextus as administrator.
EDCS-09201821.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Afrodis Symmele, a pantomime performer, associated with a troop from Memphis and Paris.

EDCS-09201822.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, to Marcus Hortensius Primus, a musician in the sacred rites.
EDCS-09201822.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Marcus Hortensius Primus, a musician associated with religious ceremonies.

EDCS-09201823.translation: Hail Naevius, be well, whoever you are, to Gnaeus Naevius Diadumenus, a slave dealer in Greek.
EDCS-09201823.summary: This is a greeting and wish for well-being directed towards Gnaeus Naevius Diadumenus, a dealer in Greek slaves.

EDCS-09201824.translation: Gaius Terentius Romulus, also known as Drimulus, wrestler or masseur, made this in his lifetime for himself and his family.
EDCS-09201824.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Gaius Terentius Romulus, who was involved in athletic activities, for himself and his family.

EDCS-09201825.translation: Lucius Valerius Secundinus, twice master of the guild of water-skin makers of Nîmes, placed this in his lifetime.
EDCS-09201825.summary: This is a funerary monument placed by Lucius Valerius Secundinus, who twice held the leadership of the guild of water-skin makers in Nîmes.

EDCS-09201826.translation: To Gaius Maius Saturninus, a horn-blower.
EDCS-09201826.summary: This is a dedication to Gaius Maius Saturninus, who held the rank of cornicularius, possibly a military or administrative official.

EDCS-09201827.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Publius Brittius Saturninus.

EDCS-09201828.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Faustus Terpnus Strobilus had this made at his own expense for Lucius Iulius Phtongus, his most devoted patron.
EDCS-09201828.summary: This funerary dedication, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE, honors a patron named Lucius Iulius Phtongus, with Faustus Terpnus Strobilus as the dedicator.

EDCS-09201830.translation: The first of the freedmen magistrates, Gnaeus Aemilius Dionysius, had this made at his own expense.
EDCS-09201830.summary: This inscription records Gnaeus Aemilius Dionysius, holding the office of first freedman magistrate, commissioning a work at his own expense.

EDCS-09201831.translation: To Albucius Postumus of the Voltinian tribe, from Aquae, and to Titus Albucius Tertius of the Voltinian tribe, from Aquae.
EDCS-09201831.summary: This inscription records a dedication to two individuals, Albucius Postumus and Titus Albucius Tertius, both from Aquae and belonging to the Voltinian tribe.

EDCS-09201832.translation: Titus Firmius Marinus, son of Firmanus, of the Voltinian tribe, a Vocontian, made this for himself while alive.
EDCS-09201832.summary: This is a self-funded funerary monument erected by Titus Firmius Marinus, indicating his tribal affiliation and origin.

EDCS-09201833.summary: This inscription simply identifies Sextus Iulius Balbus and notes his likely origin or association with Galatia.

EDCS-09201834.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Iulia Articilla placed this, while alive, for her most excellent husband, Tertius Pompeius Maternus, a citizen of Reia, and for herself.
EDCS-09201834.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up by Iulia Articilla for her husband Tertius Pompeius Maternus and herself, identifying him as a citizen of Reia.

EDCS-09201835.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Parents [set this up] for Lucius Taurinus Aurelius, citizen of Elusa, aged 23.
EDCS-09201835.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Lucius Taurinus Aurelius, a 23-year-old citizen of Elusa, commemorated by his parents.

EDCS-09201836.translation: Andusia Brugetia, Tedusia, Vatrute, Ugerni, Sextantius Briginnus, Statuma, Virinnus, Ucetia, Segusion.
EDCS-09201836.summary: This inscription appears to be a list of names, possibly a dedication or record of individuals associated with a particular place or event, likely of Gallic origin.

EDCS-09201838.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Publius Acilius Ionicus; his wife Domitia [placed this].
EDCS-09201838.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Publius Acilius Ionicus, placed by his wife Domitia.

EDCS-09201839.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Publius Acilius Thesmi, the host, his freedman [placed this].
EDCS-09201839.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Publius Acilius Thesmi, the host, placed by his freedman.

EDCS-09201841.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Quintus Acutius Hermetis; Quintus Atilius Acutius, his patron, [placed this].
EDCS-09201841.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Quintus Acutius Hermetis, placed by his patron Quintus Atilius Acutius.

EDCS-09201842.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Lucius Acutius Severinus; Ventidia Nice placed this for her husband and for herself while alive, and Lucius Acutius Ventidius, his son, [also contributed].
EDCS-09201842.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Lucius Acutius Severinus, placed by his wife Ventidia Nice and their son Lucius Acutius Ventidius.

EDCS-09201844.translation: Adgennus, son of Cassicus, made [this] for his parents and for himself while alive.
EDCS-09201844.summary: This is a dedication made by Adgennus, son of Cassicus, for his parents and himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-09201845.translation: Adgonna, daughter of Excingillus, for herself and her family.
EDCS-09201845.summary: This is a dedication by Adgonna, daughter of Excingillus, for herself and her family.

EDCS-09201846.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Aelius Seneucus; Senucia Acte placed [this] for her excellent freedman.
EDCS-09201846.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Aelius Seneucus, placed by Senucia Acte for her freedman.

EDCS-09201847.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Aelia Athenais; Lucius Aelius Thallus [placed this] for his most chaste wife.
EDCS-09201847.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Aelia Athenais, placed by her husband Lucius Aelius Thallus.

EDCS-09201848.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Aelia Hermis; Aelius Dionysius [placed this] for his incomparable and most loving wife.
EDCS-09201848.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Aelia Hermis, placed by her husband Aelius Dionysius.

EDCS-09201849.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Aemilius [dedicated this] for himself and for his dearest wife.
EDCS-09201849.summary: This funerary inscription records a self-dedication and dedication to a wife by Lucius Aemilius.

EDCS-09201850.translation: Quintus Aemilius Daccus, son of Quintus, of the Voltinia tribe, [dedicated this] for himself and for Secunda, daughter of Sextus, his wife.
EDCS-09201850.summary: This funerary inscription records a self-dedication and dedication to his wife Secunda by Quintus Aemilius Daccus.

EDCS-09201851.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Titius Aemilius Diadumenus. Aemilius Dubl, his freedman, [dedicated this] to the most dutiful.
EDCS-09201851.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication to Titius Aemilius Diadumenus by his freedman Aemilius Dubl.

EDCS-09201852.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Titus Aemilius Diocletus. Senucia Maxima [dedicated this] to her most excellent, dearest, and dutiful husband.
EDCS-09201852.summary: This funerary inscription records Senucia Maxima dedicating a monument to her husband, Titus Aemilius Diocletus.

EDCS-09201853.translation: To Aemilia Spragis, daughter of Lucius Aemilius. To Baebia Primula, wife of Aemilius Festus, son of Lucius. Secundinus and Restituta, their freedmen, [dedicated this].
EDCS-09201853.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication to Aemilia Spragis and Baebia Primula by their freedmen Secundinus and Restituta.

EDCS-09201854.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Lucius Aemilius Optatus. Quarta Lucilla [dedicated this] to her most excellent husband.
EDCS-09201854.summary: This funerary inscription records Quarta Lucilla dedicating a monument to her husband, Lucius Aemilius Optatus.

EDCS-09201855.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Sextus Aemilius Verus and Titia, his wife. Paratus and Mansuetus, his freedmen, [dedicated this] according to his will.
EDCS-09201855.summary: This funerary inscription records freedmen Paratus and Mansuetus dedicating a monument to Sextus Aemilius Verus and his wife Titia, as per his will.

EDCS-09201856.translation: Lucius Aemilius Vinius [dedicated this] for himself and for his brother Marcus Aemilius Catulus, and for his sisters Maxima and Secunda.
EDCS-09201856.summary: This funerary inscription records a self-dedication and dedication to siblings by Lucius Aemilius Vinius.

EDCS-09201857.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication to Aemilia, daughter of Lucius.

EDCS-09201858.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Aemilia Achillia. Aemilius Achilleus, her daughter, [dedicated this] to the most loving daughter.
EDCS-09201858.summary: This funerary inscription records Aemilius Achilleus dedicating a monument to his daughter Aemilia Achillia.

EDCS-09201859.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Gaius Cepionius Primus set up this monument to his incomparable wife Aemilia Calligenia and to himself while alive.
EDCS-09201859.summary: A funerary monument set up by Gaius Cepionius Primus for his wife Aemilia Calligenia and himself.

EDCS-09201860.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Aemilia Eupraxia, who lived 30 years. Aemilia Onesime, her mother, set this up for her freedmen and freedwomen and for herself while alive.
EDCS-09201860.summary: A funerary monument set up by Aemilia Onesime for her daughter Aemilia Eupraxia, her freedpersons, and herself.

EDCS-09201861.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Aemilia Primitiva. Her husband Privatus set this up.
EDCS-09201861.summary: A funerary monument set up by Privatus for his wife Aemilia Primitiva.

EDCS-09201862.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Aemilia Secunda, daughter of Valerius. Marcus Cornelius Carpophorus set this up for his most deserving wife.
EDCS-09201862.summary: A funerary monument set up by Marcus Cornelius Carpophorus for his wife Aemilia Secunda.

EDCS-09201863.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Aemilia Zoe, their most dutiful daughter. Her parents set this up.
EDCS-09201863.summary: A funerary monument set up by the parents for their daughter Aemilia Zoe.

EDCS-09201864.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Aetoria Glycera. Aetorius Hermes set this up for his wife.
EDCS-09201864.summary: A funerary monument set up by Aetorius Hermes for his wife Aetoria Glycera.

EDCS-09201865.translation: To his most dutiful daughter, to his excellent wife.
EDCS-09201865.summary: A funerary monument set up by an unnamed man for his daughter and wife.

EDCS-09201866.translation: To Belatulla. Tertius Honoratus, a citizen, and Valentina, daughter of Aulus, set this up for their parents and sister.
EDCS-09201866.summary: A funerary monument set up by Tertius Honoratus and Valentina for their parents and sister.

EDCS-09201867.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Albinus. His colleagues set this up.
EDCS-09201867.summary: A funerary monument set up by the colleagues for Albinus.

EDCS-09201868.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Albinus Adiutor. His son Vitalis made this.
EDCS-09201868.summary: A funerary monument set up by Vitalis for his father Albinus Adiutor.

EDCS-09201869.translation: To Albisia Secunda, daughter of Cnaeus, by her will.
EDCS-09201869.summary: This inscription records a posthumous dedication to Albisia Secunda, likely made according to her testamentary provisions.

EDCS-09201870.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Naevia Chrysa erected this for Alexander the Augur, her dearest husband, and for herself while alive.
EDCS-09201870.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Naevia Chrysa for her husband, Alexander the Augur, with provision for herself.

EDCS-09201871.translation: To Alleyorigis Crappai, his wife Iulia.
EDCS-09201871.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Iulia to her husband, Alleyorigis Crappai.

EDCS-09201872.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld for Lucius Allidius I.
EDCS-09201872.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Lucius Allidius I.

EDCS-09201873.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld for Caius Allius, son of Caius, Voltinia Macrini; Euporus and Tryphaena, freedmen.
EDCS-09201873.summary: This funerary inscription is set up by the freedmen Euporus and Tryphaena for their patron, Caius Allius, son of Caius, of the Voltinian tribe.

EDCS-09201874.translation: Marcus Allius Vitalis made this by his will.
EDCS-09201874.summary: This inscription records a monument constructed by Marcus Allius Vitalis according to his will.

EDCS-09201876.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld for Ambridius Filiscus; Aurelia Titia, to her most excellent husband.
EDCS-09201876.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Aurelia Titia to her husband, Ambridius Filiscus.

EDCS-09201877.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Decimus Anicius Alpinus.

EDCS-09201878.translation: To Caius Anicius Fronton, of the Voltinian tribe.
EDCS-09201878.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Caius Anicius Fronton, who belonged to the Voltinian tribe.

EDCS-09201879.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld for Caius Annius Diadumenus; Rusticus, Secundinus, and Primula, freedmen.
EDCS-09201879.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by the freedmen Rusticus, Secundinus, and Primula for their deceased patron, Caius Annius Diadumenus.

EDCS-09201880.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Coionius Eutyches to his dearest wife and sister Annia Eutycheides and Mascellionis, whom he survived by 15 days.
EDCS-09201880.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Annia Eutycheides and Mascellionis, dedicated by Coionius Eutyches, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201881.translation: To the Chthonic Gods. Appius Annius Apollaustianus to his most devoted mother, Annia Eutychia.
EDCS-09201881.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the chthonic gods for Annia Eutychia, made by her son Appius Annius Apollaustianus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201882.translation: To Annia Conni, daughter of Mogillo. Statutus, her husband.
EDCS-09201882.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Annia Conni, dedicated by her husband Statutus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201883.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Flavia, wife to Antilochus.
EDCS-09201883.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Antilochus, dedicated by his wife Flavia, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201884.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Caius Antistius Epictetus and Pompeia Quintilla, parents, to their son Cai Antistius Quintillus, who lived 12 years and 10 months.
EDCS-09201884.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Cai Antistius Quintillus, dedicated by his parents Caius Antistius Epictetus and Pompeia Quintilla, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201885.translation: To the Spirits of Antoni Secundus Vassedonis.
EDCS-09201885.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Antoni Secundus Vassedonis, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201886.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Valeria Pompeia to her most dutiful son, Sextus Antonius Valerianus.
EDCS-09201886.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sextus Antonius Valerianus, dedicated by his mother Valeria Pompeia, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201887.translation: To Antonia Fica, to her deserving wife.
EDCS-09201887.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Antonia Fica, dedicated by her husband, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201888.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. To Antonia Virilis, daughter of Severa. To the Spirits of the Underworld. Lucius Trexius Valerianus, son, to Lucius Trexius Epagatus.
EDCS-09201888.summary: This is a complex funerary epitaph commemorating Antonia Virilis and Lucius Trexius Epagatus, with dedications from their respective relatives, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201889.translation: To the Spirits of Apicius Marcellus. Apicius Primulus, grandson.
EDCS-09201889.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Apicius Marcellus, dedicated by his grandson Apicius Primulus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201890.translation: To the Divine Shades. Caius Quartius Quintinus, a friend, set this up for Caius Apisius Zosimus and his wife Romogillia Festa.
EDCS-09201890.summary: Funerary monument set up by a friend for a couple, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201891.translation: To the Divine Shades. Macria Primula, a most devoted sister, set this up for her brother Lucius Aponianus, who lived 10 years, 6 months, and 2 days.
EDCS-09201891.summary: Funerary monument set up by a sister for her brother, recording his age at death, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201892.summary: Dedication or funerary marker for Gaius Appius Primulus, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201893.translation: For Aprilis Attia, to her well-deserving partner.
EDCS-09201893.summary: Funerary monument set up by a woman for her partner, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201894.translation: To the Divine Shades.rania Aphrodisia, mother, [set this up] for her rani Aphrodisius.
EDCS-09201894.summary: Funerary monument set up by a mother for her son, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201895.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Gaius Apronius Fulvus and his wife Servata.
EDCS-09201895.summary: Funerary monument for a couple, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201896.summary: Dedication or funerary marker for Quintus Apuleius Salitus, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201898.translation: To the Divine Shades. Callirhoe, daughter, set this up for Aquilius Fortesminus.
EDCS-09201898.summary: Funerary monument set up by a daughter for her father, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201899.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Lucius Aquilius Privatus. Lycoris Anicia, wife, and Quartius, freedman.
EDCS-09201899.summary: Funerary monument for Lucius Aquilius Privatus, set up by his wife and freedman, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201900.translation: To the Divine Shades. Quintus Cornelius Tertullinus [set this up] for Arsinoë, a virtuous and faithful woman.
EDCS-09201900.summary: Funerary monument set up by Quintus Cornelius Tertullinus for Arsinoë, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201901.translation: To the divine spirits of Asconia Quintia, mother of Asconius Auspicatus.
EDCS-09201901.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a mother for her son, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201902.translation: To Asellia Muta, Publius Fannius Optatus, Asellia Synete, Publius Fannius Buccio.
EDCS-09201902.summary: This inscription lists names, possibly of family members or individuals associated with a single tomb or funerary dedication, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201903.translation: To the divine spirits of Astylus Peregrinus, a most dutiful son.
EDCS-09201903.summary: This is a funerary dedication for a son, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201904.translation: To Gaius Asuius Atepilla, his father Gaius Asuius Messius, son of Atessatis; Asuia, daughter of Asuius, for herself and her family, according to her will.
EDCS-09201904.summary: This inscription records a dedication and testament, likely for a family tomb, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201905.translation: To Gaius Atilius Eutyches, his most excellent comrade Stephanis.
EDCS-09201905.summary: This is a dedication to a comrade, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201906.translation: To the divine spirits of Lucius Atilius Veratianus; Veratia Valentina, his daughter, placed this for him and for herself while alive.
EDCS-09201906.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a daughter for her father, who also made arrangements for herself, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201907.translation: To the divine spirits of Lucius Atilius Victor.
EDCS-09201907.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Lucius Atilius Victor, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201908.translation: To our Lucius Attalius, his client.
EDCS-09201908.summary: This inscription records a dedication by a client to his patron, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201909.translation: To the divine spirits of Attis, aged four years.
EDCS-09201909.summary: This is a funerary dedication for a child, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201910.translation: To the divine spirits of Gaius Attius Achilleus; Iulia Severina, to her most excellent husband.
EDCS-09201910.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a wife to her husband, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201911.summary: This is a dedication to Gaius Attius Albanus.

EDCS-09201912.translation: Attius Iulius Niger, son of Corradus, for himself and his parents.
EDCS-09201912.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Attius Iulius Niger for himself and his parents.

EDCS-09201913.summary: This is a dedication to Titus Attius Su Martialis.

EDCS-09201914.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Quartus Attius, son of Voltinia Primula.
EDCS-09201914.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Quartus Attius, son of Voltinia Primula.

EDCS-09201915.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Tertiatus Attius, son of Trasias, his father.
EDCS-09201915.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Tertiatus Attius, son of Trasias, for his father.

EDCS-09201916.translation: To Gaius Attius Urbanus, son of Attius, by his will.
EDCS-09201916.summary: This inscription records a bequest in a will for Gaius Attius Urbanus, son of Attius.

EDCS-09201917.translation: Attia Euphemia, who lived 6 years, 5 months. Attius Epaphroditus [erected this] for his most cherished freedwoman.
EDCS-09201917.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Attius Epaphroditus for his freedwoman Attia Euphemia, who died at a young age.

EDCS-09201918.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Attia Exoche. Decimus Iulius Philadespotus erected this for his most devoted wife, Decimus Iulius Philadespotus, while alive.
EDCS-09201918.summary: This funerary inscription records Decimus Iulius Philadespotus setting up a monument for his wife Attia Exoche while he was still alive.

EDCS-09201919.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Attia Felicula. Attia Danae [erected this] for her most devoted sister.
EDCS-09201919.summary: This funerary inscription records Attia Danae setting up a monument for her sister Attia Felicula.

EDCS-09201920.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Attia Peculiaris. Quintus Iulius Attianus [erected this] for his excellent mother.
EDCS-09201920.summary: This funerary inscription records Quintus Iulius Attianus setting up a monument for his mother Attia Peculiaris.

EDCS-09201921.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Quintus Attius Agathopus to his dearest freedwoman and wife, Attia Victorina.
EDCS-09201921.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a freedman to his wife and freedwoman, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09201922.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Caecilia Paullina, a student, set this up to Attia Zosimes and her husband Sextus Vatinus Stephano.
EDCS-09201922.summary: This funerary monument was erected by a student to commemorate her teacher and the teacher's husband.

EDCS-09201923.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Quintus Aemilius Felix to his deserving wife, Augusti Volumniae.
EDCS-09201923.summary: This tombstone records the dedication by a husband to his wife, likely dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-09201924.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Augustal Euphemus to his fellow Augustal, S.B. Epictesis.
EDCS-09201924.summary: A funerary dedication from a member of the Augustales cult to a fellow member, probably from an urban center in the Roman Empire.

EDCS-09201925.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Nemonia Cinge to her partner Aviti Gemelli.
EDCS-09201925.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication from a woman to her male partner, likely indicating a cohabiting relationship.

EDCS-09201926.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Gaius Aviulius S. Cnus set this up to his most worthy wife, Iulia Servanda.
EDCS-09201926.summary: A funerary dedication by a husband, Gaius Aviulius S. Cnus, to his wife Iulia Servanda, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201927.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Catius Gratinus [set this up] to his wife Aviullia Paternus, daughter of Aviullius, and to his freedman Lucius Valerius Pharnaces, and to his daughter-in-law Catia Gratina, daughter of Catius.
EDCS-09201927.summary: This complex funerary inscription records dedications by Catius Gratinus to his wife, his freedman, and his daughter-in-law, suggesting multiple burials or familial rights.

EDCS-09201928.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Licinia Faustina to her most deserving husband, Sextus Avilius Capellianus, set up beneath the axe.
EDCS-09201928.summary: This tombstone records a wife's dedication to her husband, noting it was 'sub ascia', a common funerary practice, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-09201929.translation: To the spirits of the departed. The heirs of Sextus Aurelius Agathones.
EDCS-09201929.summary: This short inscription indicates that the heirs of Sextus Aurelius Agathones have established a funerary monument.

EDCS-09201930.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Titus Aurelius Diadumenus to his fellow freedman, Titus Aurelius Cerinthus.
EDCS-09201930.summary: This is a funerary inscription by one freedman dedicating a monument to a fellow freedman, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201931.translation: To the Divine Manes of Marcus Aurelius Eutyches. Naturia Chrysis dedicated this for her excellent husband and for herself while alive.
EDCS-09201931.summary: A funerary dedication by Naturia Chrysis for her deceased husband, Marcus Aurelius Eutyches, and herself.

EDCS-09201932.translation: To the Divine Manes of Marcus Aurelius Kareis. Marcus Aurelius Cassianus, his son, and Cassia Charite dedicated this for their excellent father and husband, who deserved well of them, and for themselves while alive.
EDCS-09201932.summary: A funerary dedication by Marcus Aurelius Cassianus and Cassia Charite for their deceased husband and father, Marcus Aurelius Kareis, and for themselves.

EDCS-09201933.translation: To the Divine Manes of Lucius Aurelius Utilis.
EDCS-09201933.summary: A simple funerary dedication to Lucius Aurelius Utilis.

EDCS-09201934.translation: To the Divine Manes of Attia, daughter of Caius Aurelius, of the tribe Voltinia.
EDCS-09201934.summary: A funerary dedication to Attia, daughter of Caius Aurelius.

EDCS-09201935.translation: To the Divine Manes of Aurelia Severa, my most dutiful sister. Aurelia Rhode dedicated this.
EDCS-09201935.summary: A funerary dedication by Aurelia Rhode for her sister, Aurelia Severa.

EDCS-09201936.translation: To the Divine Manes of Titia Aurellia, wife of Gnaeus Aurellius, most rare. To the Divine Manes of Decima Aurellia, Titia Aurellia, my sister, and C...
EDCS-09201936.summary: A fragmented funerary dedication likely for Titia Aurellia, wife of Gnaeus Aurellius, and her sister Decima Aurellia.

EDCS-09201937.translation: For Gaius Autestius Paluster, son of Quintus, of the tribe Voltinia.
EDCS-09201937.summary: An inscription honoring Gaius Autestius Paluster.

EDCS-09201938.translation: Baebius Cornutus made this for himself and for his wife, Titia Restituta, while alive.
EDCS-09201938.summary: A funerary monument commissioned by Baebius Cornutus for himself and his wife, Titia Restituta.

EDCS-09201939.translation: The spirits of Lucius Baebius Secundus lie here.
EDCS-09201939.summary: An epitaph indicating the burial place of Lucius Baebius Secundus.

EDCS-09201940.translation: To the Divine Manes of Baebia Pyrallis. Baebia Secundilla, her most dutiful freedwoman, dedicated this.
EDCS-09201940.summary: A funerary dedication by the freedwoman Baebia Secundilla for her patroness, Baebia Pyrallis.

EDCS-09201941.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld, for Balonia Marcia, daughter of Balonius, her most excellent mother.
EDCS-09201941.summary: This is a funerary dedication to a mother, Balonia Marcia.

EDCS-09201942.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld, for Barbarula, who lived 22 years, 2 months, and 4 days. Barbara and Philumenus, parents, and Helicon, for their dearest fellow-soldier. Barbara and Philumenus, alive, placed this for themselves.
EDCS-09201942.summary: This funerary monument was dedicated by parents and a fellow-soldier to Barbarula, and also includes a self-dedication by Barbara and Philumenus.

EDCS-09201943.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld, for Basilice. Lucius Aemilius Hermas.
EDCS-09201943.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lucius Aemilius Hermas to Basilice.

EDCS-09201944.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld, for Belia Primi, daughter of Belia. Marcus Vibius Campanus, for his most excellent wife.
EDCS-09201944.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Marcus Vibius Campanus to his wife, Belia Primi.

EDCS-09201945.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld, for Bellia Secundilla. For Lucius Iulius Callimorphus, his most dutiful freedman.
EDCS-09201945.summary: This is a funerary dedication for a freedman, Lucius Iulius Callimorphus, by Bellia Secundilla.

EDCS-09201946.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld, for Sextus Betutius Trypho. Betutia Polla placed this for her most excellent husband and for herself while alive.
EDCS-09201946.summary: This funerary monument was placed by Betutia Polla for her husband Sextus Betutius Trypho and for herself.

EDCS-09201947.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld, for Betutia Prima, alive for herself and for Publius Popilius Victor, her friend.
EDCS-09201947.summary: This funerary dedication was made by Betutia Prima for herself and for her friend Publius Popilius Victor.

EDCS-09201948.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld, for Titus Blaesius Titianus. Flavia Restituta, for her most dutiful son.
EDCS-09201948.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Flavia Restituta to her son, Titus Blaesius Titianus.

EDCS-09201949.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld, for Hygiae, freedwoman of Sextus Blaesius.
EDCS-09201949.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Hygiae, a freedwoman of Sextus Blaesius.

EDCS-09201950.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld, for Caius Boduacus Maximus. Maximia Paterna, his daughter, and Anthis, freedwoman.
EDCS-09201950.summary: This funerary dedication was made by Maximia Paterna, daughter of Caius Boduacus Maximus, and his freedwoman Anthis.

EDCS-09201951.translation: To the Divine Shades. Phillus erected this for his most dutiful wife, Bonitas.
EDCS-09201951.summary: A funerary dedication by Phillus to his wife, Bonitas.

EDCS-09201952.translation: To the Divine Shades. Terentia Marcella, daughter of Marcus, (erected this) for her excellent mother, Boudia Primula.
EDCS-09201952.summary: A funerary dedication by Terentia Marcella to her mother, Boudia Primula.

EDCS-09201953.translation: Silvana, wife of Boudo son of Valerius Urittonis, (erected this) from her own means.
EDCS-09201953.summary: A funerary dedication by Silvana for her husband, Boudo son of Valerius Urittonis.

EDCS-09201954.translation: To the Divine Shades. Iulius Marcianus, his natural son, (erected this) for Bruis son of Isiada.
EDCS-09201954.summary: A funerary dedication by Iulius Marcianus to Bruis son of Isiada.

EDCS-09201955.translation: To the Divine Shades. Sigeni's mother (erected this) for her most dutiful daughter, Bucconia, and Eutyches, her fellow soldier/companion.
EDCS-09201955.summary: A funerary dedication by Sigeni's mother for her daughter Bucconia and her companion Eutyches.

EDCS-09201956.translation: LIV Ulanus, his son, erected this for his mother, Byrria Fortunata, while she was alive.
EDCS-09201956.summary: A funerary dedication by LIV Ulanus to his mother, Byrria Fortunata, set up during her lifetime.

EDCS-09201957.summary: The name of Publius Caecilius, possibly a tombstone or a dedication fragment.

EDCS-09201958.translation: To the Divine Shades. Homericus, freedman of Lucius Caecilius Aristonius and his heir, (erected this).
EDCS-09201958.summary: A funerary dedication by Homericus, freedman and heir, for Lucius Caecilius Aristonius.

EDCS-09201959.translation: To Lucius Caecilius Atro, in accordance with his will.
EDCS-09201959.summary: A dedication to Lucius Caecilius Atro, established by his will.

EDCS-09201960.translation: To the Divine Shades. Caecilia Campana (erected this) for her most dutiful fellow freedman, Publius Caecilius Bellicus.
EDCS-09201960.summary: A funerary dedication by Caecilia Campana to her fellow freedman, Publius Caecilius Bellicus.

EDCS-09201961.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Caecilius Eutychus made this for himself and his family while alive.
EDCS-09201961.summary: A funerary dedication by Lucius Caecilius Eutychus for himself and his family.

EDCS-09201962.summary: A dedication to Quintus Caecilius Primus, likely a tombstone or a dedicatory tablet.

EDCS-09201963.translation: Quintus Caecilius Nundinus set up this monument while alive to his parents, his wife, his son, and himself: to Quintus Caecilius Rufinus, father, and Faustae Cracconis, mother; to Quintus Caecilius Faustinus, son. The wife Syntyche restored [it].
EDCS-09201963.summary: A funerary monument set up by Quintus Caecilius Nundinus for his family, with a later restoration by his wife Syntyche.

EDCS-09201965.translation: Lucius Caecilius Sextianus [made this] for himself and his family.
EDCS-09201965.summary: A dedication by Lucius Caecilius Sextianus for himself and his family, likely a funerary monument.

EDCS-09201966.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcellus, [his] freedman [dedicated this to] Quintus Caecilius Valerianus.
EDCS-09201966.summary: A funerary dedication by Marcellus, a freedman, to his former master Quintus Caecilius Valerianus.

EDCS-09201967.summary: A dedication to Caecilia, wife of the dedicator, likely a tombstone.

EDCS-09201968.translation: To Caecilia Lucula, daughter of Quintus, [his] granddaughter.
EDCS-09201968.summary: A dedication to Caecilia Lucula, granddaughter of the dedicator, likely a tombstone.

EDCS-09201969.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Caecilia Matures. Iccius Vitalis, [her] companion in the barracks.
EDCS-09201969.summary: A funerary dedication by Iccius Vitalis to Caecilia Matures, indicating a close relationship likely involving military service or shared living quarters.

EDCS-09201970.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Aulus Veratius Onesimus [dedicated this] to his most dutiful wife, Caecilia Onesimes.
EDCS-09201970.summary: A funerary dedication by Aulus Veratius Onesimus to his wife, Caecilia Onesimes.

EDCS-09201971.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Caecilia Saturnina, daughter of Titus.
EDCS-09201971.summary: A funerary dedication to Caecilia Saturnina, daughter of Titus.

EDCS-09201972.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Longus and Eudaemon, freedmen, [erected this] for Caecilia Thalusae.
EDCS-09201972.summary: A funerary dedication by freedmen for their deceased patroness, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09201973.translation: For Caerellia Secundi, for herself and for Hospita.
EDCS-09201973.summary: A funerary dedication for Caerellia Secundi and Hospita, possibly a paired tomb or a dedication to two individuals, dated to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09201974.translation: Marcus Fuscius Nedymus [sent] greetings to his dearest wife, Caesonia Horaeae, [and wishes] greetings to [her].
EDCS-09201974.summary: An unusual epitaph combining a greeting to the deceased with a reciprocal greeting, likely from the late Republic or early Imperial period.

EDCS-09201975.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Calicatius Nigrinus, [son] of Calicatius Niger, father [of] Antonia Servata, mother, erected this for himself and for his wife Optata, while alive.
EDCS-09201975.summary: A funerary dedication by Calicatius Nigrinus for himself, his wife Optata, and commemorating his parents, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09201976.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Helvia Secundilla [erected this] for her excellent husband, Publius Calvius Nasonis.
EDCS-09201976.summary: A funerary dedication by a wife for her deceased husband, Publius Calvius Nasonis, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09201977.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Titus Calvius Pompeiani. Lucius Calvius Secundus and Pompeia Quinti, his daughter Severilla, [erected this] for their most dutiful and most longed-for son, who was undeservedly taken away, a young man of the rarest example, aged 17 years, 5 months, and 6 days.
EDCS-09201977.summary: A detailed funerary inscription by parents and a sibling for a young man who died at 17, likely from the late 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09201978.translation: Cambiae Helenes and Quintus Cambi Cyriadis erected this for themselves and their wife, while alive.
EDCS-09201978.summary: A funerary dedication by two individuals (possibly partners) for themselves and a wife, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09201979.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Quintus Capitonius Messoris.
EDCS-09201979.summary: A simple funerary dedication for Quintus Capitonius Messoris, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09201980.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Sextus Caratus Onesimus. Cambaria Chrysanthe [erected this] for her excellent husband.
EDCS-09201980.summary: A funerary dedication by a wife for her deceased husband, Sextus Caratus Onesimus, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09201981.translation: Titus Carior Ingenuus and Tertius, sons, [erected this] for their wife Corasia Posilla.
EDCS-09201981.summary: A funerary dedication by two sons for their mother, Corasia Posilla, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09201982.translation: To the Divine Manes. Carpophorus and Paulina, parents, to their most dutiful son, Eucarpus.
EDCS-09201982.summary: A funerary dedication by parents to their son, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201983.translation: To the Divine Manes. Volkacius Dioscorus to his most dutiful son, the freedman of Quintus Cassius Eutyches.
EDCS-09201983.summary: A funerary dedication by a father to his son, identifying the son as a freedman, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201984.summary: A dedication to Sassia Libera, possibly funerary, by Cassius T.

EDCS-09201985.translation: To the Divine Manes. Cassia [dedicated this].
EDCS-09201985.summary: A funerary dedication to Cassia Severa, by Cassia.

EDCS-09201986.translation: Caius L. placed this for his daughter Cassia Tertia from his own means.
EDCS-09201986.summary: A funerary dedication by a father, Caius L., for his daughter Cassia Tertia, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201987.translation: To the Manes. Cassicius Isidorus to his beloved fellow freedwoman, Cassicia.
EDCS-09201987.summary: A funerary dedication by a freedman, Cassicius Isidorus, to his fellow freedwoman, Cassicia, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201988.translation: To the Divine Manes. Quintus Soillius Chirisophus to his most exceptional wife, Casunia Philete.
EDCS-09201988.summary: A funerary dedication by a husband, Quintus Soillius Chirisophus, to his wife, Casunia Philete, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201989.translation: To the Divine Manes. Casuria to her most dutiful brother, Marcus Casurius Hortensianus.
EDCS-09201989.summary: A funerary dedication by a sister, Casuria, to her brother, Marcus Casurius Hortensianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201990.translation: To Gnaeus Cerudius Tacitus, son of Marcus.
EDCS-09201990.summary: An inscription honoring Gnaeus Cerudius Tacitus, son of Marcus, possibly funerary or commemorative.

EDCS-09201991.translation: Castus and Romula, freedmen, [dedicated this] to Quintus Cestius Benignus.
EDCS-09201991.summary: A dedication by freedmen, Castus and Romula, to Quintus Cestius Benignus, likely funerary, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201992.translation: To the Divine Shades of Lucius Charitus, to his most excellent wife Hermia.
EDCS-09201992.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Lucius Charitus and his wife Hermia, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09201993.translation: Tatula, to the faithful Cinthia Honorata.
EDCS-09201993.summary: This inscription is a dedication from Tatula to Cinthia Honorata, probably a tombstone from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09201994.translation: Donata Cirratia, wife, to Marcus Cirratius Severus.
EDCS-09201994.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Donata Cirratia to her husband Marcus Cirratius Severus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09201995.translation: Felix, the freedman, erected this to Tiberius Claudius Chrysantus, to the Divine Shades.
EDCS-09201995.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by the freedman Felix to Tiberius Claudius Chrysantus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09201996.translation: To the Divine Shades of Quintus Clodius Vettianus, Indamia Chresime [erected this] for her most excellent husband and Victorinus.
EDCS-09201996.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Indamia Chresime to her husband Quintus Clodius Vettianus and Victorinus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09201997.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Cocusiae Masuciae Cocusia Eutychis liberta piissima\n
EDCS-09201997.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Cocusia Masucia, freedwoman of Cocusia Eutychis, [dedicated this] with the utmost piety.
EDCS-09201997.summary: A funerary dedication for Cocusia Masucia, a freedwoman, by her former owner, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09201998.translation: To the Divine Shades of Quintus Coelius Epytuncanus, Helvia Secundilla [dedicated this] to her comrade.
EDCS-09201998.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Helvia Secundilla to her comrade Quintus Coelius Epytuncanus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09201999.translation: To the Divine Shades of Quintus Coelius Pompeianus, his most unhappy parents, Felix and Alun, [dedicated this to] Coelius Apollinaris and Coelia Eutychia.
EDCS-09201999.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by the parents Felix and Alun to their children Quintus Coelius Pompeianus, Coelius Apollinaris, and Coelia Eutychia, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09202000.translation: To Marcus Collius Faustus, freedman of Ennaeus, of the Palatine tribe, and to Marcus Collius Atticus, freedman of Faustus, of the Palatine tribe.
EDCS-09202000.summary: This inscription records two individuals, Marcus Collius Faustus and Marcus Collius Atticus, both freedmen of members of the Collii family, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09202001.translation: To Publius Cominius Aedemon, to his friends Vadu.
EDCS-09202001.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Publius Cominius Aedemon to his friends Vadu, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09202002.translation: To the Divine Shades of Titus Cominius Asprenas.
EDCS-09202002.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Titus Cominius Asprenas, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09202004.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Congennicia Cornelia.
EDCS-09202004.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Congennicia Cornelia, likely a tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-09202005.translation: Connius Quartulus, son of Numpius, twice freedman.
EDCS-09202005.summary: This inscription seems to record the name and status of Connius Quartulus, possibly on a tombstone or a personal dedication.

EDCS-09202007.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription honoring Gaius Cornelius and Cornelia.

EDCS-09202008.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Lucius Cornelius Athenaeus. His father Anthus.
EDCS-09202008.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Cornelius Athenaeus, dedicated by his father Anthus.

EDCS-09202009.translation: For Titia Sollavia. Marcus Cornelius Helius.
EDCS-09202009.summary: This inscription likely records a dedication or memorial for Titia Sollavia, possibly set up by Marcus Cornelius Helius.

EDCS-09202010.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Caius Cornelius Hermetis.
EDCS-09202010.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Caius Cornelius Hermetis.

EDCS-09202011.translation: To Titus Cornelius Saturio, son of Titus.
EDCS-09202011.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription for Titus Cornelius Saturio, son of Titus.

EDCS-09202012.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Quintus Cornelius Secundus. His wife Hospita.
EDCS-09202012.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Cornelius Secundus, dedicated by his wife Hospita.

EDCS-09202013.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Quintus Cornelius. His testamentary heirs in the Voltinia tribe, Tertes.
EDCS-09202013.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Cornelius, dedicated by his testamentary heirs, Tertes, who are registered in the Voltinia tribe.

EDCS-09202014.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Cornelia Attica.
EDCS-09202014.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Cornelia Attica.

EDCS-09202015.translation: To the departed spirits, Cornelia Chreste.
EDCS-09202015.summary: This is a funerary dedication to a freedwoman named Cornelia Chreste.

EDCS-09202016.translation: To the departed spirits, Cornelia Helpidis. Sergia Corneliane [dedicated this] to her most devoted mother.
EDCS-09202016.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Sergia Corneliane to her mother, Cornelia Helpidis.

EDCS-09202017.translation: Cornelia Etta Mecia made this for herself, her husband, and her son while alive.
EDCS-09202017.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Cornelia Etta Mecia for herself, her husband, and her son.

EDCS-09202018.translation: To the departed spirits, Cornelia Grata. Titus Connius Silanus [dedicated this] to his wife.
EDCS-09202018.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Titus Connius Silanus to his wife, Cornelia Grata.

EDCS-09202019.translation: To the departed spirits, Cornelia Servata. Sextus Cornelius Vitalis [dedicated this] to his excellent mother.
EDCS-09202019.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Sextus Cornelius Vitalis to his mother, Cornelia Servata.

EDCS-09202020.translation: To the departed spirits of Quintus Cosconius Onesimus. Iulia Firmina, his wife [dedicated this].
EDCS-09202020.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Iulia Firmina to her husband, Quintus Cosconius Onesimus.

EDCS-09202021.translation: To the departed spirits. Primulus set this up for his excellent slave woman.
EDCS-09202021.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Primulus for his excellent slave woman.

EDCS-09202022.translation: To the departed spirits, Crispia Aphrodisia. Titus Crispius Corinthus [dedicated this].
EDCS-09202022.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Titus Crispius Corinthus to Crispia Aphrodisia.

EDCS-09202023.translation: To the departed spirits, Caius Cusinius Hermias. Licinia Nice set this up for him, who deserved well of her, and for herself while alive.
EDCS-09202023.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up by Licinia Nice for Caius Cusinius Hermias and herself while alive.

EDCS-09202025.translation: To the departed spirits of Quintus Deccius Senecio.
EDCS-09202025.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Quintus Deccius Senecio.

EDCS-09202026.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Fabius Hermes to his sweetest daughter Decciae Fabiae.
EDCS-09202026.summary: A funerary dedication by a father to his daughter, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09202028.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. To Decurtia, daughter of Titus, named Titula.
EDCS-09202028.summary: A funerary dedication to Decurtia, daughter of Titus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09202029.translation: To Delicatus. To the spirits of the underworld. To Gemina.
EDCS-09202029.summary: A funerary dedication to Gemina, possibly by Delicatus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09202031.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Domitia Maximilla to her excellent freedman Abascanti, freedman of Quintus Domitius.
EDCS-09202031.summary: A funerary dedication by a freedwoman to her freedman, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09202032.summary: A dedication to Lucius Domitius Pusion, likely funerary and from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09202033.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Sextus Gamus, freedman, to his son Sextus Domitius Sparsus.
EDCS-09202033.summary: A funerary dedication by a freedman to his son, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09202034.translation: To Perpetual Rest. To Domitius Tatianus, a most beloved infant, whom cruel death snatched away in the flower of his youth, who lived 3 years, 6 months, 20 days. Donatus and Iovina, his father and mother from Agrippinenses, placed this for their dearest son.
EDCS-09202034.summary: A funerary monument for a young child, Domitius Tatianus, set up by his parents, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-09202035.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Iulia Tyche to her excellent husband Sextus Domitius Tertullinus and for herself, while alive.
EDCS-09202035.summary: A funerary dedication by a wife to her husband, who also set it up for himself during his lifetime, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09202036.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Albius Munatius Epaphroditus to his excellent wife Domitia Chysis.
EDCS-09202036.summary: A funerary dedication by a husband to his wife, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09202037.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Decimus Caecilius Socrates to his wife Domitia Philumene, a woman of the rarest example, and for himself, while alive.
EDCS-09202037.summary: A funerary dedication by a husband to his wife, who also set it up for himself during his lifetime, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09202038.translation: To the divine shades of Domitia Victorina, Gaius Valerius Martius placed this for his most devoted wife and one who deserved well of him, and for himself while alive.
EDCS-09202038.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a husband for his wife and himself, indicating a private grave monument from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202040.translation: Apollonius to Dorcas, his tent-mate and brother.
EDCS-09202040.summary: This is a funerary epitaph likely commemorating a close relationship, possibly military or familial, with the dedicant Apollonius and recipient Dorcas.

EDCS-09202041.translation: Caius Drusius made this for himself and for B., daughter of Cornelius, while alive.
EDCS-09202041.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Caius Drusius for himself and for a woman named B. while he was still alive, suggesting a private tomb or memorial.

EDCS-09202042.translation: Eliponia Hygia, wife, [erected this] to the divine shades of Lucius Eliponius Titullinus.
EDCS-09202042.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a wife for her deceased husband, Lucius Eliponius Titullinus.

EDCS-09202043.translation: Epaphra, the freedwoman, saw to its construction.
EDCS-09202043.summary: This inscription records that Epaphra, a freedwoman, commissioned a construction, likely a funerary monument or a public work.

EDCS-09202045.translation: To the divine shades of Epidia Peculiaris, his freedwoman. Hedone [dedicated this] to her most beloved wife.
EDCS-09202045.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Titus Subrius Hyginus for his wife Hedone, who was formerly his freedwoman.

EDCS-09202046.translation: Verula, daughter of Quintus, to Arignotus, her beloved.
EDCS-09202046.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Verula to her beloved Arignotus, likely a funerary monument or a token of affection.

EDCS-09202048.translation: To the divine shades of Erotis, [the freedman] of Lucius Iulius Iulianus. Terphne, his tent-mate.
EDCS-09202048.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Terphne to her tent-mate Erotis, who was a freedman of Lucius Iulius Iulianus.

EDCS-09202049.translation: Euaristus, the freedman of Titus, and Senecio, the freedman of Ianus.
EDCS-09202049.summary: This inscription records two freedmen, Euaristus and Senecio, possibly related to a shared funerary monument or a legal association.

EDCS-09202050.translation: To his daughter Eunomia, who lived 32 years, 3 months, and 2 days. Potamon, tent-mate, [and others] to Areus T. PI.
EDCS-09202050.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Eunomia, detailing her lifespan and mentioning her tent-mate Potamon and possibly other relatives or associates.

EDCS-09202051.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Eutyches, a boy of 7 years. His mother Tyche and Cesstius Treption.
EDCS-09202051.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a young boy named Eutyches, set up by his mother and another individual.

EDCS-09202052.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph or dedication, identifying Excingomarus by his patronymic.

EDCS-09202054.translation: To the spirits of the departed: For Fabia Crispina, daughter of Quintus. Her mother Quintia Crispa.
EDCS-09202054.summary: This funerary inscription honors Fabia Crispina, with her mother Quintia Crispa as the dedicator.

EDCS-09202055.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Lucius Helvius Epictetus to his most dutiful wife, Fabia Grata.
EDCS-09202055.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Lucius Helvius Epictetus for his wife Fabia Grata.

EDCS-09202056.translation: To the spirits of the departed: For Fabia Servata, daughter of Lucius. Her daughter Pompia, daughter of Cnaeus, Servatilla.
EDCS-09202056.summary: This funerary inscription is for Fabia Servata, set up by her daughters Pompia and Servatilla.

EDCS-09202057.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Iulia Graecina set this up while alive for her husband Titus Faius Severus and for herself, and for their beloved Primitiva.
EDCS-09202057.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Iulia Graecina for her husband and herself, and for Primitiva.

EDCS-09202058.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Titus Firmius Marinus for his parents, Firmanus, son of Firmus, and Terentia, daughter of Tertius.
EDCS-09202058.summary: This funerary inscription honors parents Firmanus and Terentia, set up by their son Titus Firmius Marinus.

EDCS-09202059.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Firminus, son of Senovius.

EDCS-09202060.translation: To the spirits of the departed: The heir ordered this to be set up by will for Titus Firmius Blausus.
EDCS-09202060.summary: This funerary inscription records that the heir commissioned the monument for Titus Firmius Blausus according to his will.

EDCS-09202063.translation: Flordia Avita, daughter of Quintus, for herself and her husband and her son, while alive.
EDCS-09202063.summary: This funerary inscription records Flordia Avita setting up a monument for herself, her husband, and her son during her lifetime.

EDCS-09202064.translation: Floria Fortunata for herself and her spouse.
EDCS-09202064.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Floria Fortunata for herself and her spouse.

EDCS-09202065.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Fortunata, [from] Primitius, [her] mother.
EDCS-09202065.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Primitius for his mother, Fortunata.

EDCS-09202066.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Frontonis, son of Donnus.
EDCS-09202066.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Frontonis, son of Donnus.

EDCS-09202068.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Furia, daughter of Publius, wife of Titus Tertius Italicus, by the will of her father, Publius Furius Homuncio.
EDCS-09202068.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Furia, daughter of Publius and wife of Titus Tertius Italicus, established by her father's will.

EDCS-09202069.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Fuscina, daughter of Buccio, [his] wife.
EDCS-09202069.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Fuscina, daughter of Buccio and his wife.

EDCS-09202070.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Helene Gaetulia, [from] Titus Gaetulius Iarus for his wife, and for himself, and for Gaetulia Iavina, [his] patroness.
EDCS-09202070.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Titus Gaetulius Iarus for his wife Helene Gaetulia, himself, and his patroness Gaetulia Iavina.

EDCS-09202071.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Gellius, son of Cornelius.
EDCS-09202071.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Gellius, son of Cornelius.

EDCS-09202072.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Gemella, [from] Albanus, [her] tent-mate.
EDCS-09202072.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Albanus for his tent-mate Gemella.

EDCS-09202073.translation: Titus Geminius Titullus for his father, Titus, son of Geminius.
EDCS-09202073.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Titus Geminius Titullus for his father.

EDCS-09202075.translation: To his son, brother, [from] Q. Girta.
EDCS-09202075.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Q. Girta for his son and brother.

EDCS-09202076.translation: To the safety of Glycera, Titus Pitius Plution [erected this] for his dearest life-companion.
EDCS-09202076.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Titus Pitius Plution to his companion Glycera.

EDCS-09202077.translation: To Gaius Gnatian Iulius, son of Gaius, to his father, to Suaducconi, daughter of Sextus of Histria, to his mother and wife, pious, Gaius Gnatian Iulius made [this] for himself and his own while alive.
EDCS-09202077.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Gaius Gnatian Iulius for his father, mother, and wife, and for himself and his family.

EDCS-09202078.translation: To Sextus Granius, son of Sextus, Boudo and Disetoni, freedmen of Homullus Iapys Alchimedes, [erected this] for their mother.
EDCS-09202078.summary: This is a funerary dedication by freedmen to their mother, Sextus Granius.

EDCS-09202080.translation: To the departed spirits of Haretusa, Charis [erected this] for his life-companion.
EDCS-09202080.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Charis to his companion Haretusa.

EDCS-09202081.translation: To the departed spirits of Lucius Helvius Epagathio and Lucius Helvius Nicia, Lucius Helvius Phileros, his freedman, and Popilia Mystis [erected this].
EDCS-09202081.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lucius Helvius Phileros and Popilia Mystis for Lucius Helvius Epagathio and Lucius Helvius Nicia.

EDCS-09202082.translation: To the departed spirits of Lucius Helvius Secundinus.
EDCS-09202082.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Lucius Helvius Secundinus.

EDCS-09202083.translation: To the departed spirits of Helvia Iucundilla, Titus Auctus Helvianus [erected this] for his most pious mother, and Velianius Ianuaris for his excellent wife.
EDCS-09202083.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Titus Auctus Helvianus for his mother and by Velianius Ianuaris for his wife, Helvia Iucundilla.

EDCS-09202084.translation: To the departed spirits of Helvia Micia.
EDCS-09202084.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Helvia Micia.

EDCS-09202085.translation: To the departed spirits of Helvia Priscilla, Quinta, her freedwoman, [erected this].
EDCS-09202085.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Quinta, a freedwoman, to Helvia Priscilla.

EDCS-09202086.translation: To the departed spirits of Helvia, daughter of Helvius, Valeria, Marcus Valerius Maximus and Marcus Numerius Martialis, the heirs, erected [this].
EDCS-09202086.summary: This is a funerary dedication by heirs Marcus Valerius Maximus and Marcus Numerius Martialis for Helvia Valeria.

EDCS-09202087.translation: To the divine spirits, Sextus Avius Varus [erected this] to Hermes, his excellent slave.
EDCS-09202087.summary: A funerary dedication by Sextus Avius Varus to his slave Hermes, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09202088.translation: Verinus, freedman, [erected this] to Titus Homullus Leon, his patron.
EDCS-09202088.summary: A funerary dedication by a freedman to his patron, likely from the early imperial period.

EDCS-09202089.summary: A simple dedication to Marcus Hortensius, possibly funerary or commemorative, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09202090.translation: To the divine spirits, Sulpicia, daughter of Quintus Honorata, [erected this] to her most dutiful mother, Hortensia, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-09202090.summary: A funerary dedication by a daughter to her mother, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09202091.translation: Callistus and Philete placed [this] to the divine spirits, to their mother Hortensia Martina.
EDCS-09202091.summary: A funerary dedication by two individuals, Callistus and Philete, to their mother Hortensia Martina, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09202092.translation: Publius Aulius Alexander [erected this] to the divine spirits, to his incomparable wife, Hortensia Primitiva.
EDCS-09202092.summary: A funerary dedication by a husband to his wife, Hortensia Primitiva, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09202093.translation: To the divine spirits, Secundus and Iulia [and...] to Hospita.
EDCS-09202093.summary: A fragmentary funerary dedication by Secundus and Iulia to someone named Hospita, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09202094.translation: This monument, a mausoleum, prepared for the sake of monuments and dedicated to the sacred rites of ancestors, so that those who were the owner of this may enjoy [it], I forbid to be sold, and I ask by the divinity of the gods, if she wishes to sell, the buyer is forbidden by this inscription, Hostilia, daughter of Lucius, erected this while alive.
EDCS-09202094.summary: An unusual funerary monument inscription by Hostilia, daughter of Lucius, establishing rules for the inheritance and sale of her mausoleum, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09202095.summary: A brief epitaph recording the lifespan of Iaecia Euticias, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09202096.translation: To the divine spirits, Severia Severina [erected this] to Ianuarius, slave of Porcia Rhodines.
EDCS-09202096.summary: A funerary dedication by Severia Severina to a slave named Ianuarius, who belonged to Porcia Rhodines, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09202097.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Inventus, son of Sarro, and Quartula, his wife, placed this monument for herself and her husband while still alive.
EDCS-09202097.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by a wife for herself and her deceased husband, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202098.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Quintus Aurelius Euelpistion for his most dutiful wife, Lucconia Severilla.
EDCS-09202098.summary: This funerary inscription records a husband's dedication to his wife, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202101.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Iulia Cupita for her most deserving and most indulgent patron, Lucius Julius Agat[...]angelus.
EDCS-09202101.summary: This funerary inscription records a freedwoman's dedication to her patron, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202102.translation: To the spirits of the underworld of Quintus Julius Alypus.
EDCS-09202102.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription recording the death of Quintus Julius Alypus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202103.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Lucius Julius Apollonius, Valeria Hellas, a freedwoman of Julianus, and Cosmus, a son of Julianus, a household slave.
EDCS-09202103.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by a freedwoman and a household slave to Lucius Julius Apollonius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202104.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Spuria Marcia for her most dutiful husband, Gaius Julius Atticus.
EDCS-09202104.summary: This funerary inscription records a wife's dedication to her husband, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202105.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. The heirs of Tiberius Julius Aulinus.
EDCS-09202105.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication by the heirs of Tiberius Julius Aulinus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202106.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Avita succeeds in the inheritance for her best husband, Lucius Julius Capratinus.
EDCS-09202106.summary: This funerary inscription records a wife's dedication to her husband and her succession to his inheritance, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202108.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Eutycias, a freedman of Lucius Julius Epictetus.
EDCS-09202108.summary: This funerary inscription records a freedman's dedication to his former master, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202109.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Iulia Ammias for her best husband, Gaius Julius Eutyches, and for herself, while still alive.
EDCS-09202109.summary: This funerary inscription records a wife's dedication to her husband and herself, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202110.translation: Iulia Chrysis, patroness, and her sons Iulius Chryses and Quietus, for Iulius Eutyches.
EDCS-09202110.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Iulius Eutyches by his patroness and sons.

EDCS-09202111.translation: To the spirits of the departed of Lucius Iulius Gerus.
EDCS-09202111.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Iulius Gerus.

EDCS-09202112.translation: In the consulship of Marcus Arreccinus Clemens II and Lucius Baebius Honoratus, Iulius Graptus Mag [improved?] the mausoleum and, in order that it might be fruitful with planted trees, vines, and rose gardens, he remitted the immunity offered to him by his freedmen and the title by which his goodwill was maintained, so that he might not appear burdensome in any way with their benefits, contenting himself with the title which he set up at his own expense.
EDCS-09202112.summary: This inscription details Iulius Graptus Mag's improvements to a mausoleum, including landscaping and concessions to his freedmen, during the consulship of Marcus Arreccinus Clemens II and Lucius Baebius Honoratus.

EDCS-09202113.translation: To the spirits of the departed of Lucius Iulius Hermes, who ordered this to be made by his will.
EDCS-09202113.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Iulius Hermes, established by his will.

EDCS-09202114.translation: To the spirits of the departed of Lucius Iulius Hermes, for his brother Lycydas and for himself.
EDCS-09202114.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the spirits of Lucius Iulius Hermes, for his brother Lycydas and himself.

EDCS-09202115.translation: To the spirits of the departed of Caius Iulius Olostus, son, for his father.
EDCS-09202115.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the spirits of Caius Iulius Olostus, for his father.

EDCS-09202116.translation: To the spirits of the departed of Marcus Iulius Lucullus.
EDCS-09202116.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Iulius Lucullus.

EDCS-09202117.summary: This inscription appears to be a simple dedication or identification of Lucius Iulius Maeta.

EDCS-09202118.translation: To the spirits of the departed of Caius Iulius Voltinius Mansuetus Taucius, from his will.
EDCS-09202118.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Caius Iulius Voltinius Mansuetus Taucius, established by his will.

EDCS-09202119.translation: To the spirits of the departed of Sextus Iulius Messianus; Sextus Iulius Dionysius set this up alive for his most dutiful son and for himself.
EDCS-09202119.summary: This funerary inscription was set up by Sextus Iulius Dionysius for his son Sextus Iulius Messianus and for himself during their lifetime.

EDCS-09202120.translation: Julius Severus and Julius Severianus set up this monument to their dearest father, Aulus Julius Myronis, and to their mother, Camulatia Seveara, while she was still living.
EDCS-09202120.summary: This is a funerary dedication by two sons to their living mother and deceased father, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09202121.translation: To the departed spirits of Lucius Julius Natalis, most dutiful. Larienus Paternus set this up.
EDCS-09202121.summary: A funerary inscription recording the dedication by Larienus Paternus to the spirit of the deceased Lucius Julius Natalis.

EDCS-09202122.translation: To the departed spirits. Recillia Menefane set this up to her incomparable husband, Lucius Julius Nicander.
EDCS-09202122.summary: A funerary inscription by a wife, Recillia Menefane, dedicated to her deceased husband, Lucius Julius Nicander.

EDCS-09202123.translation: To the departed spirits of Titus Julius Nicostratus. Julia Nice set this up to her most dutiful brother.
EDCS-09202123.summary: A funerary inscription by Julia Nice dedicated to her deceased brother, Titus Julius Nicostratus.

EDCS-09202124.translation: To the departed spirits of Lucius Julius Nigrinus. Lucius Julius Peculiaris set this up to his best and most dutiful freedman.
EDCS-09202124.summary: A funerary inscription by Lucius Julius Peculiaris dedicating a monument to his freedman, Lucius Julius Nigrinus.

EDCS-09202125.translation: To the departed spirits of the son of Sextus Julius Sextus. Alcimus, Marcion, and Euangelia, freedmen, set this up to their brother and to Julius Optatus, brother, and Julia Optata, sister.
EDCS-09202125.summary: A funerary inscription by three freedmen dedicating a monument to their brother and two other siblings, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09202126.translation: To the departed spirits of Lucius Julius Onesimus. Sammia Charitus set this up to her excellent husband and for herself while alive.
EDCS-09202126.summary: A funerary inscription by Sammia Charitus to her deceased husband, Lucius Julius Onesimus, and for herself while living, possibly indicating a shared tomb.

EDCS-09202127.translation: To the departed spirits of Quintus Julius Perpetuus. His father set this up to his most dutiful son.
EDCS-09202127.summary: A funerary inscription by a father dedicating a monument to his deceased son, Quintus Julius Perpetuus.

EDCS-09202128.summary: A simple dedication to Sextus Julius Quartulus, likely a funerary marker or honorific inscription.

EDCS-09202129.translation: To the spirits of Sextus Julius Servatus.
EDCS-09202129.summary: A brief funerary inscription dedicated to the spirit of Sextus Julius Servatus.

EDCS-09202130.translation: To Sextus Julius Servatus and his wife Optata.
EDCS-09202130.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Sextus Julius Servatus and Optata.

EDCS-09202131.translation: Frontina erected this for her partner Exoratus Lacaena.
EDCS-09202131.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Frontina to her partner Exoratus Lacaena.

EDCS-09202132.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Caninia Eutychia for her excellent husband Lucius Julius Telesphorus.
EDCS-09202132.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by Caninia Eutychia to her husband Lucius Julius Telesphorus.

EDCS-09202133.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Lucius Julius Terpnus, for himself while alive, to whom the right to choose a place.
EDCS-09202133.summary: This inscription is a self-dedication for funerary purposes by Lucius Julius Terpnus.

EDCS-09202134.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Quarto Julius Varus.

EDCS-09202135.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Vatinia Callityche for her husband Caius Julius Verus, who deserved well of her.
EDCS-09202135.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by Vatinia Callityche to her husband Caius Julius Verus.

EDCS-09202136.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Mettia Quintina for her excellent husband Titus Julius Victor. To the Spirits of the Underworld. Maria Marituma for her freedwoman Maria Nemausina.
EDCS-09202136.summary: This inscription records funerary dedications by Mettia Quintina to her husband Titus Julius Victor and by Maria Marituma to her freedwoman Maria Nemausina.

EDCS-09202137.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Caius Julius Zosimus and his son Protus.
EDCS-09202137.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication to Caius Julius Zosimus and his son Protus.

EDCS-09202138.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Julia Seneca. Iulia Paterna for her excellent mother.
EDCS-09202138.summary: This inscription records a funerary dedication by Iulia Paterna to her mother Julia Senecae.

EDCS-09202139.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Julia Ampella. Sextus Valerius Theodorus, heir, and Caius Atilius Fortunatus, friend.
EDCS-09202139.summary: This inscription records a funerary dedication for Julia Ampella by her heir Sextus Valerius Theodorus and her friend Caius Atilius Fortunatus.

EDCS-09202140.translation: To the Divine Manes. To Julia Antistia, [dedicated by] Julia Thymelae, her most devoted sister.
EDCS-09202140.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Julia Antistia, set up by her sister Julia Thymelae.

EDCS-09202141.translation: To the Divine Manes. Quintus Aelius Saturninus erected this for Julia Aspasia.
EDCS-09202141.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Julia Aspasia, erected by Quintus Aelius Saturninus.

EDCS-09202142.translation: To the Divine Manes. To Julia Bessa.
EDCS-09202142.summary: This is a brief funerary dedication to Julia Bessa.

EDCS-09202143.translation: To the Divine Manes. To Julia Callityche, [dedicated by] Lucius Cornelius Vitalis, to his most excellent wife.
EDCS-09202143.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Julia Callityche, set up by her husband Lucius Cornelius Vitalis.

EDCS-09202144.translation: To the Divine Manes. To Julia Chresis, Titus Aemilius Trophimas [erected this] for his wife, who deserved exceedingly well of him.
EDCS-09202144.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Julia Chresis, set up by her husband Titus Aemilius Trophimas.

EDCS-09202145.translation: To the Divine Manes. Julia Chrysis erected this for herself while alive. In the year 4 (of some unspecified era).
EDCS-09202145.summary: This is a self-dedication tombstone for Julia Chrysis, erected during her lifetime, possibly in the year 4 of an imperial reign or local era.

EDCS-09202146.translation: To the Divine Manes. To Julia Concessa, daughter of Iulius Verris. Her mother, Aemilia, [erected this] for her most devoted daughter.
EDCS-09202146.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Julia Concessa, set up by her mother Aemilia.

EDCS-09202147.translation: To the Divine Gods. To Titia Julia Pheida, her dearest mother.
EDCS-09202147.summary: This is a funerary dedication in Greek to Titia Julia Pheida, described as 'dearest mother'.

EDCS-09202148.translation: To the Divine Manes. To Julia Grata, [dedicated by] Aulus Pompeius Gratinianus, her adopted son, and Iulia Servatilla, his dearest sister, and Aulus Pompeius Trophimas, his dearest wife.
EDCS-09202148.summary: This funerary inscription honors Julia Grata, with dedications from her adopted son Aulus Pompeius Gratinianus, his sister Iulia Servatilla, and his wife Aulus Pompeius Trophimas.

EDCS-09202149.translation: To the Divine Manes. Caius Pompeius Phoebus erected this for his wife, Julia Helpis, while alive.
EDCS-09202149.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Julia Helpis, erected by her husband Caius Pompeius Phoebus during her lifetime.

EDCS-09202150.translation: To Iulia Honorata, daughter of Gnaeus, from Rustica, daughter of Titus, her mother.
EDCS-09202150.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iulia Honorata, set up by her mother Rustica.

EDCS-09202151.translation: To the Divine Shades: Iulia, from Protoctetus and Secundus.
