EDCS-09202151.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iulia, dedicated by Protoctetus and Secundus.

EDCS-09202152.translation: Iulia Marcella, daughter of Decimus, set this up for herself while alive.
EDCS-09202152.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iulia Marcella, who provided for her own burial during her lifetime.

EDCS-09202153.translation: To the Divine Shades: Lucius Iulius Gratinus for Iulia Marcella, daughter of Lucius, his aunt.
EDCS-09202153.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iulia Marcella, dedicated by her nephew Lucius Iulius Gratinus.

EDCS-09202154.translation: Iulia Quartina for herself and her family, and for Iulia Marcella, her friend, and her family.
EDCS-09202154.summary: A funerary epitaph where Iulia Quartina makes provisions for herself, her family, and her friend Iulia Marcella and her family.

EDCS-09202155.translation: To the Divine Shades: Iulia Quartula, daughter of Sextus, her father set this up.
EDCS-09202155.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iulia Quartula, set up by her father.

EDCS-09202156.translation: To the Divine Shades: For Iulia Rhodia, dearest wife, from Lucius Iulius Epictetus, and for his most dutiful mother, from Iulii Perpetuus and Paternus.
EDCS-09202156.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iulia Rhodia, dedicated by her husband Lucius Iulius Epictetus, and also mentioning her sons Iulii Perpetuus and Paternus who dedicated it for their mother.

EDCS-09202157.translation: To the Divine Shades: for Iulia Sergia, who lived 7 years and 35 days, from Iulia Sergia, most dutiful daughter (II).
EDCS-09202157.summary: A funerary epitaph for the young Iulia Sergia, recording her age and dedicated by her daughter (or possibly the same person if 'II' refers to a second dedication or a repetition).

EDCS-09202158.translation: To the Divine Shades: for Iulia Severina, from Iulius Patercalus, her cousin, and from Attia Aphrodite, her friend.
EDCS-09202158.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iulia Severina, dedicated by her cousin Iulius Patercalus and her friend Attia Aphrodite.

EDCS-09202159.translation: To the Divine Shades: for Iullinus, son of Iullinus, from Carparius, his brother.
EDCS-09202159.summary: A funerary epitaph for Iullinus, dedicated by his brother Carparius.

EDCS-09202161.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Iunia Auxesis and Iunius Graecus, freedman, [erected this] for Iunia Primilla.
EDCS-09202161.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Iunia Primilla, set up by Iunia Auxesis and her freedman Iunius Graecus.

EDCS-09202162.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Iustus Carinus Acrus.

EDCS-09202163.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: For Lucius Iuventus Arellus.
EDCS-09202163.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Lucius Iuventus Arellus.

EDCS-09202164.summary: This is a funerary dedication, likely for a woman named Iuventia.

EDCS-09202165.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Maelia Procilla placed this for her most devoted mother, Iuventia Primula.
EDCS-09202165.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Iuventia Primula, set up by her devoted daughter Maelia Procilla.

EDCS-09202166.translation: For K(a)no Marinus, son, to his mother; Sextus Gillius, father; Sextus, brother; in accordance with the will.
EDCS-09202166.summary: This inscription records a dedication made according to a will, likely funerary, for Kano Marinus, his mother, and his brother Sextus, with Sextus Gillius identified as the father.

EDCS-09202167.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Lucius Kareius Secundinus for his freedwoman, Kareia Victorina. To the spirits of the underworld. M D R [illegible].
EDCS-09202167.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Kareia Victorina, set up by her patron Lucius Kareius Secundinus, with an additional illegible phrase to the spirits of the underworld.

EDCS-09202168.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: For their most devoted son, Lucius Karius Aemilianus. Lucius Karius Communis and Aemilia Zosime.
EDCS-09202168.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Lucius Karius Aemilianus, set up by his parents, Lucius Karius Communis and Aemilia Zosime.

EDCS-09202169.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: For her most devoted uncle, Karo Mansuetus. Quartina, daughter of Maternus.
EDCS-09202169.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Karo Mansuetus, set up by his devoted niece Quartina, daughter of Maternus.

EDCS-09202171.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, likely the beginning of a name or dedication.

EDCS-09202172.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Gaius Licinius Quartus, his freedman, [erected this] for Gaius Licinius Artemidorus.
EDCS-09202172.summary: A funerary dedication by a freedman for his former master, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09202173.translation: Gaius Licinius Kapitinus, of the Voltinian tribe.
EDCS-09202173.summary: A simple funerary inscription identifying an individual by name and tribal affiliation, likely from the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-09202174.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Quintus Aurelius Ianuaris, as a friend, erected this in memory of Quintus Licinius Peticianus and Peticia Cosmices, and of [their] mother and sons.
EDCS-09202174.summary: A funerary dedication by a friend for a family, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09202175.translation: [Name illegible] Lades. Quintus Cosconius Severus made [this] for his excellent wife and himself.
EDCS-09202175.summary: A funerary monument set up by a husband for his wife and himself, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09202176.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lade, freedwoman of Gaius Licinius Soterichus.
EDCS-09202176.summary: A funerary dedication for a freedwoman by her former master, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09202177.translation: Licinia Lade, while alive, [erected this] for herself and for her descendants, freedmen and freedwomen, born and yet to be born.
EDCS-09202177.summary: A self-funded funerary monument intended for the owner and her extended household, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09202178.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Licinia Lade, freedwoman of Bathyllus. Sextus Avillius Cupitus [erected this] for his most cherished wife, who lived 16 years, 1 month, and 36 days.
EDCS-09202178.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young freedwoman, including her age at death and erected by her husband, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09202179.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Licinia Marcella, daughter of Marcus, wife of Sextus Coelius Advena. Marcus Licinius Cosmio, his freedman, [erected this].
EDCS-09202179.summary: A funerary dedication for a woman by her husband, likely set up by the husband's freedman, from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09202180.translation: For Licinia Pr [name illegible]. Lucius Valerius Narcissus made [this] for his most cherished wife and for himself.
EDCS-09202180.summary: A funerary monument set up by a husband for his wife and himself, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09202181.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Licinia Sozousa. Elafio, who lived 11 years, 11 months, and 14 days. Licinia Maxima, daughter of Marcus, and Sextus Cambarius Severinus, who were alive, placed [this] for their most cherished ward and for themselves.
EDCS-09202181.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young girl, including her age at death and erected by her guardians, from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09202182.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Caius Lucanius Secundus to his most devoted father, Lucius Lucanius.
EDCS-09202182.summary: This funerary inscription records a son's dedication to his father, Lucius Lucanius.

EDCS-09202183.translation: To the memory of his father Lucanus. Pompeianus, his son.
EDCS-09202183.summary: This funerary inscription records a son's dedication to his father, Lucanus.

EDCS-09202184.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Quintus Seccius Mercurius made this for his excellent wife, Lucia Quincta, and for himself while alive.
EDCS-09202184.summary: This funerary inscription records a husband's memorial for his wife, Lucia Quincta, and himself.

EDCS-09202185.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Lucia Verecunda.
EDCS-09202185.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication to Lucia Verecunda.

EDCS-09202186.translation: Lucilla, may you shine among the spirits of the underworld. Publius Atettius Saturninus to his most rare wife, Lucilia, daughter of Lucius Secundilla, who lived with him for 20 years. This monument will not pass to an heir after me. Secundilla, hail!
EDCS-09202186.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Publius Atettius Saturninus to his wife Lucilia, specifying the duration of their marriage and that the monument is not to be inherited.

EDCS-09202187.translation: To Lucius Lucretius Calidianus. Caius Parucius Trophimus and Calidia, his freedwoman.
EDCS-09202187.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Lucius Lucretius Calidianus by Caius Parucius Trophimus and his freedwoman Calidia.

EDCS-09202189.translation: To Caius Lucretius Virilis. Lucius Licinius Chryseros, his client.
EDCS-09202189.summary: This inscription records a client's dedication to his patron, Caius Lucretius Virilis.

EDCS-09202190.translation: Lucretia Pannychis set this up while alive.
EDCS-09202190.summary: This funerary inscription records Lucretia Pannychis setting up her own monument during her lifetime.

EDCS-09202191.translation: To the spirits of Lutatia, daughter of Caius Careia.
EDCS-09202191.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication to Lutatia, daughter of Caius Careia.

EDCS-09202193.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Macciana Saturnina. Tertulla, mother, and Maccius, father.
EDCS-09202193.summary: This funerary inscription records parents dedicating a monument to their daughter, Macciana Saturnina.

EDCS-09202194.translation: To the spirits of the departed: his mother and Marcus Valerius Valerianus, his grandson, [erected this] for Macrinus Mansuetus, son of Comius Quartus.
EDCS-09202194.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Macrinus Mansuetus, mentioning his mother and grandson.

EDCS-09202195.translation: The heirs of Tiberius Maecius Maturus.
EDCS-09202195.summary: This inscription records the names of the heirs of Tiberius Maecius Maturus, likely on a tomb or monument.

EDCS-09202196.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Maelinus, his brother, [erected this] for Lucius Maelo, son of Maelo.
EDCS-09202196.summary: A funerary dedication from Maelinus to his brother, Lucius Maelo.

EDCS-09202197.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Fortunatus [erected this] for Sextus Magius Hermetes.
EDCS-09202197.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Fortunatus for Sextus Magius Hermetes.

EDCS-09202198.translation: Titus Magius Verus [erected this] for himself while alive, and for his wife Septumia, and for his father, and for his mother.
EDCS-09202198.summary: A funerary dedication made by Titus Magius Verus for himself and his family during his lifetime.

EDCS-09202199.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Caius Iulius Facundus [erected this] for his excellent friend Lucius Magunus Mansuetus.
EDCS-09202199.summary: A funerary dedication from Caius Iulius Facundus to his friend Lucius Magunus Mansuetus.

EDCS-09202200.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Moderatus, his most devoted brother, [erected this] for Mainas Memnonis.
EDCS-09202200.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Moderatus to his brother, Mainas Memnonis.

EDCS-09202201.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Marcus Manlius Tullus [erected this] for himself and for his dearest wife.
EDCS-09202201.summary: A funerary dedication by Marcus Manlius Tullus for himself and his wife.

EDCS-09202202.translation: For Marcella, his most devoted wife.
EDCS-09202202.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Marcella, described as a devoted wife.

EDCS-09202203.translation: Titus Cimarius Docilis placed [this] for his wife Marcellina, daughter of Victor, and for himself while alive.
EDCS-09202203.summary: A funerary dedication by Titus Cimarius Docilis for himself and his wife Marcellina, daughter of Victor.

EDCS-09202204.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Balbius Iulius Mercurialis to his most excellent wife, Marcia Philetes.
EDCS-09202204.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Balbius Iulius Mercurialis for his wife, Marcia Philetes.

EDCS-09202205.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Titus Calpurnius Eros to his wife, Marcia Prima.
EDCS-09202205.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Titus Calpurnius Eros for his wife, Marcia Prima.

EDCS-09202207.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Marcellinus and Marcellina to their most dutiful father, Marcus Nigrinus.
EDCS-09202207.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Marcellinus and Marcellina for their father, Marcus Nigrinus.

EDCS-09202209.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Gaius Marius Dubius for himself and his family, during his lifetime.
EDCS-09202209.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Gaius Marius Dubius for himself and his family.

EDCS-09202210.translation: To Lucius Marius Volkameno, son of Lucius.
EDCS-09202210.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Marius Volkameno.

EDCS-09202211.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Crispina, freedwoman of Avitus, set this up for her husband, Martialis, son of Silvinus, during her lifetime.
EDCS-09202211.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Crispina for her husband, Martialis.

EDCS-09202212.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. To our son.
EDCS-09202212.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a son.

EDCS-09202213.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. To Martina A, and to her daughter, the most dutiful mother.
EDCS-09202213.summary: This is a funerary epitaph likely for Martina A and her daughter.

EDCS-09202214.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Materna, daughter of Catullus.

EDCS-09202215.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Reliquiae to his comrade, Materna.
EDCS-09202215.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Reliquiae for his comrade, Materna.

EDCS-09202216.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Marcus Numerius Maximinus (erected this) for his wife Maximia Nigella.
EDCS-09202216.summary: This funerary epitaph records Marcus Numerius Maximinus dedicating a tomb to his wife, Maximia Nigella.

EDCS-09202217.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For his most dutiful wife Maximilla, daughter of Maximus, Marcus Apicius Vitalis, and for their most devoted mother, Maximus and Servata.
EDCS-09202217.summary: This funerary epitaph records Marcus Apicius Vitalis dedicating a tomb to his wife Maximilla, and Maximus and Servata dedicating it to their mother.

EDCS-09202218.translation: For Sextus Melicius Honoratus, our son.
EDCS-09202218.summary: This funerary epitaph records a dedication to Sextus Melicius Honoratus, likely by his parents.

EDCS-09202219.translation: Lucius Melius Paternus, son of Caius, of the Voltinian tribe, (erected this) for himself while alive.
EDCS-09202219.summary: This funerary epitaph records Lucius Melius Paternus dedicating a tomb for himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-09202220.translation: Sedatus, son of Caius, of the Voltinian tribe, Caius Melius, (erected this) for himself while alive.
EDCS-09202220.summary: This funerary epitaph records Caius Melius Sedatus dedicating a tomb for himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-09202221.translation: Caius Melius Trophimus (erected this) for Crecentius Donatus.
EDCS-09202221.summary: This inscription records Caius Melius Trophimus dedicating something, possibly a tomb, to Crecentius Donatus.

EDCS-09202222.summary: This funerary epitaph records a dedication to Messius Indedus, likely by his parents.

EDCS-09202223.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Titus Messius Anicetus, his most excellent father, Messia Titia and Messia Lucretia; and for Lucretia, her most excellent husband.
EDCS-09202223.summary: This funerary epitaph records Messia Titia and Messia Lucretia dedicating a tomb to their father Anicetus, and Lucretia to her husband.

EDCS-09202224.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. (He) dedicated (this) for himself while alive, Titus Messius Bellinus.
EDCS-09202224.summary: This funerary epitaph records Titus Messius Bellinus dedicating a tomb for himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-09202225.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For his dearest wife, Messia Callityches, Artemidorus brought forth these years: 27.
EDCS-09202225.summary: This funerary epitaph records Artemidorus dedicating a tomb to his wife Callityches, who died at the age of 27.

EDCS-09202226.translation: To the Divine Spirits. To Mettia Firmina, daughter of Titus, my mother.
EDCS-09202226.summary: A funerary dedication to the deceased Mettia Firmina by her son.

EDCS-09202227.translation: To Mnemosyne, Melodes. Lucius Iulius Iustus, comrade in arms.
EDCS-09202227.summary: A funerary dedication to Mnemosyne Melodes by her comrade Lucius Iulius Iustus.

EDCS-09202228.summary: A brief funerary dedication, likely to a deceased person named Mnesteres.

EDCS-09202229.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Lucius Pompeius Doras, to his wife Modesta, freedwoman of Nundinus.
EDCS-09202229.summary: A funerary dedication to Modesta, freedwoman of Nundinus, by her husband Lucius Pompeius Doras.

EDCS-09202231.summary: A funerary dedication to Montanus, son of Montanus.

EDCS-09202232.translation: To the Divine Spirits. To Caius Nemonius Euphemus, to his best friend, Sextus Caratius Onesimus and Cambaria Chrysante.
EDCS-09202232.summary: A funerary dedication to Caius Nemonius Euphemus by his friends Sextus Caratius Onesimus and Cambaria Chrysante.

EDCS-09202233.translation: To the Divine Spirits. To Musicus.
EDCS-09202233.summary: A funerary dedication to a deceased person named Musicus.

EDCS-09202234.translation: To the Divine Spirits. To Naevia Privata, his best wife. Gnaeus Naevius Diadumenus.
EDCS-09202234.summary: A funerary dedication to Naevia Privata by her husband Gnaeus Naevius Diadumenus.

EDCS-09202235.summary: An inscription identifying Naso Pompeius and his profession as a whip-maker.

EDCS-09202236.translation: To the Divine Spirits. To Caius Nemonius Plocamus, his most devoted patron. Caius Nemonius Paederos, his freedman.
EDCS-09202236.summary: A funerary dedication to the patron Caius Nemonius Plocamus by his freedman Caius Nemonius Paederos.

EDCS-09202237.translation: Gaius Nemonius Plocamus to his wife Nemonia Niceni.
EDCS-09202237.summary: This inscription is a dedication from a husband to his wife.

EDCS-09202239.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Gaius Licinius Iulianus for his parents, Nigrus son of Cippacus, and Servata of Craxa.
EDCS-09202239.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the deceased parents of Gaius Licinius Iulianus.

EDCS-09202240.translation: Gaius Nonius Acoristus for himself and his family.
EDCS-09202240.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Gaius Nonius Acoristus for himself and his household.

EDCS-09202241.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Valeria Severina, mother, for her son Titas Norbanus Nivalis.
EDCS-09202241.summary: This inscription is a dedication from a mother to her deceased son, Titas Norbanus Nivalis.

EDCS-09202242.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Marcella, mother, for Novella.
EDCS-09202242.summary: This inscription is a dedication from a mother, Marcella, to her deceased daughter, Novella.

EDCS-09202243.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: for Novia Exoches.
EDCS-09202243.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the deceased Novia Exoches.

EDCS-09202244.translation: Iulius Nundinus [to] his wife Iulia Glaritta.
EDCS-09202244.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication from Iulius Nundinus to his wife, Iulia Glaritta.

EDCS-09202246.translation: Titus Octavius Lupulus, while living, for himself.
EDCS-09202246.summary: This is a self-dedication made by Titus Octavius Lupulus during his lifetime.

EDCS-09202247.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Marcus Octavius Marullus, freedman, for Marcus Octavius Marcellinus.
EDCS-09202247.summary: This inscription is a dedication made by the freedman Marcus Octavius Marullus for his patron, Marcus Octavius Marcellinus.

EDCS-09202248.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Octavius Servatus.

EDCS-09202249.translation: To Octavia Marcella, daughter of Gaius, Sextus Virillus Severinus, Gaius Curtius Primitius and his wife Celsina, their clients.
EDCS-09202249.summary: This inscription is a dedication by clients to their patroness, Octavia Marcella.

EDCS-09202250.summary: This is a dedication to Sextus Oleatius Honoratus, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-09202251.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Ombania Aphrodisia, the mother, set this up for Gaius Ombanus Aphrodisius.
EDCS-09202251.summary: This funerary inscription records a mother's dedication to her deceased son, Gaius Ombanus Aphrodisius.

EDCS-09202252.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. A monument was erected.
EDCS-09202252.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication, stating that a monument was set up for an unnamed person.

EDCS-09202253.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed, for Onesime, most dutiful.
EDCS-09202253.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication to Onesime, described as 'most dutiful'.

EDCS-09202254.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Artemisia, his tent-mate.
EDCS-09202254.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Artemisia to her deceased partner, Onychis.

EDCS-09202255.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Oppia Aphidis. Trophime, daughter of Marcus Oppiola, to her most dutiful mother.
EDCS-09202255.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Trophime to her mother, Oppia Aphidis.

EDCS-09202256.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Oppia, daughter of Lucius, aged 6 years, 9 months, and 5 days. Oppia Secundilla, daughter of Lucius, set this up for her dearest daughter.
EDCS-09202256.summary: This funerary inscription records a mother, Oppia Secundilla, setting up a monument for her daughter Oppia, who died at the age of 6.

EDCS-09202257.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Orfia, aged 11 years. Attius and Numeria set this up for their slave.
EDCS-09202257.summary: This funerary inscription records Attius and Numeria setting up a monument for their young slave, Orfia.

EDCS-09202258.translation: Quinti Ovidi Marcionis. Ovidia Lais set this up while alive for her most dutiful husband, and also for herself, and for him as patron.
EDCS-09202258.summary: This inscription records Ovidia Lais setting up a monument for her husband and herself, also honoring him as a patron.

EDCS-09202260.translation: To the divine Manes of Papius Cundius, freedman of Mercator. Licia [dedicated this].
EDCS-09202260.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the divine Manes of Papius Cundius, likely by Licia, his freedwoman, and Mercator, his former master.

EDCS-09202261.translation: To the divine Manes of Lucius Papirius Priscus, from his brother Gaius.
EDCS-09202261.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Lucius Papirius Priscus, set up by his brother Gaius.

EDCS-09202262.translation: To the divine Manes. Sextus Passonus Paternus to his most excellent father and Severia Severina to her most exceptional husband.
EDCS-09202262.summary: This is a joint funerary dedication by Sextus Passonus Paternus to his father and Severia Severina to her husband, likely both named Paternus or with related family names.

EDCS-09202263.translation: To the divine Manes of Sextus Paternus Maccius, from his granddaughter Lucia Severa.
EDCS-09202263.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication to Sextus Paternus Maccius, made by his granddaughter Lucia Severa.

EDCS-09202264.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Paternus, son of Quintus.

EDCS-09202265.translation: To Paternus, son of Sextilius, and to Aemilia Phoebe, from Saturius Paternus, her freedman.
EDCS-09202265.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Paternus, son of Sextilius, and Aemilia Phoebe, by Saturius Paternus, who was their freedman.

EDCS-09202266.translation: To the divine Manes of Paternus, daughter of Publius. To Sauro, her freedman.
EDCS-09202266.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Paternus, daughter of Publius, and to her freedman Sauro.

EDCS-09202267.translation: To the divine Manes of Patricius, aged 16, from Veratius Sedatus.
EDCS-09202267.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Patricius, who died at the age of 16, set up by Veratius Sedatus.

EDCS-09202268.translation: To the divine Manes. From his mother and father, to their most dutiful son Paulianus.
EDCS-09202268.summary: This is a funerary dedication from parents to their beloved son Paulianus.

EDCS-09202269.translation: To the divine Manes of Pedia Helpidis, from her most dutiful daughter Pedia Filina.
EDCS-09202269.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Pedia Helpidis by her devoted daughter Pedia Filina.

EDCS-09202270.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Hieria erected this monument to her husband Pelagius, whom she loved, in memory.
EDCS-09202270.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Hieria to her husband Pelagius.

EDCS-09202271.summary: This inscription seems to be a record of accounts belonging to someone named Peregrinus.

EDCS-09202272.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Philetes, and for Iulia Pantonice, a well-deserving slave.
EDCS-09202272.summary: This funerary inscription honors Philetes and the slave Iulia Pantonice.

EDCS-09202274.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Philomusus, who lived for 5 years, 1 month, and 22 days of his age. Iulia erected this for her most devoted foster-child.
EDCS-09202274.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Philomusus, who died at a young age, erected by his foster-mother Iulia.

EDCS-09202275.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Olius Plautius Saturninus.
EDCS-09202275.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Olius Plautius Saturninus.

EDCS-09202276.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Lucius Plotus Apollonidis, who lived 13 years, 2 months, and 10 days.
EDCS-09202276.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Plotus Apollonidis, who died at the age of 13.

EDCS-09202277.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Gaius Publicius Ingenuus and Cypareni, freedman and wife. To the spirits of the departed, for Publica Cypareni.
EDCS-09202277.summary: This funerary inscription honors Gaius Publicius Ingenuus and his wife Cypareni, and also Publica Cypareni.

EDCS-09202278.translation: To Gnaeus Pompeius Caranto's son, a warrior of the Atessates.
EDCS-09202278.summary: This inscription honors Gnaeus Pompeius, son of Caranto, identified as a warrior from the Atessates tribe.

EDCS-09202279.translation: Sextilia Atthis erected this for her husband Lucius Pompeius Callistus and for Primula Sulpicia, her mother, while she was alive.
EDCS-09202279.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Sextilia Atthis for her husband Lucius Pompeius Callistus and her mother Primula Sulpicia.

EDCS-09202281.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Lucius Pompeius Dora, alive, for himself.
EDCS-09202281.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Lucius Pompeius Dora for himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-09202282.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Quintus Pompeius D[---] Eivini P[---].
EDCS-09202282.summary: A funerary dedication to Quintus Pompeius D[---] Eivini P[---].

EDCS-09202283.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Valeria Callityche for her husband Cnaeus Pompeius Epitynchanus.
EDCS-09202283.summary: A funerary dedication by Valeria Callityche for her husband, Cnaeus Pompeius Epitynchanus.

EDCS-09202284.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Quintus Pompeius Clinias, freedman, for Quintus Pompeius Eutyches.
EDCS-09202284.summary: A funerary dedication by the freedman Quintus Pompeius Clinias for Quintus Pompeius Eutyches.

EDCS-09202285.translation: For Cnaeus Pompeius Lemiso, freedman of Sextus, of the Palatine tribe, his freedmen Fronto and Felix.
EDCS-09202285.summary: A funerary dedication by the freedmen Fronto and Felix for their patron Cnaeus Pompeius Lemiso.

EDCS-09202286.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Pompeius Martialis.
EDCS-09202286.summary: A funerary dedication to Pompeius Martialis.

EDCS-09202287.translation: For Marcus Pompeius Maximus, son of Marcus, of the Voltinian tribe.
EDCS-09202287.summary: A dedication to Marcus Pompeius Maximus, son of Marcus, likely a civic honor or funerary monument.

EDCS-09202288.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Vettia Nice placed this for her husband Sextus Pompeius Mercurialis, the best of husbands, and for herself while alive.
EDCS-09202288.summary: A funerary dedication by Vettia Nice for her husband Sextus Pompeius Mercurialis and for herself, made during her lifetime.

EDCS-09202289.summary: A dedication to Quintus Pompeius Oceanus.

EDCS-09202290.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Firmia Helpis for her husband Gnaeus Pompeius Primitivus, the best of husbands.
EDCS-09202290.summary: A funerary dedication by Firmia Helpis for her husband Gnaeus Pompeius Primitivus.

EDCS-09202291.summary: The name Sextus Pompeius A Restitutus, likely a tombstone inscription.

EDCS-09202292.translation: To the Divine Shades. To Caius Pompeius Secundus, aged thirteen, his parents for their most devoted son.
EDCS-09202292.summary: This is a funerary dedication by parents for their thirteen-year-old son, Caius Pompeius Secundus.

EDCS-09202293.translation: Gnaeus Pompeius Varus, son of Gnaeus, of the Voltinia tribe, and Pompeia, daughter of Titus, his wife.
EDCS-09202293.summary: This inscription records the names and tribal affiliations of a man, Gnaeus Pompeius Varus, and his wife, Pompeia.

EDCS-09202294.translation: To the Divine Shades. Aulus Pompeius Verecundus made this for himself while alive.
EDCS-09202294.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Aulus Pompeius Verecundus for himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-09202295.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Pompeia Flavia, their most wretched mother.
EDCS-09202295.summary: This funerary dedication is for Pompeia Flavia, identified as a "most wretched mother."

EDCS-09202296.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Pompeia Materna, daughter of Titus, [made by] Fabricia Quintina, daughter of Quintus.
EDCS-09202296.summary: This funerary dedication by Fabricia Quintina is for her mother, Pompeia Materna, daughter of Titus.

EDCS-09202297.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Pompeia Pannyichis, Lucius Iunius Eutychus and Iunia Tryphosa.
EDCS-09202297.summary: This funerary dedication is made by Lucius Iunius Eutychus and Iunia Tryphosa for Pompeia Pannyichis.

EDCS-09202298.translation: Gaius Iuventius Thallion placed this for his dearest comrade Pompeia Primula and for himself while alive.
EDCS-09202298.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Gaius Iuventius Thallion for his dearest comrade Pompeia Primula and for himself.

EDCS-09202300.translation: For Pompeia Soc [---]tilia, [for herself] while alive.
EDCS-09202300.summary: This incomplete inscription records that Pompeia Soc[---]tilia made this for herself while alive.

EDCS-09202301.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Pompeia Hygia. Her husband, Lucius Vitalis, son of Lucinus, and her sister, Sorote [made this].
EDCS-09202301.summary: This funerary dedication is made by Pompeia Erotice and her husband, Lucius Vitalis, for Pompeia Hygia.

EDCS-09202302.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Pompeia Servata, daughter of Gnaeus. Lucius Vegetius Ingenuus for his most excellent wife.
EDCS-09202302.summary: This funerary dedication by Lucius Vegetius Ingenuus is for his wife, Pompeia Servata, daughter of Gnaeus.

EDCS-09202303.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Lucius Tettius Ianuarius set this up for his most excellent wife, Pontia Lesbia.
EDCS-09202303.summary: A funerary dedication set up by a husband for his wife.

EDCS-09202304.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Amandus and Fortunata, slaves, set this up while alive for Sextus Porcius Dama.
EDCS-09202304.summary: A funerary dedication set up by slaves for their master, possibly commemorating a freedman.

EDCS-09202306.translation: Gnaeus Domitius Zosimus set this up for his most excellent wife, Sextus Porcius Marcellus, and for his patroness.
EDCS-09202306.summary: A funerary dedication mentioning a wife and a patroness, likely set up by a freedman.

EDCS-09202307.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Sextus Porcius Bacchylus, a friend, [set this up] for Sextus Porcius Severus.
EDCS-09202307.summary: A funerary dedication set up by a friend for the deceased.

EDCS-09202308.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Epafra, freedman, and Syntyche and Anatole, slaves, set this up while alive for their most dutiful educators, Porcia Lade and Optatus.
EDCS-09202308.summary: A funerary dedication set up by freedmen and slaves for their former educators and masters.

EDCS-09202309.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Marcus Porcius Pompeianus, Quintus Pompeius Nivalis, and Pompeius Hermionis [set this up] for Porcia Pompeia.
EDCS-09202309.summary: A funerary dedication set up by several individuals for Porcia Pompeia, possibly family members or associates.

EDCS-09202310.translation: Posilla, daughter of Sextus, [set this up] for her brother Sextus Servenius, while alive.
EDCS-09202310.summary: A funerary dedication set up by a sister for her brother.

EDCS-09202311.translation: Potitia Secundina, wife, and Potitia Paterna, daughter, [set this up] for their father, Lucius Potitius Bulicus, to the spirits of the departed.
EDCS-09202311.summary: A funerary dedication set up by a wife and daughter for the deceased.

EDCS-09202312.summary: A dedication for a freedwoman, likely a funerary monument.

EDCS-09202313.translation: For the memory of Priamus, Pompeius, his son, [set this up].
EDCS-09202313.summary: A funerary dedication set up by a son for his father.

EDCS-09202314.translation: To the departed spirits. Marcus Iulius Montanus [made this] for his excellent slave woman Primitiva.
EDCS-09202314.summary: A funerary dedication by Marcus Iulius Montanus for his slave Primitiva.

EDCS-09202315.translation: To the departed spirits. Cundus, son of Primulus, made this memorial for himself.
EDCS-09202315.summary: A funerary dedication by Cundus for himself, son of Primulus.

EDCS-09202316.translation: To Primulus, son of Capauson. Primula his mother and Rulina his wife [made this].
EDCS-09202316.summary: A funerary dedication for Primulus, son of Capauson, by his mother Primula and wife Rulina.

EDCS-09202317.translation: To the departed spirits. For Primulus, son of Quintulus.
EDCS-09202317.summary: A funerary dedication for Primulus, son of Quintulus.

EDCS-09202318.translation: To the departed spirits. Primula, daughter of Certus Ventidius, made this for herself and her husband Lucius Sentius Optatus while she was alive.
EDCS-09202318.summary: A funerary dedication made by Primula, daughter of Certus Ventidius, for herself and her husband Lucius Sentius Optatus.

EDCS-09202319.translation: To the departed spirits. For Primula, daughter of Certus, and her father Certus Ventidius, and her mother Caprilia, daughter of Cai, and her brother Cai Certus, and her husband Lucius Sentius Optatus. Nice, his freedwoman, and her son Lucius Acutius Ventidius, ordered this to be made by will.
EDCS-09202319.summary: A complex funerary dedication for Primula, her parents, brother, and husband, ordered to be executed by will by her freedwoman Nice and her son Lucius Acutius Ventidius.

EDCS-09202320.translation: To the departed spirits. Fabia Mercatilla and her sister Prima [made this] for Primi.
EDCS-09202320.summary: A funerary dedication by Fabia Mercatilla and her sister Prima for Primi.

EDCS-09202322.translation: Prima [dedicated this] to Soli Montanus, Gaius Eum [as recipient].
EDCS-09202322.summary: A dedication by Prima to Soli Montanus and Gaius Eum.

EDCS-09202323.summary: A dedication for Lucius, son of Publius.

EDCS-09202324.translation: Publia Pompeia, daughter, placed this for her excellent father while she was alive.
EDCS-09202324.summary: A funerary dedication placed by Publia Pompeia for her father.

EDCS-09202325.translation: To the departed spirits of Publicia Aphrodisia, from Sextus Iunius Paullinus, to his dearest wife.
EDCS-09202325.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a husband for his beloved wife, Publicia Aphrodisia.

EDCS-09202326.translation: To the departed spirits of Pusonia, daughter of Publius, of Pedulla, from Publius Pusonius Pedo, her foster-son.
EDCS-09202326.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a foster-son, Publius Pusonius Pedo, for his foster-mother, Pusonia.

EDCS-09202327.translation: To the departed spirits of Quartinia Paternus, from Marcus Mogovius Bredo, to his most exceptional wife and for himself, while living.
EDCS-09202327.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Marcus Mogovius Bredo for his wife Quartinia Paternus and himself, erected during his lifetime.

EDCS-09202328.translation: To the spirits of Quartulus, son of Quartio.
EDCS-09202328.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quartulus, son of Quartio.

EDCS-09202329.translation: To the departed spirits of Quartula, daughter of Maximu, from her heirs, Marcus Valerius Primus and Acte, a freedwoman.
EDCS-09202329.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quartula, daughter of Maximu, set up by her heirs, Marcus Valerius Primus and Acte.

EDCS-09202330.translation: To the departed spirits of Quintina Austeris and Titus Calvius Perigenus, from Titus Calvius Calvinus and Titus Calvius Secundus, sons.
EDCS-09202330.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintina Austeris and Titus Calvius Perigenus, set up by their sons, Titus Calvius Calvinus and Titus Calvius Secundus.

EDCS-09202331.translation: To Quintulus, son of Quintus, and Allia, his sweetest wife, and to the grandson Quintinus.
EDCS-09202331.summary: This is a funerary epitaph commemorating Quintulus, his wife Allia, and their grandson Quintinus.

EDCS-09202332.translation: To the departed spirits of Quintus, son of Quintus, from Restituta, granddaughter, from her own funds.
EDCS-09202332.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus, son of Quintus, funded by his granddaughter Restituta.

EDCS-09202334.translation: To the departed spirits of Raricus, the most faithful slave.
EDCS-09202334.summary: This is a funerary epitaph honoring Raricus, a loyal slave.

EDCS-09202335.translation: To the departed spirits of Reburria Suavis; she ordered this to be made for herself and her family by her will.
EDCS-09202335.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Reburria Suavis, who stipulated in her will for it to be erected for herself and her relatives.

EDCS-09202336.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Valeria Tyche to her dearest grandson, Gnaeus Reiconius Noricus.
EDCS-09202336.summary: A funerary dedication to a grandson by his grandmother, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202337.translation: If any of those listed above should not be living when I die, or should die after my death, those who remain should substitute others in place of those who have died, by vote, whom they consider most worthy, provided that there are not less than thirty in perpetuity; and it shall be permitted for those who cannot be present on those days to send a guest from among their friends in their place. The keys of his mausoleum are entrusted to two of my freedmen and the curator of that year. Titus Rovcius Maternus, Caius Licinius Sotericus, Aulus Fulvius Tarentinus, Titus Iulius Cosmus, Tiberius Claudius Etoemus, Publius Acilius Philodespotus, Quintus Caninius Eutychus, Quintus Iuventius Venustus, Lucius Valerius Cupitus.
EDCS-09202337.summary: This lengthy inscription outlines detailed instructions for the succession of custodians of a mausoleum and lists the names of individuals entrusted with its care, suggesting a private burial complex likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202338.summary: A funerary dedication to Gaius Rusus Celaedus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202339.translation: Rustica, daughter of Aquillus, had this made for her parents, sister, and herself.
EDCS-09202339.summary: This funerary monument was commissioned by Rustica for her family, including herself, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202340.translation: To the Divine Spirits. To Rustica Auxes, the patroness.
EDCS-09202340.summary: A funerary dedication to Rustica Auxes, identified as a patroness, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202341.translation: To the Divine Spirits. To Sabinus, his excellent brother.
EDCS-09202341.summary: A funerary dedication from one brother to another, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202342.translation: To the Divine Spirits. To Lucius Atettius Cornelianus, the heir of Iulius Sabinus Quintilianus.
EDCS-09202342.summary: A funerary dedication by an heir, Lucius Atettius Cornelianus, for Iulius Sabinus Quintilianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202343.translation: To the Divine Spirits. To Sabina, daughter of Sabinus.
EDCS-09202343.summary: A funerary dedication to Sabina, daughter of Sabinus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202344.translation: To the son of Salvius Secundinus.
EDCS-09202344.summary: A funerary dedication to the son of Salvius Secundinus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202345.translation: To Lucius Sammus, son of Lucius, of the Voltinian tribe.
EDCS-09202345.summary: A funerary dedication to Lucius Sammus, noting his father and tribal affiliation, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202346.translation: To the Divine Shades. Sammia Helpizusa, mother, [erected this] for Sextus Sammius Apronianus.
EDCS-09202346.summary: A funerary dedication by a mother to her deceased son, Sextus Sammius Apronianus.

EDCS-09202347.translation: To the Divine Shades. Sextus Sammius Mercurialis erected [this] for his dearest wife, Sammia Laidias.
EDCS-09202347.summary: A funerary dedication by a husband to his wife, Sammia Laidias.

EDCS-09202348.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Sappius, son of Lucius, of the Voltinian tribe, and for Marcellus, daughter of Numerius, wife of Sappius, and daughter of Calvius.
EDCS-09202348.summary: A funerary dedication to Sappius, son of Lucius, and his wife Marcellus.

EDCS-09202349.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Marcus Sappius, son of Lucius, of the Voltinian tribe, and for Tertius Sappius, son of Lucius, of the Voltinian tribe.
EDCS-09202349.summary: A funerary dedication to Marcus Sappius and Tertius Sappius, both sons of Lucius.

EDCS-09202350.translation: To the Divine Shades. Spuria Felicula [erected this] for her husband, Gnaeus Satrius Chresimus.
EDCS-09202350.summary: A funerary dedication by a wife to her deceased husband, Gnaeus Satrius Chresimus.

EDCS-09202351.translation: For eternal memory. Maximia Calvina [erected this] for her mother, Sattia Myrtales, and for her father, Calvinius Mirtaloris.
EDCS-09202351.summary: A funerary dedication by a daughter, Maximia Calvina, to her parents, Sattia Myrtales and Calvinius Mirtaloris.

EDCS-09202352.translation: To the Divine Shades. Avita, wife [erected this] for her husband, Satullus Hospis, son of [---].
EDCS-09202352.summary: A funerary dedication by a wife to her deceased husband, Satullus Hospis.

EDCS-09202353.translation: For Satullus, son of Lucius, [and] for Parucia Concessa.
EDCS-09202353.summary: A dedication to Satullus, son of Lucius, and Parucia Concessa.

EDCS-09202355.summary: A dedication to Saturninus, son of Erucius.

EDCS-09202356.translation: To the Divine Shades. Rustica, mother, [erected this] for her most dutiful daughter, Saturnina, daughter of Tertius, and for her wife Caius Attius Atimetus, who deserved exceptionally well of her.
EDCS-09202356.summary: A funerary dedication by a mother to her daughter Saturnina and her wife Caius Attius Atimetus, who deserved exceptionally well of her.

EDCS-09202357.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Erotis, the most unhappy mother, sets up [this monument] for her daughter Secia Protogenia while she herself is alive.
EDCS-09202357.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a mother for her daughter.

EDCS-09202358.translation: To the Divine Spirits and memory of [her] sweetest daughter Secunda, who lived 35 years, [a monument of] piety.
EDCS-09202358.summary: This is a funerary epitaph commemorating Secunda, who died at the age of 35.

EDCS-09202359.summary: This inscription records the name and filiation of Secundus.

EDCS-09202360.summary: This is a dedication to Secundus, son of Dannomus.

EDCS-09202361.translation: To Secundus, [son] of Iulius, [and] to Iulia Severa, [his] parents.
EDCS-09202361.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Secundus and his parents, Iulius and Iulia Severa.

EDCS-09202362.summary: This is a dedication to Secundus, son of Sapalo.

EDCS-09202363.translation: Lucius Trebius Clymenus to his wife Erenis, daughter of Cai, called Secunda.
EDCS-09202363.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by a husband to his wife, Erenis (also known as Secunda).

EDCS-09202364.translation: To the Spirits. Sextus Porcius Hecataeus to his dearest wife Secunda Maior, daughter of Secundus.
EDCS-09202364.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by a husband to his wife, Secunda Maior.

EDCS-09202365.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Marcus Cornelius Cassianus to his excellent freedwoman Secunda Tertulla, his ward.
EDCS-09202365.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by a patron to his freedwoman and ward, Secunda Tertulla.

EDCS-09202366.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Domitia to her dearest father Secundinus, freedman of Senilis, and to her husband Dubitata, [her] best husband.
EDCS-09202366.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Domitia to her father Secundinus and her husband Dubitata.

EDCS-09202367.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Gaius Propertius Epapra, to Secundina, daughter of Primus, his wife.
EDCS-09202367.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by Gaius Propertius Epapra to his wife Secundina.

EDCS-09202368.translation: Gaius Seius Epagathio made this while alive for himself, his patroness, and his wife.
EDCS-09202368.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Gaius Seius Epagathio for himself, his patroness, and his wife.

EDCS-09202369.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Helius, freedman of Gaius Seius Vestalis, dedicated this to his excellent patron.
EDCS-09202369.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Helius, a freedman, to his patron Gaius Seius Vestalis.

EDCS-09202370.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Titus Sempronius Mercurius, Titus Sempronius Helpidianus his son, and Setulcia Elpis his wife.
EDCS-09202370.summary: This funerary inscription records Titus Sempronius Mercurius, his son, and his wife Setulcia Elpis.

EDCS-09202371.translation: To the spirits of the departed: To Sempronia Secunda, daughter of Primula Vegeti, a most dutiful mother.
EDCS-09202371.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Primula Vegeti to her dutiful mother, Sempronia Secunda.

EDCS-09202372.translation: To Senecio, son of Anniccus: Titus Aelius Piperculus, to his brother.
EDCS-09202372.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Titus Aelius Piperculus to his brother Senecio.

EDCS-09202373.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Gaius Senius Pyramus. Tioccia Peregrina made this for herself and her husband while alive.
EDCS-09202373.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Tioccia Peregrina for herself and her husband Gaius Senius Pyramus.

EDCS-09202374.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Of Marcus Sennius Antius.
EDCS-09202374.summary: This is a simple funerary dedication to Marcus Sennius Antius.

EDCS-09202375.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Hermogenes, son of Lucius Sennius, who lived 22 years and 7 months. Titia Epictesis, his nurse, placed this.
EDCS-09202375.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by Titia Epictesis, nurse, for Hermogenes, son of Lucius Sennius, who died at age 22.

EDCS-09202376.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Of Quintus Sennius Onesiphorus. Sennia Porpuris, his mother, to her most dutiful son.
EDCS-09202376.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Sennia Porpuris to her son Quintus Sennius Onesiphorus.

EDCS-09202377.translation: To the Divine Spirits of Lucius Sennius Primus Vitalis, his freedman.
EDCS-09202377.summary: This is a funerary dedication from a freedman to Lucius Sennius Primus, likely his patron, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202378.translation: Sennia Hygia made this for herself while alive.
EDCS-09202378.summary: This is a self-funded funerary monument set up by Sennia Hygia during her lifetime, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202379.translation: To the Divine Spirits of Septimia Philotera, who lived 25 years, 2 months, and 1 day. Maria Dione to her dearest friend.
EDCS-09202379.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Maria Dione to her friend Septimia Philotera, including her age at death, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202380.translation: To the Divine Spirits of Sergia Montania. Acilia Sergiana, to her most excellent mother, and Marcus Montanius Epictetus Junior, freedman.
EDCS-09202380.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Acilia Sergiana and Marcus Montanius Epictetus Junior to Sergia Montania, likely the mother of one of the dedicants.

EDCS-09202382.translation: The heirs of Lucius Sertullius Oceanus.
EDCS-09202382.summary: This inscription records the heirs of Lucius Sertullius Oceanus, likely related to the administration of his estate or a funerary context.

EDCS-09202383.translation: To the Divine Spirits of Servatus Ver.
EDCS-09202383.summary: This is a simple funerary dedication to Servatus Ver, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202384.translation: To the Divine Spirits of Gnaeus Servilius, freedman of Papirius Fundanus Ephesius Servilius.
EDCS-09202384.summary: This is a funerary dedication from a freedman to Gnaeus Servilius, likely his former owner, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202385.translation: Gnaeus Servilius Vetus erected this for Gnaeus Servilius Seranus.
EDCS-09202385.summary: This inscription records Gnaeus Servilius Vetus setting up a monument for Gnaeus Servilius Seranus, likely a relative or patron.

EDCS-09202386.translation: To the Divine Spirits of Servilia Adiecta, by Vitalis, her freedman fellow-slave, to his most dutiful fellow-slave.
EDCS-09202386.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Vitalis to his fellow-slave and partner, Servilia Adiecta, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202387.translation: Lucius Omivius Honorius and Terentius Terentullus, clients, to Lucius Servius Labeo.
EDCS-09202387.summary: This inscription records a dedication from clients Lucius Omivius Honorius and Terentius Terentullus to their patron Lucius Servius Labeo.

EDCS-09202388.translation: Severina, Severus, son of Secundus, and Julia Fabricia, to their most dutiful daughter.
EDCS-09202388.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication by Severus and Julia Fabricia to their daughter Severina, likely a funerary monument.

EDCS-09202389.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Severia Parthenope made this for her most dutiful husband, Marcus Severus Marcianus, who lived 47 years, and for herself while alive.
EDCS-09202389.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Severia Parthenope for her husband Marcus Severus Marcianus and herself.

EDCS-09202390.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Sextus Severius Quartinus, to his most dutiful daughter, Severia, daughter of Sextus, Quartina.
EDCS-09202390.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by Sextus Severius Quartinus to his daughter Severia Quartina.

EDCS-09202392.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Sextia Dubitata to an unnamed patroness.

EDCS-09202393.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Iaxsucus, to his wife, Severina, daughter of Kari.
EDCS-09202393.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Iaxsucus for his wife Severina.

EDCS-09202394.translation: Silvania Iulia, to her most dutiful husband, Primo, son of Nasonis, and to her most beloved mother-in-law, Montana, most dutiful.
EDCS-09202394.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by Silvania Iulia to her husband Primo and mother-in-law Montana.

EDCS-09202395.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Sinicus Bandinus to his spouse.

EDCS-09202396.translation: Lucius Smerius, son of Spurius, arranged for this to be made for Smerius, his father, and Ingenua, his mother, and Tuta, his sister.
EDCS-09202396.summary: This is a funerary commission by Lucius Smerius for his deceased parents and sister.

EDCS-09202397.translation: To the memory of Socrates and Antiochus, most dutiful brothers, by their sisters and fellow-household members.
EDCS-09202397.summary: This is a memorial inscription for two brothers, Socrates and Antiochus, set up by their sisters and contubernales (fellow-members of a mess or tent group).

EDCS-09202398.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Sextus Solibit to an unnamed brother.

EDCS-09202399.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the 'Solemn Shades'.

EDCS-09202400.translation: To the Shades of Solonia Helpis, Quintus Solon Alcimus for his wife
EDCS-09202400.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Quintus Solon Alcimus to the memory of his wife, Solonia Helpis.

EDCS-09202401.translation: To the Shades of Iulius Sosimenus, for his best aunt Iulia Nicaris
EDCS-09202401.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Iulius Sosimenus to his aunt, Iulia Nicaris.

EDCS-09202402.translation: To the Shades of Quintus Speccius Senilis, for himself and his wife Pompeia Ampliata, daughter of Sextus
EDCS-09202402.summary: This funerary inscription records Quintus Speccius Senilis dedicating a monument for himself and his wife, Pompeia Ampliata.

EDCS-09202403.translation: Spurius Statutus for himself and for his wife Decumia Remulla and for his son Sextus Spurius Decuminus
EDCS-09202403.summary: This inscription records Spurius Statutus dedicating a monument for himself, his wife Decumia Remulla, and his son Sextus Spurius Decuminus.

EDCS-09202404.translation: To the Shades of Statia Deuteris, Statia Festa for her patroness
EDCS-09202404.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Statia Festa to her patroness, Statia Deuteris.

EDCS-09202405.translation: Suavinus Catulus, freedman, for his wife Secundina, daughter of Actalius Secundus, for his son Catulinus, for his son Sabinus. Secunda Actali, daughter, made this for herself and her family while alive.
EDCS-09202405.summary: This inscription records Secunda Actali, daughter of Actalius Secundus, making a funerary monument for herself, her family, and freedmen, including her husband and sons.

EDCS-09202406.translation: [...] for himself and for his wife [...] and for Successus, his son, and for Quartulus, his son, made
EDCS-09202406.summary: This inscription records a person dedicating a monument for himself, his wife, and his sons Successus and Quartulus.

EDCS-09202407.translation: To Sulpicia Legituma, Lucius Licinius Narcissus for his excellent wife
EDCS-09202407.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Lucius Licinius Narcissus to his wife, Sulpicia Legituma.

EDCS-09202408.translation: To the Shades of Suria Navica, Sextus Concennus Seranus for his dearest wife
EDCS-09202408.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Sextus Concennus Seranus to his wife, Suria Navica.

EDCS-09202409.translation: Sympherusa, while alive, erected this for herself and for her patroness Paramone.
EDCS-09202409.summary: This funerary inscription records a woman named Sympherusa dedicating a monument to herself and her patroness, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202410.translation: To the departed spirits of Sympherus.
EDCS-09202410.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription to the 'Dis Manibus' (departed spirits), likely for an individual named Sympherus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202411.translation: Titus Tancius for his brother Titus Tancius Titullus.
EDCS-09202411.summary: This inscription records Titus Tancius dedicating something to his brother Titus Tancius Titullus, likely a tombstone or monument, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202412.translation: To the departed spirits of Tarcia Marcia for Domitia Macaria.
EDCS-09202412.summary: This dedicatory inscription to the 'Dis Manibus' records Tarcia Marcia honoring Domitia Macaria, likely a funerary monument from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202413.translation: To the departed spirits of Titus Tavillius Honoratus, son of Titus, of the Voltinia tribe; (erected by) Tavillia Titulla for her brother, while alive, at her own expense.
EDCS-09202413.summary: This funerary inscription records Tavillia Titulla dedicating a monument to her brother Titus Tavillius Honoratus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202414.translation: To the departed spirits of Marcus Terentius Blaesus. Pompeia Quartula, for herself and for her most excellent husband, erected this while alive.
EDCS-09202414.summary: This funerary inscription records Pompeia Quartula dedicating a monument to herself and her husband, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202415.translation: To the departed spirits of Titus Terentius Onesimus. He erected this for himself while alive, and for his deceased Fortunata.
EDCS-09202415.summary: This funerary inscription records Titus Terentius Onesimus dedicating a monument to himself and his deceased wife Fortunata, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202416.summary: This inscription is a dedication or memorial for Terentia Primula, likely a tombstone from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202417.translation: To the departed spirits of Terentia Titulla, daughter of Titus, aged 26.
EDCS-09202417.summary: This funerary inscription records the age and parentage of Terentia Titulla, dedicated to her departed spirit, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202418.translation: To the departed spirits of Tertius Bucanus and Marcus Rufius Iustinus. Marcus Rufius Maximinus and Rufia Quartina for their most excellent father and brother.
EDCS-09202418.summary: This funerary inscription records Marcus Rufius Maximinus and Rufia Quartina dedicating a monument to their father and brother, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202419.translation: Tertius, son of Cintullus, for himself, and for his father Cintullus, son of Atepo, and for his mother Iulia, daughter of Troucillus, and for his sister Quinta, daughter of Cintullus, and for his wife Secunda, daughter of Toutillus, according to his will.
EDCS-09202419.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication established by Tertius for himself and his family members, made according to a will, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09202420.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Titus Tertius Paullus, and his freedman Titus Tertius Verecundus, for Primigenia Aurelia, his wife.
EDCS-09202420.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Titus Tertius Verecundus and Titus Tertius Paullus for Aurelia Primigenia, his wife, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09202421.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Primus, the patron, and Delphinus, the heirs, placed this.
EDCS-09202421.summary: This funerary inscription records that Primus, the patron, and Delphinus, his heir, erected this monument for Lucius Tertullius Marcianus, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09202422.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Tertulia, daughter of Successus, placed this for herself while alive.
EDCS-09202422.summary: This is a self-funded funerary dedication by Tertulia, daughter of Successus, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09202423.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Tertulia Spuria.
EDCS-09202423.summary: This is a simple funerary dedication to Tertulia Spuria, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09202425.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Annia Tuta for her excellent mother, Tertulla.
EDCS-09202425.summary: This funerary inscription records Annia Tuta dedicating this monument to her mother, Tertulla, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09202426.translation: Gaius Tessius Avitus, son of Gaius, of the Voltinia tribe, for himself while alive.
EDCS-09202426.summary: This is a dedication by Gaius Tessius Avitus for himself, likely a tombstone or memorial, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09202427.translation: Thaumastus for his wife, and Sollius Eleutherius for his foster child.
EDCS-09202427.summary: This inscription appears to record two separate dedications: one by Thaumastus for his wife, and another by Sollius Eleutherius for his foster child, likely funerary, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09202428.translation: Tingilonaia Valentina and her brothers, at the request of their mother.
EDCS-09202428.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Tingilonaia Valentina and her brothers, commissioned by their mother, likely a funerary monument, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09202429.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Marcus Domitius Aprilis for his excellent wife, Titia Amabilis.
EDCS-09202429.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Marcus Domitius Aprilis for his wife, Titia Amabilis, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09202430.translation: To Tittia Crescentiana, who lived 22 years and 14 days, from Caecilia Crescentiane, her most devoted mother, most unhappy.
EDCS-09202430.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Tittia Crescentiana, set up by her mother.

EDCS-09202431.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Tittia Severina, from her husband Iuvenalis Octavius, for his most excellent wife.
EDCS-09202431.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Tittia Severina, set up by her husband.

EDCS-09202432.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Tittia Tita, his beloved daughter, and for his mother-in-law Carisia, daughter of Sextius, for his wife. Marcus Licinius Hermes erected this while alive.
EDCS-09202432.summary: This funerary dedication was set up by Marcus Licinius Hermes for his wife Tittia Tita and his mother-in-law Carisia.

EDCS-09202433.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Tittulus Successor, his son. His wife Nundina set this up.
EDCS-09202433.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Tittulus Successor, set up by his wife.

EDCS-09202434.translation: To Tittulla, from her brother Titullus.
EDCS-09202434.summary: This is a dedication from Titullus to his sister Tittulla.

EDCS-09202435.translation: To Togiacius Phileros and Julia Antiquilla, from Julia Rufina, their most excellent friend, and from Mesophilus, son of their patron and of Julia Antiquilla.
EDCS-09202435.summary: This dedication is made to Togiacius Phileros and Julia Antiquilla by Julia Rufina and Mesophilus.

EDCS-09202437.translation: To Quintus Trogus Lydus, from Quintus Trogus Hermetus, his most excellent patron.
EDCS-09202437.summary: This is a dedication to Quintus Trogus Lydus from his client Quintus Trogus Hermetus.

EDCS-09202438.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Turpilius Pumilio.

EDCS-09202439.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Tuta, daughter of Maxumus. Utulius, son of Verus Velagenus, to the spirits of the departed.
EDCS-09202439.summary: This funerary dedication mentions Tuta, daughter of Maxumus, and Utulius, son of Verus Velagenus.

EDCS-09202440.translation: To Quintus Titius Martinus, from his son Titius Tarcius and Tarcia Egie.
EDCS-09202440.summary: This dedication is to Quintus Titius Martinus by his son Titius Tarcius and Tarcia Egie.

EDCS-09202441.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Tyches, a fellow slave.
EDCS-09202441.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the underworld spirits for a deceased fellow slave named Tyches.

EDCS-09202442.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Tyches, most dutiful daughter. Tertia Doris, most unhappy mother, erected this for herself and her daughter.
EDCS-09202442.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Tyches, set up by her mother, Tertia Doris.

EDCS-09202443.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Valentina, most dutiful sister. Her brothers and sisters erected this.
EDCS-09202443.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by siblings to their most dutiful sister, Valentina.

EDCS-09202444.translation: Valeria Blaesia erected this for her daughter Valerilla.
EDCS-09202444.summary: This is a dedication by Valeria Blaesia for her daughter Valerilla.

EDCS-09202445.summary: This is a very brief inscription likely marking a tomb for Lucius Valerius.

EDCS-09202446.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Valerius, son of Sabinus, and for Maternus, for his daughter of the same name, and for Maternus, his most dutiful son, for his mother.
EDCS-09202446.summary: This complex funerary dedication honors multiple family members, including Valerius (son of Sabinus) and Maternus with his son and daughter.

EDCS-09202447.translation: Lucius Valerius Apiles for himself and for his wife, Sac [---] Lucretia.
EDCS-09202447.summary: This inscription records a self-dedication and dedication for his wife, Lucretia, by Lucius Valerius Apiles.

EDCS-09202448.translation: Serana, wife of Marcus Valerius Avitus.
EDCS-09202448.summary: This inscription marks the tomb or memory of Serana, wife of Marcus Valerius Avitus.

EDCS-09202449.summary: This inscription likely refers to a deceased individual, Caius Valerius Eutychetes, identified as a patron.

EDCS-09202450.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Valerius Primulus.
EDCS-09202450.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the underworld spirits for Valerius Primulus.

EDCS-09202451.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Titus Valerius Valerianus to his most excellent father, Titus Valerius Primus, son of Titus, of the Voltinia tribe.
EDCS-09202451.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Titus Valerius Valerianus for his father, Titus Valerius Primus, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09202452.translation: He made this while alive for the spirits of the departed, for Iulius Valerius Primus and Iunia Tryphosa.
EDCS-09202452.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by a living person for themselves and for Iulius Valerius Primus and Iunia Tryphosa, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09202453.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Domitia Sabina, his wife, and for herself.
EDCS-09202453.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Domitia Sabina for the spirits of the departed and for herself, likely for her deceased husband Valerius Repentinus, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09202454.translation: Marcus Dumerius, while alive, placed this for Lucius Valerius Riouercus, son of Dudio.
EDCS-09202454.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by Marcus Dumerius for Lucius Valerius Riouercus, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09202455.translation: Quintus Valerius Primulus, Quintus Valerius Secundinus, and Quintus Valerius Gratus, sons, set this up to the spirits of the departed, for their father Quintus Valerius Scaeva and their wife Vegetae.
EDCS-09202455.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by three sons for their deceased father, Quintus Valerius Scaeva, and their wife Vegetae, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09202456.translation: Annula for herself and her family to Valerius Verticon, son of Maxsume, and to Pompeia Secundo, son of Annula.
EDCS-09202456.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Annula for herself and her family, honoring Valerius Vertico and Pompeia Secundo, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09202457.translation: To the spirits of the departed Valeria.
EDCS-09202457.summary: A fragmented funerary epitaph simply mentioning Valeria, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09202458.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for mother Valeria Rustica and brother Valerius Lucius.
EDCS-09202458.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicating to the spirits of the departed for a mother, Valeria Rustica, and a brother, Valerius Lucius, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09202459.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Valeria Maximinia, aged 3 years and 23 days. Maximinus and Veladus, sons of Maxsimus, and Lucina, daughter of Lucullus, her parents.
EDCS-09202459.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young child, Valeria Maximinia, set up by her parents, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09202460.translation: She ordered this to be set up to the spirits of the departed, for herself and her son, Valeria Scotii daughter.
EDCS-09202460.summary: A funerary epitaph indicating a woman, Valeria, daughter of Scotii, ordered her own funerary monument and one for her son, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09202461.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Valeria, daughter of Valerius.
EDCS-09202461.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Valeria, daughter of Valerius.

EDCS-09202462.translation: To Valerin, son of Valerius, aged 11 years and 10 months, grandson of Dubia Amabilis, freedwoman.
EDCS-09202462.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Valerin, son of Valerius, aged 11 years and 10 months.

EDCS-09202463.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Valeria Agricae; Sextus Aurelius Zosimus set this up for his most excellent wife.
EDCS-09202463.summary: This funerary inscription records Sextus Aurelius Zosimus setting up a monument for his wife, Valeria Agricae.

EDCS-09202464.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Valeria Aphro; Gnaeus Pompeius Halieus set this up for his most excellent wife.
EDCS-09202464.summary: This funerary inscription records Gnaeus Pompeius Halieus setting up a monument for his wife, Valeria Aphro.

EDCS-09202465.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Valeria Callistenes, most deserving.
EDCS-09202465.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Valeria Callistenes, who is described as 'most deserving'.

EDCS-09202466.translation: Valeria Candida set this up while alive for Gaius Marcius Cosmio, who deserved well.
EDCS-09202466.summary: This inscription records Valeria Candida setting up a monument for Gaius Marcius Cosmio.

EDCS-09202467.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Valeria Celsina; Valerius Celsus and Valeria Ianuaria set this up for their most dutiful daughter and for themselves while alive.
EDCS-09202467.summary: This funerary inscription records Valerius Celsus and Valeria Ianuaria setting up a monument for their daughter Valeria Celsina and for themselves.

EDCS-09202468.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Valeria Fortunata; Successus, freedman.
EDCS-09202468.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Valeria Fortunata by her freedman, Successus.

EDCS-09202469.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Valeria Maxima; Lucius Valerius Maximinus, her son.
EDCS-09202469.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Valeria Maxima by her son, Lucius Valerius Maximinus.

EDCS-09202470.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, for Valeria Mogonia; Gaius Iulius Maternus, for his most devoted wife.
EDCS-09202470.summary: This funerary inscription records Gaius Iulius Maternus setting up a monument for his wife, Valeria Mogonia.

EDCS-09202471.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Lucius Munatius Titullus for his sister Valeriane Munatia, and Munatia Marcella for her grandmother.
EDCS-09202471.summary: This epitaph is a dedication by Lucius Munatius Titullus and Munatia Marcella for their deceased relatives Valeriane Munatia and her grandmother.

EDCS-09202472.translation: To the spirits of the departed: For Valeriane Octavia, from her most dutiful daughter Valeria Vera.
EDCS-09202472.summary: This epitaph is a dedication by Valeria Vera for her most dutiful daughter Valeriane Octavia.

EDCS-09202473.translation: To the spirits of the departed: For Valeriane Primilla.
EDCS-09202473.summary: This is a simple epitaph dedicated to the spirits of the departed for Valeriane Primilla.

EDCS-09202474.translation: To the spirits of the departed: For Valeriane Saturnina, aged nine months. Valerianus.
EDCS-09202474.summary: This epitaph records the death of a young child, Valeriane Saturnina, aged nine months, with a dedication by Valerianus.

EDCS-09202475.translation: To the spirits of the departed: For Valeriane Servata, from her freedwoman Valeria Isias.
EDCS-09202475.summary: This epitaph is a dedication by Valeria Isias, a freedwoman, for her deceased patron Valeriane Servata.

EDCS-09202476.translation: To the spirits of the departed: For Valeriane, daughter of Titus, called Titulla. Her most dutiful daughter Valeria Gemina erected this.
EDCS-09202476.summary: This epitaph is a dedication by Valeria Gemina for her most dutiful mother, Valeriane, daughter of Titus, also known as Titulla.

EDCS-09202477.translation: To the spirits of the departed: For Verula, daughter of Valerius.
EDCS-09202477.summary: This epitaph is a dedication to the spirits of the departed for Verula, daughter of Valerius.

EDCS-09202478.translation: To the spirits of the departed: For her excellent brother Vallonius. Quartina.
EDCS-09202478.summary: This epitaph is a dedication by Quartina for her excellent brother Vallonius.

EDCS-09202479.translation: To the spirits of the departed: For his incomparable wife Varenia Augenis and for himself in his lifetime. Caesius Patroclus.
EDCS-09202479.summary: This epitaph is a dedication made during his lifetime by Caesius Patroclus for his incomparable wife Varenia Augenis and for himself.

EDCS-09202480.translation: To the spirits of the departed: For Vedia Musa.
EDCS-09202480.summary: This is a simple epitaph dedicated to the spirits of the departed for Vedia Musa.

EDCS-09202481.translation: Venator, son of Sextus, and Tertius, son of Sextus, and Garkal, son of Ateioucos, made this for their mother and for themselves and their families while alive.
EDCS-09202481.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by sons and their father for their mother.

EDCS-09202482.translation: To the departed spirits. Marcus Vinovaleius Paternus set this up for his most dear parent, Marcus Venicotena Valeriana.
EDCS-09202482.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up by a son for his parent.

EDCS-09202483.translation: To the departed spirits. Solisetia Serana placed this for her most dear husband, Lucius Vercellius Felicio.
EDCS-09202483.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up by a wife for her husband.

EDCS-09202484.translation: Verecundus, freedman of Quintus Vercellius Maximus Catulus, to Verecunda Cestia, his freedwoman and companion.
EDCS-09202484.summary: This is a dedication by a freedman to his freedwoman companion.

EDCS-09202485.translation: To the departed spirits. Quintus Verinius Virilis set this up for his most dutiful father, Verinus Verus.
EDCS-09202485.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up by a son for his father.

EDCS-09202486.translation: To the departed spirits. Marcus Annius Paternus set this up for his excellent mother, Vettitia Dubitata.
EDCS-09202486.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up by a son for his mother.

EDCS-09202487.translation: To the departed spirits. Caius Gnatus Caecilianus, the stepson, and Caecilia Haple, the wife, [set this up] for Caius Vettius Dionysus.
EDCS-09202487.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up by a stepson and wife for the deceased.

EDCS-09202488.translation: To the departed spirits. Vettia Euporia set this up for her most excellent husband, Titus Vettius Victor.
EDCS-09202488.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up by a wife for her husband.

EDCS-09202489.translation: To the departed spirits. Domitia Maximilla, his wife, placed this for Caius Vibius Asiaticus and for herself.
EDCS-09202489.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up by a wife for her husband and herself.

EDCS-09202490.translation: To the departed spirits of Caius Vibius Licinianus, aged 16 years and 6 months. Caius Vibius Agathopus and Licinia Nomas [set this up] for their most excellent and dutiful son. May many flowers bloom on your newly made tomb, not thorny brambles nor dry Aegilops, but violets and wild marjoram and watery narcissus; and may roses bloom for you, Vibius, and around you.
EDCS-09202490.summary: This is a funerary dedication for a young boy, including Greek verses wishing for beautiful flowers on his tomb.

EDCS-09202491.translation: Lucius Vibius, freedman of Lucius, to his wife Fausta, by his will.
EDCS-09202491.summary: This inscription records a funerary dedication made by Lucius Vibius to his wife Fausta, as specified in his will.

EDCS-09202492.translation: Vibia Lais made this for herself and her husband Aurelius Statutus while she was alive.
EDCS-09202492.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Vibia Lais for herself and her husband Aurelius Statutus, made during her lifetime.

EDCS-09202493.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Victor, from Baebia Helpidiana, his mother (?).
EDCS-09202493.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the spirits of the departed, likely for Victor, set up by Baebia Helpidiana.

EDCS-09202495.summary: This is a simple dedication, likely funerary, to Titus Vinicius Gratus.

EDCS-09202496.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Vinicius Ionicus.
EDCS-09202496.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Vinicius Ionicus.

EDCS-09202497.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Secundilla to her most dutiful sister, Vinivallia Paternus.
EDCS-09202497.summary: This funerary inscription records Secundilla's dedication to her sister, Vinivallia Paternus.

EDCS-09202498.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Caius Quintilius Eutychus to his excellent wife, Servata, daughter of Vinnucia Montanus.
EDCS-09202498.summary: This funerary inscription records Caius Quintilius Eutychus's dedication to his wife Servata, daughter of Vinnucia Montanus.

EDCS-09202499.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Viricia Termais, his most dutiful granddaughter, erected this for Viricia Eufemia.
EDCS-09202499.summary: This funerary inscription records Viricia Termais's dedication to her grandmother Viricia Eufemia.

EDCS-09202500.translation: To Virillio, son of Montanus, and his wife Secunda.
EDCS-09202500.summary: This inscription is a dedication, likely funerary, to Virillio, son of Montanus, and his wife Secunda.

EDCS-09202501.summary: This is a simple dedication, likely funerary, to Titus Virillius Vitalis.

EDCS-09202502.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Gaius Pantuleius Anatellon and Marcus Ulpius Successus, the heirs, [erected this for] Ulpia Theodota, daughter of Marcus, a woman of the rarest example.
EDCS-09202502.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Ulpia Theodota by her heirs.
