EDCS-09202503.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Lucius Utulius Seianus, Lucius Utulius Celsinus, Lucius Utulius Aventin, Lucius Utulius Inventus, and Lucius Utulius Nigellio, freedmen, [dedicated this] to their patron Lucius Utulius Albinus Avitus, and to their wife Iulia Servata.
EDCS-09202503.summary: This funerary inscription was dedicated by freedmen to their patron and his wife.

EDCS-09202504.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Munatia Sabina [erected this for] her most excellent son, Lucius Utulius Euprepes.
EDCS-09202504.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by a mother to her son.

EDCS-09202505.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Crescens [dedicated this for] his partner Utulia Amabilis.
EDCS-09202505.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication by Crescens to his partner Utulia Amabilis.

EDCS-09202506.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Zoe, most dutiful daughter, and for her partner Substitutus.
EDCS-09202506.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Zoe and her partner Substitutus.

EDCS-09202507.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. The parents [erected this for] Zosimus.
EDCS-09202507.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by parents to their son Zosimus.

EDCS-09202508.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Ammillinus, who lived 58 years. Marcus Api Genialis [dedicated this] to his most excellent wife, and Maximus, his son, to his most dutiful mother.
EDCS-09202508.summary: This funerary inscription dedicates a monument to Ammillinus by his wife and son.

EDCS-09202509.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. POIFATAE XORATS BRVOBX.
EDCS-09202509.summary: This inscription is too fragmentary to determine its specific purpose, but it is dedicated to the Dis Manes.

EDCS-09202510.translation: His wife [dedicated this] to her most devoted husband.
EDCS-09202510.summary: This funerary inscription records a wife's dedication to her husband.

EDCS-09202512.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For their parent, they themselves, while alive, made this.
EDCS-09202512.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication made by children to their parent while they were alive.

EDCS-09202533.translation: Eucarpia set this up for herself while alive, and set it up for her most dutiful father.
EDCS-09202533.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Eucarpia for herself and her father.

EDCS-09202541.translation: For Caecilia Pedullina, daughter of Titus, and for Lucius Cominius Castus, her husband. Titus Caecilius Glyptus and his freedwoman Caecilia Aple [are responsible].
EDCS-09202541.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Caecilia Pedullina and Lucius Cominius Castus, likely set up by family members.

EDCS-09202542.translation: For Caria Servata, his most remarkable wife. Iunius Quintus set this up for her and for himself while alive.
EDCS-09202542.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Iunius Quintus for his wife Caria Servata and himself.

EDCS-09202543.translation: To the divine shades, for Lucenia Dubitata, [set up by] Caius Iulius Honoratus, her most excellent mother.
EDCS-09202543.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Caius Iulius Honoratus to his mother, Lucenia Dubitata.

EDCS-09202545.summary: This is a dedication to Titus Cadio Titullus, likely on a monument.

EDCS-09202546.translation: To his wife Longinus Bitoni, by her will.
EDCS-09202546.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Longinus Bitoni, established according to her will.

EDCS-09202547.translation: To the divine shades, for Servata, who lived 16 years.
EDCS-09202547.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Servata, a sixteen-year-old girl.

EDCS-09202548.translation: Sacred to Diana Augusta. [Set up by] Trophimius, freedman of Caius Octavius Pedo, a six-member Augustalis priest, a decurion, and an ornamentarius.
EDCS-09202548.summary: This is a religious dedication to Diana Augusta, made by Trophimius, a freedman holding several public and religious offices.

EDCS-09202549.translation: Sacred to Luna and Augusta Isis. Trophimius, freedman of Caius Octavius Pedo, a six-member Augustalis priest, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-09202549.summary: This is a religious dedication to Luna and Isis Augusta, with the vow fulfilled by Trophimius, a freedman and Augustalis priest.

EDCS-09202550.translation: Born for the good of the state.
EDCS-09202550.summary: An epitaph possibly for a child or young person, highlighting their potential or presumed contribution to public life, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202551.translation: To the divine shades, for Quintus Frontonius, son of Quintus, of the Voltinian tribe. [Set up by] Valerius, a four-member official, while alive.
EDCS-09202551.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Valerius for Quintus Frontonius, commemorating his status as a magistrate.

EDCS-09202553.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Marcus Vedetius Melaenus, an Augustalis priest.
EDCS-09202553.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Vedetius Melaenus, who held the office of Augustalis priest, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202554.translation: To Blaesa, daughter of Blandus, sister, and wife of Servatus, son of Titus. Optatus, son of Blandus, set this up for himself and his family.
EDCS-09202554.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Optatus for his family members, including his wife Blaesa, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202555.summary: This is an honorary inscription dedicated to Quintus Pompeius Primus, who served as censor, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202556.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Valeria Fullonia.
EDCS-09202556.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Valeria Fullonia, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202557.translation: To Lucius Avillius Albanus, from Secundina, his camp-mate.
EDCS-09202557.summary: This is a funerary or commemorative inscription dedicated to Lucius Avillius Albanus by his contubernalis Secundina, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202558.translation: Faustus, his freedman, set this up for Titus Aurelius Nerva.
EDCS-09202558.summary: This is a funerary or commemorative inscription set up by the freedman Faustus for his former master Titus Aurelius Nerva, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202560.translation: To Mars Augustus: Gaius Iulius Palus, an Augustalis priest, honored with the ornaments of a decurion.
EDCS-09202560.summary: This is an honorary inscription dedicated to Mars Augustus and honoring Gaius Iulius Palus, an Augustalis priest who also received decurional honors, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202561.translation: Of Apollinaris, brother of the colony of Julia Augusta.
EDCS-09202561.summary: This inscription likely refers to a monument or dedication belonging to Apollinaris, who was associated with the colony of Julia Augusta, possibly dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202563.translation: Here rests in peace Leo of good memory, who lived for about nine years and died on the first day of December in the fourteenth indiction.
EDCS-09202563.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death of Leo, who lived for approximately nine years and died on December 1st of an unspecified year but indicated by the 14th indiction, likely dating to the Late Roman or early Byzantine period.

EDCS-09202565.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Cornelia I[---].
EDCS-09202565.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for Cornelia, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202566.translation: To the Divine Manes of Classia Theodora, Aurelius Taurinus [erected this] to his dearest wife.
EDCS-09202566.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Aurelius Taurinus to his wife, Classia Theodora.

EDCS-09202567.translation: To the Divine Manes of Valerianus, son of Lucretius. Secundina, daughter of Secundus, his wife, set this up for herself while alive and for Valerius, son of Valerianus, for his excellent father.
EDCS-09202567.summary: This funerary dedication by Secundina for herself and her husband Valerianus also commemorates their son Valerius.

EDCS-09202568.translation: To the Divine Manes of Caius Octavius Saturninus, Attia Severilla set this up for her most beloved husband and for herself.
EDCS-09202568.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Attia Severilla for her husband Caius Octavius Saturninus and herself.

EDCS-09202569.translation: To the Divine Manes of Caius Iulius Paternus, Nigria Nigrinia [set this up] for her excellent husband.
EDCS-09202569.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Nigria Nigrinia for her husband, Caius Iulius Paternus.

EDCS-09202570.translation: To the Divine Manes of Pedusia Maxsimilla.
EDCS-09202570.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Pedusia Maxsimilla.

EDCS-09202571.translation: To Marcus Octavius Messor, his son.
EDCS-09202571.summary: This is a dedication by a son to his father, Marcus Octavius Messor.

EDCS-09202572.translation: To the Divine Manes of Terentia Primillae, Lucia Terentia [set this up] for her most dutiful daughter.
EDCS-09202572.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lucia Terentia to her daughter, Terentia Primillae.

EDCS-09202574.translation: To the Divine Manes of Acilia Pompeia. Pammachius Karus [and] Acilius Fortunatus [set this up].
EDCS-09202574.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Pammachius Karus and Acilius Fortunatus to Acilia Pompeia.

EDCS-09202575.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Aviulli Macrini filii Cornelia Candida filio \n
EDCS-09202575.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Cornelia Candida, [dedicated this] for her son Aviullus Macrinus.
EDCS-09202575.summary: A funerary dedication for Aviullus Macrinus by his mother Cornelia Candida, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202577.translation: To the Manes of Quintus Gallicius Cinna, Gallicia his daughter and Optatus his son.
EDCS-09202577.summary: This funerary dedication is by the children, Gallicia and Optatus, to their father, Quintus Gallicius Cinna.

EDCS-09202578.translation: To Diana, Lucius Cassius Amarantus [dedicated this].
EDCS-09202578.summary: This is a religious dedication to the goddess Diana by Lucius Cassius Amarantus.

EDCS-09202579.translation: The lightning bolt has been buried.
EDCS-09202579.summary: This inscription records the burial of a lightning strike, a common practice in Roman religion when a lightning strike was believed to have divine origin and needed to be ritually interred.

EDCS-09202580.translation: Volt Barbara Oldra freely and deservedly fulfilled her vow to the August goddesses.
EDCS-09202580.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made by Volt Barbara Oldra to the August goddesses, likely a personal dedication.

EDCS-09202582.translation: Quintus C. R. [dedicated this] to Silvanus Augustus by order.
EDCS-09202582.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Quintus C. R. to Silvanus Augustus, indicating a religious offering likely from an official capacity.

EDCS-09202583.translation: To the Divine Manes of Sextus Bucculus Servandus, son of the quaestor of the colony of Buccula, and his wife Graecina.
EDCS-09202583.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Sextus Bucculus Servandus and his wife Graecina, commemorating their memory.

EDCS-09202584.translation: To Lucius Cassius Marinus, a member of the college of six Augustales.
EDCS-09202584.summary: This inscription records an honorific dedication to Lucius Cassius Marinus, a prominent local official, likely from his colleagues or the community.

EDCS-09202587.translation: To Gaius Annius Agricola, by his will.
EDCS-09202587.summary: This inscription records a dedication or bequest made in memory of Gaius Annius Agricola, as stipulated in his will.

EDCS-09202588.translation: To the Divine Manes of Gaius Aventinius Avitus and Licinia Servilia, from their son Gaius Aventinius Servilius, to his dearest parents.
EDCS-09202588.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Gaius Aventinius Servilius to his parents, Gaius Aventinius Avitus and Licinia Servilia.

EDCS-09202589.translation: To the Divine Manes of Titus Aurelius Voltinius, son of Albus.
EDCS-09202589.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Titus Aurelius Voltinius, son of Albus, commemorating his memory.

EDCS-09202591.translation: To the Divine Manes of Publius Calvius Receptus and Messena, daughter of Gnaeus, wife of Publius Calvius Receptus.
EDCS-09202591.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Publius Calvius Receptus and his wife Messena.

EDCS-09202592.summary: This inscription is likely a dedication or memorial to Lucius Cassius Optatus, possibly a tomb or a public monument.

EDCS-09202593.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Lucius Cassius Vocontius, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-09202594.translation: Quintus C. Marcius Cat made this to be set up for his father.
EDCS-09202594.summary: This inscription records that Quintus C. Marcius Cat erected this monument for his father.

EDCS-09202595.translation: To the Divine Shades. Marcus Sualius Cattius Cominius to his incomparable wife, Cattia Baetica.
EDCS-09202595.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Marcus Sualius Cattius Cominius to his wife Cattia Baetica, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09202596.translation: For eternal memory. To the Divine Shades. [---] had arranged for 7 months. [---] Claudius with whom life was lived, except whom he remembers with shed tears, with renewed grief.
EDCS-09202596.summary: This fragmented funerary inscription is a memorial to an individual, possibly related to Claudius, lamenting the deceased with renewed grief after a period of seven months.

EDCS-09202597.translation: To the Divine Shades of Caius Cornelius E[---] R I[---].
EDCS-09202597.summary: This is a partial funerary dedication to Caius Cornelius, the rest of whose name and the details of the monument are lost.

EDCS-09202598.translation: To the Divine Shades. Occia Tertulla set this up for her brother Caius Elvius Sextinus.
EDCS-09202598.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication set up by Occia Tertulla for her brother, Caius Elvius Sextinus.

EDCS-09202600.translation: To the Divine Shades. Valeria Casta set this up for her dearest husband Titus Flavius Avianus, for herself while alive.
EDCS-09202600.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Valeria Casta for her husband Titus Flavius Avianus and for herself, indicating it was a family tomb prepared in advance.

EDCS-09202601.translation: To the Divine Shades. To Frontonius Rusticus I N[---].
EDCS-09202601.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription dedicated to Frontonius Rusticus.

EDCS-09202602.translation: To the Divine Shades. Lucius Gratius Eutyches arranged his eternal home for himself while alive, so that he would not trouble his heir. These things.
EDCS-09202602.summary: This inscription records that Lucius Gratius Eutyches prepaid for his tomb, intended for himself while alive, to avoid burdening his heirs.

EDCS-09202605.translation: To Mastria Redonis. Aurelia Tyche, daughter, to her most sacred mother. Aurelius, son of Quarti, to his most sacred wife.
EDCS-09202605.summary: This inscription honors two individuals, possibly a mother and daughter or mother and daughter-in-law, Aurelia Tyche and Mastria Redonis, with dedications from Aurelius Quarti. f. and possibly another Aurelius.

EDCS-09202606.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Luci Mellius Myresmus, also known as Myron, who lived [for the Spirits of the Underworld]. To the Spirits of the Underworld Mellia Helena and Scotta.
EDCS-09202606.summary: This epitaph is dedicated to Luci Mellius Myresmus and also to Mellia Helena and Scotta, likely family members, under the invocation of the Manes (spirits of the underworld).

EDCS-09202607.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Maxsimus, son of Marcius, [erected this] for his most dutiful mother, Omulla, daughter of Aretullus.
EDCS-09202607.summary: This funerary inscription records Maxsimus setting up a monument for his mother, Omulla.

EDCS-09202608.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Pompeia Diogena. Aemilius Severinus, [her] brother, [erected this] for his dearest sister.
EDCS-09202608.summary: A brother, Aemilius Severinus, dedicates this epitaph to his sister, Pompeia Diogena.

EDCS-09202609.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Valeria Secundina.
EDCS-09202609.summary: A simple epitaph dedicated to Valeria Secundina under the invocation of the Manes.

EDCS-09202610.translation: For Vegetius, son of Aurelius, and for Quartula, daughter of Justus.
EDCS-09202610.summary: This inscription records the names of Vegetius and Quartula, likely a couple or related individuals, possibly for a shared tomb or dedication.

EDCS-09202611.translation: For the eternal memory of Mitius.
EDCS-09202611.summary: This inscription is a brief dedication to Mitius for eternal remembrance.

EDCS-09300337.translation: Marcus Sextilius Secius erected [this] for his excellent mother, Dometia Marcellina.
EDCS-09300337.summary: Marcus Sextilius Secius dedicated this monument to his mother, Dometia Marcellina.

EDCS-09300338.translation: To Apollo. Pamphorus, [serving as] administrator for our Faustina.
EDCS-09300338.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the god Apollo by Pamphorus, who was an administrator for a woman named Faustina.

EDCS-09300339.translation: Lucius Carulus, son of Lucius, [of the] Menenia [tribe].
EDCS-09300339.summary: This is a formal dedication or tomb inscription identifying Lucius Carulus, son of Lucius, and his tribal affiliation.

EDCS-09300340.summary: This is a simple inscription identifying Gaius Utius, son of Gaius, likely for a tomb or property marker.

EDCS-09300341.translation: Metrodorus, freedman of Marcus Nonius Marcellus, priest of Ceres, aged 88, lived piously for 88 years; he is buried here.
EDCS-09300341.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Metrodorus, a priest of Ceres, giving his age and lifespan.

EDCS-09300342.translation: Lucius Valerius, freedman of Augusta, from the records office.
EDCS-09300342.summary: This is a brief funerary epitaph identifying Lucius Valerius by his status and former occupation.

EDCS-09300343.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely a name in a funerary context.

EDCS-09300345.summary: This is an incomplete inscription, likely the beginning of a name.

EDCS-09300346.summary: This is a brief inscription, likely a name in a funerary context.

EDCS-09300347.translation: To the departed spirits, for the eternal memory of Marciana, his most pious wife. Paulus Derius, a good husband, erected this tomb and gave this sepulchre.
EDCS-09300347.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Paulus Derius to his wife Marciana, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-09300349.translation: Tertia Doia, daughter of Caius, took care to have this made for her father Lucius Doius, son of Lucius, of the tribe Tromentina; her mother Pa[---] Arrecina, daughter of Publius, Sedata; and for Decimus Arrecinus, son of Publius, of the tribe Papiria, and Vindicius.
EDCS-09300349.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Tertia Doia for her father, mother, and other relatives, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09300354.translation: [At the] third day before the Kalends of September, under the consulship of Felix, a most distinguished man.
EDCS-09300354.summary: This is a dating clause referring to a specific date and a consul, likely from the later Roman Empire.

EDCS-09300355.translation: Quintius, son of Solius, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mercury.
EDCS-09300355.summary: This is a votive inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow to the god Mercury.

EDCS-09300358.translation: Titus Maternius Valerianus, of Materni Mari.
EDCS-09300358.summary: This is a brief inscription identifying Titus Maternius Valerianus, possibly indicating his family or origin.

EDCS-09300361.summary: This is a dedication by Sextus Coelius Sigerus to Quintilla, likely a funerary monument.

EDCS-09300362.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Valerianus, freedman of Potitus, to his son.
EDCS-09300362.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Valerianus, freedman of Potitus, to his son.

EDCS-09300365.translation: To Lucius, son of Lucius, surnamed Veteranus.
EDCS-09300365.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Lucius, son of Lucius, surnamed Veteranus.

EDCS-09300367.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Caius Petronicus Iunior, son of Caius, of the Voltinia tribe, decurion of the Albenses, a young man of integrity, patron of the six-member collegium and the clothworkers. Petronius Barbarus and Nice, his parents.
EDCS-09300367.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Petronius Barbarus and Nice to their son, Caius Petronicus Iunior, who held various civic and collegial offices, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-09300368.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Caius Maximius Marius to his brother, Caius Maximus Marianus.
EDCS-09300368.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Caius Maximius Marius to his brother, Caius Maximus Marianus.

EDCS-09300369.translation: To the spirits of the departed. The mother to her most dutiful son, Pardulus.
EDCS-09300369.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a mother to her dutiful son, Pardulus.

EDCS-09300370.translation: Pennelus asks the advocates for victory, that he may prevail and be exiled.
EDCS-09300370.summary: This inscription records a plea for victory to advocates, possibly related to a legal or military dispute, with a paradoxical request for exile.

EDCS-09300371.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Naeviae Aprhodisiae sic vixit annisa amicae optimae\n
EDCS-09300371.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. To Naevia Aphrodisia, his most excellent friend, who lived [this many] years.
EDCS-09300371.summary: A funerary dedication for Naevia Aphrodisia, described as a 'most excellent friend', likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09300372.text_edition: \n Paula sive Eustathia qui vixit fidelis annum unum et mensis septem et dies XXII\n
EDCS-09300372.translation: Paula or Eustathia, who lived faithfully for one year, seven months, and twenty-two days.
EDCS-09300372.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Paula or Eustathia, dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-09300373.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Telesphorus to his most deserving fellow slave, Novellus.
EDCS-09300373.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Telesphorus to his fellow slave, Novellus.

EDCS-09300374.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Severa, wife, to Lucius Julius Isidorus.
EDCS-09300374.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Severa to her husband, Lucius Julius Isidorus.

EDCS-09300375.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Titia Severa, sister, and Titus Valerius Macedo, son, to Titus Valerius Senilis.
EDCS-09300375.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Titia Severa and Titus Valerius Macedo to Titus Valerius Senilis.

EDCS-09301095.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Titus Flavius Parmenigeus
EDCS-09301095.summary: Funerary dedication to Titus Flavius Parmenigeus.

EDCS-09301096.translation: To the most noble Caesar Flavius Claudius Constantine the Younger, son of the Emperor Flavius Valerius Constantinus the Pious, Fortunate, Unconquered Augustus.
EDCS-09301096.summary: An honorific inscription likely dedicated to Constantine I (the Great) or his son, Constantine II, during the 4th century CE.

EDCS-09301097.translation: Severus, son of Sution, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow for Severa, his daughter.
EDCS-09301097.summary: A votive inscription from Severus dedicating fulfillment of a vow for his daughter Severa.

EDCS-09301304.translation: Iulius I willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow; he willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-09301304.summary: A repetitive votive inscription where Iulius I declares fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-09301305.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Licinia Secundina, most dutiful daughter of Licinia Paterna.

EDCS-09301306.translation: Caius Pedullius Amerianus set this up while alive for his most dutiful brother Lucius Pedullius Valerianus and for himself.
EDCS-09301306.summary: A funerary monument set up by Caius Pedullius Amerianus for his brother and himself.

EDCS-09301307.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Zene Athenais set this up for her companion [contubernalis] Retillus out of regard for his devotion.
EDCS-09301307.summary: A funerary dedication from Zene Athenais to her companion Retillus.

EDCS-09301308.summary: A dedication to Terra Mater, likely part of a larger inscription.

EDCS-09301309.translation: For Aemilius, son of Titus, and for Antulla, parents, from Emilia, daughter, in accordance with the will.
EDCS-09301309.summary: A dedication by Emilia for her parents, executed according to a will.

EDCS-09301310.translation: Lucius Gratinius, while alive, made this for the spirits of the departed, for Grata, daughter of Boturo, for Lucia, daughter of Lucius Lotus, mother of Lucius Gratinius, and for Grata, daughter of Gratus, sister of Lucius Terentius Gratus.
EDCS-09301310.summary: A complex funerary inscription by Lucius Gratinius for multiple deceased family members, likely set up during his lifetime.

EDCS-09301311.translation: Spuria Cassia, daughter of Quintullus, placed this for her excellent husband Tullianus Paterni, and for herself while alive.
EDCS-09301311.summary: A tombstone set up by a wife for her husband and herself.

EDCS-09301312.translation: For Sextus Terentius Novellus and Sextia Bara, parents.

EDCS-09301313.translation: For Lucius Tissius and his wife Quartula.
EDCS-09301313.summary: A dedication to a husband and wife.

EDCS-09301315.summary: A votive dedication to the god Silvanus.

EDCS-09301316.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed, for Dubia, daughter of Regulus; to the Spirits of the Departed, for Vitlius Classi, freedman.
EDCS-09301316.summary: A tombstone for two individuals dedicated to the underworld deities.

EDCS-09301317.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed, for Messoris, son of Hortensius.
EDCS-09301317.summary: A tombstone for Messoris, son of Hortensius, dedicated to the underworld deities.

EDCS-09301318.translation: Cremius and Carinus placed this for their parents, Scontus, son of Domitius, and Sollonia, daughter of Avilius.
EDCS-09301318.summary: A tombstone set up by sons for their parents.

EDCS-09301319.translation: Seccia Secundina, daughter of Seccius, made this for herself while alive, to the Spirits of the Departed.
EDCS-09301319.summary: A tombstone prepared by a woman for herself, dedicated to the underworld deities.

EDCS-09301320.translation: For Senilius, son of Decumus, and his wife Materilla.
EDCS-09301320.summary: A dedication to a husband and wife.

EDCS-09301321.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed, for Quintus Cassius Secundus. Quintus Cassius Secundus and Quintus Cassius Tertullius placed this for their excellent father.
EDCS-09301321.summary: A tombstone set up by two sons for their father, dedicated to the underworld deities.

EDCS-09301322.translation: To the spirits of the dead. Titi Eburii's wife, Terentia Primula, from her own funds.
EDCS-09301322.summary: This funerary inscription records that Terentia Primula dedicated a monument to her deceased husband, Titius Eburius, using her own money.

EDCS-09301323.translation: To the spirits of the dead. His neighbours, Arandunicus and others, erected this.
EDCS-09301323.summary: This funerary inscription records that the neighbours of Titius Iulius Avitus erected this monument to him.

EDCS-09301324.translation: For himself and his wife, Lutonia.
EDCS-09301324.summary: This is a funerary inscription intended for the deceased and his wife, Lutonia.

EDCS-09301325.translation: To the spirits of the dead. The heirs of Marcia Titulla.
EDCS-09301325.summary: This funerary inscription records that the heirs of Marcia Titulla erected this monument.

EDCS-09301326.translation: For Marcus Octavius Messor of the Voltinian tribe.
EDCS-09301326.summary: This inscription likely records a dedication or memorial for Marcus Octavius Messor of the Voltinian tribe.

EDCS-09301327.translation: To the spirits of the dead. Maria Secundina, mother, had this funerary monument made from the burial fund.
EDCS-09301327.summary: This funerary inscription records that Maria Secundina, the mother, commissioned the construction of a burial monument for Marcus Quietus Severinus from the designated burial funds.

EDCS-09301328.translation: Qu(intus) ta Rutundus, Quintulus, Demogeta, Messina, Senicio, Messinus, willingly and deservedly paid their vow.
EDCS-09301328.summary: This inscription records a group of individuals, including Quintus Rutundus, Quintulus, Demogeta, Messina, Senicio, and Messinus, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-09301329.summary: This inscription records a dedication or memorial for Italia, who was a freedwoman of Nundina.

EDCS-09301330.translation: Nundina made this for Pompeia, her fellow slave.
EDCS-09301330.summary: This inscription records that Nundina dedicated this monument to her fellow slave, Pompeia.

EDCS-09301331.translation: To the spirits of the dead. Sabina, daughter of Tertius Vassetius Maximus, made this for herself and for her father, Tertius Vassetius, while alive.
EDCS-09301331.summary: This funerary inscription records that Sabina, daughter of Tertius Vassetius Maximus, erected this monument for herself and her father during their lifetimes.

EDCS-09301332.translation: To the departed spirits. Disenius Papianus to his patron Fortunatus, and Valerius Augurius.
EDCS-09301332.summary: Funerary dedication by Disenius Papianus and Valerius Augurius to their patron Fortunatus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301333.translation: To Mate, wife of Maelius and Sextus.
EDCS-09301333.summary: Dedication to Mate, wife of Maelius and Sextus, the context of which is unclear but likely funerary or dedicatory, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301334.translation: To Vattus and Carata, his wife.
EDCS-09301334.summary: Dedication to Vattus and his wife Carata, the purpose of which is unclear but possibly funerary, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301335.translation: To the departed spirits. Secundinus Nigidius Paternus, Iulia Paterna, and Iulia Severa placed this for their parents, Sextus Iulius Valerianus and Nigidia Servanda.
EDCS-09301335.summary: Funerary monument erected by children for their parents, Sextus Iulius Valerianus and Nigidia Servanda, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301337.translation: Gaius Statius Cantaber and Lucius Statius Novellus.
EDCS-09301337.summary: Names of two individuals, Gaius Statius Cantaber and Lucius Statius Novellus, likely representing a dedication or memorial, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301338.translation: Sacred to Mars Augustus. Gnaeus Pompeius Volens, son of Gnaeus, freely gave and dedicated this gift.
EDCS-09301338.summary: Religious dedication to Mars Augustus by Gnaeus Pompeius Volens, who offered the gift willingly, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301339.translation: To the departed spirits. Martia, a freedwoman of Flavia, placed this for herself while alive.
EDCS-09301339.summary: Funerary dedication made by a freedwoman named Martia for herself during her lifetime, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301340.summary: Dedication by Licinia to Jupiter and Augustus, possibly for religious or civic reasons, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301341.translation: To the god Silvanus, Aulus Annius Eros willingly paid his vow as deserved.
EDCS-09301341.summary: Religious offering to the god Silvanus by Aulus Annius Eros, who fulfilled a vow, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301342.translation: To the departed spirits. Quintula, mother, placed this for her dearest son, Quintus Lollins Quintinus.
EDCS-09301342.summary: Funerary monument erected by a mother, Quintula, for her beloved son, Quintus Lollins Quintinus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301343.translation: To the spirits of the dead; his freedmen erected [this monument] for Gaius Catius Maternus.
EDCS-09301343.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaius Catius Maternus, erected by his freedmen.

EDCS-09301344.translation: To the spirits of the dead; Marcus Caecilius Tincianus [erected this monument] for his mother, Tincia Maternus, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-09301344.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Tincia Maternus, erected by her son Marcus Caecilius Tincianus.

EDCS-09301345.translation: Quintus Maximius Secundinus [erected this monument] for his wife, Titulla, daughter of Titullus.
EDCS-09301345.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Titulla, erected by her husband Quintus Maximius Secundinus.

EDCS-09301346.translation: Titus Bitucius, Titus [son of Titus], and his wife Sulpicia Nigrina, [and their] clients.
EDCS-09301346.summary: This inscription likely records the patrons and clients of a household, possibly associated with a funerary monument.

EDCS-09301348.translation: To the spirits of the dead; Quintus Antonius Servatus and Domitia, daughter of Caius, [erected this monument] for their most devoted son, Quintus Labienus Porcianus.
EDCS-09301348.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Labienus Porcianus, erected by his parents Quintus Antonius Servatus and Domitia.

EDCS-09301349.translation: To the spirits of the dead; Tincia Servata, daughter of Julius, [erected this monument] for Gaius Tincius.
EDCS-09301349.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaius Tincius, erected by his daughter Tincia Servata.

EDCS-09301350.translation: Marcus Cornelius Fronto of the Voltinia tribe.
EDCS-09301350.summary: This inscription records the name and tribal affiliation of Marcus Cornelius Fronto, likely related to citizenship or identity.

EDCS-09301352.translation: Sacred to Isis; Coelius ordered it to be made in accordance with his will.
EDCS-09301352.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Isis, commissioned by Coelius through his will.

EDCS-09301353.translation: Attia Pacula fulfilled her vow to Minerva willingly and deservedly for herself and her family.
EDCS-09301353.summary: This is a votive inscription to Minerva by Attia Pacula, fulfilling a vow for herself and her family.

EDCS-09301356.translation: To the spirits of the dead; Cornelia, daughter of Lucius, placed [this monument] at her own expense for her father, Publius Anthius Logus, [who was in charge of] the sacred rites.
EDCS-09301356.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Publius Anthius Logus, erected by his daughter Cornelia.

EDCS-09301357.translation: Gnaeus Plaetorius Macrinus [provided this] for the colonists and inhabitants from that money which was collected for him for statues.
EDCS-09301357.summary: This is a dedication by Gnaeus Plaetorius Macrinus, likely in the Roman Imperial period, for the benefit of the local population using funds collected for statues.

EDCS-09301358.translation: Sextus Vetto and Caius Pedo, as aediles, saw to the repair of the road and lake, according to the decree of the decurions.
EDCS-09301358.summary: This inscription records the repair of a road and lake by the aediles Sextus Vetto and Caius Pedo, likely during the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-09301359.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Caius Vettius Eutyches, a priest of the six, ordered this to be made in his will while alive.
EDCS-09301359.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Caius Vettius Eutyches, likely from the Roman Imperial period, indicating he arranged for his own tomb in his will.

EDCS-09301360.translation: The place for the monument of Grata, freedwoman of Cnaeus Atettius, in front 25 feet, in the field 15 feet.
EDCS-09301360.summary: This is a property boundary marker for a burial plot belonging to Grata, a freedwoman, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301362.translation: To the spirits of the departed. From the will of the patroness, Cascellia Olympiades.
EDCS-09301362.summary: This is a funerary inscription, likely from the Roman Imperial period, indicating that Cascellia Olympiades was honored by her patroness's will.

EDCS-09301363.summary: This is a dedication, likely from the Roman Imperial period, to Sextus Cassius Exoratus.

EDCS-09301364.translation: To the wife of Decimus, Cornelia Digitus.
EDCS-09301364.summary: This is a dedication, likely from the Roman Imperial period, to Cornelia Digitus, the wife of Decimus.

EDCS-09301365.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Cornelius Helicon placed this for his excellent wife Cornelia Soteria and for himself while alive.
EDCS-09301365.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Lucius Cornelius Helicon for his wife Cornelia Soteria and himself, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301366.summary: This is a dedication, likely from the Roman Imperial period, to Musca, daughter of Escornb.

EDCS-09301367.translation: To Gaius Geminius Aper. Gaius Geminius Voltinia [dedicated this] to his father.
EDCS-09301367.summary: This is a dedication by Gaius Geminius Voltinia to his father, Gaius Geminius Aper, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301368.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Ombania Soszusa set up this monument for her excellent husband Lucius Julius Chrysio and for herself while alive.
EDCS-09301368.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a wife for her husband and herself.

EDCS-09301369.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely a name on a tomb or object.

EDCS-09301370.translation: Gaius Messius Sulla, freedman, made this for himself and his family while alive.
EDCS-09301370.summary: This funerary epitaph records a freedman who dedicated a monument for himself and his family.

EDCS-09301372.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Myr, a freedman of Varro.

EDCS-09301374.translation: To Gaius Ocratio Messori, son of Voltinia, daughter of Vossillus, and Marituma.
EDCS-09301374.summary: This is a dedication to several individuals, likely a family group, with complex naming conventions.

EDCS-09301375.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For Sextus Pompeius Germanus and Pusonia Euterpe, while alive for themselves.
EDCS-09301375.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a couple for themselves.

EDCS-09301376.translation: To Quintus Pompeius, from his wife Domitia.
EDCS-09301376.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by a wife to her husband.

EDCS-09301377.translation: Quarta, daughter of Masclus, made this for herself and for her husband Quartinus, son of Gratus, by her will.
EDCS-09301377.summary: This funerary epitaph was set up by a woman for herself, her husband, and son, according to her will.

EDCS-09301378.summary: This fragment records a dedication to Quintus Ferrinius, son.

EDCS-09301379.translation: To the Divine Spirits. His mother set this up for Saturninus, son of Maternos.
EDCS-09301379.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a mother for her son.

EDCS-09301380.summary: This is a funerary dedication from an unknown date, likely for a child or relative.

EDCS-09301381.summary: This is a funerary dedication from an unknown date.

EDCS-09301382.translation: Arius Sumptus of Vettius, a freedman, a soldier, willingly and deservedly (erected this).
EDCS-09301382.summary: This is a dedication, likely funerary, from an unknown date, possibly honoring Arius Sumptus.

EDCS-09301384.translation: Licinia Terentulla willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow to the native gods.
EDCS-09301384.summary: This is a votive inscription from an unknown date, recording a vow fulfilled by Licinia Terentulla.

EDCS-09301385.translation: Mediocratus Verus and Blaesidia (?) Extricata gave this from their own funds.
EDCS-09301385.summary: This is a dedication, likely of a monument or offering, by Mediocratus Verus and Blaesidia Extricata, with an indication that they funded it themselves, dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-09301386.translation: Lucius Coelius Rufus, his wife Iulia Severa, and his son Lucius Coelius Mangius willingly and deservedly fulfilled their vow to Divannus and the Martes.
EDCS-09301386.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow by Lucius Coelius Rufus, his wife Iulia Severa, and son Lucius Coelius Mangius to the deities Divannus and the Martes, dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-09301388.translation: Decimus Caecilius Optatus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mars.
EDCS-09301388.summary: This is a votive inscription, likely from the Imperial period, recording a vow fulfilled by Decimus Caecilius Optatus to the god Mars.

EDCS-09301389.translation: Marcus Cornelius Genialis vowed to his Mars.
EDCS-09301389.summary: This is a votive inscription from an unknown date, recording a vow made by Marcus Cornelius Genialis to the god Mars.

EDCS-09301390.translation: Publius Pomponius Pudens willingly and deservedly (fulfilled his vow) to his Mars.
EDCS-09301390.summary: This is a votive inscription from an unknown date, recording a vow fulfilled by Publius Pomponius Pudens to the god Mars.

EDCS-09301391.translation: Marcus Licinius Sabinus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Menmado.
EDCS-09301391.summary: This is a votive inscription from an unknown date, recording a vow fulfilled by Marcus Licinius Sabinus to the deity Menmado.

EDCS-09301393.translation: Caius Pequius Catlinus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Ricoria.
EDCS-09301393.summary: This is a votive inscription from an unknown date, recording a vow fulfilled by Caius Pequius Catlinus to the deity Ricoria.

EDCS-09301395.translation: The people of Baeterras dedicated this to Marcus Julius Philippus, most noble Caesar, prince of youth.
EDCS-09301395.summary: This is a dedication by the inhabitants of Baeterras to Marcus Julius Philippus, likely a young imperial prince, dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-09301399.translation: Titus Atius Vitalis, a soldier, placed this at his own expense for Attia Felicula, who deserved well of him, to the Divine Shades.
EDCS-09301399.summary: This is a funerary monument from an unknown date, erected by Titus Atius Vitalis for Attia Felicula.

EDCS-09301400.translation: To Gaius Cassius Primus, son of Publius, of the Pupinia tribe, twice chief magistrate, quaestor, honored with the ornaments of a flamen, prefect of the First Cohort of Raetians, tribune of a thousand-man cohort.
EDCS-09301400.summary: This is a career summary for Gaius Cassius Primus, a military and political official, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09301405.translation: To Atia Fausta, daughter of Lucius, priestess.
EDCS-09301405.summary: This inscription records Atia Fausta, a priestess, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09301406.translation: To Quintus Caecilius Homullus, son of Quintus, of the Pupinia tribe, quaestor, aedile, and twice duovir of the colony of Victrix Iulia Baeterra, […
EDCS-09301406.summary: This is a dedication to Quintus Caecilius Homullus, a prominent local official in the colony of Baeterras, dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-09301407.translation: To Gaius Coponius Gratus, holder of the office of Augustalis six times.
EDCS-09301407.summary: This inscription honors Gaius Coponius Gratus, a local official who held the Augustalis priesthood multiple times, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09301410.translation: To Sextus Domitius, holder of the office of Augustalis six times.
EDCS-09301410.summary: This inscription honors Sextus Domitius, a local official who held the Augustalis priesthood multiple times, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09301411.translation: To Flavia Quincta, freedwoman of the emperor. A plot was granted by decree of the decurions, by her freedmen.
EDCS-09301411.summary: This inscription records the granting of a burial plot by freedmen to Flavia Quincta, a freedwoman of the emperor, by order of the local council, dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-09301412.translation: Julia Celsa, daughter of Celsus, priestess of the public cult, was carried to her burial with a public funeral by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-09301412.summary: This inscription records the burial of Julia Celsa, a priestess, honored with a public funeral by local authorities, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09301413.translation: To the Augustalis priest Iulius Tertullus, son of Titus, and his daughter Procula, of the Decian tribe; their heirs, from the will.
EDCS-09301413.summary: This inscription records dedication to Iulius Tertullus and his daughter Procula, both holding the Augustalis priesthood, with their heirs acting as dedicator, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09301414.translation: Quintus Lutatius Narcissus, freedman of Celsus, holder of the office of Augustalis six times, made this monument for himself.
EDCS-09301414.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Quintus Lutatius Narcissus, a freedman and local official, for himself, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09301416.translation: Portico and wall, by Tertius, son of Quintus.
EDCS-09301416.summary: This inscription records the construction of a portico and wall by Tertius, son of Quintus, likely a private benefactor from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09301417.translation: To Tullia Avia, daughter of Quintus, priestess of Julia Augusta.
EDCS-09301417.summary: This inscription dedicates a monument to Tullia Avia, daughter of Quintus, who served as a priestess for the cult of Julia Augusta, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09301422.translation: To Aurelius Saturio, from the record office of the province, of Mauretania, Narbonensis, Syria, and Palaestina. Mummia Lucia with her children made this for her most beloved husband, with whom she lived for 33 years.
EDCS-09301422.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Mummia Lucia and her children to her husband Aurelius Saturio, a provincial official, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09301424.translation: Raecia Tertia, freedwoman of Sextus, from Claterna, 12 feet in the front and 12 feet in depth.
EDCS-09301424.summary: This inscription records a land measurement, likely for a property boundary or a burial plot, specifying dimensions in feet.

EDCS-09301425.translation: To the Divine Shades. Aemilius Felicissimus and Aemilia Felicissima [erected this] for their most deserving patroness, Aemilia Parda.
EDCS-09301425.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up by freedmen for their beloved patroness, Aemilia Parda.

EDCS-09301426.translation: Quintus Ancharius Primus, freedman of Mundus, for himself and for his sister Ancharia Mundana, freedwoman of Quintus; for Quintus Ancharius Primulus, freedman of Quintus; and for Ancharia Prisca, freedwoman of Quintus.
EDCS-09301426.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the allocation of burial plots by Quintus Ancharius Primus for himself, his sister, and other relatives, all of whom were freedmen or freedwomen, dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-09301428.translation: To the Divine Shades. Annia Aprulla, mother, [erected this] for her most dutiful daughter, Annia Memphia; Lucius Petronius Tychicus set it up at his own expense.
EDCS-09301428.summary: This is a funerary dedication from a mother for her daughter, with a further contribution from Lucius Petronius Tychicus.

EDCS-09301429.summary: This very brief inscription likely refers to a person named Salvius Anto, perhaps indicating a second individual with that name or a second mention.

EDCS-09301430.translation: To Atilius Hed, Atilia Amer, to Hecata.
EDCS-09301430.summary: This inscription lists names, possibly of dedicants or individuals associated with a cult, including a dedication to the goddess Hecate.

EDCS-09301431.translation: Gaius Caninius Faustus, son of Gaius, freedman of Sextus Caninius.
EDCS-09301431.summary: This is a funerary or commemorative epitaph identifying a freedman, Gaius Caninius Faustus, and his patron.

EDCS-09301433.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. ...lius Coelius Quintio ... his daughter Vera made this.
EDCS-09301433.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, likely set up by Vera for her father Coelius Quintio, dedicated to the underworld deities, dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-09301434.translation: To Gaius Coponius Felix, to Gaius Coponius Antho.
EDCS-09301434.summary: This inscription records a dedication or memorial to two individuals named Gaius Coponius Felix and Gaius Coponius Antho.

EDCS-09301435.translation: Gaius Cornelius Fuscus and Valeria Severa made [this] while alive.
EDCS-09301435.summary: This inscription records that Gaius Cornelius Fuscus and Valeria Severa commissioned their own monument during their lifetime.

EDCS-09301436.translation: They ordered that [this monument] be made from their will for themselves, for Cornelia Quinta, his wife, and for their son Lucius Ofillius Successus.
EDCS-09301436.summary: This inscription indicates a funerary monument was to be erected according to a will for the testators, their wife, and their son.

EDCS-09301437.translation: Under the supervision of Invita, freedwoman of Cornelia.
EDCS-09301437.summary: This inscription notes the supervision of the construction or placement of a monument by a freedwoman named Invita.

EDCS-09301438.translation: Cornelia for herself and for her husband Publius Umidius and for her son Publius Umidius.
EDCS-09301438.summary: This epitaph records Cornelia dedicating a tomb for herself and her family members, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301439.translation: Viva made this for Domitia Rodope in the field, 15 feet.
EDCS-09301439.summary: This funerary inscription records Viva dedicating a plot of land measuring 15 feet to Domitia Rodope, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301440.translation: To the departed spirits. Publius Vibius Basileus placed this for Ennia Pelagia, most deserving.
EDCS-09301440.summary: This tombstone records Publius Vibius Basileus dedicating a monument to Ennia Pelagia, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301441.translation: By the authority of Erotis, freedman of Decimus, and of Murranus, freedman.
EDCS-09301441.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely refers to the administration or division of property overseen by two freedmen, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301444.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely an epitaph or a name on a monument, belonging to Gaius Herennius, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301445.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Iulia Eutychia, a most distinguished woman. She [made this] for herself.
EDCS-09301445.summary: This is a self-funded funerary epitaph for Iulia Eutychia, a distinguished woman, dedicated to the underworld deities, dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-09301446.summary: This inscription likely refers to an heir's claim or dedication related to Laurentius Celtus, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301447.translation: To the departed spirits. Ennia Iulia, her alumna, for the deserving Licinia Montana.
EDCS-09301447.summary: This funerary inscription records Ennia Iulia dedicating a monument to her alumna, Licinia Montana, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301448.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Maecius Alexander made this for his dearest wife, Maecia Vera, and for himself while alive.
EDCS-09301448.summary: A funerary monument set up by a husband for his wife and himself, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-09301449.summary: This fragmentary inscription records Nigenia and Domitina setting up a monument, likely funerary, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301450.translation: Publius Pollius Primus, freedman of Silonis, for Publius Pollio, freedman of Publius, son of Silonis, his patron; for Publius Pollio, freedman of Silonis; for Primus, for Attia Faustae, his wife.
EDCS-09301450.summary: This complex funerary inscription records the burial arrangements and dedications by Publius Pollius Primus for himself, his wife, and other family members within the Pollia gens, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301451.translation: Lives Gaius Pompeius Anterus, freedman of Caius.
EDCS-09301451.summary: This inscription records the survival or commemoration of Gaius Pompeius Anterus, freedman of Caius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301454.translation: Rus, son of Silvinus, [erected this] for himself and his family.
EDCS-09301454.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Rus, son of Silvinus, indicating it was dedicated for himself and his family.

EDCS-09301456.translation: To the Divine Manes, for Valeria Chrysis, his most dutiful daughter, Panthera.
EDCS-09301456.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Valeria Chrysis by Panthera.

EDCS-09301457.translation: Vesius Modestus, son of Caius, [erected this] for Vesia Placidia, freedwoman of Titus Cassius, his partner.
EDCS-09301457.summary: This is a funerary inscription erected by Vesius Modestus for his partner Vesia Placidia.

EDCS-09301476.translation: Othia, a presbyter, in the 33rd year of his priesthood, built and dedicated the basilica from her vow in honor of the holy martyrs Vincent, Agnes, and Eulalia, when Valentinianus and Avienus were consuls.
EDCS-09301476.summary: This inscription records the construction and dedication of a basilica by Othia, a presbyter, in honor of martyrs, dated to the consulship of Valentinianus and Avienus.

EDCS-09301477.translation: Here rests in peace the well-remembered Leodais, who lived about 35 years, died on the Kalends of August, in the 15th indiction, in the 14th year of the reign of our lord King Leovild.
EDCS-09301477.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Leodais, recording his lifespan and death date within the reign of King Leovild.

EDCS-09301481.translation: Gnaeus Pompeius Hyla, freedman of Gnaeus, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Hercules Ilunno Andose; he made the statue of the Unconquered Hercules, made of silver, weighing 12 pounds, from his own money.
EDCS-09301481.summary: This inscription records Gnaeus Pompeius Hyla fulfilling a vow by dedicating a silver statue of Hercules.

EDCS-09301482.translation: Sacred to Juno. For Appeae Cila, freedwoman of Sextus.
EDCS-09301482.summary: A religious dedication to Juno, likely a private offering, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301484.translation: To the August Lares, from a vow: Lucius Cornelius Senex, Lucius Cornelius Caprarius, Lucius Caesellius Phoebus.
EDCS-09301484.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the August Lares made by Lucius Cornelius Senex, Lucius Cornelius Caprarius, and Lucius Caesellius Phoebus, likely from a vow.

EDCS-09301485.translation: Caius Salius Ste, a sevir and magistrate and viator, restored [this] for the Lares from his own funds.
EDCS-09301485.summary: This inscription records Caius Salius Ste, a sevir and official, restoring something for the Lares at his own expense.

EDCS-09301487.translation: For the Mother of the Gods. The taurobolium, which Axia, daughter of Caius, Paulina, priestess, performed, dedicated by Quintus Paquius Chrestus.
EDCS-09301487.summary: A record of a taurobolium ritual performed for the Magna Mater, involving a priestess and a dedicant, possibly from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-09301488.translation: Under the rule of the Mother of the Gods, a bull sacrifice from the province of Narbonensis, performed by Gaius Battonius Primus, flamen of the Augusti, for the safety of the lords Emperors Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus and Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus [.
EDCS-09301488.summary: This inscription records a taurobolium (bull sacrifice) performed by the flamen Gaius Battonius Primus for the safety of Emperors Septimius Severus and Caracalla in the province of Narbonensis.

EDCS-09301489.translation: [dedicated by] Iunia Balbina to Lucius Junius Domnus, by decree of Marcus Nummius Albinus Fulvius Maximus, consuls.
EDCS-09301489.summary: This fragmented inscription likely records a dedication by Iunia Balbina to Lucius Junius Domnus, dated to the consulship of Marcus Nummius Albinus Fulvius Maximus.

EDCS-09301490.translation: For the Mother of the Gods. Liguria Thymele received the taurobolium by decree and set up the altar (?) for the rites.
EDCS-09301490.summary: A dedication to the Mother of the Gods recording the reception of a taurobolium and the erection of an altar, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301497.translation: For Apollo Augustus and the Divine Spirits of the Emperors. Sacred. Iulia Natalis arranged for the addition of a tetrastyle and all the bronze fittings at her own expense and dedicated them herself. The site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-09301497.summary: A public works dedication by Iulia Natalis for Apollo and the Imperial numina, including architectural additions, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09301500.translation: Titus Domitius Romulus dedicated a vow to Imperial Peace, because he received his freedman Phoebus.
EDCS-09301500.summary: This inscription records a private vow dedicated to Imperial Peace by Titus Domitius Romulus.

EDCS-09301503.translation: Quintus Vibius Maximus, son of Quintus, and Marcus Varius Capito, son of Lucius, as Praetors and Duovirs, supervised the construction of an altar to Vulcan, a surrounding wall, and a pool, to be built from public funds, as decreed by the decurions; Quintus Vibius Maximus, son of Quintus, approved it.
EDCS-09301503.summary: This is a public works inscription recording the construction of an altar, wall, and pool by two magistrates, Quintus Vibius Maximus and Marcus Varius Capito, in an unspecified location.

EDCS-09301504.translation: Modestus, son of Lucius, of the Papirian tribe, [dedicated this].
EDCS-09301504.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription recording the dedication by Modestus, son of Lucius.

EDCS-09301506.translation: For the Emperor Caesar Nerva Trajan Augustus Germanicus, son of the deified Nerva, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power, consul for the second time. Quintus S...ilius S...anus, member of the IIII viri Augustales, ordered this to be made and set up from his modest means. At the urn of power (?).
EDCS-09301506.summary: A dedication to Emperor Trajan by a local magistrate (IIII vir Augustalis), likely from the early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09301509.translation: For the Emperor Caesar Lucius Aurelius Verus Augustus, son of the deified Antoninus Pius, grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus, great-great-grandson of the deified Nerva, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the fourth time, imperator for the second time, consul for the second time, proconsul. The decumani of Narbonne.
EDCS-09301509.summary: An official dedication to Emperor Lucius Verus, likely from the 160s CE, by the public officials (decumani) of Narbonne.

EDCS-09301510.translation: For Iulia Domna Augusta, wife of Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus, father of the fatherland, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the fourth time, imperator for the eighth time, consul for the second time, and for Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Caesar, mother of the Emperor and also of the camps. The decumani of Narbonne.
EDCS-09301510.summary: A dedication to Julia Domna and the imperial family by the decumani of Narbonne, likely from the period 202-211 CE.

EDCS-09301512.translation: For the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Pius Felix, Arabicus, Adiabenicus, Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, Germanicus Maximus, father of the fatherland. The people of Narbonne.
EDCS-09301512.summary: A public dedication to Emperor Marcus Aurelius, likely from the late 170s or early 180s CE, by the citizens of Narbonne.

EDCS-09301519.translation: Lucius Aemilius Moschus, IIII vir Augustalis, dedicated this for his most excellent patron, Lucius Aemilius Arcanus, son of Lucius, of the Papiria tribe, tribune of the soldiers of the XI Gemina legion and tribune of the soldiers of the I Minervia legion, also tribune of the soldiers of the II Augusta legion, who had held all the magistracies in his own colony, was admitted into the most distinguished order by the Emperor Caesar Hadrian Augustus, served as a IIII vir of Roman knights, pontifex, urban quaestor, tribune of the plebs, and praetor designate. After his death, Lucius Aemilius Moschus, IIII vir Augustalis, contributed 4,000 sesterces from the treasury of the sevirate for the place and protection of the statue. The site was granted by decree of the IIII viri, and with the sportula.
EDCS-09301519.summary: A funerary monument and statue base erected by a freedman patron (Lucius Aemilius Moschus) for his deceased patron (Lucius Aemilius Arcanus), a distinguished local official, likely from the Hadrianic period.

EDCS-09301521.translation: To himself, the living veteran Quintus Asellius Montanus.
EDCS-09301521.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Quintus Asellius Montanus, a veteran, dedicating it to himself.

EDCS-09301522.translation: To Lucius Aufidius Vinicianus Epagatinus, son of Lucius, of the Aemilian tribe, prefect of the engineers, twice tribune of the soldiers, twice aedile for five years, and to Nice, his freedwoman wife, of Fundi and Olia.
EDCS-09301522.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Aufidius Vinicianus Epagatinus, a military and civic official, and his wife Nice.

EDCS-09301523.translation: To the living Lucius Baebius Niger, son of Lucius, of the Papirian tribe, prefect of the engineers; the living Lucius Baebius Auctus, his freedman.
EDCS-09301523.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Lucius Baebius Niger and his freedman Lucius Baebius Auctus.

EDCS-09301524.translation: Papiria Caesius, brother, lives [after] 24 years of service.
EDCS-09301524.summary: This inscription records that Papiria Caesius, identified as 'brother', lived through 24 years of military service.

EDCS-09301526.translation: Titus Cornelius, son of Publius, a soldier of the Parmian legion, lives.
EDCS-09301526.summary: This is a brief inscription stating that Titus Cornelius, a soldier in the Parmian legion, is alive.

EDCS-09301527.translation: Marcus Fulvius Italus Cordus, son of Marcus, tribune of the soldiers.
EDCS-09301527.summary: This inscription identifies Marcus Fulvius Italus Cordus as a son of Marcus and a military tribune.

EDCS-09301528.translation: To Gallo, former aedile and curator of grain(?), to Caesar(?), prefect of the engineers, and to his brother Senicio, aedile and curator of grain(?), to his sister Messia, daughter of Marcus, Quartae, of the Voltinian tribe.
EDCS-09301528.summary: This inscription, likely a funerary monument, lists several individuals holding various magistracies and family relationships.

EDCS-09301529.translation: To Marcus Maecius Oceanus, son of Marcus, freedman of Numisia. To Gaius Maecius Ingenuus, equestrian of the X Gemina legion. To Quintus Pompeius Philotaerus, deceased. To Valeria Severa, daughter of Lucius, alive.
EDCS-09301529.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring multiple individuals, including a soldier and freedmen, with some deceased and some alive.

EDCS-09301530.translation: Marcus Marcius Rufus, son of [3], standard-bearer of the IIII Macedonica legion, for his share, for himself and his family, and for his fellow soldier Antistius [3], son of [3], of the Galerian tribe, Paternus, 15 feet in front and 15 feet in depth.
EDCS-09301530.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a standard-bearer of the IIII Macedonica legion, dedicating a plot of land for himself, his family, and a fellow soldier.

EDCS-09301532.translation: To Aulus Rubrius Priscus, son of [3], of the Pollian tribe, a veteran.
EDCS-09301532.summary: This is a dedication to Aulus Rubrius Priscus, a veteran of the Pollian tribe.

EDCS-09301533.translation: To Quintus Septimius [3] and the standard-bearer of the IIII Macedonica legion, from Forum Julii, and to Hortensia Montana, wife.
EDCS-09301533.summary: This inscription dedicates a plot of land or monument to Quintus Septimius and a standard-bearer of the IIII Macedonica legion from Forum Julii, and to his wife Hortensia Montana.

EDCS-09301534.translation: By the authority of Lucius Tre[---], a standard-bearer.
EDCS-09301534.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription indicating an action taken by the authority of Lucius Tre[---], a military officer.

EDCS-09301535.translation: While alive, Valerius Titullus, son of Titus, of the Fabia tribe, from Gabales, a veteran.
EDCS-09301535.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Valerius Titullus, a veteran from Gabales, set up by himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-09301536.text_edition: \n duomvir quinquennalis duomvir iterum praefectus pro duoviro augur tribunus militum primipilus praefectus navium ex conlegio Honoris et Virtutis arbitratu Zenonis liberti\n
EDCS-09301536.translation: Duovir for five years, duovir for a second term, prefect, acting duovir, augur, military tribune, primipilus, prefect of the ships, from the college of Honor and Virtue, by the judgment of Zeno, freedman.
EDCS-09301536.summary: This inscription lists the extensive career and honors of an individual, likely a magistrate, and mentions a college and a freedman named Zeno.

EDCS-09301539.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription recording a personal name, Aemilius, and a mention of omen, likely from a tombstone or a dedication.

EDCS-09301540.translation: While alive, to Lucius Aemilius Philomusus, a seviro Augustale.
EDCS-09301540.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Aemilius Philomusus, a member of the seviri Augustales, set up by himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-09301541.translation: Lucius Afranius Cerialis, freedman of Eros, one of the six Augustal priests, from Tarraco, hospitable, from Gallo, a chicken-butcher. Afrania Cerialis, freedwoman of Procilla, his wife. Uranie, freedwoman of Afrania, his daughter, aged 11, is placed here.
EDCS-09301541.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Lucius Afranius Cerialis, a freedman of a freedman, along with his wife and daughter, and mentions his origin and profession.

EDCS-09301542.translation: Quintus Akanius Rufus, son of Quintus, of the Teretina tribe, dictator in Iuniliciis.
EDCS-09301542.summary: This inscription records Quintus Akanius Rufus, a local magistrate (dictator) in the settlement of Iuniliciis, identified by his tribe and father.

EDCS-09301544.translation: To Gaius Allius, son of Lucius [3], husband of N[3], [set up] by his wife [3] in Narbo Martius [3].
EDCS-09301544.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaius Allius, dedicated by his wife and likely from Narbo Martius.

EDCS-09301545.translation: Numerius Annius Eugenius, freedman of Niger, a sevir Augustalis.
EDCS-09301545.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription recording Numerius Annius Eugenius, a freedman and a member of the collegium of sevir Augustalis.

EDCS-09301546.translation: Deceased. To Gaius Annius Proculus, son of Gaius [3], a duovir Augustalis, 15 feet in the field.
EDCS-09301546.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaius Annius Proculus, a duovir Augustalis, recording a plot of land.

EDCS-09301547.translation: To Lucius Aponius Homullus, one of the six Augustal priests; to Aponia Nephela, his wife; to Aponia Faustae, his freedwoman.
EDCS-09301547.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription honoring Lucius Aponius Homullus, a prominent local official, and members of his household.

EDCS-09301548.translation: To Athenion Olympianus, a sevir Augustalis.
EDCS-09301548.summary: This inscription records the name of Athenion Olympianus, who held the position of sevir Augustalis, likely a dedication or funerary marker.

EDCS-09301549.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely names a sevirus Augustalis, a prominent freedman official in Roman towns, and his patron or a co-official, with the date and specific context lost.

EDCS-09301551.translation: Marcus Caesius, son of Titus, aedile.
EDCS-09301551.summary: This inscription records Marcus Caesius, son of Titus, who served as an aedile, a local magistrate responsible for public buildings and games.

EDCS-09301553.translation: Titus Cominius, son of Caius, of the Pollia tribe, duovir, aedile, interrex.
EDCS-09301553.summary: This inscription records Titus Cominius, son of Caius, who held multiple high magistracies (duovir, aedile, interrex) in his community.

EDCS-09301554.translation: To Communi's freedman Cinnamus, (a) sevirus Augustalis of the colony Narbo Martius. To Priscia his wife, Concessa, Priscia, Priscus. This monument will not pass to his heir, nor to the heir of his heir.
EDCS-09301554.summary: This is a funerary epitaph in Narbo Martius, setting up a tomb for Communi's freedman Cinnamus, his wife Priscia, and others, with a stipulation that the monument is not inheritable.

EDCS-09301555.translation: To Sextus Fadius Papirius Secundus Musa, who held all offices in the colony Narbo. Curator of the new temple of Augustus in Narbo Martius. The sub-aediani (artisans working under the aedes) of Narbonenses, to their patron, for his merits. The place was granted by decree of the decurions. The exemplar of an epistula of Sextus Fadius Papirius Secundi Musae in the words written below. Fadius Secundus to the college of Narbonensian artisans, greetings. Although it is difficult to repay your many and constant merits towards me, I know that it will be most pleasing to your affection, provided that I donate sixteen million sesterces among children and the most distinguished grandson Iucundus on the Kalends of May, the first day of my birthday, to your chest, and on that day I will pay the interest of the entire year at eight asses per person, so that my gift may be even more welcome. Henceforth I ask of your devotion that you divide the interest of this sum on that day in the most honorable dress among those present and feasting, forever, and that this sum be not converted to any other use, since I both provide for this with this letter and will provide for it in my subsequent tablets, so that if the condition written above is changed or omitted, that money may belong to [---] or if they delay in demanding the money, to the treasury of the greatest prince. If you approve of this my will, and your assent, I most earnestly ask that you inscribe it on bronze tablets and display it before the temple of Augustus (?) and write it on the left side of the statue which you have erected for me, so that there may be more certain proof of future observance in my desire. Then it was noted by the hand of Fadius Secundus. I have written this by mandate on the Kalends of October, when Orfitus and Priscus were consuls. You will keep the letter as a completed instrument. I wish you to be well, my best and dearest masters. For the purpose of the perpetual preservation and celebration of this liberality, the subaediani artisans of Narbo have decreed that the exemplar, compared with the bronze tablet, be placed in a most frequented place before the temple.
EDCS-09301555.summary: This lengthy inscription from Narbo Martius details a substantial endowment by Sextus Fadius Secundus Musa, a former official, to the college of local artisans, providing for an annual feast and distribution of interest, with instructions for its perpetual observance and inscription on public records.

EDCS-09301556.translation: To Titus Fadius Masclus, freedman of Titus, one of the six Augustal priests; to Fadia Mascellina, daughter of Titus; to Titus Fadius Vegetus, freedman of Titus, a sevir Augustalis; to Titus Fadius Verecundus, freedman of Titus.
EDCS-09301556.summary: This inscription honors multiple members of the Fadius family, including freedmen who served as Augustales and possibly their relatives.

EDCS-09301557.inscription_type: tituli honorarii, tituli operum, tituli sacri
EDCS-09301557.translation: To Sex(tus) Fadius Secundus Musa, of the Papiria tribe, who has fulfilled all offices in the colony of Narbo, perhaps first curator of the new Temple of Augustus in Narbo Martius, the subaedial craftsmen of Narbo dedicated this space to their patron by decree of the decurions for his merits. Exemplary letter of Sex(tus) Fadius Secundus Musa to the guild of craftsmen of Narbo: "Fadius Secundus to the guild of craftsmen of Narbo, greetings. Although it is difficult to repay your many and constant services to me, I know what will be most welcome to your affection: I will deposit 16,000 sesterces in your treasury on the Kalends of May, my birthday, and on that day I will pay the interest for the entire year at eight asses, so that my gift may be even more pleasing. Furthermore, I ask of your piety that you divide the interest of this sum annually on that day, in the most honorable attire among those present and feasting, and that this sum be converted to no other use, since I am providing for this in this letter and will provide for it in my will, so that if the condition written above is changed or omitted, that money shall pertain to the treasury of the most excellent prince, or if they delay in requesting the money, to the treasury of the most excellent prince. If you approve of this my will and your consent, I most urgently request that you inscribe it on bronze tablets and display it before the Temple of Augustus and write it on the left side of the base of the statue which you have erected for me, so that there may be proof of future observance in my desire. Then it was noted by the hand of Fadius Secundus. Written by mandate, I have written this on the Kalends of October, with Orfitus and Priscus as consuls. You will keep the letter as a complete instrument. I wish you to be well, my best and dearest masters. For the sake of the perpetual preservation and celebration of this generosity, the subaedial craftsmen of Narbo have resolved that a copy, compared with the bronze tablet, should be placed before the temple in a very public place."
EDCS-09301557.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription followed by a letter from a patron to the guild of craftsmen of Narbo, detailing a bequest of 16,000 sesterces for an annual feast and specifying the inscription of his will on bronze tablets.

EDCS-09301558.translation: Fannia Celsina, freedwoman of Titus, for herself and for Gaius Trebonius Abundus, her husband, a sevirus Augustalis of Narbo Martius.
EDCS-09301558.summary: This is a funerary epitaph from Narbo Martius for Fannia Celsina and her husband Gaius Trebonius Abundus, who was a sevirus Augustalis.

EDCS-09301559.translation: To Quintus Fullonius Tolosanus, a sevirus Augustalis. By Caecilia Tertuliana, daughter of Lucius, his wife.
EDCS-09301559.summary: This is a funerary epitaph from Narbo Martius for Quintus Fullonius Tolosanus, a sevirus Augustalis, dedicated by his wife Caecilia Tertuliana.

EDCS-09301560.translation: To Gaius Ignius, son of Caius, of the Papiria tribe, aedile, prefect acting as duovir, and duovir.
EDCS-09301560.summary: This inscription records Gaius Ignius, son of Caius, who served as an aedile and progressed to holding the office of duovir, a chief magistrate.

EDCS-09301561.translation: Licinia Pallas to her most excellent husband Quintus Julius Servandus, an Augustalis duovir, in the colony Iulia Paterna Claudia Narbo Martius; a thousand coins having been paid into the chest of the duovirs for the protection of the statue, the place was granted by decree of the duovirs.
EDCS-09301561.summary: This inscription records the granting of a plot of land by the duovirs of Narbo to Licinia Pallas in memory of her husband, an Augustalis duovir, in return for a payment made for the protection of a statue.

EDCS-09301562.translation: To the divine spirits. To Tiberius Iunius Eudoxus, shipowner of the sea, of the colony Narbo Martius. Tiberius Iunius Fadianus, a sevirus Augustalis of the colony Narbo Martius, and contractor of the ironworks on the right bank, for his most devoted brother.
EDCS-09301562.summary: This is a funerary epitaph from Narbo Martius for Tiberius Iunius Eudoxus, a maritime shipowner, dedicated by his brother Tiberius Iunius Fadianus, who was also a sevirus Augustalis and a contractor for ironworks.

EDCS-09301563.translation: To Frontina, daughter of Quintus and Liguria, wife of Quintus Hortensius Catullus; the order of Narbo publicly decreed funeral rites and all exemptions for her.
EDCS-09301563.summary: This inscription records a public funeral and exemptions decreed by the local government of Narbo for Frontina, wife of Quintus Hortensius Catullus.

EDCS-09301564.translation: Lucius Lorinus Felix, an Augustalis duovir, [erected this] while alive.
EDCS-09301564.summary: This is a dedication by Lucius Lorinus Felix, an Augustalis duovir, indicating he erected the monument during his lifetime.

EDCS-09301567.translation: [---] to Modestus, governor acting as duovir, while alive. To Modesta, his wife.
EDCS-09301567.summary: This inscription, though fragmentary, appears to honor a governor acting as a duovir and his wife, Modesta, in a Roman town, likely Narbo Martius given the context of other inscriptions.

EDCS-09301570.translation: By decree of the Augustalis duovirs, [this monument is dedicated] to Publius Olitius Apollonius, an Augustalis duovir and shipowner, of the colony Iulia Paterna Claudia Narbo Martius, for his merits and generosity; he used the honor decreed [to him] and remitted the expense, and erected a statue at his own cost.
EDCS-09301570.summary: This inscription honors Publius Olitius Apollonius, an Augustalis duovir and shipowner from Narbo, who was recognized for his merits and generosity by having a statue erected in his name after he waived certain expenses.

EDCS-09301571.translation: In the consulship of Sextus Papinius, Quintus Plautius, Gaius Vettius Rufus, Marcus Porcius Cato.
EDCS-09301571.summary: This inscription records the names of six consuls, likely marking a specific year or event, though the location and full context are lost.

EDCS-09301572.translation: To Gaius Pellius Agathodorus, Gaius Pellius Anthos, Gaius Pellius Silvanus, one of the six priests of the Augustales.
EDCS-09301572.summary: This inscription from Narbo Martius lists three individuals, with Gaius Pellius Silvanus identified as a sevirus Augustalis, likely serving as a dedication or funerary monument.

EDCS-09301573.translation: [This monument was erected] by will by ...us, son of Publius, of the Voltinian tribe, praetor of Aquae Sextiae, for himself and for his freedwoman wife, Philonica.
EDCS-09301573.summary: This is a funerary inscription stating that a man, identified by his tribe and praetorship in Aquae Sextiae, ordered the monument to be built in his will for himself and his freedwoman wife.

EDCS-09301574.translation: Marcus Pilius Diophantus, freedman of Marcus; Marcus Turpio, son of Marcus; Caius Pollio, son of Marcus, prefect; Pilia Andromaca, freedwoman of Marcus, mother.
EDCS-09301574.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, likely family members, including Marcus Pilius Diophantus, Marcus Turpio, Caius Pollio (a prefect), and Pilia Andromaca, all associated with a Marcus.
