EDCS-09301575.translation: Cnaeus Metellus Amandus, freedman of Cnaeus, ordered this to be set up by will to Metella Rufilla, daughter of Cnaeus, flaminica, and to Metella Rusticilla, daughter of Cnaeus, flaminica.
EDCS-09301575.summary: This inscription records that Cnaeus Metellus Amandus, a freedman, erected this monument by his will in honor of two women, Metella Rufilla and Metella Rusticilla, both flaminicae and daughters of a Cnaeus.

EDCS-09301576.translation: While alive, [this monument was erected] to Aulus Pompeius Festus, an Augustalis duovir, to Aulus Pompeius Alexi and his wife Pompeia, and to Pompeius [---]; 12 feet in front and 15 feet in the field.
EDCS-09301576.summary: This is a dedication, made during the lifetime of the honorees, to Aulus Pompeius Festus (Augustalis duovir), Aulus Pompeius Alexi, his wife Pompeia, and another Pompeius, and includes land dimensions.

EDCS-09301577.translation: While alive, [this monument was erected] to Aulus Pompeius Festus, an Augustalis duovir, to Aulus Pompeius Alexi and his wife Pompeia, and to Pompeius [---].
EDCS-09301577.summary: This inscription dedicates a monument, erected during their lifetime, to Aulus Pompeius Festus (an Augustalis duovir), Aulus Pompeius Alexi, his wife Pompeia, and another individual named Pompeius.

EDCS-09301578.translation: Chrysogonus, freedman of Caius Quadronius Fidelis, an Augustalis duovir, of the colony Iulia Paterna Claudia Narbo Martius, and of the colony Iulia Aquae Sextiae, made this; 15 feet in the field.
EDCS-09301578.summary: This inscription states that Chrysogonus, a freedman of Caius Quadronius Fidelis (an Augustalis duovir in both Narbo and Aquae Sextiae), dedicated this monument, including a measurement of land.

EDCS-09301580.translation: To Quintus Rammius Fronton, son of freedman Quintus, freedman of Quintus, *sevir* Augustalis, 15 feet in the field.
EDCS-09301580.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Rammius Fronton, noting his status as a freedman and *sevir* Augustalis.

EDCS-09301581.translation: To Rammia Stasia, freedwoman of Cn. Cn., his wife; to Publius Vinicius, son of Marcus, *aedile*, *praefect* for the *duumvirate*.
EDCS-09301581.summary: This inscription honors Rammia Stasia and Publius Vinicius, detailing their civic and administrative roles.

EDCS-09301582.translation: To Lucius Roscius Maximus, son of Lucius, decurion of the colony of Paterna, Claudia, of Narbo, Martius, the city publicly provided funeral rites and a burial place for him.
EDCS-09301582.summary: This inscription records the public burial of Lucius Roscius Maximus, a decurion of Narbo.

EDCS-09301583.translation: To Lucius Scanianius Atticus, patron, *sevir* Augustalis.
EDCS-09301583.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Scanianius Atticus, recognizing him as a patron and *sevir* Augustalis.

EDCS-09301585.translation: To Gaius Septimienus Nedymus, freedman of Sapula, freedman of Gaius, *sevir* Augustalis.
EDCS-09301585.summary: This inscription records Gaius Septimienus Nedymus, a freedman and *sevir* Augustalis.

EDCS-09301586.translation: Quintus Terentius Serenus, son of freedman Quintus, freedman of Quintus, *sevir* Augustalis of the colony Julia Patera Claudia Narbonensis Martius, alive, [erected this] to his most excellent and most devoted patron and to Octavia Valentina and her husband Titus Pompeius Firmus, and to their children Firmus and Pompeia Firmula, and to all their freedmen and freedwomen and their children and freedmen, and to himself and his family.
EDCS-09301586.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Quintus Terentius Serenus for his patron, family members, and himself, detailing his status as a *sevir* Augustalis in Narbonne.

EDCS-09301587.summary: This is a fragmented inscription mentioning Veiatius as an *aedile*.

EDCS-09301588.translation: To Lucius Vercio Priscus, *sevir* Augustalis of the colony Julia Patera Claudia Narbonensis Martius, and to the Baths of Sextis. Marcus Aurunceius, son of Marcus [---], to his most excellent friend.
EDCS-09301588.summary: This inscription dedicates a monument to Lucius Vercio Priscus, a *sevir* Augustalis, and also mentions the Baths of Sextis, with a dedication to a friend.

EDCS-09301589.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. To Publius Umidius Zoilus, *sevir* Augustalis of the corporate body in Narbonne. Pompeia Myrine to her most devoted husband.
EDCS-09301589.summary: This is a funerary inscription from Narbonne, dedicated by Pompeia Myrine to her husband, Publius Umidius Zoilus, a *sevir* Augustalis.

EDCS-09301611.translation: Cornelius Paetus, son of Publius, *lictore viator* of the colony Julia Patera Narbonensis Martius, 15 feet.
EDCS-09301611.summary: This inscription records Cornelius Paetus, identified as a *lictore viator* in Narbonne.

EDCS-09301612.translation: Gaius Manlius Rufus Umber, son of Gaius, of the Papirian tribe, made [this] for himself and his family from the *decuria* of *lictores viatores* which is in the colony Julia Patera Narbonensis Martius, with altars, to Gaius Cassius Clement, and to [---]sidia Restituta, his companion, and to Gaius Cassius Exoratus, his son, and to Gaius Cassius Viator, his freedman.
EDCS-09301612.summary: This is a funerary monument created by Gaius Manlius Rufus Umber for his family and associates, noting his membership in the *decuria* of *lictores viatores* in Narbonne.

EDCS-09301614.translation: To the Divine Shades. Geminia Chrsis lived 13 years. Geminius Chrestus and Chrysogonus, her co-freedmen, [parents].
EDCS-09301614.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Geminia Chrsis at age 13, set up by her co-freedmen.

EDCS-09301615.translation: Myrinus, slave of Faustus of the colony of Narbonensians, the deputy, is buried here. Boethus, his partner, [provided].
EDCS-09301615.summary: This tombstone records the burial of Myrinus, a slave and deputy in Narbo, with his partner Boethus mentioned.

EDCS-09301619.translation: Philomusus, freedman of Caius, a flask-maker. Frugi is buried here.
EDCS-09301619.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Philomusus, a freedman and flask-maker, and Frugi, likely his associate or family member, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09301620.translation: In his lifetime, Numerius Consius Dionysius, a ring-maker, for himself and for his deceased patron Numerius Consius Eronus. 15 feet in front.
EDCS-09301620.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Numerius Consius Dionysius, a freedman and ring-maker, for himself and his deceased patron, dating to the Imperial period and specifying the plot size.

EDCS-09301621.translation: Quintus Fuficius Eleuter, freedman of Quintus, son of Titus, and Philotis, freedwoman of [---], silver-workers, made from their own resources.
EDCS-09301621.summary: This is a dedication by two silver-workers, Quintus Fuficius Eleuter and Philotis, who may have been freedpersons, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09301622.translation: Philonicus, freedman of Quintus Numerius, the silversmith.
EDCS-09301622.summary: This is a simple epitaph identifying Philonicus, a freedman and silversmith.

EDCS-09301623.translation: to the silver-worker; to Turpa, freedwoman of Caius, daughter of [---].
EDCS-09301623.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription that likely records a dedication to a silver-worker and a freedwoman, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09301624.translation: May they live: Herophilus the [---]-maker, for himself and for Lendia Riccia, and for his son, and for the freedman Cassius Popilius. This monument will not pass to his heir, nor to his freedmen, nor to his descendants. 15 feet in every direction.
EDCS-09301624.summary: This is a funerary inscription intended to ensure the plot is not inherited by heirs, freedmen, or descendants, specifying its dimensions, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09301626.translation: To O., son of Caius, Papiria [made this?], the silversmith.
EDCS-09301626.summary: This inscription likely records a memorial for O., son of Caius, a silversmith, possibly dedicated by someone named Papiria.

EDCS-09301628.summary: This is a brief inscription identifying Lucius Cornelius Amandus as a goldsmith, likely from a tombstone or dedication, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09301629.translation: In his lifetime, Cornelius Castor, freedman of Caius, for himself and for the deceased Marcus Fonteius Acanthus, goldsmith, and for his companion Gluco, and for Chloe Valeria.
EDCS-09301629.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Cornelius Castor, a freedman and goldsmith, for himself and several others including his companion, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09301630.translation: May they live: Lucius Oppius Quietus, a bridle-maker, and Malia Cara, his companion for [3] years, live without quarreling.
EDCS-09301630.summary: This is an inscription expressing a wish for the peaceful coexistence of Lucius Oppius Quietus, a bridle-maker, and his companion Malia Cara, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09301631.translation: May they live: Lucius Cervius Zetus, freedman of Lucius, a club-bearer and material supplier, for himself and for Notae, freedwoman. Iucunda, a freedwoman of Frugi, made it. [3] feet into the land.
EDCS-09301631.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Iucunda, a freedwoman, for Lucius Cervius Zetus, a freedman and his associates, specifying the plot size, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09301632.translation: He lives. Manius Egnatius Lugius, cook. Antistia Elpis, freedwoman of a woman, partner. 15 feet in every direction.
EDCS-09301632.summary: This inscription records the life and death of Manius Egnatius Lugius, a cook, and his partner Antistia Elpis, also specifying the dimensions of his burial plot.

EDCS-09301633.translation: Gaius Julius Servatus, son of Gaius, and Gaius Salius Primus, son of Gaius, wine-merchants, erected this at their own expense.
EDCS-09301633.summary: This is a dedication by two wine-merchants, Gaius Julius Servatus and Gaius Salius Primus, to an unspecified deity or for a public purpose, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09301634.translation: To Quintus Catins Hermes, freedman of Quintus, a kitchen worker. [Measurements: in the field 30 feet, in the front 20 feet.]
EDCS-09301634.summary: This inscription seems to record land boundaries or a property marker for Quintus Catins Hermes, a freedman employed in the kitchen.

EDCS-09301635.translation: To the Divine Shades. Erasinus, administrator of Augustus, and Aurelia Secundina made [this] for themselves.
EDCS-09301635.summary: This funerary monument was dedicated to the Divine Shades by Erasinus, an imperial administrator, and Aurelia Secundina.

EDCS-09301636.translation: Lives Marcus Paquius Dama, freedman of Marcus, a rope maker. [Measurement: 15 feet in the field.]
EDCS-09301636.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Paquius Dama, a freedman and rope maker, indicating his place of burial or a memorial plot.

EDCS-09301637.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or memorial to Hilarius, a smelter.

EDCS-09301638.summary: This inscription identifies Gaius Cornelius Philonicus as a silversmith.

EDCS-09301639.translation: Quintus Baebius Tertius, freedman of Quintus, a sieve maker, rests here on his own property.
EDCS-09301639.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Baebius Tertius, a freedman and sieve maker, who is buried on his own land.

EDCS-09301640.translation: Lives Mustius Surito, a sieve maker. [Incomplete inscription]
EDCS-09301640.summary: This is an incomplete funerary inscription for Mustius Surito, identified as a sieve maker.

EDCS-09301643.text_edition: \n Vivit Publius Usulenus Hilarae libertus Anoptes gypsarius |(obitus) et Communi filio vivae Usulenae Publi libertae Hilarae uxsori sic in fronte pedes XII\n
EDCS-09301643.translation: Lives Publius Usulenus Anoptes, freedman of Hilara, a plasterer, and his daughter Communi, and his living wife Usulena, freedwoman of Publius Hilara. [Measurement: 12 feet in the front.]
EDCS-09301643.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Publius Usulenus Anoptes, a freedman and plasterer, his daughter Communi, and his wife Usulena, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09301645.translation: Gaius Nigidius Primus, a wool dealer, for himself and Probus, Meros (?), and his freedmen (?).
EDCS-09301645.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or a funerary marker for Gaius Nigidius Primus, a wool dealer, and potentially other individuals including freedmen.

EDCS-09301646.translation: Lives Lucius Sabidius Capito, freedman of Lucius, a wool dealer.
EDCS-09301646.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Sabidius Capito, a freedman and wool dealer.

EDCS-09301647.translation: Lucius Nerfinius Primus, freedman of Potitus, a pork butcher, for himself and [...]
EDCS-09301647.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication for Lucius Nerfinius Primus, a freedman and pork butcher, for himself and possibly others.

EDCS-09301648.translation: V[---]ius Varus, freedman of Anterotis, a linen weaver, for himself and for his wife Betutia Privata, freedwoman of Marcus. [Measurement: 15 feet in the front.]
EDCS-09301648.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial place of Varus, a freedman and linen weaver, and his wife Betutia Privata, with specified front dimensions.

EDCS-09301649.summary: This inscription records a dedication or memorial to Auctus, a freedman who was a doctor.

EDCS-09301651.translation: Heraclides, freedman of Xanth(e)rmis, doctor, here buried. Iacchus Lepotinis made this for his patron Lepos, aged 13, from his own funds.
EDCS-09301651.summary: A tombstone commemorating Heraclides, a doctor, and his patron Lepos, who died at age 13, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09301652.translation: Died. Publius Lucceius Menes, freedman of Philinus, doctor. Kaninia Attice, living, freedwoman of Publius, [provided this].
EDCS-09301652.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Publius Lucceius Menes, a doctor and freedman, and indicates that Kaninia Attice, his freedwoman partner, erected the monument.

EDCS-09301653.translation: Lucius Pomponius Diocles, freedman of Lucius, doctor, while alive, for himself and for his wife Atilia Quarta.
EDCS-09301653.summary: A funerary monument erected by Lucius Pomponius Diocles, a doctor, for himself and his wife, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09301654.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For Marcus Ulpius Eutychetes, freedman of Augustus, a most deserving surveyor, and his freedman patron.
EDCS-09301654.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Ulpius Eutychetes, a freedman and surveyor, and his freedman patron.

EDCS-09301655.translation: Gaius Vettienus, son of Titus, of the Pollia tribe, money changer, is buried here.
EDCS-09301655.summary: A tombstone for Gaius Vettienus, a money changer, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09301656.translation: Gaius Offellius Zetus, freedman of Gaius, honest merchant.
EDCS-09301656.summary: An epitaph for Gaius Offellius Zetus, a merchant and freedman, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09301657.translation: Lucius Gaienina Masclus, ship owner, lives on for himself and his family, 15 feet in front.
EDCS-09301657.summary: A funerary monument indicating a burial plot of 15 feet in front, for Lucius Gaienina Masclus, a ship owner, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09301658.translation: Gaius Valerius Gemellus of Forum Iulii, ship owner, lives on for himself and his wife Iulia Quina, daughter of Marcus, 15 feet in every direction.
EDCS-09301658.summary: A tombstone for Gaius Valerius Gemellus, a ship owner from Forum Iulii, and his wife Iulia Quina, specifying a burial plot of 15 feet in all directions, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09301659.translation: For Decimus Uleius Auctus, freedman of Decimus, ship owner, and for his wife Lucia Clara, now deceased.
EDCS-09301659.summary: A tombstone for Decimus Uleius Auctus, a ship owner, and his wife Lucia Clara, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09301660.translation: [...]enon the businessman and his wife, Sextus Avio [...] lives on by the arbitration of Communis [...].
EDCS-09301660.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription mentioning a businessman and his wife, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09301661.translation: Lucius Baebius Lepidus, money changer, lives on.
EDCS-09301661.summary: An epitaph for Lucius Baebius Lepidus, a money changer, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09301663.translation: Publius Granius Communis, freedman of Publius, olive oil dealer, lives on for himself and for Grania Flora, freedwoman of Publius.
EDCS-09301663.summary: A tombstone for Publius Granius Communis, an olive oil dealer, and his freedwoman Grania Flora, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09301664.translation: Anicia Hilara, daughter of Titus, made this for herself and for her freedman, the purse-maker Sextus Vibius Pamphilus.
EDCS-09301664.summary: This funerary inscription records a woman, Anicia Hilara, dedicating a monument to herself and her freedman, Sextus Vibius Pamphilus, who was a purse-maker.

EDCS-09301665.translation: Lives Publius Gallonius Capito, freedman of Publius, a pillar-maker, and also the freedwoman Chyteris. Gallonia Clienta, freedwoman of Publius, lived; Publius Gallonius Cliens, freedman of Capito, lives; this monument will not pass to an heir.
EDCS-09301665.summary: This funerary inscription records the living status of several individuals, including Publius Gallonius Capito, a pillar-maker, and indicates that the monument is not inheritable.

EDCS-09301666.translation: For Lucius Aponius Eros, freedman of Celatus, a candidate baker. Venusta, his partner, and Ospeus Ducieus...
EDCS-09301666.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication for Lucius Aponius Eros, freedman of Celatus, who was a candidate baker, with contributions from his partner Venusta and Ospeus Ducieus.

EDCS-09301667.translation: Lives Lucius Decumius Felix, freedman of Lucius, from Rome, a baker, for himself and for the deceased Lucius Decumius Hilarus, patron. Also to the seven altars.
EDCS-09301667.summary: This funerary inscription records Lucius Decumius Felix, a baker from Rome, dedicating the monument to himself and his patron Lucius Decumius Hilarus, also mentioning seven altars.

EDCS-09301668.translation: Lives Voltilia Secunda, freedwoman of the woman, for herself and for her husband Gnaeus Domitius Auctus, a painter.
EDCS-09301668.summary: This funerary inscription records Voltilia Secunda dedicating a monument to herself and her husband Gnaeus Domitius Auctus, a painter.

EDCS-09301669.translation: To Usinius, auctioneer of Antiope, in the field, feet.
EDCS-09301669.summary: This is a fragmented inscription likely related to a burial or property boundary involving an auctioneer.

EDCS-09301670.translation: Lives Publius Albius [---]cinus, freedman of the woman, a provisioner, salaried(?), for himself and for the deceased Plania Tertia, daughter of Marcus, and for the deceased Plania Secunda, daughter of Marcus. In the field, 15 feet.
EDCS-09301670.summary: This funerary inscription records Publius Albius [---]cinus, a provisioner, dedicating a monument to himself and two women, Plania Tertia and Plania Secunda, and specifies a plot size of 15 feet.

EDCS-09301671.translation: To Aulus Sempronius Laetus, freedman of Gallaecus, a dyer, and to Sempronia Modesta, his wife.
EDCS-09301671.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Aulus Sempronius Laetus, a freedman dyer, and his wife Sempronia Modesta.

EDCS-09301672.translation: Lives Aulus Sempronius Laetus, freedman of Gallaecus, a dyer, for himself and Sempronia Modesta.
EDCS-09301672.summary: This funerary inscription records Aulus Sempronius Laetus, a freedman dyer, dedicating the monument to himself and Sempronia Modesta.

EDCS-09301673.translation: Lucius Actorius Sphaerus, freedman of Lucius, a maker of nets or straps.
EDCS-09301673.summary: This inscription identifies Lucius Actorius Sphaerus, freedman of Lucius, as a maker of nets or straps (sagarius).

EDCS-09301674.summary: This inscription identifies Lucius Braetius Litorinus as a sandal-maker (solearius).

EDCS-09301675.translation: Lucius Autronius Rufus, the builder, lives; Geminia Amoena, freedwoman of Aulus, lives.
EDCS-09301675.summary: This inscription records two individuals, Lucius Autronius Rufus and Geminia Amoena, who are noted as living, with Rufus identified as a builder (constructor).

EDCS-09301676.translation: Gaius Rabirius Hilarius, the scribe, lives.
EDCS-09301676.summary: This inscription records the survival of Gaius Rabirius Hilarius, identified as a scribe (tabellarius).

EDCS-09301677.translation: Lucrio, freedman, made [this] for Papirius Rufus, the shopkeeper, and for his wife, Silvana, and for [---]raia. Lives; Antonia, freedwoman of Titus; [---]vena, freedwoman of Titus.
EDCS-09301677.summary: This inscription records the creation of a monument by Lucrio for Papirius Rufus, a shopkeeper, and his wife Silvana, also mentioning other individuals who are noted as living.

EDCS-09301678.translation: Marcus Coelius Onesimus, freedman of Marcus, for himself and for Primigenia, his freedwoman companion, and for his mother Cervia Fusca, the hairdresser.
EDCS-09301678.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Marcus Coelius Onesimus for himself, his companion Primigenia, and his mother Cervia Fusca, a hairdresser.

EDCS-09301679.translation: Titus Olitius Hermes, the hairdresser, made [this] for himself, and for his wife Olitia Amabilis, and for his son Olitius Iulianus, and for their descendants. Lives.
EDCS-09301679.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by Titus Olitius Hermes, a hairdresser, for himself, his wife, son, and descendants.

EDCS-09301680.translation: Voltilia Optata, daughter of Decimus, lives. For father and mother, Decimus Voltilius Auctus, the hairdresser, and Optata, daughter of Spurius, 15 feet in all directions.
EDCS-09301680.summary: This inscription records the survival of Voltilia Optata and the dedication of a burial plot of 15 square feet by Decimus Voltilius Auctus, a hairdresser, and Optata for their parents.

EDCS-09301681.translation: the hairdresser, human, 15 feet in all directions.
EDCS-09301681.summary: This inscription records a burial plot of 15 square feet belonging to an individual identified only as a hairdresser.

EDCS-09301682.translation: Euphorus Casius Niger [for his] freedman Nigro, the incense seller.
EDCS-09301682.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Euphorus Casius Niger to his freedman Nigro, who was an incense seller (thurarius).

EDCS-09301683.summary: This inscription appears to be a simple dedication or naming of individuals, possibly Primulus and Publius Usienius.

EDCS-09301684.translation: Marcus Accius Primus, freedman of Marcus, the clothier, lives; for himself and for Optatus, his freedman.
EDCS-09301684.summary: This inscription records the survival of Marcus Accius Primus, a clothier, and his dedication for himself and his freedman Optatus.

EDCS-09301685.translation: Publius Licinius Licinus, freedman of Publius, the clothier, lives; for himself and his family. Sergia [---], for herself and her family.
EDCS-09301685.summary: This inscription records the survival of Publius Licinius Licinus, a clothier, and his dedication for his family, as well as a similar dedication by Sergia.

EDCS-09301686.translation: Aulus Turranius Niger, a basket-maker, lives [here]; Turrania Montana, his wife, [lives here too], in the field, 10 feet.
EDCS-09301686.summary: This funerary inscription records the deceased Aulus Turranius Niger, a basket-maker, and his wife Turrania Montana.

EDCS-09301687.translation: Titus Catius Acutus, freedman of Teucrus, lives [here].
EDCS-09301687.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Titus Catius Acutus, a freedman.

EDCS-09301689.translation: To Lucius Manlius Primigenius, magistrate three times; [dedicated by] Primigenius.
EDCS-09301689.summary: This inscription dedicates something to Lucius Manlius Primigenius, who held the office of magistrate three times.

EDCS-09301690.translation: Marcus Umbricius Hilarus Aeclanus, freedman of Marcus, is buried here. Farewell, and you too.
EDCS-09301690.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Umbricius Hilarus Aeclanus, a freedman.

EDCS-09301691.translation: For Publius Stasius Nasoni, freedman of Caius, of the Voltinian tribe, from Aquae Sextiae.
EDCS-09301691.summary: This is a dedication to Publius Stasius Nasoni, a freedman from Aquae Sextiae.

EDCS-09301692.translation: Fadius, one of the six Augustan priests, [in] the Iulia Augusta colony of Aquae Sextiae, [and his] freedwomen.
EDCS-09301692.summary: This inscription mentions Fadius, an Augustan priest in the colony of Aquae Sextiae, and his freedwomen.

EDCS-09301693.translation: Titus Vipongius Homullus of Bergusium is buried here.
EDCS-09301693.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Titus Vipongius Homullus of Bergusium.

EDCS-09301695.translation: R. Ruflanus, of the Palatina tribe, with good fortune.
EDCS-09301695.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely a personal note or an epitaph fragment mentioning a man named R. Ruflanus.

EDCS-09301696.translation: Gaius Autronius, son of Gaius, from Ferraris.
EDCS-09301696.summary: This inscription identifies Gaius Autronius, son of Gaius, and notes his origin from Ferraris, likely a place name.

EDCS-09301697.translation: Aulus Cornelius Metellus, son of Aulus, of the Voltinia tribe, from Forum Iulii, [erected this] for himself and for his daughter Voconia Optata, daughter of Quintus, and for Aulus Cornelius, and for Quartus and Cornelia Sentra, [after their] death.
EDCS-09301697.summary: This funerary inscription records Aulus Cornelius Metellus dedicating a monument for himself, his daughter, and other family members, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-09301698.translation: Prima [erected this] for herself and for her daughter Pontia Optata, daughter of Lucius, and for Lucius Vibius Iunior, and for Lucius Vibius Niger, and for Nigrinus, [after their] death, [from] Forum Iulii.
EDCS-09301698.summary: This funerary inscription records Prima dedicating a monument for herself and her daughter Pontia Optata, as well as for Lucius Vibius Iunior, Lucius Vibius Niger, and Nigrinus.

EDCS-09301699.translation: Titus Valerius Verna, son of Titus, of the Foro Iuliensi [tribe or origin], [erected this] for his mother Marcia Tertulla and his daughter Titus Valerius Verna.
EDCS-09301699.summary: This inscription records Titus Valerius Verna dedicating a monument for his mother Marcia Tertulla and his daughter, also named Titus Valerius Verna.

EDCS-09301700.translation: Gaius Julius Italus, son of Gaius, of the Galeria tribe, a Roman knight, from Hispania Citerior, from Segobriga.
EDCS-09301700.summary: This inscription identifies Gaius Julius Italus, a Roman knight originating from Segobriga in Hispania Citerior.

EDCS-09301701.translation: For Betutia Secunda, for her daughter, and for Lamponius and Primigenius, from Kabilii.
EDCS-09301701.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Betutia Secunda and her daughter, as well as Lamponius and Primigenius, possibly specifying their place of origin as Kabilii.

EDCS-09301702.translation: Gaius Autronius Agastus, son of Gaius, is buried here; [this was erected by] Auge, daughter of Gaius, freedwoman of Minicia, for herself and for her living husband Lucius Carisius Iucundus, son of Lucius, from Lugudunum.
EDCS-09301702.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Gaius Autronius Agastus and the dedication of the tomb by Auge for herself and her husband Lucius Carisius Iucundus, specifying their origins and relationship.

EDCS-09301703.translation: To Titus Vicorlius, son of Titus, Sextus Manlius Lusitanus [erected this].
EDCS-09301703.summary: This inscription is a dedication from Sextus Manlius Lusitanus to Titus Vicorlius, son of Titus.

EDCS-09301704.summary: This very brief inscription likely identifies Macer and his association with Caesar, possibly as a soldier or a freedman.

EDCS-09301705.translation: Marcus Abillius Silvanus, freedman of Marcus, of the Galeria tribe, made this while alive for himself and his family, 25 feet at the front.
EDCS-09301705.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the purchase of a plot of land for burial by Marcus Abillius Silvanus for himself and his family.

EDCS-09301706.translation: For Publius' freedman Acastus and Publius Usulenus Isochrysus, 15 feet.
EDCS-09301706.summary: This is a funerary inscription allocating a burial plot of 15 feet to Acastus, freedman of Publius, and Publius Usulenus Isochrysus.

EDCS-09301707.summary: This is a very short inscription, possibly a name on a tombstone or a boundary marker.

EDCS-09301708.translation: Aufustia Acyme, freedwoman of Lucius, and Lucius Salonius Petro, freedman of Lucius, made this for Lucius Aufustius Messor, son of Lucius, and for themselves.
EDCS-09301708.summary: This funerary inscription records the creation of a monument by two freedpersons for their patron and for themselves.

EDCS-09301709.translation: For Marcus Aqutius Genialis, freedman of Marcus, and Marcus Aqutius Fidus, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-09301709.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating a burial plot to two freedmen of Marcus Aqutius.

EDCS-09301710.translation: For Marcus Aqutius Thuranus, freedman of Marcus, and Marcus Aqutius Iucundus, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-09301710.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating a burial plot to two freedmen of Marcus Aqutius.

EDCS-09301712.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. To Aelia Restituta, sweetest soul. Bellator, freedman of the Emperor, for his most rare wife who deserved well of him. Friends, 'while we live, let us live'.
EDCS-09301712.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated by a freedman to his wife, expressing a sentiment about enjoying life.

EDCS-09301713.translation: Lucius Aemilius Acutus, freedman of Lucius Philomus, lives on, 15 feet in all directions.
EDCS-09301713.summary: This funerary inscription marks a burial plot of 15 feet in all directions for Lucius Aemilius Acutus, a freedman.

EDCS-09301714.translation: To the divine spirits. Caio Aemilio Dioscuro lived 19 years. Usidia Iuventina, his most devoted mother, [dedicated this].
EDCS-09301714.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Caio Aemilio Dioscuro, who died at age 19, dedicated by his devoted mother.

EDCS-09301715.translation: Cnaeus Aemilius Eros, freedman of Cnaeus, lives on.
EDCS-09301715.summary: This funerary inscription marks the burial place of Cnaeus Aemilius Eros, a freedman.

EDCS-09301716.translation: Gaius Aemilius Philonicus for himself and for his wife Aemilia Secunda and for his daughter Satriena, daughter of Caius.
EDCS-09301716.summary: This funerary inscription records Gaius Aemilius Philonicus making provisions for himself, his wife, and his daughter.

EDCS-09301717.summary: This is a funerary epitaph identifying Tingandus as a freedman of Lucius Aemilius.

EDCS-09301719.translation: To Valeria Quarta, wife of Publius Pomponius Titedus, son of Publius Pomponius, freedman of Publius Pomponius, son of Publius.
EDCS-09301719.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Valeria Quarta, wife of Publius Pomponius Titedus, with complex patron-client relationships indicated.

EDCS-09301720.translation: To the departed spirits. Aemilius Eutyches made this for his dearest wife, Laid, freedwoman of Caius Aemilius.
EDCS-09301720.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Aemilius Eutyches for his wife, Laid, a freedwoman.

EDCS-09301721.translation: To Iuppiter Optimus Maximus. To Aemilia Rhodope.
EDCS-09301721.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aemilia Rhodope, possibly with a dedication to Jupiter.

EDCS-09301722.translation: Aeneas lives, and for Publius Atilius, from the Volusina tribe. Publius Atilius [erected this].
EDCS-09301722.summary: This inscription records that Aeneas is alive and likely commemorates Publius Atilius from the Volusina tribe.

EDCS-09301723.translation: Eros Ascelus, freedman of Caius Aeneas Olympus, [erected this] while alive, for himself and his family.
EDCS-09301723.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Eros Ascelus, freedman of Caius Aeneas Olympus, for himself and his family.

EDCS-09301724.translation: To the departed spirits. Titus Aebutius Agahorus Vibus, [freedman] of Titus Aen Proclianus, [erected this] for his wife Varia Ura.
EDCS-09301724.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Titus Aebutius Agahorus Vibus for his wife Varia Ura.

EDCS-09301725.translation: To Alarius, for Onentius, in place of Anonia Iura Maxima, mother.
EDCS-09301725.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Alarius, possibly on behalf of Onentius, for Anonia Iura Maxima.

EDCS-09301726.translation: Grata, freedwoman of Decimus Albanus, [erected this] while alive, for herself and for Publius Iuventius Cephalio, freedman of Publius, her husband, and for Caius Aufustius Synerotus, freedman of Caius.
EDCS-09301726.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Grata, freedwoman of Decimus Albanus, for herself, her husband Publius Iuventius Cephalio, and Caius Aufustius Synerotus.

EDCS-09301728.translation: To Alcimus, freedman of Decimus Edro [erected this].
EDCS-09301728.summary: This is a funerary epitaph honoring Alcimus, freedman of Decimus Edro.

EDCS-09301729.translation: To the divine spirit [of] Ivo Scanian, for himself and Ultromae Auristiae.
EDCS-09301729.summary: This is an epitaph for Ivo Scanian and Ultromae Auristiae.

EDCS-09301730.translation: [---] lived for 50 years with Lucius Lexa.
EDCS-09301730.summary: This epitaph records the lifespan of an individual who lived with Lucius Lexa.

EDCS-09301732.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely mentioning a person named Alexander.

EDCS-09301733.translation: To the departed spirits. Alphius Secundus, freedman, [erected this] for his most excellent patron Quintus Alphium Quintillus, and Rammia Primitiva, wife, for her most devoted husband.
EDCS-09301733.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a freedman and his wife to their patron and husband, respectively.

EDCS-09301734.translation: To Amoena, wife of L. Antilius, and Usaia Iadenlia, his wife, V. Metius Lacrinus, through his freedman Laodetus, and V. Marcus Julius, [this plot] in the field, 20 feet.
EDCS-09301734.summary: This inscription seems to record a land grant or burial plot of 20 feet in size to Amoena and Usaia Iadenlia, associated with V. Metius Lacrinus and V. Marcus Julius.

EDCS-09301735.translation: Ampelius is buried here. Oca, his wife, placed [this monument]. 15 feet in all directions.
EDCS-09301735.summary: This is a tomb inscription recording the burial of Ampelius, placed by his wife Oca, with dimensions of 15 feet in all directions.

EDCS-09301736.translation: For the life of Gaius Anbivius Clemens, and Rammia Tertiola, his wife, and Gaius Anbivius Tertius, his brother, 15 feet in front.
EDCS-09301736.summary: This inscription seems to be a dedication or memorial for Gaius Anbivius Clemens, his wife Rammia Tertiola, and his brother Gaius Anbivius Tertius, indicating a front dimension of 15 feet.

EDCS-09301737.translation: Death of Ancharius Alcaeus, [dedicated] to Iulia Secunda, wife; death of Ancharius Amphion, brother, [dedicated] to Octavia Arcusae, wife.
EDCS-09301737.summary: This inscription records the deaths of Ancharius Alcaeus and Ancharius Amphion, with dedications to their respective wives, Iulia Secunda and Octavia Arcusae.

EDCS-09301738.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely identifying a person named Lucius Ancharius Philonicus.

EDCS-09301739.translation: Quintus Ancharius Mundus, freedman, [dedicated this] for himself, and for Ancharia Quinti, freedwoman, daughter of Mundus; for Quintus Ancharius Primulus, freedman of Quintus; and for Ancharia Prisca, freedwoman of Quintus.
EDCS-09301739.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Quintus Ancharius Mundus, a freedman, for himself and several other freed individuals, including his sister.

EDCS-09301741.translation: Marcus Anelius Rotui, son of Titus, Accilius, lives.
EDCS-09301741.summary: This funerary inscription records the survival of Marcus Anelius Rotui Accilius.

EDCS-09301743.translation: Aninia Hospita, freedwoman of Publius, for herself, and her heir Aninius Viator, freedman of Publius, and C. Iuli for his own part.
EDCS-09301743.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial arrangements made by Aninia Hospita, freedwoman of Publius, and others for themselves and their heirs.

EDCS-09301744.translation: Annidia Secunda, freedwoman of Quintus, has died for herself, and for Quintus Annidius Diopantus, freedman of Quintus, her patron, and has died for Publius Lucius Festus, son of Publius Lucius, and has died for Faustus, freedman of Publius Lucius.
EDCS-09301744.summary: This funerary inscription records the death and burial arrangements of Annidia Secunda and others, including her patron.

EDCS-09301747.translation: Marcus Annius Flavus, son of Marcus, of the Voltinia tribe, for himself and for his father Marcus Annius Rutilianus and for his mother Licinia, daughter of Titus.
EDCS-09301747.summary: This funerary inscription records a self-dedication and dedication to parents by Marcus Annius Flavus.

EDCS-09301748.translation: Marcus Annius Canus, son of Lucius, of the Fabia tribe, lives, [and] Licinia Rustica, daughter of Titus.
EDCS-09301748.summary: This inscription records the survival of Marcus Annius Canus and Licinia Rustica.

EDCS-09301749.translation: Lucius Annius Labeo, son of Lucius, of the Papiria tribe, and Annia Argentilla, freedwoman of Lucius, for themselves, and for their patron, 15 feet in front.
EDCS-09301749.summary: This funerary inscription records a burial space purchased by Lucius Annius Labeo and Annia Argentilla for themselves and their patron.

EDCS-09301750.translation: The wife is buried here. Marcus Annius Maxumus, son of Marcus.
EDCS-09301750.summary: This inscription marks the burial place of the wife of Marcus Annius Maxumus.

EDCS-09301751.translation: Aucta, freedwoman of Primi, is buried here for herself and her patron. [---] is buried here on the side of...
EDCS-09301751.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Aucta, freedwoman of Primi, and indicates further burials.

EDCS-09301752.translation: Annia Optata, daughter of Spurius, for herself and for her husband Lucius Numisius Sabinus, most excellent man, 15 feet in front.
EDCS-09301752.summary: This funerary inscription records a burial space purchased by Annia Optata for herself and her husband.

EDCS-09301753.translation: To the departed spirits. Annonia Panthera, freedwoman of Annonius Fortunatus, [in memory of] Annonius Fortunatus, aged 6 years and 5 months. Annonia Panthera, mother, made this for her son.
EDCS-09301753.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Annonia Panthera to her deceased son, Annonius Fortunatus.

EDCS-09301755.translation: To Lucius Anterus, by the decision of N., (?)
EDCS-09301755.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Anterus, likely an official or prominent figure, as indicated by "arbitratu" (by decision/arbitration), with the recipient's name partially preserved. The date is indeterminate from the text alone.

EDCS-09301756.translation: Anthis, wife of Titus Sornius, most loving wife to her husband and brother
EDCS-09301756.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Anthis, wife of Titus Sornius, highlighting her devotion to her husband and brother, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09301757.translation: Gaius Nimphius, freedman of Caius, to his most dutiful freedwoman Nympha, freedwoman of Julia Aetene, 15 feet in front in all directions
EDCS-09301757.summary: This funerary monument or boundary marker was erected by Gaius Nimphius, a freedman, for his freedwoman Nympha, indicating a relationship and specifying dimensions, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09301758.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription indicating the status of an individual as a freedman of Antimedis, with the full context and date missing.

EDCS-09301759.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying an individual named Antiochus as the freedman of Aulus, possibly indicating he made the monument, with its date indeterminate.

EDCS-09301760.translation: Voltilia Flora, freedwoman of Titus, wife of Titus Voltilus, freedman of Titus, made this for herself and for Titus Voltilus, freedman of Titus, while alive
EDCS-09301760.summary: This is a funerary monument or tombstone erected by Voltilia Flora for herself and her husband Titus Voltilus, both freedpersons, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09301761.translation: Marcus Antonius Chryseros to Auruncia Urtica, well-deserving, and to his own people
EDCS-09301761.summary: This is a dedication, likely funerary or commemorative, by Marcus Antonius Chryseros to Auruncia Urtica and his family, implying a relationship of gratitude or affection, from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09301762.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely naming an individual, Antonius Lucrio, with no further context or date inferable.

EDCS-09301764.translation: and to Antonia, daughter of Gnaeus, he made [this] for himself and for Gaius Julius
EDCS-09301764.summary: This is a fragmentary dedication or funerary inscription detailing the erection of a monument by an unnamed individual for Antonia, daughter of Gnaeus, and for himself and Gaius Julius, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09301765.translation: While alive, Antonia, freedwoman of Lucius, made this for Lucius Antonius Victor, freedman, aged 20
EDCS-09301765.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Antonia for her freedman Lucius Antonius Victor, who died at the age of 20, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09301766.translation: Antonia Elia for herself and her own, for Antonius Spurius, son of Spurius, called Fidelis, for Antonius Spurius, son of Spurius, called Felix, for Antonius Respectus, son of Caius, this monument will not follow an heir, 15 feet in any direction in the land.
EDCS-09301766.summary: This funerary monument specifies that it is not to pass to heirs and defines its extent in the land.

EDCS-09301767.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph for Antonia Secunda.

EDCS-09301768.translation: Lucius Antronius Celer, son of Publius, for himself, for Scanianis Gemella, freedwoman of Stactinis, and for Ametia Restituta, freedwoman of his wife.
EDCS-09301768.summary: This funerary monument is dedicated by Lucius Antronius Celer for himself and for two freedwomen.

EDCS-09301769.translation: Us, freedman of Decimus, of the Palatine tribe, Ap...
EDCS-09301769.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph for a freedman named Us.

EDCS-09301770.translation: Abascantus [dedicated this] for Marcus Apicius Peregrinus, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-09301770.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Abascantus for Marcus Apicius Peregrinus.

EDCS-09301771.translation: Marcus Apirius Aster, freedman of Marcus, is buried here.
EDCS-09301771.summary: This is a funerary epitaph stating that Marcus Apirius Aster, a freedman, is buried here.

EDCS-09301772.summary: This appears to be a simple funerary epitaph or marker for Lucius Antiochus.

EDCS-09301773.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Aponius to L. Autronius.

EDCS-09301774.translation: Lucius Aponius Felix, freedman of Lucius, lives on [here], 15 feet in front.
EDCS-09301774.summary: This funerary epitaph indicates the burial place of Lucius Aponius Felix, a freedman, and its dimensions.

EDCS-09301775.translation: Lucius Aponius Optatus, freedman of Lucius, died. Lucius Aponius Eros, freedman of Lucius, and Tu...
EDCS-09301775.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Lucius Aponius Optatus and mentions Lucius Aponius Eros and another individual.

EDCS-09301776.translation: To Aponius Philocalus and his wife Aponia Rhodia.
EDCS-09301776.summary: This is a dedication to Aponius Philocalus and his wife Aponia Rhodia.

EDCS-09301777.translation: Lucius Aponius Phrastes made this for himself and for Exorata, a freedwoman, during his lifetime.
EDCS-09301777.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Lucius Aponius Phrastes for himself and his freedwoman Exorata.

EDCS-09301778.translation: Aponia Iusta for herself, and for Aponius Philogenus, and for her family.
EDCS-09301778.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Aponia Iusta for herself and her family members, including Aponius Philogenus.

EDCS-09301780.translation: Sextus Appaeus Olympus for himself, and for Fonteia Pamphila, and for his parents, and...
EDCS-09301780.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Sextus Appaeus Olympus for himself, his partner Fonteia Pamphila, and his parents.

EDCS-09301781.translation: Illius Voltinia Arbuscula Fausta, having come from...
EDCS-09301781.summary: This inscription likely records a dedication or memorial related to Illius Voltinia Arbuscula Fausta.

EDCS-09301782.summary: This is a brief epitaph stating that Arentia Quarta is alive, possibly implying survival or a tomb inscription.

EDCS-09301783.translation: To Gnaeus Aristius Acantus, my friend.
EDCS-09301783.summary: This is a dedication or memorial to a friend named Gnaeus Aristius Acantus.

EDCS-09301784.translation: Philocles Quartus, freedman of Arruntius Quarti, and Ata, freedman of Publius Arruntius Quarti.
EDCS-09301784.summary: This inscription records two freedmen, Philocles Quartus and Ata, identifying their patrons.

EDCS-09301785.translation: To Publius Arruntius Verru, Publius Arruntius [set this up].
EDCS-09301785.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Publius Arruntius to Publius Arruntius Verru.

EDCS-09301786.translation: To Gaius Artorius Ortan, Valeria Tertia, his mother, [dedicated this].
EDCS-09301786.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Valeria Tertia to her son Gaius Artorius Ortan.

EDCS-09301788.translation: To Ascanius, from Calicis, freedwoman of Publius, 13 feet.
EDCS-09301788.summary: This is a boundary marker for a plot of land measuring 13 feet, dedicated to Ascanius.

EDCS-09301789.translation: Caius Asellius Iustus, son, is alive.
EDCS-09301789.summary: This funerary inscription records the survival of Caius Asellius Iustus, son of someone.

EDCS-09301790.translation: Quintus Asellius Gemellus, freedman of Quintus, for himself and for Vibiae Tertia, freedwoman of Lucius, and for Quintus Asellius Genialis, freedman.
EDCS-09301790.summary: This funerary inscription records Quintus Asellius Gemellus dedicating a tomb for himself, his wife Vibiae Tertia, and their freedman Quintus Asellius Genialis.

EDCS-09301791.translation: Salvia, freedwoman of Aulus, is alive. Eleutera, freedwoman of Aulus Asellius, is buried here.
EDCS-09301791.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Eleutera, freedwoman of Aulus Asellius, and mentions that Salvia, also a freedwoman of Aulus, is alive.

EDCS-09301792.translation: Asicia Exapila made this at her own expense.
EDCS-09301792.summary: This inscription records Asicia Exapila funding the construction of a monument.

EDCS-09301793.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription likely related to a road or a person with the cognomen Sep...

EDCS-09301794.translation: Atilius, son of Caius, Atilia, daughter of Caius, Atilius, son of Caius, to their father.
EDCS-09301794.summary: This inscription records Atilius, son of Caius, Atilia, daughter of Caius, and another Atilius, son of Caius, dedicating something to their father.

EDCS-09301795.translation: Publius Atilius Inventus, freedman of Publius, for his relatives and freedmen.
EDCS-09301795.summary: This funerary inscription records Publius Atilius Inventus dedicating a tomb for his family and freedmen.

EDCS-09301796.translation: Titus Atilius Telesphor, freedman of Titus, and Atilia Alce made this for Titus Atilius Voltus, son of Titus, an excellent and most dutiful son, and for themselves and their family.
EDCS-09301796.summary: This funerary inscription records Titus Atilius Telesphor and Atilia Alce dedicating a tomb for Titus Atilius Voltus, described as an excellent and dutiful son, and for themselves and their family.

EDCS-09301798.translation: Atilia Satulla, daughter of Publius, for herself and for her brother Publius Atilius Secundus, son of Publius.
EDCS-09301798.summary: This funerary inscription records Atilia Satulla dedicating a tomb for herself and her brother Publius Atilius Secundus.

EDCS-09301799.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Apidanus, a freedman.

EDCS-09301800.translation: To the spirits of the underworld; for Nigrus, son of Lucius Attius, of the Papirian tribe.
EDCS-09301800.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Nigrus.

EDCS-09301802.translation: For Publius Attius Midas, freedman of Publius Attius, by the arbitration of Venustus, freedman of Publius Attius, fellow freedman.
EDCS-09301802.summary: This inscription records an arrangement concerning Publius Attius Midas, a freedman, with fellow freedmen involved in the arbitration.

EDCS-09301803.translation: Lucius Attius Nicridius Celadus lives; for himself, and for Julia Lepida Phosfora, his fellow slave and partner, and Attia, his mother; 12 feet in front.
EDCS-09301803.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Attius Nicridius Celadus, who prepaid for his burial and that of his partner and mother.

EDCS-09301804.translation: Quintus Attius Togiacus, son of Sextus, lives; Sextus Attius Rufus, son of Sextus, his brother, has died.
EDCS-09301804.summary: This inscription marks the life of Quintus Attius Togiacus and records the death of his brother, Sextus Attius Rufus.

EDCS-09301805.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription for Gaius Attius Venustus.

EDCS-09301806.translation: For the fellow freedmen of Ausius Auctus.
EDCS-09301806.summary: This inscription seems to commemorate or address fellow freedmen of Ausius Auctus.

EDCS-09301807.translation: By the arbitration of Aucta, freedwoman of Caius, wife of Repentinus, freedman of Caius Fulvius.
EDCS-09301807.summary: This inscription records an arbitration involving Aucta, wife of Repentinus, and related to a freedman named Caius Fulvius.

EDCS-09301808.translation: For Gaius Aufidius, father of our Paulla, and mother Quintus.
EDCS-09301808.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaius Aufidius, father of Paulla, and mentioning his mother.

EDCS-09301809.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely a name on a monument or tomb.

EDCS-09301810.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely formed part of a larger dedication or funerary monument.

EDCS-09301811.translation: Lucius Aufidius Marsus, freedman of Lucius, is buried here, by the decision of Gaius Numitorius.
EDCS-09301811.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Aufidius Marsus, specifying his burial arrangement by the decision of Gaius Numitorius.

EDCS-09301812.translation: Aufidius Teucroti and Mesia are alive for themselves and their freedman Erasinus.
EDCS-09301812.summary: This inscription records the establishment of a burial space for Aufidius Teucroti, Mesia, and their freedman Erasinus.

EDCS-09301813.translation: Publius Aviedius, son of Publius, by the decision of S.
EDCS-09301813.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely a funerary dedication or record of a burial arrangement.

EDCS-09301814.translation: To the departed spirits. Sulpicia Sulpiciana made this for her husband Marcus Aurelius Philetus, most excellent and most deserving of her.
EDCS-09301814.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Sulpicia Sulpiciana to her husband Marcus Aurelius Philetus.

EDCS-09301815.translation: Gaius Aurelius Pri, son of Lucius.
EDCS-09301815.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely part of a longer funerary or dedication text.

EDCS-09301816.translation: The death of Gaius Badius Horestes, fifteen feet in all directions.
EDCS-09301816.summary: This inscription marks the death of Gaius Badius Horestes and specifies the dimensions of his burial plot.

EDCS-09301817.translation: Of the sons of Baebia Aquitania, fifteen feet in all directions.
EDCS-09301817.summary: This inscription designates a burial plot of fifteen feet in all directions for the sons of Baebia Aquitania.

EDCS-09301818.translation: Lucius Baebius Ligus and Baebia Quarta, in the field, fifteen feet.
EDCS-09301818.summary: This funerary inscription records a burial plot of fifteen feet for Lucius Baebius Ligus and Baebia Quarta.

EDCS-09301819.translation: Oppia Sabina, wife, for her most deserving husband Lucius Baebius Parda.
EDCS-09301819.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Oppia Sabina to her husband Lucius Baebius Parda.

EDCS-09301820.translation: Titus Baebius Primus lives on, ten feet in front.
EDCS-09301820.summary: This inscription marks a funerary plot measuring ten feet in width, likely for Titus Baebius Primus.

EDCS-09301821.translation: To Marcus Baebius, son of Lucius, of the Teretina tribe.
EDCS-09301821.summary: This is a dedication to Marcus Baebius, son of Lucius, identified by his tribal affiliation.

EDCS-09301824.translation: [...bius] for himself and for Bassus, freedman of Quintus. Quintus Varius B[...]
EDCS-09301824.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to be a funerary dedication made by Quintus Varius B[...], for himself and his freedman Bassus.

EDCS-09301825.translation: Briccius Callistus made this for himself, for Vinicia Fida, and for his own people.
EDCS-09301825.summary: This is a funerary monument commissioned by Briccius Callistus for himself, his family, and Vinicia Fida.

EDCS-09301826.translation: Quintus Bullius Fronto, Bullia Tuche, daughter of Lucius, and Lucius Bullius, son of Lucius, live on, to [his] wife Iria.
EDCS-09301826.summary: This inscription records the continued existence of Quintus Bullius Fronto, Bullia Tuche, and Lucius Bullius, and is dedicated to Iria, presumably Lucius' wife.

EDCS-09301827.translation: To Quintus Caecilius Ingenuus. Sempronia Quintus Caecilius O[...]
EDCS-09301827.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication to Quintus Caecilius Ingenuus, possibly by Sempronia or from the family of Quintus Caecilius.

EDCS-09301828.translation: Quintus Caecilius Maxsimus lives on for himself and for his wife Modesta, daughter of Publius, daughter of Terenta.
EDCS-09301828.summary: This funerary inscription states that Quintus Caecilius Maxsimus and his wife Modesta are commemorated, likely with the intention of continuing their existence in memory.

EDCS-09301829.translation: Marcus Caecilius Vitalis lives on for himself, for his freedwoman Caecilia Meroe, and for his own people, for fifteen feet in the territory; this monument shall not pass to an heir, nor shall the place of burial.
EDCS-09301829.summary: This funerary inscription by Marcus Caecilius Vitalis states that the plot is for himself, his freedwoman, and his family, and prohibits its inheritance.

EDCS-09301830.translation: For his freedwoman Clara, for herself and her own people.
EDCS-09301830.summary: This inscription is a dedication for Clara, a freedwoman, and her family.

EDCS-09301831.translation: To Grata, freedwoman of Caecilia, to Modesta.
EDCS-09301831.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Grata, a freedwoman, and Modesta.

EDCS-09301832.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Caedicia Atirina Frontona.

EDCS-09301833.translation: Caelius, for himself and his family.
EDCS-09301833.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caelius, intended for himself and his relatives.

EDCS-09301834.translation: Marcus Caelius, while alive, for himself.
EDCS-09301834.summary: This funerary inscription records Marcus Caelius setting aside a burial place for himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-09301835.translation: Marcus Caemuleius Phyrenaeus, freedman of Marcus, lives for himself and his wife Maxuma, and for Marcus Caemuleius Maximus.
EDCS-09301835.summary: This funerary inscription records Marcus Caemuleius Phyrenaeus, a freedman, establishing a burial plot for himself, his wife Maxuma, and Marcus Caemuleius Maximus.

EDCS-09301836.translation: Gnaeus Pompeius, to his son Caesar.
EDCS-09301836.summary: This inscription is a dedication from Gnaeus Pompeius to his son Caesar.

EDCS-09301837.translation: Caius Calicius Surus, freedman of Caius, and patron, lives on, a kind man; Caius [---].
EDCS-09301837.summary: This funerary inscription honors Caius Calicius Surus, a freedman and patron, noting his kind disposition.

EDCS-09301838.translation: Calist Martia, while alive, for herself. Bon[---]
EDCS-09301838.summary: This funerary inscription records Calist Martia setting aside a burial place for herself during her lifetime.

EDCS-09301839.translation: Publius Casponius Sabinus, to his wife Procula, daughter of Caius, and for himself and his family.
EDCS-09301839.summary: This funerary inscription records Publius Casponius Sabinus dedicating a burial place for his wife Procula and his family.

EDCS-09301840.translation: Silvana, freedwoman of a woman, lives on.
EDCS-09301840.summary: This funerary inscription records the continued existence of Silvana, a freedwoman.

EDCS-09301841.translation: To Publius Caninius Felix, freedman, Salarius Oppianus, his cousin, for his deceased father, Gaius Salarius Robia, for his deceased mother, Maria Tertia, for his sister Maria Maxsima, for his deceased brother, Gaius Marius Quintio. In front 24 feet.
EDCS-09301841.summary: This funerary inscription by Salarius Oppianus dedicates a burial plot measuring 24 feet in front to his freedman relative Publius Caninius Felix, as well as his deceased parents and brother.

EDCS-09301842.translation: Caninia Musa, freedwoman of Publius, lives for herself.
EDCS-09301842.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caninia Musa, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301845.translation: To Lucius Carisius Frontonius, son of Lucius; 15 feet in all directions.
EDCS-09301845.summary: This inscription likely marks a property boundary or a grave plot measuring 15 Roman feet on each side, dedicated to Lucius Carisius Frontonius.

EDCS-09301846.translation: To the Divine Manes. Carula lived 22 years. Flavia Aura, mother, [erected this] for her daughter.
EDCS-09301846.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Carula, who died at 22, set up by her mother Flavia Aura, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301847.summary: This is a fragmented inscription likely recording a name, possibly from a tomb or public monument.

EDCS-09301848.translation: Lucius Cassius Barba [and] Lucius Cassius Hilario, freedman. Varia Tertia, freedwoman of Caius, [erected this] while alive: 12 feet in front, 15 feet in the field.
EDCS-09301848.summary: This funerary inscription records Lucius Cassius Barba and his freedman Lucius Cassius Hilario, with Varia Tertia also dedicating space while alive, likely indicating plot dimensions.

EDCS-09301851.translation: Cassia Glucera, freedwoman of [a woman named] Mulier, lives. Publius Marcius Alexander, freedman of Pilemon, is buried here.
EDCS-09301851.summary: This epitaph records the burials of Cassia Glucera and Publius Marcius Alexander, with their statuses as freedpersons indicated, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301852.summary: This is a dedication to Titus Catonius Teucer, identified as a patron, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301853.summary: This brief inscription records that Caius Neius Spurius Catulus is alive, possibly for a property marker or a pre-mortem dedication.

EDCS-09301854.translation: Lucius Numisius Celer lives and [something related to] Baebia Augini. Marcus Octavius Dento in the field, 15 feet.
EDCS-09301854.summary: This inscription mentions Lucius Numisius Celer and Baebia Augini, with Marcus Octavius Dento associated with a plot of land measuring 15 feet.

EDCS-09301855.translation: Aba [lives] for herself and for Celsus.
EDCS-09301855.summary: This is a funerary epitaph where Aba dedicates a burial space for herself and for Celsus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301856.translation: Cervaia Coradelia, daughter of Lucius, daughter of Lucius, made this for herself and her freedmen.
EDCS-09301856.summary: This inscription records a woman named Cervaia Coradelia dedicating a monument to herself and her freedmen.

EDCS-09301857.translation: Alive, Lucius Cervius, freedman of the woman, Ivo, made this for himself and his alive wife Cornelia Rustica, and for his alive fellow freedman Lucius Cervius Aieo.
EDCS-09301857.summary: This inscription records Lucius Cervius Ivo, a freedman, dedicating a monument to himself, his wife Cornelia Rustica, and a fellow freedman.

EDCS-09301858.translation: For Lucius Cervius, freedman of Fastus; for Turpio, freedwoman of Cervia Fasti; for Auge.
EDCS-09301858.summary: This inscription lists individuals, likely for funerary purposes, including freedmen and freedwomen connected to Fastus and Cervia Fasti.

EDCS-09301860.summary: This brief inscription is a dedication or memorial from Philomusus for someone named Cicero.

EDCS-09301862.translation: Gaius Ogulnius Ciratus, freedman of Gaius, alive, made this monument for himself and for Ogulnia Hilara; it will not pass to an heir, nor to the heirs of an heir.
EDCS-09301862.summary: This inscription records Gaius Ogulnius Ciratus dedicating a monument for himself and Ogulnia Hilara, stipulating it will not be inherited.

EDCS-09301864.translation: Of the freedman of Caius Messianus, in front, 15 feet.
EDCS-09301864.summary: This inscription specifies a measurement of 15 feet in front of a property belonging to the freedman of Caius Messianus.

EDCS-09301865.translation: For Claudia Tyche, for herself and her husband Marcus Antonius, and for her family: Fadiae Syntyche, her mother; Marcus Antonius Syntychus, freedman; Tiberius Claudius Syntychus; this monument will not pass to an outside heir.
EDCS-09301865.summary: This inscription records Claudia Tyche dedicating a monument for herself, her husband, her mother, and freedmen, with stipulations against outside inheritance.

EDCS-09301866.translation: Alive, Appius Clodius Carpus, for himself and his family, 15 feet in the field.
EDCS-09301866.summary: This inscription records Appius Clodius Carpus dedicating a portion of his land, measuring 15 feet, for himself and his family.

EDCS-09301867.translation: To Clodius, grandson of Lucius, by the judgement of Philargurus, freedman, according to the will.
EDCS-09301867.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Clodius, grandson of Lucius, executed by the freedman Philargurus as per a will.

EDCS-09301868.summary: This inscription is a simple statement of filiation, identifying Clodius as the son of Mani.

EDCS-09301869.translation: Manius Clodius Epapra lives, and Scantia Gemella his wife, for a frontage of 15 feet in every direction.
EDCS-09301869.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the dimensions of a plot of land belonging to Manius Clodius Epapra and his wife Scantia Gemella.

EDCS-09301870.translation: Manius Clodius Epapra lives, and Scantia Gemella his wife, for a field of 15 feet in every direction.
EDCS-09301870.summary: This is a funerary inscription specifying the dimensions of a field belonging to Manius Clodius Epapra and his wife Scantia Gemella.

EDCS-09301871.translation: Clodia, daughter of Manius, of the Pig (tribe?), Manius Clodius and Manius Clodius.
EDCS-09301871.summary: This inscription appears to record familial relationships, possibly related to inheritance or property ownership, mentioning Clodia and two individuals named Manius Clodius.

EDCS-09301872.translation: To Marcus Coelius Alcaeus, freedman of Coelia, and Urbana, freedwoman of Marcus Lorinus Eutyches.
EDCS-09301872.summary: This is a dedication on a monument, honoring Marcus Coelius Alcaeus and Urbana, specifying their relationships as freedpersons to their former owners.

EDCS-09301873.translation: To Marcus Coelius Iucundus, freedman of Marcus, and to Aurelia Primula, daughter of Caius, his wife.
EDCS-09301873.summary: This is a dedication on a monument, honoring Marcus Coelius Iucundus and his wife Aurelia Primula, noting his status as a freedman.

EDCS-09301874.translation: Marcus Coelius Olympus lives, Caecilia Calliste lives, and Marcus Furrus Himero and Magadia Corona.
EDCS-09301874.summary: This inscription records the lives of several individuals, possibly members of a family or household, indicating they are alive.

EDCS-09301875.translation: Lucius Coelius Placidus lives, for himself and for his mother Antestia Pacata, daughter of Lucius, most dutiful, and for his fellow-slave Julia Italica, freedwoman of Caius, in a field of 15 feet and in frontage of 15 feet.
EDCS-09301875.summary: This funerary inscription records Lucius Coelius Placidus dedicating a plot of land to himself, his mother, and a fellow-slave, specifying the dimensions of the property.

EDCS-09301876.translation: Coelia Anus, freedwoman, lived; Tryphera made (this) for herself and for Amaryllis, a freedwoman.
EDCS-09301876.summary: This funerary inscription records that Coelia Anus, a freedwoman, lived, and Tryphera made this monument for herself and another freedwoman, Amaryllis.

EDCS-09301877.translation: Sextus Cominius Hilarus, freedman of Sextus, lived, and Licinia Paeta, daughter of Lucius, his wife.
EDCS-09301877.summary: This funerary inscription records the lives of Sextus Cominius Hilarus, a freedman, and his wife Licinia Paeta.

EDCS-09301878.summary: This is a simple inscription identifying an individual, likely a tomb or property marker for Cominius Nerotis Primus.

EDCS-09301879.translation: V (or 'For') Paulina Communis, daughter of Veratus; Arius Quartus; Hompilius Cornelius Modestus; Cornelius Felix; Andricus Euprepes.
EDCS-09301879.summary: This inscription appears to list several names, possibly indicating a dedication or a group of individuals associated with a monument, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09301880.translation: Viva made this for Gaius Alcidius.
EDCS-09301880.summary: This is a dedication made by Viva for Gaius Alcidius, likely on a tomb or dedication, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09301881.translation: Quintus Pontenius ER (perhaps 'ex rege') with Julia for her best friend.
EDCS-09301881.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Quintus Pontenius and Julia for a close friend, possibly on a tomb or a gift, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09301882.summary: This inscription records the name of Hymnis Frugi, a freedwoman of Corania, likely marking her burial place, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09301883.translation: Cordia, freedwoman of Hilarius, is alive.
EDCS-09301883.summary: This inscription states that Cordia, freedwoman of Hilarius, is alive, likely indicating her survival or a dedication for her well-being, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09301884.summary: This brief inscription states that Cornelius is alive, possibly a votive or a dedication, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09301885.translation: For the spirits of the departed and for his eternal home, Cornelius, while alive, made and dedicated this for himself on the third day before the Kalends of July.
EDCS-09301885.summary: This is a self-dedication for a tomb by Cornelius, specifying the date of dedication as June 29th, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09301886.translation: Alive: Lucius Cornelius Cephalon and Cornelia Mansueta, daughter of Sura; with Tiberius Claudius Hermas, her husband; with Cornelius Fructus, freedman; with Ansius.
EDCS-09301886.summary: This inscription lists several individuals who are alive, likely associated with a family tomb or dedication, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09301887.translation: Deceased: Lucius Cornelius Cirratus, freedman of a woman; Cornelia, freedwoman of Lucius Marcius. Here are buried: Viva; Titus Titius Masculus; Tetitia Vitalis; and Titia Primilla.
EDCS-09301887.summary: This inscription records the deceased Lucius Cornelius Cirratus and Cornelia, and names several individuals buried here, likely on a tomb, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09301889.translation: Alive: Lucius Cornelius Gratus restored at his own expense in front of Eugenia, freedwoman of Lucius Cornelius, who had died, ten feet.
EDCS-09301889.summary: This inscription records Lucius Cornelius Gratus restoring a structure or marking a space of ten feet for Eugenia, a deceased freedwoman, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09301890.translation: Cornelius Ep, freedman of Caius, for Arni and Dama.
EDCS-09301890.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Cornelius Ep, freedman of Caius, dedicating a burial space to Arni and Dama.

EDCS-09301891.translation: To the Divine Manes. For Titus, son of Titus Cornelius Etucivus, and his friend Cocorinus, 20 feet in front.
EDCS-09301891.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Titus, son of Titus Cornelius Etucivus, and his friend Cocorinus, specifying the dimensions of the burial plot.

EDCS-09301892.translation: Publius Cornelius Exoratus is alive for himself and for Rammia Prisca, daughter of Spurius, and Publius Cornelius Firmus, son of Publius, 15 feet in every direction.
EDCS-09301892.summary: This funerary inscription records a burial plot purchased by Publius Cornelius Exoratus for himself and other family members, specifying dimensions.

EDCS-09301894.translation: Lucius Cornelius Fronto is alive. Flora, freedwoman of Loreia Vitalis, is buried here.
EDCS-09301894.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Flora, freedwoman of Loreia Vitalis, established by Lucius Cornelius Fronto.

EDCS-09301895.translation: For Lucius Cornelius Laraotus and Papiria Prima, and Valeria Ocumisa and Livonia, 13 feet in front and 13 feet in the field.
EDCS-09301895.summary: This inscription records the dimensions of a burial plot for Lucius Cornelius Laraotus, Papiria Prima, Valeria Ocumisa, and Livonia.

EDCS-09301896.translation: Caius Cornelius Libens, Cornelia Celsa, his fellow freedwoman, Cornelia Suavis, his daughter, and Caius Cornelius Quietus, his freedman, made this (tomb) alive.
EDCS-09301896.summary: This funerary inscription lists the names of Caius Cornelius Libens, his fellow freedwoman Cornelia Celsa, his daughter Cornelia Suavis, and his freedman Caius Cornelius Quietus, indicating they jointly established the burial.

EDCS-09301897.translation: Cornelius Opelianus Cassianus, freedman of Cassius, (died) the greatest; Caius Messurius Autus, freedman of Caius (died). 15 feet in front.
EDCS-09301897.summary: This inscription records the death of Cornelius Opelianus Cassianus and Caius Messurius Autus, both freedmen, specifying the front dimensions of their burial plot.

EDCS-09301899.translation: Lucius Cornelius Stephanus, freedman of Lucius, for himself and for Helvia Secunda, daughter of Ricci.
EDCS-09301899.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Lucius Cornelius Stephanus, freedman of Lucius, dedicating a burial space to himself and Helvia Secunda.

EDCS-09301900.translation: The Cornelii Zabdae live for themselves and for Aebutia Dapnis, their fellow soldier/partner, 15 feet in the field.
EDCS-09301900.summary: This funerary inscription records that the Cornelii Zabdae established a burial plot of 15 feet in the field for themselves and their partner Aebutia Dapnis.

EDCS-09301901.translation: Helena, buried here for Aevius Philomus, 15 feet in every direction.
EDCS-09301901.summary: This inscription records that Helena is buried here for Aevius Philomus, specifying the dimensions of the burial plot.

EDCS-09301902.translation: Cornelia, daughter of Lucius, made this for herself and her freedmen.
EDCS-09301902.summary: This is a funerary epitaph indicating that Cornelia, daughter of Lucius, dedicated the monument for herself and her freedmen.

EDCS-09301904.translation: To Cornelia Capella, freedwoman of Lucius, and to Natalis.
EDCS-09301904.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Cornelia Capella, a freedwoman of Lucius, and to Natalis.

EDCS-09301905.translation: To Cornelia Nutrix, freedwoman of Publius, by Pompeia Honorata, daughter of Cnaeus.
EDCS-09301905.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to Cornelia Nutrix, freedwoman of Publius, by Pompeia Honorata.

EDCS-09301906.translation: The bones are located of Cornelia Phyllis.
EDCS-09301906.summary: This is a funerary inscription stating the location of the remains of Cornelia Phyllis.

EDCS-09301907.translation: To Cornelia Quarta, daughter of Quintus; to Cornelius Mettellus; to Cornelia Maxima; to Cornelia Exorata; to Annius Verus; to Cornelius Verus.
EDCS-09301907.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, including members of the Cornelia and Cornelius families, likely commemorating them.

EDCS-09301908.translation: Cornelia Secunda, daughter of Titus, the only wife of Frugi, buried here. Oblivion of all things, death.
EDCS-09301908.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Cornelia Secunda, wife of Frugi, reflecting on mortality.

EDCS-09301909.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, possibly a dedication or epitaph, from Cornelia to someone named Valeria.

EDCS-09301910.translation: Cornelia Ursa, freedwoman of Frugi, is buried here. In front 12 feet, in the land 15 feet.
EDCS-09301910.summary: This is a funerary epitaph specifying the burial plot dimensions for Cornelia Ursa, freedwoman of Frugi.

EDCS-09301912.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Quintus Cossinius Pudentis, aged 21 years, 2 months, 16 days. Cossinia Victorina, to her most dutiful son.
EDCS-09301912.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Cossinius Pudentis, erected by his mother Cossinia Victorina, dating to his youth.

EDCS-09301913.translation: Crassia Maxuma, daughter of Marcus, is buried here. 15 feet in all directions.
EDCS-09301913.summary: This is a funerary epitaph specifying the burial plot dimensions for Crassia Maxuma, daughter of Marcus.

EDCS-09301914.translation: Onius A. Mus died. Arepereius Canax [erected this monument].
EDCS-09301914.summary: This inscription records the death of Onius A. Mus, likely with a dedication by Arepereius Canax, possibly on a tombstone.

EDCS-09301915.translation: Usa made this monument for herself from her own means while alive, for her patronino and Pi; it will not pass to heirs, nor this burial place.
EDCS-09301915.summary: This is a self-funded funerary monument erected by Usa for herself and others, stipulating it is not inheritable.

EDCS-09301916.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Candidus, friend of Caius Cummius Nepos, [erected this for him].
EDCS-09301916.summary: This is a dedication to the Divine Spirits by Candidus for his friend Caius Cummius Nepos, likely on a tomb.

EDCS-09301917.translation: Titus Curtilius Aesopus lived. He made this monument for himself, his family, and Iulia Aestas; it will not pass to heirs. In front, [space] feet; in the field, [space] feet.
EDCS-09301917.summary: This funerary inscription by Titus Curtilius Aesopus for himself and his kin specifies dimensions and a non-hereditary clause.

EDCS-09301918.translation: Aulus Curtius Zosimus and Curtia Prisca [made this monument] for themselves and their family. In the field, 15 feet.
EDCS-09301918.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Aulus Curtius Zosimus and Curtia Prisca for their household, specifying plot dimensions.

EDCS-09301919.translation: [Text illegible]. Curvia Scan [made this monument] for Urbanae. She rests... and for her patron OV.
EDCS-09301919.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely records a burial and dedication to Urbanae and a patron.

EDCS-09301920.summary: This is a simple funerary marker for a freedwoman named Cytheris.

EDCS-09301921.translation: Publius, the freedman, Davus of the Palatine tribe.
EDCS-09301921.summary: This inscription identifies Publius, a freedman belonging to the Palatine tribe.

EDCS-09301922.translation: Decumina, the wife, made [this] while alive.
EDCS-09301922.summary: This funerary inscription states that Decumina, a wife, commissioned her own monument during her lifetime.

EDCS-09301923.translation: Lucius Decumius, son of Lucius, made [this]. In front, 12 feet; in the field, 12 feet.
EDCS-09301923.summary: This inscription records Lucius Decumius, son of Lucius, as the builder of a monument with specified dimensions.

EDCS-09301924.translation: And Publius Decumius Giamillus, freedman of Titus, and Chrestus, 5 and 10 years old.
EDCS-09301924.summary: This inscription records the ages of two individuals, Giamillus and Chrestus, who were freedmen of Titus.

EDCS-09301925.translation: To Philemon Frugi, freedman of Sextus Didius.
EDCS-09301925.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Philemon Frugi, a freedman of Sextus Didius.

EDCS-09301926.translation: Nigella, freedwoman of Sextus Didius, lives, and Diochares, freedman of Sextus Didius, lives, for himself and for his deceased patron Salvius, freedman of Sextus Didius, and for his deceased son Iucundus, freedman of Sextus Didius.
EDCS-09301926.summary: This funerary inscription records the lives of Nigella and Diochares, freedmen of Sextus Didius, and commemorates their deceased patron Salvius and son Iucundus.

EDCS-09301927.translation: To Agrippina Didiena, daughter of Caius, wife and daughter.
EDCS-09301927.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Agrippina Didiena, daughter of Caius, likely by her husband and/or father.

EDCS-09301928.translation: Dimudius Lerissus lives, 15 feet in front.
EDCS-09301928.summary: This inscription marks a property boundary, indicating the dimensions of a plot associated with Dimudius Lerissus.

EDCS-09301929.translation: Aulus Dinius for himself and for the arch, his wife's son.
EDCS-09301929.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Aulus Dinius for himself and an arch, possibly indicating his familial relationship.

EDCS-09301931.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Dio, a freedwoman of Lucius.

EDCS-09301933.summary: This inscription records the age of Diophantus, likely a funerary dedication.

EDCS-09301934.translation: And to Dio Secundus, formerly of Arilius Felix.
EDCS-09301934.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Dio Secundus, noting his former association with Arilius Felix.

EDCS-09301935.translation: Lucius Do, freedman, made it for his wife, Lucius, freedman.
EDCS-09301935.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Lucius Do, a freedman, for his wife, also identified as a freedman.

EDCS-09301936.translation: Lucius Domitius Fuscus, freedman of Lucius, lives on this spot for 15 feet in front.
EDCS-09301936.summary: This funerary epitaph records the burial space allocated to Lucius Domitius Fuscus, a freedman, with a measurement of 15 feet extending forward.

EDCS-09301937.translation: To Titus Domitius Optatus, freedman of Titus Domitius Secundus.
EDCS-09301937.summary: This is a dedication to Titus Domitius Optatus, a freedman, likely setting up a tomb or monument for himself or his patron.

EDCS-09301938.summary: A very brief epitaph simply stating the name Domitius Primus, implying he is deceased and his memory endures.

EDCS-09301940.translation: Quintus Egnatius Philodamus, freedman of Quintus, is buried here, 10 feet in every direction.
