EDCS-09301940.summary: This epitaph marks the burial plot of Quintus Egnatius Philodamus, a freedman, specifying a square burial space of 10 feet on each side.

EDCS-09301941.translation: Lucius Elpius Secundus for himself and for his fellow-soldier (or partner) Aelia Successa.
EDCS-09301941.summary: This funerary inscription records Lucius Elpius Secundus dedicating a plot for himself and Aelia Successa, his contubernalis, likely a spouse or long-term partner.

EDCS-09301942.translation: Gaius Ennius Rufus, son of Gaius, is the heir.
EDCS-09301942.summary: This inscription identifies Gaius Ennius Rufus, son of Gaius, as the heir, likely related to a property or inheritance.

EDCS-09301943.translation: Gaius Ennius Tarula, son of Gaius, made this while alive for himself and his family, 15 feet in every direction.
EDCS-09301943.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Gaius Ennius Tarula for himself and his family, specifying a burial plot of 15 feet in all directions, likely from the late Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-09301944.translation: Titus Vale[rius Ephebus], freedman of Titus, [perhaps a craftsman]? L(ucius) Vitella, daughter of Lucius. Valerius Epaphroditus.
EDCS-09301944.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription listing at least three individuals, one of whom may have been a craftsman.

EDCS-09301945.summary: A simple funerary epitaph announcing the death of Eratia Sexta Eroubila.

EDCS-09301946.summary: This inscription likely refers to a funerary monument or dedication made by or for Lucius Eroneius Auginus, a freedman.

EDCS-09301947.translation: To the freedwoman, daughter of a woman, her patron, Eroneia Secunda Lepida.
EDCS-09301947.summary: This is a dedication to Eroneia Secunda Lepida, who is described as a freedwoman, daughter of a woman (potentially referencing her own status or her mother's), and patron.

EDCS-09301948.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the deity Eros, likely from a freedman.

EDCS-09301949.translation: Eros, freedman of Heraclida, lives on.
EDCS-09301949.summary: This epitaph records the continued existence or memory of Eros, the freedman of Heraclida.

EDCS-09301950.translation: Via, daughter of Caius, requested by the decurion by will for herself and her family.
EDCS-09301950.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up by a woman, Via, likely for herself and her family, as arranged in a will.

EDCS-09301951.translation: Lucius, freedman of F(abius), is buried here; he made this for himself and his wife while alive.
EDCS-09301951.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Lucius, a freedman, for himself and his wife during their lifetime.

EDCS-09301952.translation: Eulogius, freedman of Bacchis, has passed away. Quietus, freedwoman of Lucius, has passed away.
EDCS-09301952.summary: This epitaph records the deaths of two individuals, Eulogius and Quietus, identified by their patrons.

EDCS-09301953.translation: To the deceased Marcus Fabius Bassus, patron, with his [---] and [---], Marcus Fabius Firmus, freedman, made [this] while alive; to the deceased Marcellina, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-09301953.summary: This funerary monument is dedicated to the patron Marcus Fabius Bassus and his freedman Marcus Fabius Firmus, as well as Marcellina, daughter of Marcus.

EDCS-09301954.translation: Lucius Fabius Celer, son of Lucius, of the Papiria tribe, [a plot] of 15 feet.
EDCS-09301954.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot of 15 feet belonging to Lucius Fabius Celer.

EDCS-09301955.translation: Gaius Fabius Stacte made this at his own expense.
EDCS-09301955.summary: This inscription records a construction or dedication made by Gaius Fabius Stacte at his own expense.

EDCS-09301956.translation: Maia, slave of Gaius Fabius Cotta, has passed away. Alcestis, daughter [of Maia], [a plot] of 15 feet in front.
EDCS-09301956.summary: This epitaph records the death of Maia, a slave, and specifies a 15-foot plot for her daughter Alcestis.

EDCS-09301957.translation: Lucius Fabius Demosthenes, freedman of Lucius, and Fabia Lychnis, freedwoman of Lucius, [a plot] of 15 feet in front.
EDCS-09301957.summary: This funerary inscription marks a 15-foot plot for Lucius Fabius Demosthenes and Fabia Lychnis, both freedpersons of Lucius.

EDCS-09301958.translation: Lucius Fabius Faustus lives on for himself and his wife, for fifteen feet in all directions.
EDCS-09301958.summary: This inscription records an funerary monument for Lucius Fabius Faustus and his wife, stating the dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-09301959.translation: Iaso, freedman of Lucius Fabius Strabo, lives on for himself and his family, for fifteen feet in the front.
EDCS-09301959.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument for Iaso, freedman of Lucius Fabius Strabo, and his family.

EDCS-09301960.translation: Lives. Marcus Fabius Stabilio, for his father Marcus Fabius Philargurus, and for his wife Pompeia Tertullina, daughter of Lucius, and for his wet-nurse Fabia Rustica, and for his mother Fabia Salvia. In front 10 feet.
EDCS-09301960.summary: A funerary inscription that records a man dedicating a tomb to his father, wife, wet-nurse, and mother, with a measurement likely indicating the width of the plot.

EDCS-09301961.translation: Turpio, son of Lucius Fabius, lives on.
EDCS-09301961.summary: This inscription records the name of Turpio, son of Lucius Fabius, likely on a tomb.

EDCS-09301962.translation: For Marcus Fabricius Ameno, freedman of Marcus, and Fabricia Tertulla, freedwoman of Marcus.
EDCS-09301962.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Marcus Fabricius Ameno and Fabricia Tertulla, both freedpersons.

EDCS-09301963.translation: For Titus Fadius Fro, freedman of Titus, for his father Titus Fadius, for his brother Titus Fadius, son of Titus, lives on for Fadiae, freedwoman of Tiberius.
EDCS-09301963.summary: This inscription records a familial dedication, honoring multiple members including a freedwoman named Fadiae.

EDCS-09301964.translation: Titus Fadius Alaucus, freedman of Titus, is buried here, for feet in all directions.
EDCS-09301964.summary: This inscription records the burial of Titus Fadius Alaucus, a freedman, indicating the dimensions of his burial plot.

EDCS-09301965.translation: For Sextus Fadius Batullus, freedman of E., aged fifteen years.
EDCS-09301965.summary: This inscription records the name and age of Sextus Fadius Batullus, a freedman, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-09301966.translation: For himself and for his deceased companion Munnia Primula, freedwoman of Lucius, and for his deceased mother Hilara, freedwoman and co-freedwoman, and for his living mother Ofilia Faustae, mother of Munnia.
EDCS-09301966.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Caius Fadius Eranus, freedman of Saturionis, to himself and several female relatives.

EDCS-09301967.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For his son Sextus Fadius Eutychianus, who lived 11 years, 7 months, 5 days, and for his most virtuous wife Fadiae Vicanae, Marcus Ulpius Eutychus [dedicated this].
EDCS-09301967.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Marcus Ulpius Eutychus to his deceased son and wife, providing their ages and epithets.

EDCS-09301968.translation: Caius Fadius Hilarus, freedman of Caius; Daedalus; Lucius.
EDCS-09301968.summary: This inscription lists names, likely of freedmen and their patrons or family members, possibly on a tomb.

EDCS-09301969.translation: Titus Fadius Lucrio, freedman of Titus, [erected this] while alive for himself and for his patron Titus Fadius Capito, and for Titus Fadius Amphion, freedman of Titus, after his death.
EDCS-09301969.summary: This funerary epitaph records the dedication of a burial plot by a freedman for himself and his patron and another freedman, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-09301970.translation: Titus Fadius Montanus, while alive, for himself and his family, 30 feet in front.
EDCS-09301970.summary: This inscription specifies the dimensions of a burial plot purchased by Titus Fadius Montanus for his family, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-09301971.translation: by the arrangement of Titus Fadius Silonis.
EDCS-09301971.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, likely referring to an administrative arrangement or property division concerning Titus Fadius Silonis.

EDCS-09301972.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, likely part of a dedication or epitaph for a freedwoman named Fadia.

EDCS-09301973.translation: Fadia Accepta, freedwoman of Titus, lived for 15 feet in every direction.
EDCS-09301973.summary: This epitaph records the burial dimensions for Fadia Accepta, a freedwoman, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-09301974.translation: Fadius Amphion for his wife and freedwoman Fadia Quarta, 30 feet in front and 30 feet in the field.
EDCS-09301974.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial plot allocated by Fadius Amphion for his wife and freedwoman, Fadia Quarta, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-09301975.translation: Lucius Fadius Solimarus, freedman of Lucius, died; Falia Puppa, freedwoman of Sextus, lived; Lucius Fadius Atticus, freedman of Lucius, lived; 15 feet in every direction in the field. Lucius Fadius Solimarus, freedman of Lucius, died; Falia Puppa, freedwoman of Sextus, lived; Lucius Fadius Atticus, freedman of Lucius, lived; 15 feet in every direction in the field.
EDCS-09301975.summary: This fragmented epitaph records the deaths and burials of Lucius Fadius Solimarus and the lives of Falia Puppa and Lucius Fadius Atticus, specifying plot dimensions, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-09301976.translation: for Faustilla, a freedwoman, a companion in life, after death.
EDCS-09301976.summary: This fragment appears to be part of an epitaph or dedication for Faustilla, a freedwoman and companion, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-09301977.translation: for himself and for Frugi, and for Faustus
EDCS-09301977.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, likely a dedication or funerary monument specifying beneficiaries including Faustus and Frugi.

EDCS-09301978.translation: Felicis Diomiae, freedwoman of Caius, Scintus, lived.
EDCS-09301978.summary: This fragmented epitaph records that Diomia Scintus, freedwoman of Caius, and Felicis lived, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-09301979.translation: To Felix, wife of Pompeius Tanaquillus, and in memory of Pompeius Germanus, father-in-law, 18 feet in the land.
EDCS-09301979.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication to a wife and father-in-law, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09301980.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph identifying a freedwoman and her patron, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301981.translation: For Firmius, for himself and for Asia, his wife, freedwoman of Terentia Lucia, and for Coelia, daughter of Lucia, who died at 17 years.
EDCS-09301981.summary: This funerary inscription records a self-dedication along with his wife and a deceased young woman, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301983.translation: Caius Flavius Felix, freedman of Flavia Paederotis, for himself and for his freedwoman, living; 15 feet in front and 12 feet in the land.
EDCS-09301983.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording a self-dedication and for his freedwoman, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301984.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely a dedication or funerary epitaph, to Sextus Flavius Fuficius Aelius.

EDCS-09301985.summary: This is a very brief funerary inscription identifying a wife, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301986.translation: Valerius Onesimus to Fortunata, his wife, best freedwoman of Caius.
EDCS-09301986.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication from a husband to his wife, who was also a freedwoman, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301987.translation: To Titus Fotidius Secundus, Fotidia Coris, and Fotidia Gemella.
EDCS-09301987.summary: This inscription records a dedication to several individuals, likely family members, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301988.translation: To Quintus Fuficius, freedman of Quintus, and to Iucunda, freedwoman of Quintus.
EDCS-09301988.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication to two freedmen, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301989.translation: To [Quintus Fufius?], son of the grandfather and Quintus, freedman of Veda, Laelia Aucta, freedwoman of Publius.
EDCS-09301989.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription potentially recording multiple individuals and their relationships, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09301990.translation: Marcus Fulvius Hilarus, freedman of Marcus Fulvius, to his freedman Antiochus. Fulvia lives.
EDCS-09301990.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication of a monument by a freedman to his freedman, with a note about a living individual named Fulvia.

EDCS-09301991.translation: Marcus Fulvius Maius Cerdus, son of Titus.
EDCS-09301991.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragmentary dedication or an epitaph for Marcus Fulvius Maius Cerdus.

EDCS-09301992.translation: To Gaius Fulvius Quartio, from Quintus Iulius Crescentes.
EDCS-09301992.summary: This is likely a dedication or a funerary inscription from Quintus Iulius Crescentes to Gaius Fulvius Quartio.

EDCS-09301993.translation: Fulvius Tata and Flora, freedwoman of Lucius, live for themselves and their family.
EDCS-09301993.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording that Fulvius Tata and his wife Flora, a freedwoman, have established a monument for themselves and their descendants.

EDCS-09301995.translation: Furia Moschis, daughter of Caius, fifteen feet in all directions; this monument shall not pass to an heir.
EDCS-09301995.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Furia Moschis, daughter of Caius, defining the dimensions of her tomb and stipulating that it is not inheritable.

EDCS-09301996.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Gaberia Philetis, a most dutiful freedwoman of Gaberia Tigrix.
EDCS-09301996.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the memory of Gaberia Philetis, a devoted freedwoman.

EDCS-09301997.translation: Lucius Gavidius Pollio, son of Lucius, of the Papiria tribe, to his brother. Lucius Gavidius, son of Lucius, nephew of Quintus, lives for himself and his family.
EDCS-09301997.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Lucius Gavidius to his brother Lucius Gavidius Pollio and also serves as a self-dedication for the surviving Lucius Gavidius and his descendants.

EDCS-09301998.summary: This is a very brief funerary inscription, likely an epitaph, for Publius Gavius Alexander.

EDCS-09302000.translation: Marcus Fulvius Diophantus, freedman of Marcus, and Marcus Gavius Eleutherus live.
EDCS-09302000.summary: This funerary inscription records the existence of two individuals, Marcus Fulvius Diophantus (freedman of Marcus Fulvius) and Marcus Gavius Eleutherus.

EDCS-09302001.translation: Lucius Gavius Secundus, son of Titus, fifteen feet in all directions, lives.
EDCS-09302001.summary: This funerary inscription records the dimensions of the tomb and the survival of Lucius Gavius Secundus, son of Titus.

EDCS-09302002.translation: By the decision of Gavia Tertia, daughter of Lucius, and of Lucius Cornelius Firmus.
EDCS-09302002.summary: This inscription records a decision made by Gavia Tertia and Lucius Cornelius Firmus, likely related to a legal or administrative matter.

EDCS-09302003.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Marcus Geganus Pamphilus, likely an epitaph or a dedication on a monument.

EDCS-09302004.translation: By the decision of Genialis Iucundus.
EDCS-09302004.summary: This inscription records a decision made by Genialis Iucundus, likely related to a legal or administrative matter.

EDCS-09302005.translation: To Giaria Atoliso, daughter of Quintus.
EDCS-09302005.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Giaria Atoliso, likely an epitaph or a dedication on a monument.

EDCS-09302006.translation: To the Divine Shades. Aurunceius Rufus placed [this] for his most devoted friend Granius Zosimus.
EDCS-09302006.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Aurunceius Rufus set up a monument for his friend Granius Zosimus.

EDCS-09302007.translation: Gaius Helvius Eros, freedman of Gaius, is buried in this tomb.
EDCS-09302007.summary: This is a funerary inscription stating that Gaius Helvius Eros, a freedman, is buried here.

EDCS-09302008.translation: Marcus Helvius Hermogenes, freedman of Marcus, and Marcus Helvius Ingenuus, freedman of Marcus, aged 18, are buried here.
EDCS-09302008.summary: This is a funerary inscription for two individuals, Marcus Helvius Hermogenes and Marcus Helvius Ingenuus, both freedmen of Marcus.

EDCS-09302009.translation: In memory of Decimus Herennius Asellius, 15 feet in every direction.
EDCS-09302009.summary: This inscription marks the burial plot of Decimus Herennius Asellius, indicating the extent of his funerary space.

EDCS-09302011.translation: Lucius Herennius Philippus [for] himself and his family, while alive.
EDCS-09302011.summary: This is a funerary inscription indicating that Lucius Herennius Philippus prepared a tomb for himself and his family during his lifetime.

EDCS-09302012.translation: Lucius Herennuleius Amoenus, freedman of Lucius, and Ingenua [are buried here] while alive.
EDCS-09302012.summary: This is a funerary inscription indicating that Lucius Herennuleius Amoenus, a freedman, and Ingenua prepared a tomb for themselves during their lifetime.

EDCS-09302013.translation: Herennuleia Optata, freedwoman of Publius, made this in her own lifetime for herself and her husband at her own expense, since it will not follow to the heir.
EDCS-09302013.summary: This inscription records a funerary dedication made by a freedwoman for herself and her husband, likely dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-09302014.translation: Hilar, and his family, died; Gaius Vaternius Muso, patron, [made this].
EDCS-09302014.summary: This inscription records the death of Hilar and states that his patron, Gaius Vaternius Muso, set up the monument, likely a tombstone, probably in the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-09302015.translation: Hilara, freedwoman of Lucius, [belonging to] Rubrius.
EDCS-09302015.summary: This inscription seems to indicate ownership or association, possibly on a funerary monument, for Hilara, a freedwoman of Lucius, connected to a Rubrius, dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-09302016.translation: To Titus Hilarius, freedman of Curt Atticus.
EDCS-09302016.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Titus Hilarius, a freedman of Curt Atticus, likely for a tombstone or a similar funerary marker from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-09302017.translation: Lucius Hirius, son of Lucius, made this for Sextius, for himself and for his daughter Maxima, daughter of Marcus, and for his freedwoman Aucia.
EDCS-09302017.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument set up by Lucius Hirius for himself, his family, and his freedwoman, likely dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-09302019.summary: This is likely an incomplete inscription, possibly a name on a tombstone or a dedication, for Publius Hordionius, dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-09302020.translation: Hordionius Barnaeus, freedman, for himself and for Titus Hordionius.
EDCS-09302020.summary: This inscription records a funerary dedication made by Hordionius Barnaeus, a freedman, for himself and Titus Hordionius, dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-09302021.summary: This inscription appears to record two names, possibly for a shared tomb or a dedication, of Marcus Hordionius and Marcus Drienus, likely from the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-09302022.translation: Lucius Hortensius, by the arbitration of Caius Caecilius, Lucius Hortensius.
EDCS-09302022.summary: This inscription seems to record a legal or administrative matter resolved by arbitration, involving Lucius Hortensius and Caius Caecilius, dating to the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-09302023.translation: To Lucius Hortensius Epigonus, [from] Iulia Heraclea.
EDCS-09302023.summary: This inscription is a dedication from Iulia Heraclea to Lucius Hortensius Epigonus, likely on a funerary monument or a gift, dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-09302024.translation: Frugi Surillius, brother of Quintus' freedwoman Hospita.
EDCS-09302024.summary: This is a funerary dedication naming Frugi Surillius as the brother of the deceased, Quintus' freedwoman Hospita.

EDCS-09302025.summary: This is a very brief funerary inscription identifying Ian as the freedman of Lucius.

EDCS-09302026.translation: Titus Iaronius, freedman of Vibius, is buried here.
EDCS-09302026.summary: This is a funerary inscription stating that Titus Iaronius, freedman of Vibius, is buried here.

EDCS-09302027.summary: This is a funerary or memorial inscription stating that Quintus Legienus Quadratus is alive, possibly indicating he is still living or that his memory is preserved.

EDCS-09302029.translation: Lucius Ignius, freedman of Lucius, is buried here in front, 15 feet.
EDCS-09302029.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Lucius Ignius, freedman of Lucius, specifying the burial plot size of 15 feet in front.

EDCS-09302030.translation: Catulus, freedman of Sextus, is alive.
EDCS-09302030.summary: This funerary or memorial inscription states that Catulus, freedman of Sextus, is alive.

EDCS-09302031.translation: Quintus Ignius Merops is alive, for himself and for his wife Ignia Helpis and for his family.
EDCS-09302031.summary: This funerary inscription states that Quintus Ignius Merops is alive, dedicating the monument to himself, his wife Ignia Helpis, and his family.

EDCS-09302032.translation: Quintus Ignius Pullo, freedman of Caius, and his patron A. Pubrensius Urisca, a freedwoman, are alive.
EDCS-09302032.summary: This inscription states that Quintus Ignius Pullo, freedman of Caius, and his patron A. Pubrensius Urisca, a freedwoman, are alive.

EDCS-09302033.translation: Died Titus Indutus Arabus. Vireia Verberi Secunda, mother, in the field, 15 feet.
EDCS-09302033.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Titus Indutus Arabus and also mentions Vireia Verberi Secunda, his mother, and specifies a plot size of 15 feet in the field.

EDCS-09302035.translation: Irpiena Rufa, freedwoman of Marcus, alive, for herself and for her brother Marcus Irpienus Verana, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-09302035.summary: This funerary inscription states that Irpiena Rufa, freedwoman of Marcus, is alive, dedicating the monument to herself and her brother Marcus Irpienus Verana, who was also a freedman of Marcus.

EDCS-09302036.translation: He took care to have this made for himself and for his patron, Gaius Julius.
EDCS-09302036.summary: This inscription records a private dedication or construction undertaken by an individual for himself and his patron, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302038.translation: Quintus Julius, son of Quintus Julius, has a monument suitable for his 57 years, erected by his freedwoman Idonia.
EDCS-09302038.summary: This inscription is part of a tomb monument, specifying the age of Quintus Julius and indicating it was funded by his freedwoman, Idonia, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302039.translation: Alco, freedman of Gaius Julius Aquila, 12 feet in front.
EDCS-09302039.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot, indicating the dimensions of the frontage and identifying the deceased as Alco, freedman of Gaius Julius Aquila, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302040.translation: Gaius Julius made this for his wife, [---] ASTA [---] IIII A S [---].
EDCS-09302040.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by Gaius Julius to his wife, with some parts of the names and details illegible, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302041.translation: Gaius Julius Blandus, freedman of Gaius Julius, 12 feet in front and 13 feet inside.
EDCS-09302041.summary: This inscription marks a tomb, specifying the dimensions of the burial plot and identifying the owner as Gaius Julius Blandus, freedman of Gaius Julius, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302042.translation: For Quintus Julius, son of Caies, and Sontoseia Secunda.
EDCS-09302042.summary: This inscription is a dedication or memorial for Quintus Julius and Sontoseia Secunda, likely a family tomb or memorial from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302043.translation: Lucius Julius Clemens, son of Gaius Julius, lives on; died Gaius Julius Quadratus, father, aged 150; died Cornelia Iulla, daughter of Gaius Julius, his sister; died Marcus Julius Quartus, son of Gaius Julius, brother.
EDCS-09302043.summary: This is a complex funerary inscription commemorating multiple members of the Julius family, including a father, mother, and brother, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period, with an unusually high age recorded for the father.

EDCS-09302044.translation: For Quintus Julius Congenniccus, son of Tarsaeus; Titus Julius Pedo, son of Quintus; Lucius Julius Niger, son of Quintus; Sextus Julius Sextius, son of Quintus; Marcus Julius Severus, son of Quintus. Statius, freedman, to his patrons.
EDCS-09302044.summary: This inscription is a dedication by a freedman named Statius to his multiple patrons from the Julius family, indicating their names and lineage, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302045.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Iulia Potentina, daughter of Quintus, to her freedman.
EDCS-09302045.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Manes (departed spirits) by Iulia Potentina for her freedman, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302046.translation: Lives Gaius Julius Epitropus and his freedwoman Coelia Prisca. 15 feet in front. Buried here.
EDCS-09302046.summary: This inscription marks a burial plot, indicating it is for Gaius Julius Epitropus and his freedwoman Coelia Prisca, with dimensions provided, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302047.translation: Gaius Julius Erasus, freedman of Bargates, lived for 15 feet in every direction from the death of Julia, and from the death of Gaius Julius Aristio.
EDCS-09302047.summary: This inscription is a funerary marker for Gaius Julius Erasus, indicating the dimensions of his burial plot and referencing the deaths of Julia and Gaius Julius Aristio, likely family members.

EDCS-09302048.translation: Place of burial for the family of freedmen and freedwomen of Erotis, freedman of Gaius Julius Auctus.
EDCS-09302048.summary: This inscription designates a burial place for the freedmen and freedwomen belonging to the family of Erotis, a freedman of Gaius Julius Auctus.

EDCS-09302049.translation: To Gaius Julius Lucius, son of Erdanus.
EDCS-09302049.summary: This is a dedication or memorial inscription for Gaius Julius Lucius, son of Erdanus.

EDCS-09302050.translation: To the Divine Shades. Julius Eutyches made this for his dearest freedman, Julius Severianus.
EDCS-09302050.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Julius Eutyches for his beloved freedman, Julius Severianus.

EDCS-09302051.translation: Gaius Julius Helles, freedman of Isargyri, lived for himself and Verecunda, a freedwoman, for 20 feet in front and 15 feet in depth.
EDCS-09302051.summary: This inscription marks the burial plot of Gaius Julius Helles, a freedman, and his freedwoman Verecunda, specifying the dimensions of their burial space.

EDCS-09302052.translation: For Lucius Julius Hilarus and his family.
EDCS-09302052.summary: This is a dedication or memorial for Lucius Julius Hilarus and his relatives.

EDCS-09302053.translation: Gaius Julius Inachus, freedman of Licinius, for himself and for Quinta, freedwoman of Veienton, his wife.
EDCS-09302053.summary: This inscription records a burial plot purchased or designated by Gaius Julius Inachus, a freedman, for himself and his wife Quinta, a freedwoman.

EDCS-09302054.translation: Gaius Julius Iucundus, freedman of Celadus, and Anteros, his brother [and freedman?].
EDCS-09302054.summary: This inscription likely commemorates Gaius Julius Iucundus, a freedman, and his brother Anteros, possibly also a freedman, perhaps on a shared tomb.

EDCS-09302055.translation: Gaius Julius Licinus for Helena, his wife, and for his fellow freedwoman.
EDCS-09302055.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Gaius Julius Licinus for his wife Helena and another fellow freedwoman.

EDCS-09302056.translation: For Gaius Julius Lucrio, freedman of Bargatis.
EDCS-09302056.summary: This is a dedication or memorial inscription for Gaius Julius Lucrio, a freedman of Bargatis.

EDCS-09302057.translation: Gaius Julius Niger, son of Gaius, dutiful, and Iulia Condicio, daughter of Gaius, thrifty.
EDCS-09302057.summary: This inscription names two individuals, likely a brother and sister, without specifying a monument type.

EDCS-09302058.translation: Gaius Julius Niger, son of Sextus, is alive.
EDCS-09302058.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Julius Niger, indicating he is alive, possibly for a tombstone intended for later use.

EDCS-09302059.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Iulius Fuscus, freedman of Iulia Obauchia, to his most dutiful brother.
EDCS-09302059.summary: This dedication is a tomb monument by a freedman to his brother, likely in the imperial period.

EDCS-09302060.translation: To Gaius Julius Olympos, freedman, from Suriae in the town of Amme.
EDCS-09302060.summary: This is a dedication to a freedman named Gaius Julius Olympos, originating from the town of Amme in Syria.

EDCS-09302062.translation: To Gaius Julius Philemon and Pompeia Rivintia.
EDCS-09302062.summary: This inscription records a dedication or memorial to two individuals, Gaius Julius Philemon and Pompeia Rivintia.

EDCS-09302063.translation: Lucius Julius Primigenius, freedman of Lucius, is alive, for himself and his family, on all sides.
EDCS-09302063.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Lucius Julius Primigenius, intended for himself and his family, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09302064.translation: On the death of Quintus Julius Barbarus, son of Gaius, of the Voltinian tribe, an aedile of the colony of Dinia Lub. Quintus Julius Saecularis, for himself and his patron, is alive. Iulia Saecularis Urbana, for herself and her patron Philargyrus, freedman of Publius Attius Erotis, is alive. Attia, freedwoman of Publius, mother.
EDCS-09302064.summary: This complex funerary monument commemorates Quintus Julius Barbarus, an aedile, and records other family members and patrons, likely from a Roman colony.

EDCS-09302065.translation: Gaius Terentius Cerialis, alive for Gaius Julius Sentinus, son of Spurius, and for his wife R[--]tía Secunda, and for Gaius Valerius Celsinus, and for Iulia Peregrina, daughter of Iulia Quieta Secundilla, daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-09302065.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Gaius Terentius Cerialis for several individuals, including family members and possibly a patron, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09302066.translation: Lucius Julius Spendo, alive, for himself and his family.
EDCS-09302066.summary: This inscription is a tomb marker for Lucius Julius Spendo and his family, indicating he is alive, possibly for a future burial.

EDCS-09302067.translation: Quintus Julius Statius, freedman of Quintus, made [this] for himself and his family, [to the gods] etc.
EDCS-09302067.summary: This inscription records the construction of a tomb by Quintus Julius Statius, a freedman, for himself and his family, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09302068.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Quintus Julius Statius, freedman of Quintus, made this while alive for himself and for Graeceia Praesta, freedwoman of Publius, also alive, and for Quintus Julius Natalinus, freedman of Quintus, also alive, and for Julia Optata, freedwoman of Statius, also alive.
EDCS-09302068.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Quintus Julius Statius for himself and his family members, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09302069.translation: For Quintus Julius, freedman of Quintus, and for his wife Roscia Secundina.
EDCS-09302069.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Julius and his wife, Roscia Secundina, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09302070.translation: Caius Julius Verna, freedman of Heleni, for himself and for the deceased Marcia Rufa, freedwoman of Lucius.
EDCS-09302070.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Caius Julius Verna for himself and Marcia Rufa, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09302071.translation: Is alive for Caius Julius Viator, son of Caius, and for his wife Licinia Prisca, freedwoman of Lucius; and for his ward Nassius Eutycus and friend; 15 feet in the field.
EDCS-09302071.summary: This inscription appears to be a boundary marker or a declaration of ownership, also mentioning individuals potentially associated with the land, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09302072.translation: Iulia Aelion, freedwoman of Anteronis, is alive.
EDCS-09302072.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulia Aelion, a freedwoman, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09302073.translation: Is alive 10 feet in all directions; Iulia Aucta, freedwoman of Antatas.
EDCS-09302073.summary: This inscription seems to indicate a burial plot or property boundary, proclaiming the continued existence of Iulia Aucta, a freedwoman, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09302074.translation: Is alive for his wife Iulia Calliopa, and for Caius Julius Peregrinus, who died at 16 years of age.
EDCS-09302074.summary: This is a funerary epitaph that commemorates Iulia Calliopa and a young boy, Caius Julius Peregrinus, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09302075.translation: For Iulia Corinthis, daughter of Quintus, and for Iulius Decumanus and Iulia Secunda; 21 feet on the front, 20 feet in the field.
EDCS-09302075.summary: This inscription appears to mark a property or burial area, listing several individuals named Iulia and Iulius, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09302076.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Rusticius Saturninus for his dearest wife Iulia Hen, and for himself, on her property.
EDCS-09302076.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Lucius Rusticius Saturninus for his wife Iulia Hen and himself, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09302077.translation: Caius Julius Narbonensis, freedman, set this up for his patroness Iulia Heros, freedwoman of Caius, and for his own [family].
EDCS-09302077.summary: This inscription records the dedication made by a freedman for his patroness and his own household, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09302078.translation: Iulia Olympi, freedwoman, Ingenua Frugi, modest, is buried here.
EDCS-09302078.summary: This inscription is a tombstone for Iulia Olympi, a freedwoman, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302079.translation: Iulia Maxuma, daughter of Gaius, for herself and for her son Gaius Julius Genialis.
EDCS-09302079.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Iulia Maxuma for herself and her son, likely on a funerary monument.

EDCS-09302080.translation: Long live Iulia Musa, daughter; long live Iulia Erato, daughter; and Iulia Cermo, mother-in-law.
EDCS-09302080.summary: This inscription expresses wishes for the afterlife for Iulia Musa, Iulia Erato, and Iulia Cermo, likely on a family tomb.

EDCS-09302081.translation: Pitecusa, freedwoman of Iulia Lepida, while alive made this for herself and for Flora, freedwoman of Iulia Lepida, her daughter, aged 33, and for Gaius Julius Chresimus, son, aged 26.
EDCS-09302081.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Pitecusa, a freedwoman, for herself, her deceased daughter Flora, and her deceased son Gaius Julius Chresimus.

EDCS-09302082.translation: To the departed spirits. Tiberius Claudius Thalamus, to his well-deserving wife, Iulia Procula, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-09302082.summary: This is a dedication to the departed spirits by Tiberius Claudius Thalamus for his wife Iulia Procula, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302083.summary: This inscription is a simple identification of Iulia Quinta, daughter of Gaius, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-09302084.translation: Iulia Su is buried here; alive live the sisters. Quintus Julius As, freedman, [occupies] 3 feet in front in all directions.
EDCS-09302084.summary: This inscription records the burial of Iulia Su and possibly indicates that Quintus Julius As, a freedman, has reserved burial space, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302085.translation: Iulia Tessilla, freedwoman of Olympius, for herself and her family.
EDCS-09302085.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Iulia Tessilla, a freedwoman, for herself and her household, likely on a tomb.

EDCS-09302086.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Iulia Maxima, a freedwoman, possibly by her owner or a relative.

EDCS-09302087.translation: To the departed spirits. Gaius Valerius Felix, husband, for himself and his family, to his wife Iulia Victrix.
EDCS-09302087.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by Gaius Valerius Felix for himself and his family, honoring his wife Iulia Victrix.

EDCS-09302089.translation: Lucius Iunius, son of Lucius, and Iunia, freedwoman of Lucius, daughter of As.
EDCS-09302089.summary: This inscription names Lucius Iunius and Iunia, possibly a couple, with their patronymic affiliations.

EDCS-09302090.translation: Quintas Iunius Faustus, son of Caius, died; 15 feet in front.
EDCS-09302090.summary: This epitaph records the death of Quintus Iunius Faustus and specifies the dimensions of his burial plot.

EDCS-09302091.translation: Marcus Iunius Mahes, freedman of Marcus, and Iulia Erotis, freedwoman of Felix, his wife, live; 15 feet in every direction.
EDCS-09302091.summary: This funerary inscription states that Marcus Iunius Mahes and his wife Iulia Erotis are 'alive' (in the sense of possessing their burial plot) and specifies the dimensions of their burial space.

EDCS-09302092.translation: To Gaius Iunius Maximus, from his most deserving wife, Iunia Victorina.
EDCS-09302092.summary: This is a dedication by Iunia Victorina to her husband, Gaius Iunius Maximus, indicating a spouse's memorial.

EDCS-09302094.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Publius Licinius Faustus and Fausta, freedwoman of Publius Licinius, his wife, are buried here. Also Calvia, freedwoman of Gaius, Secunda.
EDCS-09302094.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Publius Licinius Faustus and his wife Fausta, also mentioning Calvia Secunda, likely a relative or another interred individual.

EDCS-09302095.translation: [...]cio, freedman of Marcus, to his brother [...]onio, and to [...]cio, freedman of Marcus, [and to his freedman] Labio.
EDCS-09302095.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or memorial for several individuals, including freedmen, possibly by a relative.

EDCS-09302096.translation: Aulus Laelius Rusticus to his father Aulus Laelius Licinus, and to Aulus Laelius Quartus.
EDCS-09302096.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Aulus Laelius Rusticus to his father Aulus Laelius Licinus and another individual named Aulus Laelius Quartus.

EDCS-09302097.translation: Laetus, son of Crispus, and Fabia Secunda, freedwoman of Lucius, are alive; 15 feet in the field.
EDCS-09302097.summary: This funerary inscription states that Laetus and Fabia Secunda are 'alive' (possessing their burial plot) and specifies the plot size within a field.

EDCS-09302098.translation: Lafrena Secunda, daughter of Gaius, his pious and sensible wife, is buried here; 15 feet in every direction.
EDCS-09302098.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Lafrena Secunda, described as a pious and sensible wife, and details the dimensions of her burial plot.

EDCS-09302103.translation: For Quintus, son of [---], of the Papirian tribe, and for Lepida, who has passed away, for herself and her patron.
EDCS-09302103.summary: This is a funerary inscription, likely for a woman named Lepida, dedicated to herself and her patron, possibly relating to Quintus.

EDCS-09302104.translation: Publius Licinius Quartus, son of Publius, of the Papirian tribe, and his wife Iulia Campana, are alive.
EDCS-09302104.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording that Publius Licinius Quartus and his wife Iulia Campana are alive, likely indicating the tomb is for their use.

EDCS-09302105.translation: The freedman of Lucius Licinius, Ru[---].
EDCS-09302105.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying a freedman of Lucius Licinius.

EDCS-09302106.translation: Publius Licinius Sulla will not follow his heir in this monument.
EDCS-09302106.summary: This is a funerary inscription stating that the tomb of Publius Licinius Sulla is not to be inherited.

EDCS-09302107.translation: Licinia Antulla, daughter of Publius, is alive and [possesses/will possess] fifteen feet in the field.
EDCS-09302107.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Licinia Antulla, indicating she is alive and has a plot of land fifteen feet in size.

EDCS-09302108.translation: Licinia Successi for herself and Licinia Dotice.
EDCS-09302108.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Licinia Successi dedicates the monument to herself and Licinia Dotice.

EDCS-09302109.translation: He made this for his patron Licinius Frugi while alive; he is buried here.
EDCS-09302109.summary: This is a funerary inscription by an unknown freedman dedicated to his patron Licinius Frugi, made during the patron's lifetime.

EDCS-09302110.translation: Auctus, freedman of Maxumus, son of Caius Livanius, and his wife Maxuma, daughter of Sextus, are alive.
EDCS-09302110.summary: This funerary inscription records that Auctus, a freedman, and his wife Maxuma are alive, likely indicating the tomb is for their use.

EDCS-09302111.translation: Caius Livanius Maxumus is alive for his son.
EDCS-09302111.summary: This funerary inscription states that Caius Livanius Maxumus is alive, dedicated to his son.

EDCS-09302112.translation: Marcus Livius Menander, freedman of Marcus, is alive.
EDCS-09302112.summary: This funerary inscription states that Marcus Livius Menander, a freedman, is alive, likely indicating the tomb is for his use.

EDCS-09302114.translation: Lucius Lorinus Philomusus, freedman of Lucius, lives, and Lucius Lorinus Montanus, son of Marcus, lives.
EDCS-09302114.summary: This inscription records the perpetual existence, possibly a funerary marker, for Lucius Lorinus Philomusus and his son Lucius Lorinus Montanus.

EDCS-09302115.translation: Marcus Luccius, freedman of Marcus, lives; Marcus Luccius Tertius, freedman of Marcus, lives; [and] Eromene, freedwoman of Luccius, mother.
EDCS-09302115.summary: This inscription declares the perpetual existence of Marcus Luccius, Marcus Luccius Tertius, and Eromene, likely on a funerary monument.

EDCS-09302116.translation: Auctus, freedman of Publius Lucius, and Lucia Secunda, daughter of Publius, wife of Bella.
EDCS-09302116.summary: This inscription lists Auctus, freedman of Publius Lucius, and Lucia Secunda, daughter of Publius and wife of Bella, possibly on a shared funerary monument.

EDCS-09302117.translation: Publius Lucius Auctus, freedman of Publius Lucius, and Annidia Bella, daughter of Lucia, wife of Secundus, and Publius Lucius Auctus, freedman of Auctus, and Lucius and Placida, wife of Publius Lucius Auctus, and Publius Lucius Felix, freedman of Auctus, and Alba, freedwoman of Lucia Felicis, and Lactitia, freedwoman of Lucia Felicis, shall be placed in this location, none except those whose names are written.
EDCS-09302117.summary: This is a complex funerary inscription detailing burial rights and restrictions for multiple individuals within a specific burial plot.

EDCS-09302118.translation: Publius Lucius Hilarus, of Greek origin, lives for himself and for Pompeia Tertulla, living daughter of Lucius, and for Publius Lucius Philadelphus, living freedman of Graecus, and for Lucia Lepida, deceased freedwoman of Lucius Graecus.
EDCS-09302118.summary: This funerary inscription records the perpetual existence for Publius Lucius Hilarus, his family members, and freedmen, indicating a family tomb.

EDCS-09302119.translation: Lucretia Maxuma, daughter of Lucius, lives, for herself and for her husband Lucius Voconius Diphilus, freedman of Lucius; this monument will not pass to an heir.
EDCS-09302119.summary: This funerary inscription states that Lucretia Maxuma and her husband Lucius Voconius Diphilus are interred here and the monument is not inheritable.

EDCS-09302120.translation: Lucius Maecius Pamphilus, freedman of Lucius, is buried here, and his wife Sappo.
EDCS-09302120.summary: This is a simple tomb inscription recording the burial of Lucius Maecius Pamphilus and his wife Sappo.

EDCS-09302121.translation: Living Marcus Maessius Rufinus for himself and for his deceased wife Capella, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-09302121.summary: This funerary inscription records the perpetual existence for Marcus Maessius Rufinus and his deceased wife Capella.

EDCS-09302122.translation: Magidius Boiscus and Magidia Quarta, his partner, live; 15 feet in front.
EDCS-09302122.summary: This inscription records the perpetual existence of Magidius Boiscus and Magidia Quarta, along with the dimensions of the frontage of their burial plot.

EDCS-09302123.translation: Third daughter of Spurius Magida lives; Vibia, daughter of Spurius Fausta, lives; 15 feet in front.
EDCS-09302123.summary: This funerary inscription records the perpetual existence of Third Magida and Vibia Fausta, daughters of Spurius, and indicates the frontage of their plot.

EDCS-09302124.translation: Masculus, freedman of Gaius Maius Philargyrus, and Urbana, freedwoman of Secunda.
EDCS-09302124.summary: This is a funerary epitaph listing two freedpersons, Masculus and Urbana, likely for a tomb or monument.

EDCS-09302125.translation: and Baebius Primus to Gaius Maius Montanus, freedman, while alive.
EDCS-09302125.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the dedication by Baebius Primus to Gaius Maius Montanus, a freedman, likely for a tomb or monument.

EDCS-09302126.translation: Maia, freedwoman of Gaius, Bara, I wish to have buried Caius Baebius Primus in it for herself and for Gaius Maius Montanus, freedman, while alive.
EDCS-09302126.summary: This funerary epitaph records Maia's wish to bury Caius Baebius Primus in a monument she is establishing for herself and for Gaius Maius Montanus.

EDCS-09302127.translation: Maia Maxuma, daughter of Gaius, mother; Lucius Iuvenalis, son of Quintus, brother; and Lucius, father, son of Quintus.
EDCS-09302127.summary: This inscription lists family members: a mother, a son who is also a brother, and a father, likely identifying individuals associated with a tomb.

EDCS-09302128.translation: to Malchio, freedman of Marcus Aulus, and to Rupha, freedwoman of Publius, of the road.
EDCS-09302128.summary: This is a dedication, possibly for a public work or a funerary monument, to two freedpersons, Malchio and Rupha.

EDCS-09302129.translation: Lucius Manilius Acutus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-09302129.summary: This is a name inscription, likely for a tomb or monument, identifying Lucius Manilius Acutus.

EDCS-09302130.translation: Marcus Manilius Antiocus, freedman of Marcus, lives.
EDCS-09302130.summary: This inscription states that Marcus Manilius Antiocus, a freedman, is alive, likely on a monument intended for his burial or commemoration.

EDCS-09302131.translation: Manilius Rufus, father of Rufi, this monument follows no one except [himself] or whom he may wish to be buried.
EDCS-09302131.summary: This funerary inscription from Manilius Rufus reserves the right to bury himself and others of his choosing in this monument.

EDCS-09302132.translation: Marcia Anilia, wife of Publius Sadilius, lives; and Augela, freedwoman of Caius, to Caius Aprius Iucundus.
EDCS-09302132.summary: This inscription records two individuals, Marcia Anilia and Augela, and their relationship or dedication to Caius Aprius Iucundus, likely on a tomb.

EDCS-09302135.summary: This is a name inscription, likely for a tomb or monument, identifying Lucius Manlius.

EDCS-09302136.translation: Gaius Manlius Rufus, son of Caius, of the Papiria tribe, is alive for himself and his wife Attedia Maxima, daughter of Quintus, with whom I have lived for 18 years without offense.
EDCS-09302136.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording a man, Gaius Manlius Rufus, and his wife Attedia Maxima, with a statement about their harmonious marriage, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-09302137.translation: Manlius Salaverus for himself and Mi...
EDCS-09302137.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely records a funerary dedication by Manlius Salaverus for himself and another individual, its date and precise context are unknown due to its brevity.

EDCS-09302138.translation: Manneia Primula for herself and her patroness Lacta.
EDCS-09302138.summary: This epitaph records a dedication by Manneia Primula for herself and her patroness Lacta, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09302139.translation: Lucius Marcius Anteros, freedman of Lucius, is buried here in 15 feet of land.
EDCS-09302139.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Marcius Anteros, a freedman, specifying the burial plot size, probably dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-09302140.translation: Maurilla, freedwoman of Marcia and the woman (?), is deceased, and for her freedwoman Marcia Suavini.
EDCS-09302140.summary: This inscription seems to record the death of Maurilla, a freedwoman, and a dedication or commemoration for another freedwoman, Marcia Suavini, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09302141.translation: Lives. For Lucius Marius Masclus, son of Lucius, a leatherworker, and for Gimia Optata, his companion [---] Marius [---] his wife.
EDCS-09302141.summary: A funerary inscription for a leatherworker and his companion and wife.

EDCS-09302142.translation: Gaius Marius Mysticus, 15 feet in every direction, for Cornelia Prima.
EDCS-09302142.summary: This inscription appears to mark a burial plot of 15 feet in all directions, dedicated by Gaius Marius Mysticus for Cornelia Prima, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09302143.translation: Viva made (this) for Maria Quinta, freedwoman of Caius, and for Antonia Quarta, daughter of Lucius, and for Antonia Tertia, daughter of Lucius, and for Quintus Marius Minor, and for her own family.
EDCS-09302143.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Viva, likely a freedwoman herself, for several relatives including Maria Quinta and Antonia Quarta and Tertia, and Quintus Marius Minor, from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09302144.translation: ] Martius, freedman of the colony Diocha[res]. Sabidia [---] daughter of Numerius. [---] Lucaea. Is buried here.
EDCS-09302144.summary: A funerary inscription indicating that at least three individuals, including a freedman of the colony, are buried here.

EDCS-09302145.translation: To the Divine Shades. Cornelius December made (this) for his dearest wife, Martia Antonia, from his own property.
EDCS-09302145.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Cornelius December for his beloved wife Martia Antonia, specifying it was made at his expense, typical of the Imperial period.

EDCS-09302146.translation: To the Divine Shades. Maskarus Marcello Pria...
EDCS-09302146.summary: This fragmentary inscription is a dedication to the Divine Shades (funerary spirits), mentioning Maskarus and Marcello, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09302147.translation: For daughter Matugena and for Scribonia Maxumilla and for themselves, 15 feet in front and 15 feet in the field.
EDCS-09302147.summary: This inscription records a funerary plot of 15 feet by 15 feet, intended for Matugena, Scribonia Maxumilla, and others, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09302148.translation: Maxumus, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, freedman of Celsus.
EDCS-09302148.summary: This inscription records a man, Maxumus, and identifies his father, tribe, and patron.

EDCS-09302149.translation: Meculonarius, son of Publius, is alive for himself and for his living father Publius Attius Privatus, and for his living mother Mecullonia Successa, daughter of Marcus, and for his living brother Marcus Meculanus Festus.
EDCS-09302149.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Meculonarius, who made provisions for himself and his living family members.

EDCS-09302150.translation: Protogenia, a freedwoman of Messia, died, according to her will and at the direction of the executor, in front.
EDCS-09302150.summary: This inscription records the death of Protogenia, a freedwoman, according to her will.

EDCS-09302151.translation: Metilia, daughter of Cnaeus, Nigrina and the living Caius Quintilius Celsus made this for themselves and
EDCS-09302151.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Metilia and Caius Quintilius Celsus are making provisions for themselves and others.

EDCS-09302152.translation: Marcus Mevius Isargyrus, freedman of Marcus, is alive.
EDCS-09302152.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the survival of Marcus Mevius Isargyrus, a freedman.

EDCS-09302153.translation: Varus, freedman of Minatius, son of Publius, is alive for himself and for his deceased freedwoman Optata, for 15 feet in front.
EDCS-09302153.summary: This funerary inscription records Varus, a freedman, and his deceased freedwoman Optata, with a measurement of the plot.

EDCS-09302154.translation: to his freedman Li, and to his fellow soldier Ianuaria Melite, who deserved well of him.
EDCS-09302154.summary: This is a dedication to a freedman and a fellow soldier, Ianuaria Melite, for their good service.

EDCS-09302156.translation: To Publius Mominus, freedman of Publius, son of Caius, Antenor; to Publius, freedman of Publius, Celer; to Publius, son of Publius, Heliodorus; to Publius, son of Publius, Maxumus; to Caius Philomus; Lucius Eleuter.
EDCS-09302156.summary: This is a dedication listing several individuals, likely patrons and freedmen, with their familial and patron relationships.

EDCS-09302157.translation: Caius Mustilius Truphoninus, freedman of Caius, is alive; he made this for himself and for his fellow freedman.
EDCS-09302157.summary: This funerary inscription records Caius Mustilius Truphoninus, a freedman, who made provisions for himself and a fellow freedman.

EDCS-09302158.translation: Caius Mustus Optata, freedman of Caius, is alive; he is buried here.
EDCS-09302158.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Caius Mustus Optata, a freedman.

EDCS-09302159.translation: Egnatia, freedwoman of Quintus, alive, for herself and for Alexander, freedman of Lucius, son of Lucius Pompeius.
EDCS-09302159.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Egnatia for herself and Alexander, likely a husband or close relation, possibly on a tombstone.

EDCS-09302160.translation: Natalis, daughter of Cn. Victorinus, lives.
EDCS-09302160.summary: This inscription records the life of Natalis, daughter of Cn. Victorinus, possibly on a tombstone or a dedication to her.

EDCS-09302162.translation: To Lucius Nerfinius Potitus, the patron.
EDCS-09302162.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Nerfinius Potitus, identified as a patron, likely on a public monument or tomb.

EDCS-09302163.translation: To Neria, wife of I., fifteen feet in all directions.
EDCS-09302163.summary: This inscription specifies the dimensions of a plot of land, fifteen feet in all directions, dedicated to Neria, wife of I., likely marking a burial space.

EDCS-09302164.translation: To the Divine Shades. Fotidius Nicephorus, father, and mother, made this for their most dutiful son Nicostratus, aged twenty-four years and thirty days.
EDCS-09302164.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by parents for their son Nicostratus, providing his age at death.

EDCS-09302165.translation: Hedone, of the Papirian tribe, daughter of Flavius Niger, made this alive for her most dutiful father.
EDCS-09302165.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a daughter, Hedone, for her father during her lifetime.

EDCS-09302168.translation: And Niger, son of Ecritonis and Viratus, lives. For Valeria Sextia, daughter of Sextillus Optatus, for Sextia, daughter of Sextillus.
EDCS-09302168.summary: This inscription records the continued life of Niger and possibly his family members, specifying land dimensions (12 feet in depth, 4 feet in front), likely related to property or funerary use.

EDCS-09302169.translation: To the Divine Shades. The heirs [made this] for Marcus Nigrius.
EDCS-09302169.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Nigrius, erected by his heirs.

EDCS-09302170.translation: To Caius Nonius, freedman of Caius, the patron, and for himself.
EDCS-09302170.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a freedman, Caius, for his patron Caius and for himself.

EDCS-09302171.translation: Marcus Norbanus, freedman of Marcus, Rufio, and Dellia, freedwoman of Lucius, Helena, are buried here.
EDCS-09302171.summary: This inscription marks the burial place of Marcus Norbanus Rufio and Dellia Helena, freedpersons, indicating a shared tomb or funerary plot.

EDCS-09302172.translation: Publius Novanus Aescinus, freedman of Publius, is buried here with his slave-woman, for fifteen feet in every direction.
EDCS-09302172.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Novanus Aescinus, a freedman, indicating the burial space around his tomb.

EDCS-09302173.translation: Publius Novanus Cupitus, freedman of Publius, and Familiaris Novana, freedwoman of Publius, for themselves and for their patron and mother.
EDCS-09302173.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Novanus Cupitus and Familiaris Novana, freedpeople, dedicating the tomb for themselves and their patron/mother.

EDCS-09302174.translation: To the Divine Spirits of Lucius Novanius Pardulus.
EDCS-09302174.summary: This is a dedication to the Divine Spirits for Lucius Novanius Pardulus, likely part of a funerary monument.

EDCS-09302175.translation: For fifteen feet in every direction, Marcus Novius Seloucus, freedman of Marcus, lives.
EDCS-09302175.summary: This epitaph for Marcus Novius Seloucus, a freedman, possibly marks a burial plot with a specified size.

EDCS-09302176.translation: For fifteen feet in every direction, Marcus Novius Sotericus, freedman of Marcus, is placed.
EDCS-09302176.summary: This epitaph for Marcus Novius Sotericus, a freedman, marks his burial site and the surrounding space.

EDCS-09302177.translation: Numisia Mneme, freedwoman of Lucius, is buried here; this monument does not pass to an heir, by the decision of Eubulus, her cohabitant.
EDCS-09302177.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Numisia Mneme, a freedwoman, stating that the tomb is not heritable and was arranged by her partner Eubulus.

EDCS-09302178.translation: Obienia Vera, freedwoman of Quintus, is buried here for her patron Quintus Teucer.
EDCS-09302178.summary: This funerary epitaph records the burial of Obienia Vera, a freedwoman, for her patron Quintus Teucer.

EDCS-09302179.translation: For Marcus Octavius. Titus Octavius, freedman of Marcus, lives.
EDCS-09302179.summary: This epitaph indicates that Titus Octavius, a freedman, is alive, possibly while commemorating Marcus Octavius.

EDCS-09302180.translation: Decimus Octavius Nigellio lives for his wife Litugena, freedwoman of Titus, and for his son Decimus Octavius Gratus.
EDCS-09302180.summary: This epitaph states that Decimus Octavius Nigellio is alive and honors his wife Litugena and son Decimus Octavius Gratus.

EDCS-09302182.translation: Caius Ofellius E, freedman of Excingius, lives.
EDCS-09302182.summary: This epitaph records that Caius Ofellius, a freedman, is alive.

EDCS-09302183.translation: Caius Ofellius Excingus, freedman of Caius.
EDCS-09302183.summary: This is a funerary epitaph naming Caius Ofellius Excingus, a freedman, and his patron.

EDCS-09302184.translation: Caius Ofillius, freedman of Caius, residing in the Palatine region, lived for himself, and for his wife Prima, daughter of Marcus Mindius; and for his son Proculus, son of Caius Ofillius; and for Barbara whom the earth bore and delivered to the service of the unrighteous, seeking talent not deserved from a father; he added a name to himself and obtained it by purchase, which he could not get by entreaty; he conquered his master with his services and did not feel the lash, nor did he receive rewards; what pledges could he have? Why do you hurry, stranger? Rest is prepared for you, known to you. Hospitality is always open here for the people. The number of hours which you suspect, and in which you feel secure.
EDCS-09302184.summary: This is a complex epitaph for Caius Ofillius, a freedman, who describes his life, his family, his efforts to gain status and freedom, and offers philosophical reflections on rest and hospitality.

EDCS-09302185.translation: To Caius Ol Priscus, the feet, in all directions, 10.
EDCS-09302185.summary: This inscription appears to be a boundary marker or measurement related to property owned by Caius Ol Priscus.

EDCS-09302186.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely part of a funerary monument, mentioning Olius, son of Publius, and his mother.

EDCS-09302188.translation: Olia Iucunda, freedwoman of Quintus, the burial place for Quintus Olio Phila, freedman of Quintus.
EDCS-09302188.summary: This is a funerary epitaph granting burial rights to Olia Iucunda, a freedwoman, for herself and for Quintus Olio Phila, a freedman.

EDCS-09302189.translation: Lives. Quintus Numisius Proculus, son of Quintus, a muleteer, for himself and for Quintus Numisius Eronus, his father, and for Caelia Silvana, his mother.
EDCS-09302189.summary: A funerary inscription set up by a muleteer for himself, his father, and his mother.

EDCS-09302191.translation: Pontia Optata, daughter of Lucius, for herself and for her mother Valeria Prima.
EDCS-09302191.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Pontia Optata, daughter of Lucius, dedicating the monument to herself and her mother Valeria Prima.

EDCS-09302192.translation: Osideius Oceanus, the fuller, lived in Li[---]illicco.
EDCS-09302192.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Osideius Oceanus, identified as a fuller, with a partially preserved place name.

EDCS-09302193.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Otania, a freedwoman.

EDCS-09302194.translation: Paccius Sodalis, freedman of Quintus, lived; Paccius Ecrito, freedman of Quintus, fellow freedman; Paccius Auctus, freedman of Quintus; Paccius Faustus, freedman of Quintus; Paccius Canopus, freedman of Quintus; Paccius Iucundus, freedman of Quintus.
EDCS-09302194.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lives of multiple freedmen named Paccius, all associated with Quintus.

EDCS-09302195.translation: Titus Paconius Alexa, freedman of Titus, and Octavia Asia, freedwoman of a woman, lived.
EDCS-09302195.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Titus Paconius Alexa, a freedman, and Octavia Asia, a freedwoman.

EDCS-09302196.summary: This inscription records the supervision of a project by a person named Pamphilus.

EDCS-09302198.summary: This inscription is likely a name, possibly an owner or subject of a monument.

EDCS-09302200.translation: Prima, freedwoman of Papiria Marci, lived, and this monument, 15 feet in all directions, will not pass to an heir.
EDCS-09302200.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Prima, a freedwoman, establishing that her monument is not inheritable.

EDCS-09302204.translation: To Quintus Pescennius, son of Quintus, from Papiria Callisteni.
EDCS-09302204.summary: This is a dedication on a monument, likely funerary, to Quintus Pescennius by Papiria Callisteni.

EDCS-09302205.translation: Gaius Petronius, son of Spurius, for himself and his family.
EDCS-09302205.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Gaius Petronius for himself and his household, likely on a family tomb or monument.

EDCS-09302206.translation: Lucius Petronius, son of Publius, to Petronia.
EDCS-09302206.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Lucius Petronius to Petronia, possibly a funerary dedication.

EDCS-09302207.translation: From Philargurus, freedman of Fadius Atticus.
EDCS-09302207.summary: This inscription records the name of Philargurus, a freedman of Fadius Atticus.

EDCS-09302208.translation: To Lucius, freedman, Phileros, to his patron and to himself.
EDCS-09302208.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Phileros, a freedman, to his patron Lucius and to himself.

EDCS-09302209.translation: While alive, he made [this] for himself and for Philomus, his patron.
EDCS-09302209.summary: This funerary inscription records a person who, while alive, commissioned a monument for himself and his patron Philomus.

EDCS-09302211.summary: This inscription records the name of Phronumus, a freedman of Marcus.

EDCS-09302214.translation: Marcus Planius Maxsumus, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-09302214.summary: This is a tombstone identifying Marcus Planius Maxsumus, a freedman.

EDCS-09302215.translation: Marcus Planius Myro lives, in memory of his freedwoman Plania Chiteris, and of Lucius Planius Gratus. Twenty feet in front, fifteen feet in the field. This monument will not pass to heirs.
EDCS-09302215.summary: This funerary inscription records the deceased (Plania Chiteris, Lucius Planius Gratus) and the living owner (Marcus Planius Myro), specifying plot dimensions and disinheriting future heirs. It is likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302216.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying Plotecis, daughter of Aulus Minius.

EDCS-09302218.translation: Publius Pollus Murranus, freedman of Pancarpus, for himself and for his deceased partner Urbania Pollius, and for Publius Pollus Peplus, and for Pollia Privata. Fifteen feet in the field.
EDCS-09302218.summary: This funerary inscription names the primary owner (Publius Pollus Murranus), his deceased partner (Urbania Pollius), and other individuals (Publius Pollus Peplus, Pollia Privata), along with a plot dimension. It is likely Roman Imperial.

EDCS-09302219.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to identify a person named Quintus Pom[---] and possibly another individual, with the phrase 'while alive' suggesting it might be related to a land boundary or a dedication during one's lifetime.

EDCS-09302220.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription identifying Gnaeus Pompeius.

EDCS-09302221.translation: To the Divine Spirits, for Pompeia Hermetionis, his most dutiful partner in life, Iulia Hermione.
EDCS-09302221.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Pompeia Hermetionis by her partner Iulia Hermione, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302222.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Marcus Pompeius Saturninus.

EDCS-09302223.translation: Titus Pompeius Venustus, and for his wife Artoria Procula, daughter of Caius, and for his daughter Pompeia Venusta, and ---
EDCS-09302223.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription commemorating Titus Pompeius Venustus, his wife Artoria Procula, and his daughter Pompeia Venusta, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302224.translation: To the Divine Spirits, for Pompeia Myrina, his most dutiful wife. Granius Felicianus.
EDCS-09302224.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Pompeia Myrina by her husband Granius Felicianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302225.summary: This is a funerary monument made by the freedwoman Pompeia Quartilla for someone.

EDCS-09302226.translation: Pompeia Sega, freedwoman of Lepidus, lives; on the death of her son Titus Pompeius Celadus, this monument will not pass to an heir; 15 feet in front.
EDCS-09302226.summary: This funerary inscription records that Pompeia Sega, a freedwoman, erected a monument for her son Titus Pompeius Celadus, stipulating that it would not pass to heirs and specifying its dimensions.

EDCS-09302227.translation: Pompeia Soteria, daughter of Caius, lives; 15 feet in the field.
EDCS-09302227.summary: This inscription marks a funerary plot of 15 feet in a field belonging to Pompeia Soteria.

EDCS-09302228.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription identifying Pompeia Urbana, daughter of Cnaeus.

EDCS-09302229.translation: To the departed spirits of Pomponia Philena, who lived 76 years; her heirs... 131 years...
EDCS-09302229.summary: This funerary inscription records the lifespan of Pomponia Philena and mentions her heirs.

EDCS-09302230.translation: Pomponia Procula, wife, 15 feet in the field.
EDCS-09302230.summary: This inscription marks a funerary plot of 15 feet in a field belonging to Pomponia Procula.

EDCS-09302231.translation: Lives Marcus Porcius Victor, a deserving student.
EDCS-09302231.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Porcius Victor, a student, and indicates he is still alive.

EDCS-09302232.translation: On the death of Primigenius, the most devoted and frugal slave of his master.
EDCS-09302232.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Primigenius, a devoted and frugal slave.

EDCS-09302234.summary: This fragment likely refers to a funerary monument or plot belonging to the freedwoman Primula.

EDCS-09302235.translation: Primo Isops, freedman, to his patron and...
EDCS-09302235.summary: This is a dedication by a freedman, Primo Isops, to his patron.

EDCS-09302236.translation: Compina Prima, his wife, in the field, 15 feet.
EDCS-09302236.summary: This is a boundary marker for a plot of land belonging to Compina Prima.

EDCS-09302237.translation: To Prisca, daughter of Lucius, from Gaius Julius Alexander, his patronesses Felix and Rusa, on the front 20 feet, in the field 30 feet.
EDCS-09302237.summary: This is a dedication of land, likely for funerary or property purposes, to Prisca, from Gaius Julius Alexander and his patronesses.

EDCS-09302238.translation: Gaius Quadronius Chrysogonus for himself and Aemilia Censorina.
EDCS-09302238.summary: This inscription records a self-dedication and dedication to Aemilia Censorina, likely for a tomb or property.

EDCS-09302239.translation: To Quartilla, Nicerotes' most devoted friend, an assistant, on the front 30 feet, in the field 15 feet.
EDCS-09302239.summary: This is a dedication to Quartilla, possibly honoring her for her assistance, with specified land dimensions.

EDCS-09302241.translation: Liniaa Quarta, V Vercillus, son of Ateponis.
EDCS-09302241.summary: This inscription appears to record a property division or ownership, mentioning Liniaa Quarta and Vercillus.

EDCS-09302244.translation: Maxima, daughter of Lucius Rauricia, made this while alive for her son Quintus Cornelius Capito, son of Caius, aged 30 at death, for her son Celsus, son of Caius, aged 8 at death.
EDCS-09302244.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Maxima for her two deceased sons, Quintus Cornelius Capito and Celsus.

EDCS-09302245.translation: Vivius Repentinus, for himself and his family.
EDCS-09302245.summary: This inscription records a self-dedication for Vivius Repentinus and his family, likely for a tomb or property.

EDCS-09302246.translation: For himself and his wife, Lusiana Restituta.
EDCS-09302246.summary: This inscription records a self-dedication and dedication to his wife, Lusiana Restituta, likely for a tomb or property.

EDCS-09302247.translation: To the divine spirits, from the heirs of Gaius Rigius Silvanus.
EDCS-09302247.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the gods of the underworld by the heirs of Gaius Rigius Silvanus.

EDCS-09302248.translation: Publius Rinnius Licinus, freedman of Publius, is alive.
EDCS-09302248.summary: This inscription records that Publius Rinnius Licinus, a freedman, is alive, possibly as a marker of ownership or status.

EDCS-09302249.translation: Here lies buried Lucia Rinnia Prima, freedwoman of Lucia Rinnia, freedwoman of Publius. Here lies buried Aucta, freedwoman of Prima and patroness. [This is] half of a tombstone.
EDCS-09302249.summary: An epitaph for Lucia Rinnia Prima and her freedwoman Aucta, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302251.translation: Feilius [dedicated this] to his mother Roscia Pia.
EDCS-09302251.summary: A dedication by Feilius to his mother Roscia Pia, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302252.translation: Lucius Rubrius, son of Lucius, of the Fabia tribe, and Sura, freedwoman of Quintus Ignia, lives.
EDCS-09302252.summary: A tomb inscription indicating the survival of Lucius Rubrius and Sura, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302254.translation: Ruerius Monimus, daughter of Titus Sertorius; his sister Secunda, daughter of Caius Sertorius, granted [this].
EDCS-09302254.summary: A funerary dedication mentioning Ruerius Monimus and his sister Secunda, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302258.translation: Lucius Runnius Pollio, son of Gnaeus, of the Papiria tribe, [wishes] more enjoyment in my monument where I must sleep and remain here.
EDCS-09302258.summary: An epitaph for Lucius Runnius Pollio, expressing his desire for eternal rest in his monument, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302259.translation: Quintus Pupilius Princeps, freedman of Quintus, [erected this] for himself and for his patron Quintus Rupilius Hilarus, freedman of Quintus; for his fellow freedwoman Blastae, freedwoman of Quintus; and for his freedwoman Aucta, freedwoman of Rupilia Princeps.
EDCS-09302259.summary: A funerary monument inscription detailing dedications by Quintus Pupilius Princeps to his patron, fellow freedmen, and freedwomen, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302260.summary: A fragmentary inscription identifying Rupilia as a freedwoman and daughter, likely Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302261.translation: To the Divine Shades. Lucius Rusticanius Boethos made [this] for his most devoted wife, Catia Iulina.
EDCS-09302261.summary: A funerary dedication by Lucius Rusticanius Boethos for his wife Catia Iulina, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302262.translation: For Publius Rutilius Gallicanus, son of Publius. Publius Rutilius Martialis, freedman of Publius, [dedicated this] to his most dutiful patron Rutilius Hospitus, and to Publius Didius Peregrinus.
EDCS-09302262.summary: A funerary inscription by Publius Rutilius Martialis dedicating a monument to his patron Rutilius Hospitus and Publius Didius Peregrinus, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302263.translation: For Gaius Rutilius Maxsumus. His wife Campana.
EDCS-09302263.summary: A funerary dedication by Campana for her husband Gaius Rutilius Maxsumus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302264.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph identifying the deceased, Sabinus, by his given name and patronymic.

EDCS-09302265.translation: To Gaius Safinius Labeo, son of Caius, with his wife Cervia Tertia, daughter of Lucius, alive, Safinius made this at the age of 32, and his son.
EDCS-09302265.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Cervia Tertia to her husband Gaius Safinius Labeo and their son, likely dating to the 1st century BCE or 1st century CE, given the mention of Cervia being alive and the age of the deceased.

EDCS-09302266.translation: To Gaius Salius Philo, by the judgment of Publius Secundus, son of Lucius, and his freedman.
EDCS-09302266.summary: This inscription records a legal judgment or arbitration concerning Gaius Salius Philo and others, likely related to property or inheritance.

EDCS-09302267.translation: Optatus, freedman of Lucius Salivius Anchialus, and Albia Tertia, freedwoman of Albia, and Albia, daughter of Caius, alive, made this for Publius Salivius Optatus, freedman of Publius, in front 15 feet, she lived and for Gaius Albius Nigellio.
EDCS-09302267.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, likely for a family plot, with multiple individuals being commemorated, including freedmen and their patrons.

EDCS-09302268.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Gaius Sallustius Isochrysus.
EDCS-09302268.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to the Manes (spirits of the dead) by Gaius Sallustius Isochrysus.

EDCS-09302269.translation: Venusta, freedwoman of Salonia, daughter of Lucius, died, for herself and...
EDCS-09302269.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, indicating that Venusta, a freedwoman, dedicated the monument to herself and possibly others.

EDCS-09302270.translation: ...son of Gnaeus Marcius, to his freedman Salvius.
EDCS-09302270.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, likely a dedication or a funerary epitaph mentioning a freedman and his patron.

EDCS-09302271.translation: Titus Salvius Eros, freedman of Titus, lived, for himself and for Titus Salvius Titullus, son of Lucius, his patron, and for his wife Babuleia Theophila, 15 feet in front and 15 feet in the field.
EDCS-09302271.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Titus Salvius Eros, a freedman, who dedicated it to himself, his patron, and his wife, specifying the dimensions of the burial plot.

EDCS-09302272.translation: Salvia, freedwoman, alive, made this for herself and for Publius, son of Publius, and for Publius Rufo, son of I...
EDCS-09302272.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, likely set up by a freedwoman for herself and her son, also possibly commemorating another individual.

EDCS-09302273.translation: To Lucia Salvia, wife of V(aleri) Sentius Communis.
EDCS-09302273.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicating a monument to Lucia Salvia, the wife of V. Sentius Communis.

EDCS-09302274.translation: Salvia, daughter of Quintus, called Secunda, (dedicated this) while alive for herself and her family.
EDCS-09302274.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Salvia Secunda for herself and her family, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09302275.translation: Felix, freedman, (dedicated this) to Quintus Sariolenus Licinus, and to Celsa, freedwoman of Quintus.
EDCS-09302275.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a freedman named Felix to his patron Quintus Sariolenus Licinus and to Celsa, another freedwoman, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09302276.translation: Gaius Satrienus Philonicus (dedicated this) for himself, and for his wife Menia, daughter of Lucius, called Secunda, and for Satriena Celsa.
EDCS-09302276.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Gaius Satrienus Philonicus for himself, his wife Menia Secunda, and Satriena Celsa, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09302278.translation: To the Divine Spirits: Uturnina Marina, (to her) most devoted mother.
EDCS-09302278.summary: This is a funerary dedication to a mother named Uturnina Marina, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09302279.summary: This is a simple funerary dedication or name inscription for Marcus Scandilius, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09302280.translation: Secundus (dedicated this) to Cornelia Quarta, his wife.
EDCS-09302280.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Secundus to his wife Cornelia Quarta, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09302281.translation: Secunda (dedicated this) to her mother and to Prima, her relative.
EDCS-09302281.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Secunda to her mother and a relative named Prima, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09302282.translation: Secunda, freedwoman of Lucius, (dedicated this) to Vettius I, her husband.
