EDCS-09302282.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Secunda, freedwoman of Lucius, to her husband Vettius I, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09302283.translation: To the Divine Spirits: Lucius Segolatus Victorinus lived 6 years, 6 months, 2 days. Segolatus Primus and Segolatia Victorina (dedicated this) to their most devoted son.
EDCS-09302283.summary: This is a funerary dedication for the child Lucius Segolatus Victorinus, who died at a young age, by his parents Segolatus Primus and Segolatia Victorina, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-09302284.translation: Frug Asemp (son of) A L DO.
EDCS-09302284.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, possibly recording a name and parentage, its date and origin are unclear.

EDCS-09302285.translation: Aulus Sempronius Chilo and his freedman Aptus, 15 feet in front.
EDCS-09302285.summary: This inscription records a property boundary or measurement of 15 feet, associated with Aulus Sempronius Chilo and his freedman Aptus.

EDCS-09302286.translation: Lucius Sempronius Niger, freedman of Lucius, and Sempronia Apate, freedwoman of Lucius, made this for themselves while alive, in memory of their patron and for themselves, on account of his piety, 15 feet in front.
EDCS-09302286.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Lucius Sempronius Niger and Sempronia Apate dedicated a monument to themselves and their patron in recognition of his piety.

EDCS-09302287.translation: [---] CQ and Sempronia Maxuma, daughter of Lucius, fellow-soldier of Lucius Sempronius Saturus, her brother, 15 feet in front.
EDCS-09302287.summary: This inscription likely commemorates Sempronia Maxuma, daughter of Lucius, and her brother Lucius Sempronius Saturus, possibly relating to military service or a shared burial plot.

EDCS-09302288.translation: For Sempronia, freedwoman of Caius. Q.
EDCS-09302288.summary: This is a dedication or memorial inscription for Sempronia, a freedwoman of Caius.

EDCS-09302289.summary: This inscription likely marks a property boundary or burial plot of 24 feet belonging to Senenia.

EDCS-09302290.translation: Sergia Chia, freedwoman of Statoris, lives.
EDCS-09302290.summary: This inscription states that Sergia Chia, a freedwoman, is alive.

EDCS-09302291.translation: Lives Titus Sertorius Turpio, son of Publius, [in memory of] Tillia Paulla, daughter of Cnaeus, [who passed away].
EDCS-09302291.summary: This inscription commemorates Tillia Paulla, daughter of Cnaeus, and states that Titus Sertorius Turpio, son of Publius, is alive, suggesting a memorial to the deceased.

EDCS-09302292.summary: This is an incomplete inscription honoring Quintus Servenius Fucianus.

EDCS-09302293.translation: To Lucius Servenius Seleucus, freedman of Lucius, and to Munatia Benigna, freedwoman of Lucius, his wife.
EDCS-09302293.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Lucius Servenius Seleucus and his wife Munatia Benigna.

EDCS-09302294.translation: Sextilia Nape made this for herself while alive, for her husband Catius Nereus, for her son Catius Ingenuus, for her fellow-soldier (?) Hilarus, for her associate Licinius Severus, son of Decimus, for her guardian Fadiae, the freedwoman of Titus, and for Communi.
EDCS-09302294.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Sextilia Nape for herself and various family members and associates, including her husband, son, and others.

EDCS-09302295.translation: Publius Sextius Genialis' freedman Felix lives for himself and his family.
EDCS-09302295.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the perpetual life (memoria) for Felix, freedman of Publius Sextius Genialis, and his family.

EDCS-09302296.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld for Sibilia Prima and Cai Erianus, 15 feet in front.
EDCS-09302296.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Sibilia Prima and Cai Erianus, specifying the dimensions of the funerary plot.

EDCS-09302297.translation: Silvanus for himself and for Aulus Minatius Hilarus, his father, and Minatia, Aulus' freedwoman, his devoted mother.
EDCS-09302297.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording Silvanus' provision for himself and his parents, Aulus Minatius Hilarus and Minatia.

EDCS-09302298.translation: for himself and for his wife Sophe and for Quintus Critonius.
EDCS-09302298.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording provision for the deceased and Quintus Critonius.

EDCS-09302300.translation: Lucius Staius Antigonus, freedman of Lucius Staius, lives for Staias Do [---].
EDCS-09302300.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the perpetual life (memoria) for Lucius Staius Antigonus, freedman of Lucius Staius, and Staias Do.

EDCS-09302301.translation: Quintus Statius Eros, freedman of Quintus Statius, lives for himself and for the deceased Quintus Statius Hermogenes, freedman of a woman, his patron, and Lucius A Z [---].
EDCS-09302301.summary: This funerary inscription records Quintus Statius Eros' provision for himself, his patron Quintus Statius Hermogenes, and Lucius A Z.

EDCS-09302303.translation: Stertinius Heuresis, freedwoman of Caius, lives for herself and for Caius Aveius Severus, her deceased husband.
EDCS-09302303.summary: This funerary inscription records Stertinia Heuresis' provision for herself and her deceased husband, Caius Aveius Severus.

EDCS-09302304.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning Rivius and Lucius Spail Surillionis.

EDCS-09302305.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription specifying provision for Suavis, Marcus' freedwoman.

EDCS-09302306.translation: For the deceased Suavis, his brother, and for Flavia Musa, his living sister, 15 feet in the field.
EDCS-09302306.summary: This funerary inscription records provision for the deceased Suavis and the living Flavia Musa, specifying plot dimensions.

EDCS-09302307.translation: Gaius Sulpicius, son of Marcus, lives for himself and his freedmen, friends, and clients, with 11 feet of land.
EDCS-09302307.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording land set aside for a man, his freedmen, friends, and clients, likely dating to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-09302308.translation: Secunda, freedwoman of Varia Licinilla, lives for herself and for those written below: alive, Masculus, freedman of Decimus Terentius, son of Decimus; alive, Primus, freedman of Gaius Varius, son of Potitus; alive, Varius, freedman of Crassus; alive, Varius, freedman of Crassus; alive, Varius, freedman of Crassus; Varia, freedwoman of Crassus; Gaius Varius Licinius.
EDCS-09302308.summary: This funerary inscription records the individuals for whom a plot of land is reserved, including a freedwoman, her associates, and other freedmen and women, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302310.translation: Lucius Tatinius Felix and his wife Coelia Primula, daughter of Lucius, live for themselves, with 15 feet of land in every direction.
EDCS-09302310.summary: This is a funerary inscription marking a plot of land reserved for a couple, Lucius Tatinius Felix and Coelia Primula, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302311.translation: To the Divine Shades of Taurus Amabilis, dearest brother.
EDCS-09302311.summary: This is a funerary dedication to a beloved brother, Taurus Amabilis, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302312.translation: Publia Martia made this for the Divine Shades of Terefia Materna, most dutiful mother.
EDCS-09302312.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Publia Martia for her mother, Terefia Materna, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302313.summary: This is a brief funerary inscription stating that Publius Terefrius Tertius is commemorated, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302314.translation: For Titus Terentius Faustus, son of Titus, and alive for Titus Terentius, freedman of Titus.
EDCS-09302314.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication for Titus Terentius Faustus and his freedman, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302315.translation: Marcus Terentius Liberalis, freedman of Speratus, lives for himself and for living Agilis, freedwoman of Speratus; Marcus Terentius Speratus (died); with 17 feet of land in the field and 15 feet in the front.
EDCS-09302315.summary: This funerary inscription records a plot of land reserved for a freedman, his freedwoman associate, and the man who established it, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302316.translation: Quintus Terentius, freedman of Quintus, S. (lives).
EDCS-09302316.summary: This is a brief funerary inscription, possibly marking a grave plot, for Quintus Terentius, a freedman, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302317.translation: For Sextus Terentius Segeius, freedman of Sextus, and 15 feet in the front.
EDCS-09302317.summary: This funerary inscription dedicates a plot of land, 15 feet in width, to Sextus Terentius Segeius, a freedman, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302318.translation: and for Terentia Grata, wife of Terentius, daughter of Aulus, Prima.
EDCS-09302318.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Terentia Grata, wife of Terentius, likely part of a larger funerary monument.

EDCS-09302319.translation: Tes, freedwoman of Marcus, rests here by his will.
EDCS-09302319.summary: This inscription records the burial of Tes, a freedwoman of Marcus, with her resting place specified by his will.

EDCS-09302321.translation: Quintus Titius, son of Titus, of the Voltinia tribe, is buried here for Quintius; his plot is 29 feet in front in every direction.
EDCS-09302321.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Quintus Titius and specifies the dimensions of his burial plot.

EDCS-09302322.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: for Aulus Tolumnius, Decimus Tolumnius, Lucius Tolumnius. Lucius Tolumnius [dedicated this].
EDCS-09302322.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Manes (spirits of the underworld) for members of the Tolumnia family, likely by Lucius Tolumnius.

EDCS-09302323.translation: For Tolumnia, daughter of Lucius, Successa, in the land 15 feet [deep].
EDCS-09302323.summary: This funerary inscription records a burial plot for Tolumnia Successa, daughter of Lucius, specifying its size.

EDCS-09302324.translation: Publius Tossius Himerus, freedman of Publius, lives [on] for himself and for Herennia Asia, freedwoman of Lucius, his partner.
EDCS-09302324.summary: This funerary inscription is a self-dedication by Publius Tossius Himerus for himself and his partner Herennia Asia.

EDCS-09302325.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Lucius Trebellius Syrillo. Roscia Asella, wife, for her most devoted husband.
EDCS-09302325.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Lucius Trebellius Syrillo by his wife Roscia Asella.

EDCS-09302326.translation: Lucius Trebius Verna, son of Lucius.
EDCS-09302326.summary: This inscription is a simple epitaph identifying Lucius Trebius Verna, son of Lucius.

EDCS-09302327.summary: This is a concise epitaph identifying Lucius Trebius Verna.

EDCS-09302328.translation: For himself and for his wife, Trute, daughter of Iog, son of Filotius.
EDCS-09302328.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication for the author and his wife, Trute.

EDCS-09302329.translation: Fin and Tullia, on the death of her husband, for Ves[---], his wife.
EDCS-09302329.summary: This inscription is a dedication made by Fin and Tullia for their deceased wife, likely a funerary monument.

EDCS-09302331.translation: By the judgment/arrangement of Lucius V[---].
EDCS-09302331.summary: This fragmentary inscription records an action or decision made under the authority of Lucius V[---].

EDCS-09302332.translation: Sextus Vabius Lepidus for himself and for Heliadis, freedwoman of Publius, his wife, 15 feet in every direction on the front.
EDCS-09302332.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Sextus Vabius Lepidus for himself and his wife Heliadis, specifying the dimensions of the funerary plot.

EDCS-09302333.translation: Viva Vabia Origo, his wife, made this for herself and...
EDCS-09302333.summary: This incomplete inscription indicates that Viva Vabia Origo, a wife, commissioned a monument for herself and possibly others.

EDCS-09302334.translation: For Publius Vaetius, son of Lucius, C[---].
EDCS-09302334.summary: This inscription is a dedication or memorial for Publius Vaetius, son of Lucius.

EDCS-09302335.translation: Gaius Valerius, son of Lucius Cornelius[---].
EDCS-09302335.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely the beginning of a dedication or epitaph for Gaius Valerius, son of Lucius Cornelius.

EDCS-09302337.translation: While he was alive, Titus Valerius[---].
EDCS-09302337.summary: This inscription seems to be the beginning of a dedication or epitaph commissioned by Titus Valerius during his lifetime.

EDCS-09302340.translation: For Lucius Valerius Felix, freedman of Maxumus, and for Antonia Cinnamis, daughter of Caius.
EDCS-09302340.summary: This inscription records a dedication or memorial for Lucius Valerius Felix and Antonia Cinnamis, possibly a married couple.

EDCS-09302341.translation: Aulus Valerius Hilarus, son of Aulus, is buried here.
EDCS-09302341.summary: This is a funerary inscription stating that Aulus Valerius Hilarus is buried in this location.

EDCS-09302342.translation: Gaius Valerius Linus for himself and for his mother Aemilia.
EDCS-09302342.summary: This funerary inscription by Gaius Valerius Linus is for himself and his mother Aemilia.

EDCS-09302343.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Aquilia Viatrix placed this for her most devoted father, Valerius Mansuetus.
EDCS-09302343.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication of a monument by Aquilia Viatrix to her father, Valerius Mansuetus.

EDCS-09302344.translation: For Valerius Maximus and Terentia Hermais and their freedwoman Terentia Grata.
EDCS-09302344.summary: This inscription records a dedication for Valerius Maximus, Terentia Hermais, and their freedwoman Terentia Grata.

EDCS-09302345.translation: Death of Lucius Valerius Maximus, son of Lucius, buried here; 10 feet in front after his death.
EDCS-09302345.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Lucius Valerius Maximus and specifies burial space.

EDCS-09302346.translation: Lives on: Lucius Valerius Philargyrus and...
EDCS-09302346.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to be a funerary dedication mentioning Lucius Valerius Philargyrus.

EDCS-09302347.translation: Valerius Philologus, freedman of Marcus, and his wife Qutia Silvana: I await my husband.
EDCS-09302347.summary: This inscription, possibly a tombstone, mentions Valerius Philologus, his wife Qutia Silvana, and a statement of waiting.

EDCS-09302348.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Lucius Valerius Chrestus and Valeria Primilla and Valeria Crescentina, natural children, to their most devoted father, Lucius Valerius Primigenius, and to Valeria Chresta, husband.
EDCS-09302348.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication by the children and spouse of Lucius Valerius Primigenius to his memory.

EDCS-09302349.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Frontonia Sextilla made this for her most dutiful husband, Valerius Quintinus.
EDCS-09302349.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication by Frontonia Sextilla for her husband, Valerius Quintinus.

EDCS-09302350.translation: To Titus Valerius Successus, from Fabia Icele, and Quintus Fabius Fuscus.
EDCS-09302350.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or memorial for Titus Valerius Successus, with mentions of Fabia Icele and Quintus Fabius Fuscus.

EDCS-09302351.summary: This is a simple dedication or memorial inscription for Marcus Valerius Tutus.

EDCS-09302352.translation: To Valerius Ursulus, from his best friend Hermione.
EDCS-09302352.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Hermione to her friend Valerius Ursulus.

EDCS-09302354.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Aurelius Crescentinus made this for his most devoted wife, Valeria Festa.
EDCS-09302354.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Aurelius Crescentinus for his wife, Valeria Festa.

EDCS-09302355.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Gnaeus Pompeius Iustus for his dearest wife, Valeria Lucilia.
EDCS-09302355.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Gnaeus Pompeius Iustus for his wife, Valeria Lucilia.

EDCS-09302356.translation: Valeria Postumina made this for herself and for her descendants.
EDCS-09302356.summary: This is a funerary epitaph purchased by Valeria Postumina for herself and her descendants.

EDCS-09302357.translation: Valeria Prima lives for herself and for Gaius Vibius Maxumus.
EDCS-09302357.summary: This is a funerary epitaph indicating that Valeria Prima purchased a burial plot for herself and Gaius Vibius Maxumus.

EDCS-09302358.translation: For the deceased Valeria Rustica, daughter of Sextus, for the deceased Valeria Tertulla, daughter of Sextus, for the deceased Marcus Laburius Gratus, for the deceased Titus Artorius Modestus, 13 feet in every direction.
EDCS-09302358.summary: This funerary epitaph records the deceased individuals for whom a burial plot of 13 feet in all directions was purchased.

EDCS-09302359.translation: Strenua, freedwoman of the deceased Valeria Faustae, mother of Narcissus, lives on 15 feet of land.
EDCS-09302359.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Strenua, a freedwoman, who purchased 15 feet of land.

EDCS-09302360.translation: Marcus Vallius Montanus lives on 15.5 feet in front.
EDCS-09302360.summary: This is a funerary epitaph indicating that Marcus Vallius Montanus purchased a plot of 15.5 feet.

EDCS-09302361.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Saturninus for his most deserving wife, Vallia Urbica.
EDCS-09302361.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Saturninus for his wife, Vallia Urbica.

EDCS-09302362.translation: Quintus Varius Nicephor, freedman of the Caian family, and Varia Pamphila, freedwoman of the Caian family, live here; they rest here.
EDCS-09302362.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Varius Nicephor and Varia Pamphila, both freedpersons, stating they are buried there.

EDCS-09302364.translation: Varia, freedwoman of the woman; Rufio, freedman of the woman.
EDCS-09302364.summary: This inscription appears to record the status of two freedpersons, Varia and Rufio, possibly in relation to their patroness.

EDCS-09302366.translation: Gaius Vatinius, son of Publius, of the Voltinia tribe; Gaius Vatinius; Caius, son of Gaius; Vatinia, daughter of Caius, Tertia.
EDCS-09302366.summary: This inscription appears to be a list of names, possibly related to a family or group, with tribal affiliations mentioned.

EDCS-09302367.translation: Marcus Uccius Optatus, freedman of Marcus, and his patron made this for themselves, fifteen feet in every direction.
EDCS-09302367.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the self-funded commission of a tomb by a freedman, Marcus Uccius Optatus, for himself and his patron.

EDCS-09302368.translation: Veia, daughter of Caius, of the Sergia tribe; Veiatia, daughter of Publius.
EDCS-09302368.summary: This inscription lists two female names with their patronymics and tribal affiliations.

EDCS-09302369.translation: Venusta, freedwoman of Atepomarus, made this for herself and for her freedman Melissus while alive.
EDCS-09302369.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording a freedwoman, Venusta, who commissioned her own tomb for herself and her freedman.

EDCS-09302371.translation: Aulus Veratius Fronto, son of Quintus, of the Voltinia tribe, and his wife Fabia Paculla, daughter of Lucius, are alive; fifteen feet.
EDCS-09302371.summary: This is a funerary inscription indicating that Aulus Veratius Fronto and his wife Fabia Paculla commissioned their tomb while alive, specifying its dimensions.

EDCS-09302372.translation: Verecundus, son of Assorenus, and Silvanus, son of Assorenus, and Primula Verria made this monument for themselves while alive, decreeing that no heir shall sell it.
EDCS-09302372.summary: This funerary inscription records the self-commissioned monument by Verecundus and Silvanus, sons of Assorenus, and Primula Verria, with a stipulation against future sale.

EDCS-09302373.translation: Quintus Vergilius Bucius, freedman of Quintus, is alive; fifteen feet in front, [---] feet in the field.
EDCS-09302373.summary: This funerary inscription marks the plot for Quintus Vergilius Bucius, a freedman, specifying front dimensions and indicating further measurements for the land.

EDCS-09302375.translation: Gaius Verrius is alive for himself and his family; Monatana Prima is alive; Lucius Pomponius.
EDCS-09302375.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, including Gaius Verrius and Lucius Pomponius, indicating they are alive and making provisions for themselves and their families.

EDCS-09302376.translation: To Marcus Verrius Ingenuus, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-09302376.summary: This is a dedication to Marcus Verrius Ingenuus, a freedman.

EDCS-09302378.summary: This inscription simply records the name Gaius Vesidius Severus.

EDCS-09302379.translation: To Gaius Vettienus Metro, freedman of Gaius Vettienus, son of Titus, of the Pollia tribe, [and to] Lucius Mirmio, freedman of Lucius, [and to] Menio, brother [of Metro], and to Heron, freedman of Gaius.
EDCS-09302379.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication for several individuals, including Metro, Lucius Mirmio, Menio, and Heron, likely within a family context.

EDCS-09302380.translation: Caius Vettius Faustus lives, on account of the death of Valeria, freedwoman of Caius. Caius Vettius Saturninus lives, Vettia Fausta, daughter of Caius, lives, Marcus Vettius December lives.
EDCS-09302380.summary: This inscription lists living members of the Vettius family, possibly on a tombstone, noting the death of Valeria.

EDCS-09302381.translation: Titus Vettius Ruga, son of Titus, of the Voltinia tribe.
EDCS-09302381.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph identifying Titus Vettius Ruga, son of Titus, and his tribal affiliation.

EDCS-09302382.translation: Lucius Veturius Propinqus [dedicated this] to Nataliae Emerauta. In front [there are] feet, in the field [there are] feet.
EDCS-09302382.summary: This inscription, likely from a tombstone or boundary marker, records Lucius Veturius Propinqus dedicating land or space to Nataliae Emerauta and specifies measurements.

EDCS-09302383.summary: This is a very brief funerary epitaph identifying Quintus Vibius, son of Quintus.

EDCS-09302384.translation: Numerius Vibius Rufus, of the Teretina tribe, freedman of Tetrinia and her husband.
EDCS-09302384.summary: This inscription identifies Numerius Vibius Rufus, his tribal affiliation, and his status as a freedman of Tetrinia and her husband.

EDCS-09302385.translation: [dedicated this] to himself, to Vibia Lida, his companion, and to Trocinoia, freedwoman.
EDCS-09302385.summary: This fragmentary funerary inscription records a dedication made by an individual to himself, his companion Vibia Lida, and a freedwoman named Trocinoia.

EDCS-09302386.translation: Vibia Tertia, freedwoman of Vari, for herself, and for Quintus Asellius Gemellus, her husband, and for [her] household.
EDCS-09302386.summary: This funerary inscription records Vibia Tertia, a freedwoman, dedicating the monument to herself, her husband Quintus Asellius Gemellus, and her household.

EDCS-09302387.translation: Vidius Fronto, son of Marcus, is buried here.
EDCS-09302387.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph stating that Vidius Fronto, son of Marcus, is buried at this location.

EDCS-09302388.translation: Lucilla placed [this] according to the will of Vifidius Ampius, freedman of Publius.
EDCS-09302388.summary: This inscription records that Lucilla erected a monument according to the will of Vifidius Ampius, who was a freedman of Publius.

EDCS-09302389.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Caius Vifidius Secundus lived 19 years. Vifidia Aventina, his mother, [erected this] for her most devoted son.
EDCS-09302389.summary: A funerary epitaph for Caius Vifidius Secundus, dedicated by his mother.

EDCS-09302391.translation: He made this from his own property for himself and for his freedman colleague, Astragalus, freedman of Marcus Vinicius Epagatinus.
EDCS-09302391.summary: A funerary inscription recording a self-dedication and dedication for a freedman colleague.

EDCS-09302392.translation: To Marcus Vinicius Cappadoces, in the field.
EDCS-09302392.summary: A fragmentary inscription, possibly a boundary marker or dedicating a plot of land to Marcus Vinicius Cappadoces.

EDCS-09302393.summary: A fragmentary inscription, likely dedicating a monument or plot of land to Marcus Vinicius Manius.

EDCS-09302394.translation: Marcus Vinucius Lascivos, freedman of Marcus, for himself and for Aemilia Apicula and for his freedman Marcus Vinicius Clemens.
EDCS-09302394.summary: A funerary inscription recording a self-dedication and dedications for family members and a freedman.

EDCS-09302395.translation: Vinicia Campana, daughter of Marcus, for herself and for her husband Lucius Licinius Asticus, fifteen feet in every direction.
EDCS-09302395.summary: An inscription recording the dimensions of a plot of land dedicated by Vinicia Campana for herself and her husband.

EDCS-09302396.translation: Sextus Serranius Se [erected this] for the living Vinicia Concessa.
EDCS-09302396.summary: A fragmentary inscription indicating a dedication made by Sextus Serranius for Vinicia Concessa.

EDCS-09302397.translation: Vinicia Donata, freedwoman of Marcus, enclosed her monument with a wall; this place and wall will not pass to an heir, nor is this a place for burial.
EDCS-09302397.summary: An inscription clarifying property rights and burial restrictions around a monument enclosed by Vinicia Donata.

EDCS-09302398.translation: Vinicia Nota, freedwoman of Epagathinus, made this while alive for after her death.
EDCS-09302398.summary: A funerary inscription recording a self-dedication made by Vinicia Nota during her lifetime for her posthumous burial.

EDCS-09302399.summary: A very fragmentary inscription mentioning Viridia as a mother, possibly part of a funerary monument.

EDCS-09302400.summary: This is a funerary inscription fragment, likely recording the deceased's name and possibly a dedication for themselves and others, from an unknown date.

EDCS-09302401.translation: Vitalis Cuarota lives, and Sextus Cato with Optata...
EDCS-09302401.summary: This funerary inscription records the names of Vitalis Cuarota and Sextus Cato with Optata, indicating they are alive, from an unknown date.

EDCS-09302402.translation: ...for Aelia Ulia, daughter of Sextus, [daughter] of Sextus P...
EDCS-09302402.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary inscription dedicating the monument to Aelia Ulia, daughter of Sextus, from an unknown date.

EDCS-09302403.translation: Quintus Ummidius Faustus, freedman of Licinius, lives; Quintus Ummidius Auctus, freedman of Faustus, lives; and Quintus Ummidius Tersita, freedman of Faustus, and Ummidia Ursa, freedwoman of Tersita, live.
EDCS-09302403.summary: This funerary inscription records the lives of Quintus Ummidius Faustus, Quintus Ummidius Auctus, Quintus Ummidius Tersita, and Ummidia Ursa, all related through freedman status, from an unknown date.

EDCS-09302404.translation: Lucius Voconius Ranae lives, Lucius Voconius and his freedwoman Rana, daughter of Valeria Sexti, wife of Elapius, having died; Voconia Primula lives, daughter of Lucius Voconius, [and] Atius...
EDCS-09302404.summary: This funerary inscription records the lives of Lucius Voconius Ranae, his freedwoman Rana, and Voconia Primula, noting the death of Elapius and mentioning Lucius Voconius, from an unknown date.

EDCS-09302405.translation: Decimus Voltilius Fronto, freedman of Decimus, is buried here; his wife Maxsuma, daughter of Publius, lives.
EDCS-09302405.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Decimus Voltilius Fronto and the life of his wife Maxsuma, from an unknown date.

EDCS-09302406.translation: Titus Voltilius Hilarius, freedman of Titus...
EDCS-09302406.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary inscription identifying Titus Voltilius Hilarius as a freedman of Titus, from an unknown date.

EDCS-09302407.translation: Publius Voltilius Rufio has died, and Mamia Tertulla lives.
EDCS-09302407.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Publius Voltilius Rufio and the continued life of Mamia Tertulla, from an unknown date.

EDCS-09302408.translation: Lucius Voltilius Suavis, freedman of Lucius, alive, for himself and for his wife Salonia Casta, for his patron Lucius Voltilius Severus, for his freedman Faustus, son of Severus...
EDCS-09302408.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Lucius Voltilius Suavis for himself, his wife Salonia Casta, his patron Lucius Voltilius Severus, and his freedman Faustus, from an unknown date.

EDCS-09302409.translation: For Voltilia Secunda, who has died.
EDCS-09302409.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Voltilia Secunda, likely recording her death, from an unknown date.

EDCS-09302410.translation: Lucius Votienus Pudens, freedman of Lucius, and Licentia, freedwoman of Fadia, are alive.
EDCS-09302410.summary: This is a funerary inscription, likely from a tomb, commemorating Lucius Votienus Pudens and Licentia, stating they are alive, suggesting they erected it themselves or it was set up in anticipation of their death.

EDCS-09302411.translation: to my patron, and to Quintus, and to Urbana, freedwoman of the woman.
EDCS-09302411.summary: This fragmented inscription seems to record dedications to a patron and two freed individuals, likely part of a larger epitaph or dedication.

EDCS-09302412.summary: This very brief inscription likely records a dedication to an individual named Ursius and the dedicator themselves, possibly on a tomb or altar.

EDCS-09302413.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For Ilianus, 10 months and 4 days. Ursa to her dear fellow freedman.
EDCS-09302413.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Ilianus after 10 months and 4 days, dedicated by Ursa, his fellow freedman.

EDCS-09302414.summary: This is a fragmented inscription likely recording a dedication or funerary notice for Urvia, a freedwoman of Publius.

EDCS-09302415.translation: to Publius Usulenus Celadus, freedman of Publius, and to Prima, freedwoman of the freedman, 15 feet of land, and to Prima, the mother.
EDCS-09302415.summary: This inscription records a bequest of 15 feet of land to Publius Usulenus Celadus, his freedwoman Prima, and Prima's mother, likely a funerary or property dedication.

EDCS-09302416.translation: Usulena Procula, daughter of Titus, died; for herself and her relatives whose names are written.
EDCS-09302416.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Usulena Procula, daughter of Titus, and states it is for herself and her relatives whose names are also inscribed.

EDCS-09302417.translation: Usulena Ursa, freedwoman of Publius, made this from her own resources for herself, and for her family, and for Herennius Rufioni, her husband, and for Usulenus Acastus, her brother.
EDCS-09302417.summary: This funerary inscription states that Usulena Ursa, a freedwoman, erected this monument for herself, her family, her husband Herennius Rufioni, and her brother Usulenus Acastus.

EDCS-09302418.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For Usulenía Lupa, patroness. Usulenius Geminianus to his most respected wife, and Voconius Eutychianus to his most respected husband.
EDCS-09302418.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Usulenía Lupa, a patroness, by Usulenius Geminianus (presumably her freedman or relative) for his wife and by Voconius Eutychianus for his husband.

EDCS-09302419.translation: Utia Philoponi, freedwoman, is alive; for herself and for Publius Utis Philoponus, freedman of Publius.
EDCS-09302419.summary: This inscription, similar to EDCS-09302410, indicates that Utia Philoponi, a freedwoman, is alive, and it is set up for herself and Publius Utis Philoponus, a freedman.

EDCS-09302420.translation: To Zosima, freedwoman of Marcus Terentius Speratus. Marcus Terentius Speratus, 15 feet in front, 15 feet in width. This monument will not pass to an heir.
EDCS-09302420.summary: A funerary monument for Zosima, freedwoman of Marcus Terentius Speratus, with specified dimensions and a clause preventing inheritance.

EDCS-09302431.summary: A funerary epitaph identifying the deceased as Poll, son of Numerius.

EDCS-09302432.translation: To the departed spirits. Six years old. Illanus tino odo.
EDCS-09302432.summary: A funerary epitaph for a child named Illanus, who died at age six.

EDCS-09302437.translation: He (dedicated this) to his parents, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-09302437.summary: An epitaph recording the dedication of a monument by a freedman of Lucius to his parents.

EDCS-09302439.summary: A funerary epitaph identifying the deceased as Ellius, son of Aulus.

EDCS-09302441.summary: An epitaph identifying Unseinius as the freedman of Publius.

EDCS-09302493.summary: An epitaph identifying Accellus as the freedman of Lucius.

EDCS-09302527.summary: A funerary epitaph identifying the deceased as Caius, son of Llo.

EDCS-09302533.translation: By the mercy of God and Christ, this threshold was set up in the 4th year of the consulship of Valentinian Augustus, the 6th day before the Kalends of December, in the 19th year of the episcopate of Rusticus, bishop, son of the bishop Bonosus, grandson of the bishop Arator, companion of bishop Venerius in the monastery, fellow presbyter of the church of Marseilles, in the 15th year of his episcopate, on the 5th day of the year, the 3rd day before the Ides of October. With Urso the presbyter and Hermetes the deacon and their followers as curators, the work of taking down the walls of the church, long since burnt, began on the 37th day, to be placed in the foundation on the fourth day. In the 2nd year, the 7th day before the Ides of October, the apse was completed. Montanus the subdeacon, Marcellus the prefect of Gaul, a worshipper of God, by entreaty compelled the bishop to undertake this task, promising the necessary expenses, which he provided during the two years of his administration. To the artisans, 600 solidi for the work and other expenses. Henceforth, offerings of the holy bishop Venerius, 100 solidi; of bishop Dynamus, 50; of Oresi, 200; of Agroecius and Deconianus Salutus.
EDCS-09302533.summary: A lengthy inscription detailing the reconstruction and rebuilding of a church in Marseilles, initiated and funded by Bishop Rusticus and others, with specific dates, officials, and financial contributions, dating to the late 4th or early 5th century AD.

EDCS-09302534.translation: Rusticus had it made in the 30th year of his episcopate.
EDCS-09302534.summary: A brief inscription stating that the monument or work was commissioned by Rusticus in the 30th year of his episcopate.

EDCS-09302535.translation: Pray for me, your Rustic. This altar is a gift from the former priest Hermetis.
EDCS-09302535.summary: This is an inscription on an altar, likely a personal offering or dedication by a priest named Hermetis, with a plea for prayers for Rusticus.

EDCS-09302536.translation: In good memory, Maximus rests in peace in these tombs, who lived 25 years, 7 months, 10 days and died on the Kalends of June, after the consulship of Anastasius and Venantius.
EDCS-09302536.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the life and death of Maximus, who died on the Kalends of June after a specific consulship, likely from the 6th century.

EDCS-09302537.translation: Here rests in peace, in good memory, Domitius, who lived more or less 37 years, died on the Kalends of July, in the 5th indiction, during the consulship of the most illustrious man Mavortius. The burial place of Domitius from the village of Tauson.
EDCS-09302537.summary: This is a funerary inscription detailing the life and death of Domitius, who died on the Kalends of July during a specific indiction and consulship, and mentions his village of origin.

EDCS-09302538.translation: Here rests in peace, in good memory, Palenope, who lived more or less 50 years, died on the 10th day before the Kalends of March, in the fourth indiction, in the 10th year of the reign of our lord Teuderecius.
EDCS-09302538.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Palenope, who died on the 10th day before the Kalends of March during the fourth indiction and the tenth regnal year of King Teuderecius.

EDCS-09302540.translation: The threshold of the gate is opened for me, so that I may deserve after your kingdoms, O Decembres, in the 4th indiction, in the 5th year of the reign of the most glorious lord Atanagild the king.
EDCS-09302540.summary: This inscription seems to be a dedication or a plea for passage, possibly related to entering a sacred space, during the reign of King Atanagild.

EDCS-09302541.translation: In good memory, Petalonius (?) rests, who lived more or less 70 years, died in July, in the first indiction, in the second year of the reign of our lord Liubanus the king.
EDCS-09302541.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Petalonius (?), who lived about 70 years, in July during the first indiction and the second regnal year of King Liubanus.

EDCS-09302542.translation: On the 4th day before the Kalends of January, in the twelfth indiction, in the seventh year of the reign of our most glorious lord Reccared the king.
EDCS-09302542.summary: This inscription marks a specific date, the 4th day before the Kalends of January, during the twelfth indiction and the seventh regnal year of King Reccared.

EDCS-09302543.translation: Here rests in peace, in good memory, Adelfius, on the 3rd day before the Ides of January.
EDCS-09302543.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Adelfius, who died on the 3rd day before the Ides of January.

EDCS-09302544.translation: On the 3rd day before the third Kalends of May, in the tenth indiction, in the sixth year of the reign of our lord Panditur, the gate is opened, and the heavenly house in which the bones of the ever illustrious Ceragus lie, where Christ now walks the starry path for all peoples.
EDCS-09302544.summary: This funerary inscription, likely from the 6th century, describes a tomb as a heavenly house for the bones of Ceragus, with a theological reflection on Christ's path.

EDCS-09302546.translation: Oppressed by many crimes, as a follower of sins, he built this temple to God with his wife Wiillesinda, always adhering to faithful companionship, who constantly urged him to become a partner in vows; they wanted to fulfill it together, and they placed their souls in eternal courts with Christ.
EDCS-09302546.summary: This is a dedication inscription for a temple built by Diusvirus (likely a mistranscription for a name) and his wife Wiillesinda, expressing their piety and devotion.

EDCS-09302547.translation: Scarcely had you passed Elysium when you entered the rosy realm, barely had three years passed for you and the vine and the cluster when you were given to Gregorio Festa, lying in your tomb. How small were the vows made then, alas! How brief is life, how brief is marriage! You were only a minor in age, although in all other respects the greatest of Festas: affection, piety, beauty, chastity, learned in angelic law, dedicated to God. Here you lie; this is pleasing to the gods above. We too shall go there, if only faith is holy, if only belief is pious, Festa, our glory. We shall certainly come together, if my life is upright, if you care for me. But you, supreme ruler of holy souls, make what we desire firm, make what we wish swift.
EDCS-09302547.summary: This inscription is a lengthy epitaph commemorating Festa, a young woman of noble qualities who died at a young age, lamenting the brevity of life and marriage.

EDCS-09302548.translation: Here rests in peace Julianus of good memory, who lived approximately 55 years. He died.
EDCS-09302548.summary: This is a simple epitaph recording the death of Julianus and his approximate age at death.

EDCS-09302549.translation: Here lies entombed in peace Maria, the abbess of venerable memory, consecrated to God, who in the days of her life studied sacred works, persevering in the Lord's commands, always eager in almsgiving, devoted to prayer and meditation, observing the monastic rules with the utmost diligence, and lived in virginity for God. She died on the 6th day before the Kalends of June.
EDCS-09302549.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Maria, an abbess of venerable memory, highlighting her piety, devotion to religious study, almsgiving, and observance of monastic rules.

EDCS-09302550.translation: Here rests in peace Martina of good memory, approximately 36 years old. Died on the 1st day before the Kalends of August in the 21st year.
EDCS-09302550.summary: This epitaph records the death of Martina, noting her approximate age and the date of her death in the 21st year (likely of an emperor or consul).

EDCS-09302551.translation: Here rests in peace Pelagia of good memory, who lived approximately 30 years. Died on the 10th day before the Kalends of January in the sixth indiction.
EDCS-09302551.summary: This epitaph records the death of Pelagia, noting her approximate age and the date of her death, including the sixth indiction.

EDCS-09302552.translation: Here rests Secundina of good memory, who lived approximately 30 years. Died on the 12th day before the Kalends of March.
EDCS-09302552.summary: This epitaph records the death of Secundina, noting her approximate age and the date of her death.

EDCS-09302557.translation: Lives. Lucius Salonius Buccio, freedman of Lucius and Publius, for himself and for the deceased Lucius Salonius Hilarus, freedman of Lucius and Publius, a salt worker.
EDCS-09302557.summary: A funerary inscription by a freedman for himself and another freedman who was a salt worker.

EDCS-09302559.translation: Evangelus, a slave of the companions, gladly paid his vow to Mercury, as was deserved.
EDCS-09302559.summary: This is a votive inscription from Evangelus, a slave, to Mercury, recording the fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-09302560.translation: To the Divine Shades. Rusticania, freedwoman of Lucius, lived 111 years and months.
EDCS-09302560.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the Divine Shades for Rusticania, a freedwoman of Lucius, recording her exceptional longevity.

EDCS-09302561.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription, likely a tombstone, bearing only the name Lucius Aelius Cantaber.

EDCS-09302562.translation: Quintus Valerius Hermetio: a plot of land was given to Mercury Augustus by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-09302562.summary: This inscription records the allocation of a plot of land to the deity Mercury Augustus by a decree of the local town council (decurions).

EDCS-09302563.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Antonius Gordianus, Pious, Fortunate, Invincible Augustus, chief priest, holding tribunician power for the second time, consul, father of the country. The decumani of Narbo.
EDCS-09302563.summary: An inscription dedicating the honor to Emperor Gordian III, likely by the tax collectors ('decumani') of Narbo.

EDCS-09302564.translation: Kantasnis and Rogamos and from Peta, let the savate save, not from Lerano, and from Uxnesos, let the apeteia and Eleta save, and from Neso, let the nuki of Nisqie be heard. The ulaten ruet P
EDCS-09302564.summary: This is an inscription with unclear content, possibly related to pleas for divine intervention or protection, with personal names and place names mentioned.

EDCS-09302565.translation: Nicasquite, we ask you, may S syatis numema, S niuldela, may the res not be, may the cumas not be.
EDCS-09302565.summary: This inscription appears to be a plea or prayer addressed to Nicasquite, asking for protection from unspecified negative forces.

EDCS-09302566.translation: Kenumene, to the greatest flaucre, his siroes, whatever is good, let it be. Laaokrios, the sculptor, made this for Atxexiaia. Not to you, M. Tatinus, your kin.
EDCS-09302566.summary: This inscription is likely a dedication or commission of a work of art, possibly a statue or relief, by Laaokrios for Atxexiaia, with a specific exclusion of M. Tatinus.

EDCS-09302570.translation: Domxsaanis, we ask you, and from Tamus, Dinno NN.
EDCS-09302570.summary: This inscription is a short invocation or request addressed to Domxsaanis and Tamus, possibly deities or significant figures, with NN likely representing unknown individuals.

EDCS-09302572.summary: This is a very brief inscription identifying a location or object named Centunculus.

EDCS-09302573.translation: Publius Cornelius Phileros gladly and deservedly paid his vow to Larrasoni.
EDCS-09302573.summary: This is a votive inscription where Publius Cornelius Phileros paid a vow to Larrasoni, likely a deity or a local spirit.

EDCS-09302574.translation: Titus Valerius Senecio, son of Caius; Publius Usulenus Phileros, freedman of Veienton; Titus Alfidius Stabilio, freedman of Titus; Marcus Usulenus Charito, freedman of Marcus. As magistrates of the pagi, from the income of the shrine, they took care to have cells built and they approved them.
EDCS-09302574.summary: An inscription by four local magistrates (magistri pagi) who oversaw the construction and approval of shrine cells using temple funds.

EDCS-09302575.translation: To Caius Cominius Bituitionus, son of Caius, of the Voltinia tribe, praetor of the colony of Carpento[rate?].
EDCS-09302575.summary: A dedication to Caius Cominius Bituitionus, identified as a praetor of the colony of Carpento[rate?].

EDCS-09302576.translation: Lucius Cornelius lived for himself and for Rutilia Exorata.
EDCS-09302576.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording that Lucius Cornelius established this monument for himself and Rutilia Exorata, indicating their relationship.

EDCS-09302577.translation: Fortunata fulfills her vow to Jupiter willingly.
EDCS-09302577.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter by Fortunata.

EDCS-09302578.translation: Cnaeus Pompeius Probus, curator of the temple, gladly and deservedly paid his vow to the Mother of the Gods.
EDCS-09302578.summary: This is a votive inscription where Cnaeus Pompeius Probus, in his role as temple curator, paid a vow to the Mother of the Gods.

EDCS-09302579.translation: Taurinus set up a vow for his father, the Manes.
EDCS-09302579.summary: This is a funerary or votive inscription where Taurinus set up a vow for his deceased father, invoking the Manes (spirits of the dead).

EDCS-09302580.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Caius Pompeius Polibius sic votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-09302580.translation: Caius Pompeius Polibius willingly and deservedly fulfills his vow to Jupiter Best and Greatest.
EDCS-09302580.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Caius Pompeius Polibius.

EDCS-09302581.translation: Caius Pompeius Quartus willingly and with a willing heart dedicates to his Mars.
EDCS-09302581.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Mars by Caius Pompeius Quartus.

EDCS-09302583.translation: To the god Erditse, consecrated. Borodates gladly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-09302583.summary: This is a votive inscription where Borodates consecrated and paid a vow to the god Erditse.

EDCS-09302584.translation: To Jupiter, Best and Greatest, Paullus, son of Paullus, willingly fulfilled his vow as was deserved.
EDCS-09302584.summary: A votive inscription from an individual named Paullus to Jupiter, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09302586.translation: Ceicos fulfilled his vow willingly as was deserved.
EDCS-09302586.summary: A votive inscription by an individual named Ceicos, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09302592.translation: During the consulship of Publius Vatinius and Quintus Fufius, these magistrates had a temple, base, and sundial constructed, and Cirratus Diallus, slave of Attius Publius, and Surus Hilarus, slave of Flavius Marcus, and Iorum, freedman of Lucius, and Philodamus, slave of Volusius Caius, and Pindarus, slave of Trebius Lucius, and Curiatius Appi, freedman, supervised their construction.
EDCS-09302592.summary: A building inscription from the time of consuls Publius Vatinius and Quintus Fufius, detailing the construction of a temple, base, and sundial supervised by several freedmen and slaves.

EDCS-09302593.translation: To Cupitus, son of Tolosanus, for Tolosanus his father, for Domestica his mother, for Graphis his sister, for himself and his descendants.
EDCS-09302593.summary: An epitaph or dedication from Cupitus to his family members, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09302594.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Marcus Iulius Lupus, for his son Phoebion.
EDCS-09302594.summary: A funerary dedication from Marcus Iulius Lupus to his son Phoebion, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09302602.translation: May peace be with you. Here rests David the priest.
EDCS-09302602.summary: A funerary inscription for a priest named David, likely from the Christian era in Roman territory.

EDCS-09302603.translation: Here rests the well-remembered Doctorbodes, who lived thirty-five years.
EDCS-09302603.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Doctorbodes, who died at the age of thirty-five.

EDCS-09302604.translation: ASTVT Ermeneldes who lived more or less 60 years rests in the Lord's day before the Kalends of August.
EDCS-09302604.summary: A funerary inscription for Ermeneldes, who lived approximately 60 years and died before the Kalends of August, likely from the Christian era.

EDCS-09302605.translation: Here lies the well-remembered Eugenius, who lived fifteen years and nine months; he rested on the 10th day before the Kalends of February.
EDCS-09302605.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Eugenius, who died at the age of fifteen years and nine months.

EDCS-09302606.translation: The burial of Felicisima, who lived 45 years, servant of God; she rested on the 13th day before the Kalends of May.
EDCS-09302606.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription for Felicisima, who died at the age of 45.

EDCS-09302607.translation: Here lies Hiraclius the newly born, who lived 21 years and [3?] months, buried [on...]
EDCS-09302607.summary: This is a fragmentary Christian funerary inscription for Hiraclius, who died at the age of 21 years and some months.

EDCS-09302608.translation: Here lies Martolus, who lived three months; he rests in peace.
EDCS-09302608.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Martolus, who died at the age of three months.

EDCS-09302609.translation: Here rests Masilia of good memory, who lived 70 years, rested in the Lord's day before the Kalends of February in the 25th year of the reign.
EDCS-09302609.summary: A funerary inscription for Masilia, who lived 70 years and died before the Kalends of February in the 25th regnal year, likely from the Christian era.

EDCS-09302611.translation: Here rests the well-remembered Rodulfus, who lived thirty-five years; he rests in the Lord's peace.
EDCS-09302611.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription for Rodulfus, who died at the age of thirty-five.

EDCS-09302612.translation: Here rests Sedata, who lived more or less 50 years.
EDCS-09302612.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sedata, who lived approximately 50 years.

EDCS-09302616.translation: Sacred to Jupiter, Best and Greatest. Quintus Iunius Rusticus, son of Quintus, of the Galeria tribe.
EDCS-09302616.summary: A dedication to Jupiter by Quintus Iunius Rusticus, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09302618.summary: A dedication or funerary inscription mentioning Atuciae Laodice and Melampus, who is identified as a patron, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09302619.translation: Marcus Valerius Servatus made this while alive.
EDCS-09302619.summary: This inscription records a memorial erected by Marcus Valerius Servatus during his lifetime.

EDCS-09302620.translation: To the underworld gods, the Manes, of Pompeius Sigern. Caius Pompeius Fortunatus [dedicated this].
EDCS-09302620.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Manes of Pompeius Sigern by Caius Pompeius Fortunatus.

EDCS-09302621.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication to Iunius Colqua, possibly by Odebia.

EDCS-09302622.translation: Under the command of Publius Mobi Asiuni.
EDCS-09302622.summary: This inscription likely refers to a military context or a command issued by Publius Mobi Asiuni.

EDCS-09302625.translation: To the Manes of Quintus Cornelius Callimorphus.
EDCS-09302625.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Manes of Quintus Cornelius Callimorphus.

EDCS-09302626.translation: Genucia Pelagia made this for her well-deserving husband, Publius Genucius Threptus.
EDCS-09302626.summary: This inscription records a memorial erected by Genucia Pelagia for her husband, Publius Genucius Threptus.

EDCS-09302627.translation: Marcus Popilius Arbustus gladly paid his vow to the eternal god.
EDCS-09302627.summary: This inscription records Marcus Popilius Arbustus fulfilling a vow to an eternal god.

EDCS-09302628.translation: Hilarus, to the Genius of Quintus.
EDCS-09302628.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Hilarus to the Genius of Quintus.

EDCS-09302642.translation: Tiberius Caesar, son of the deified Augustus, Augustus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 33rd year, repaired and restored [this] for the 14th time.
EDCS-09302642.summary: This inscription records Tiberius Caesar's extensive repairs and restorations, likely to a public building, during his 33rd year of tribunician power.

EDCS-09302653.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Quinti Claudi Paterni et Aemiliae Paternae Quintus Claudius Nepos pientissimis parentibus fecit\n
EDCS-09302653.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Quintus Claudius Nepos made this for his most dutiful parents, Quintus Claudius Paternus and Aemilia Patera.
EDCS-09302653.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by a son for his deceased parents.

EDCS-09302666.translation: Nasidia Epictesis gladly paid her well-earned vow.
EDCS-09302666.summary: This inscription records Nasidia Epictesis fulfilling a vow, possibly related to a dedication to a deity or a memorial.

EDCS-09302667.translation: To the Divine Shades and eternal rest for Titus Aelius Iucundus, a Roman knight, who lived 5 years, 2 months, and 7 days. Titus Aelius Macrobius, father, a beneficiary of the consular governor of the 8th Augustan Legion, and Numisia Lucilia, mother, his most unhappy parents, made this memorial for their sweetest son.
EDCS-09302667.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by parents for their young son, Titus Aelius Iucundus, who died at the age of five.

EDCS-09302668.translation: Carina, daughter of Caius, flaminica and priestess of Diana Thucolis, ordered this to be made by her will.
EDCS-09302668.summary: This epitaph records a funerary monument dedicated by Carina, a priestess of Diana, who made arrangements for it in her will.

EDCS-09302670.translation: To Carina, from her father Quintus Multelius.
EDCS-09302670.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a father, Quintus Multelius, for his daughter, Carina.

EDCS-09302676.translation: The vexillation of the Germaniciani willingly and deservedly paid their vow to Hercules for Quintus Valerius.
EDCS-09302676.summary: This inscription records a military unit, the vexillation of the Germaniciani, fulfilling a vow to Hercules on behalf of Quintus Valerius.

EDCS-09302677.translation: Vel Pacatus dedicated an altar to Jupiter, the Best and Greatest.
EDCS-09302677.summary: This is a dedication of an altar to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Vel Pacatus.

EDCS-09302678.translation: Quarta, daughter of Marcus Pompeius, willingly and deservedly paid her vow.
EDCS-09302678.summary: This inscription records a woman named Quarta, daughter of Marcus Pompeius, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-09302681.translation: Servilia, daughter of Lucius, [a member] of An Trebellius Tuscanus, from Tingitana, aged 10 years.
EDCS-09302681.summary: This is likely a funerary epitaph for Servilia, a ten-year-old girl, possibly connected to An Trebellius Tuscanus and from Tingitana.

EDCS-09302682.translation: Gaius Clodius, son of Gaius, of the Aniensis tribe.
EDCS-09302682.summary: This is a personal inscription, likely for Gaius Clodius, identifying his father and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-09302683.translation: To the Divine Shades. Servus, the heir of Metilia Calliste, placed this.
EDCS-09302683.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Servus, the heir of Metilia Calliste.

EDCS-09302684.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Lucius Primus Vitalis.
EDCS-09302684.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the memory of Lucius Primus Vitalis.

EDCS-09302685.translation: Marcus Statius, son of Sextus, of the Aniensis tribe, Memor.
EDCS-09302685.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Statius, identifying him by his name, filiation, and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-09302686.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Valeria Vitali, [daughter] of Valeria V.
EDCS-09302686.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Valeria Vitali, likely set up by her mother, Valeria V.

EDCS-09302712.translation: To Sextus Atilius Optatus and Cornelia Secundioni, daughter of Quintus. Sextus Atilius Firmianus [made this] for his parents.
EDCS-09302712.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by Sextus Atilius Firmianus to his parents, Sextus Atilius Optatus and Cornelia Secundioni.

EDCS-09302713.translation: Silvanus, son of Litumarius, the dutiful, rests here.
EDCS-09302713.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Silvanus, son of Litumarius, indicating he rests there.

EDCS-09302715.translation: An exceptional descendant, protected by the sign of the cross, unstained by any sin, Theodosius the little, whom his parents wished with pure heart to be baptized in the sacred font, cruel death snatched away, but the ruler of high Olympus will grant rest to his limbs where the noble sign of the cross is placed and he shall be called a Christian.
EDCS-09302715.summary: This is an epitaph for a young boy named Theodosius, highlighting his Christian faith and the grief of his parents.

EDCS-09302716.summary: This is a dedication, likely funerary or commemorative, from a teacher to their pupil, Stefanis Neaniscos.

EDCS-09302717.translation: To Melovius, in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-09302717.summary: This is a dedication to Melovius, made in fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-09302718.translation: Sextus Iulius Seranus is buried here.
EDCS-09302718.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription stating that Sextus Iulius Seranus is buried in this location.

EDCS-09302719.translation: To Julia Tesallydis, dearest wife. Marcus Annius Severus, her husband, made [this].
EDCS-09302719.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Marcus Annius Severus to his beloved wife, Julia Tesallydis.

EDCS-09302720.translation: Here rests in peace, of good memory, Iuveldis, who lived more or less 25 years. If anyone wishes to move him from this sarcophagus, let him be anathema. May he rest well.
EDCS-09302720.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Iuveldis, who died around age 25, with a curse against anyone who disturbs the burial.

EDCS-09302721.translation: Quintus Vibius Varus, son of Caius, of the Aniensis tribe, aged 21, and his wife.
EDCS-09302721.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Quintus Vibius Varus for himself and his wife, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302723.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Iulius Viator made this for his incomparable wife, Cornelia Novella, most loving, modest, and most precious in all things, who lived 31 years.
EDCS-09302723.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Iulius Viator for his wife Cornelia Novella, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302724.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Lucius Helvius Classicus made this while alive for himself and for his excellent wife, Catia Classica, and Lucius Fulvius Vin D IC III.
EDCS-09302724.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Lucius Helvius Classicus for himself and his wife Catia Classica, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302725.translation: Romana, daughter of Berulus, lived 5 years. Berulius for his freedmen and his own.
EDCS-09302725.summary: This is a funerary dedication for a young girl, Romana, made by Berulius, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302726.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription naming Caius Turpilius Daphnus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302727.translation: To Quintus Cornelius Quintinus. From mother Cornelia R. For Quintus OS V Quin made M.
EDCS-09302727.summary: This is a funerary dedication by an unnamed mother to her son Quintus Cornelius Quintinus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302729.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For Caecilia Parasceve, dearest daughter of Fortunata.
EDCS-09302729.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Fortunata for her daughter Caecilia Parasceve, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302730.translation: To the Divine Spirits. From mother to Iulius Romanus Ammianus.
EDCS-09302730.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a mother for her son Iulius Romanus Ammianus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302732.translation: Here rests Basilianus in peace, who lived 17 years.
EDCS-09302732.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Basilianus, dating to the Late Roman or Early Christian period.

EDCS-09302733.translation: Here lies Benenata the virgin in peace.
EDCS-09302733.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Benenata, a virgin, dating to the Late Roman or Early Christian period.

EDCS-09302736.translation: Gaius P. Satur gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the Nymphs.
EDCS-09302736.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the Nymphs by Gaius P. Satur, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09302737.translation: Sextus Vitalis to Victoria CumuIAIR [dedicates this].
EDCS-09302737.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Victoria CumuIAIR by Sextus Vitalis, the context of which is unclear but likely a dedication or funerary monument.

EDCS-09302742.translation: [This is] for the son of Attilius, son of Acellius.
EDCS-09302742.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription indicating a relationship between individuals named Attilius and Acellius.

EDCS-09302743.translation: M. Iunius and M. Milo, consuls.
EDCS-09302743.summary: This is an inscription mentioning two consuls, M. Iunius and M. Milo, which would allow for precise dating if the specific year of their consulship were known.

EDCS-09302744.translation: Of Marcus Valerius, son of Caius.
EDCS-09302744.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely referring to Marcus Valerius, son of Caius, possibly as a deceased individual or as a subject of a dedication.

EDCS-09302746.summary: This is a simple inscription identifying Valerius Saturninus, likely as a name on a tombstone or a monument.

EDCS-09302749.summary: This inscription indicates a connection to the Third Legion, possibly marking a military structure, a dedication by a soldier, or equipment.

EDCS-09302750.summary: This is a simple inscription identifying Gaius Attius, son of Gaius, likely on a funerary monument or as the subject of a dedication.

EDCS-09302751.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning Gaius Vit[---], possibly part of a personal name or a dedication, with the remainder illegible.

EDCS-09302753.summary: This inscription records the name Derceia, daughter of Venilatus, likely on a funerary monument.

EDCS-09302763.translation: To Aphrodisia, a most dutiful mother.
EDCS-09302763.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Aphrodisia by her child.

EDCS-09302765.translation: Petrus died on the 9th day before the Kalends of August.
EDCS-09302765.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death date of Petrus.

EDCS-09302767.translation: To Quinto Cornelius Philocles, freedman of Quintus.
EDCS-09302767.summary: This is a dedication to Quinto Cornelius Philocles, a freedman.

EDCS-09302768.translation: To Peregrina, daughter of Lucius Valerius Mantro.
EDCS-09302768.summary: This is a dedication to Peregrina, daughter of Lucius Valerius Mantro.

EDCS-09302770.summary: This is a dedication to Vindicus, son of Catullus.

EDCS-09302772.translation: To Lucius Annius Tullus, a most distinguished boy, son of Lucius Terentius Longus, a most distinguished man, and of Vibia Se, a most distinguished woman, who died at the age of 1 year, Lamyrion, and Panthera.
EDCS-09302772.summary: This is a funerary monument for Lucius Annius Tullus, a young boy, detailing his parentage and mentioning other individuals.

EDCS-09302773.translation: Nicaea, with the approval of Ves[tius?], a statue in the forum.
EDCS-09302773.summary: This inscription records Nicaea approving the placement of a statue in the forum, likely a dedication or official record.

EDCS-09302774.translation: To the departed spirits, Valeria Paterna to her most dutiful husband, Marcus Aemilius Eutyches.
EDCS-09302774.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Valeria Paterna to her husband, Marcus Aemilius Eutyches.

EDCS-09302775.translation: To Amandus, aged 20. His brother [dedicated this] with the inscription, the name [is] on this one stone, the rest above is [illegible].
EDCS-09302775.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Amandus, aged 20, dedicated by his brother, with a partially preserved text.

EDCS-09302776.translation: To the departed spirits, of Lucius Aponius Severianus, who died at the age of 4 months, 9 days.
EDCS-09302776.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Lucius Aponius Severianus, detailing his age in months and days.

EDCS-09302777.translation: To mother and father and to Auctus the freedman and to Felix.
EDCS-09302777.summary: This is a dedication to family members and a freedman, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-09302778.translation: Iulia Melete, daughter, made this for Titus Aurelius Secundus, her father.
EDCS-09302778.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a daughter for her father, Titus Aurelius Secundus.

EDCS-09302781.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Titus Flavius Glycon set this up for his children: for Flavia Glaucena, his daughter, who lived 9 years, 3 months, and 7 days; and also for his son Flavius Glycon, 13 years, 5 months, and 17 days; and for my father-in-law, Expentanius Diocles, aged sixty.
EDCS-09302781.summary: This funerary inscription records the ages of two deceased children and a father-in-law, set up by Titus Flavius Glycon.

EDCS-09302782.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Lucius Ingenuius Secundinus, father, and Mettia Nice, mother, [set this up] for their deceased daughter Secundilla, daughter of Lucius Ingenuius, aged [missing number].
EDCS-09302782.summary: This is a funerary dedication by parents for their deceased daughter, Secundilla.

EDCS-09302783.translation: To Pompeia Dativa, my dearest wife. Gaius Aufidius [set this up].
EDCS-09302783.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a husband, Gaius Aufidius, to his wife, Pompeia Dativa.

EDCS-09302784.summary: This epitaph dedicates a mirror to Valeria Pudicitia, possibly a tombstone.

EDCS-09302785.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For Marcus Victorina. S M XT TS
EDCS-09302785.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Marcus Victorina, with illegible abbreviations.

EDCS-09302791.translation: Here rests in peace of good memory Bellatus, who lived approximately 15 years and died on the 8th day before the Ides of June in the twelfth indiction.
EDCS-09302791.summary: This epitaph records the death of Bellatus, who died at approximately 15 years of age on a specific date in the 12th indiction.

EDCS-09302794.translation: Here rests in peace of good memory Leonidius, who lived approximately [missing number] years and died on the [missing day] day of the [missing month] indiction.
EDCS-09302794.summary: This epitaph records the death of Leonidius, with incomplete information about his age and date of death.

EDCS-09302795.translation: Here rests in peace of good memory Pelagia, who lived approximately 50 years and died on the third day before the Ides of December in the seventh indiction.
EDCS-09302795.summary: This epitaph records the death of Pelagia, who died at approximately 50 years of age on a specific date in the 7th indiction.

EDCS-09302798.translation: To Quintus Pontinius Capito, Augustal seviri. Pontinius [dedicated this].
EDCS-09302798.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Pontinius to Quintus Pontinius Capito, an Augustal seviri.

EDCS-09302799.translation: In memory of Barbarus. Paterni Udalcai erected this.
EDCS-09302799.summary: This inscription is a memorial erected by Paterni Udalcai for Barbarus.

EDCS-09302800.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Iulia Servata, for her most devoted husband Sextus Iulius Superstes, and for her children, because of his merit.
EDCS-09302800.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Iulia Servata to her husband Sextus Iulius Superstes and their children.

EDCS-09302802.translation: from the [city/people of] Cabellenses, leader of the youth, son of Marcus Opellius Severus Macrinus Pius Felix Augustus.
EDCS-09302802.summary: This inscription honors a young leader, possibly related to the emperor Macrinus, from the town of Cabellenses.

EDCS-09302803.summary: This very fragmentary inscription appears to be a dedication.

EDCS-09302804.translation: Cornelia Gratilla, daughter of Lucius, freely and deservedly fulfilled her vow to the Good Goddess.
EDCS-09302804.summary: This inscription records Cornelia Gratilla fulfilling a vow to the Bona Dea.

EDCS-09302806.translation: Iulianus to the god Mars Buxenus. Iulianus erected this votive offering.
EDCS-09302806.summary: This inscription records Iulianus erecting a votive offering to the god Mars Buxenus.

EDCS-09302808.translation: Burial place of Lucius Thorus Eutychus, 15 feet in front, 15 feet in width, in the land.
EDCS-09302808.summary: This inscription defines the dimensions of a burial plot for Lucius Thorus Eutychus.

EDCS-09302810.translation: Murmillo Quintus Ducenius Optatus, three times crowned. His wife Hateria Potita made this.
EDCS-09302810.summary: This inscription records a monument erected by Hateria Potita for her husband Quintus Ducenius Optatus, a gladiator who had been crowned three times.

EDCS-09302811.translation: Murmillo Primus Liber Asiaticus, 53 years old. His wife Alice made this.
EDCS-09302811.summary: This inscription records a monument erected by Alice for her husband Primus Liber Asiaticus, a gladiator.

EDCS-09302812.summary: This very fragmentary inscription likely records a dedication for Marcus Acutus.

EDCS-09302814.translation: To Sextus Valerius, to his excellent sister.
EDCS-09302814.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Sextus Valerius to his sister.

EDCS-09302815.translation: Sacred to Silvanus. Marcus T. H. [dedicated this].
EDCS-09302815.summary: This is a dedication to the god Silvanus by Marcus T. H.

EDCS-09302816.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Sabinius Veratianus [dedicated this] to Atilia Materna, his most excellent wife.
EDCS-09302816.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Sabinius Veratianus to his wife, Atilia Materna.

EDCS-09302817.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. To Verilla, daughter of Verinus. Cupitia Felicissima [dedicated this] to her most excellent patroness.
EDCS-09302817.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Cupitia Felicissima to her patroness, Verilla.

EDCS-09302818.translation: To Ilion, for herself and her family, while alive.
EDCS-09302818.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Ilion for herself and her family.

EDCS-09302822.translation: To Alambrima. Severus, son of Perpetuus, [dedicated this] in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-09302822.summary: This is a votive dedication by Severus, son of Perpetuus, to Alambrima.

EDCS-09302824.summary: This is a dedication to the god Silvanus by Servandus.

EDCS-09302825.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Messina, mother of Verinus Vatticinus, made this for herself and for him, while alive.
EDCS-09302825.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Messina, mother of Verinus Vatticinus, for herself and her son.

EDCS-09302828.translation: To Quintus Titius Amandus, a member of the board of six priests (sevir).
EDCS-09302828.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Quintus Titius Amandus, a sevir.

EDCS-09302829.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. To Thoria Rodope, for her dearest brother Tertullinus.
EDCS-09302829.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Thoria Rodope to her brother Tertullinus.

EDCS-09302834.translation: Santolus, the subdeacon, of holy and good memory, rests here in peace, who lived for more or less 85 years, died in Christ on the ninth day before the Ides of February, in the twenty-second year after the consulship of the most distinguished man Basilius, in the 13th indiction.
EDCS-09302834.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Santolus, a subdeacon, giving his age, death date, and reference to a consulship, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-09302835.translation: This inscription will cover the deacon Aemilius, whom cruel and too swift death, impious in its course, snatched away at the 38th year of his age; he lost his life but found it, because he loved the author of life alone.
EDCS-09302835.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Aemilius, a deacon, lamenting his early death at age 38 and expressing faith in the afterlife, typical of early Christian epitaphs.

EDCS-09302837.translation: To Sextus Coelius Voltinius Canus, quaestor; Primus, freedman, seviri, here and his brother, on account of their singular devotion to their family and their concord with each other, which they enjoyed in a most pleasant partnership, having reached the age of 77, were judged worthy by the order of decurions; they rewarded this merit with the munificence of the decurions by setting up a silver statue of Vienna and 200,000 sesterces. To Sextus Coelius Voltinius Niger, quaestor; Primus, freedman, seviri, here and his brother, on account of their singular devotion to their family and their concord with each other, which they enjoyed in a most pleasant partnership, having reached the age of 77, were judged worthy by the order of decurions; they rewarded this merit with the munificence of the decurions by setting up a silver statue of Vienna and 200,000 sesterces.
EDCS-09302837.summary: This inscription commemorates Sextus Coelius Voltinius Canus and Sextus Coelius Voltinius Niger, quaestors and seviri, honored by the decurions for their family devotion and concord with a silver statue and a substantial donation, indicating their civic importance in Vienna.

EDCS-09302838.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Gratia, most holy. Gratius Gratus [dedicated this] to his most dutiful father and to Gratia Grata, daughter of Gratia Gratia.
EDCS-09302838.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Gratia, honoring her parents and her father Gratius Gratus, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-09302839.translation: Perseus, father, and Primigenia, aunt, to their dearest son Perseus.
EDCS-09302839.summary: This is a tomb inscription from parents and an aunt dedicating a memorial to their beloved son named Perseus.

EDCS-09302841.translation: Ispes, a servant of the Lord Christ, of good memory, rests here in peace, who lived for more or less [number missing] years in peace.
EDCS-09302841.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Ispes, a female servant of Christ, of good memory, providing her name and noting she lived for an unspecified number of years.

EDCS-09302842.translation: Valerinus rests here in peace, of good memory, who lived for 26 years, died on the Kalends of April, in the sixth indiction.
EDCS-09302842.summary: This tomb inscription records the death of Valerinus, who died at age 26 on April 1st in the sixth indiction.

EDCS-09302845.translation: To Titus Julius Creticus, son of Titus, by his wife Iulia Decmina, daughter of Decimus, and his sons, to their parent.
EDCS-09302845.summary: This is a tomb inscription dedicated by a wife and sons to their father, Titus Julius Creticus.

EDCS-09302848.translation: To the Divine Shades, of Titia Dorcadis; by the public owners of the baths at Aquae.
EDCS-09302848.summary: This is an inscription dedicated to the Divine Shades of Titia Dorcadis, placed by the public bath owners of Aquae.

EDCS-09302849.translation: To the Divine Shades, of Catinia Moschis; by Catinia Isidora, to her most dutiful mother.
EDCS-09302849.summary: This inscription is dedicated to the Divine Shades of Catinia Moschis by her devoted daughter, Catinia Isidora.

EDCS-09302850.translation: To the Divine Shades, of Titia Sigenis; by Mascarpius and Ianuaria, to their most dutiful daughter.
EDCS-09302850.summary: This inscription is dedicated to the Divine Shades of Titia Sigenis by her parents, Mascarpius and Ianuaria.

EDCS-09302852.translation: To the god Neptune, Gaius Vitalinius Victorinus, a soldier of the 22nd legion, fulfilled his vow to the curiae, willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-09302852.summary: This is a votive inscription by a soldier of the 22nd legion dedicating to Neptune, likely from the late Roman Empire.

EDCS-09302853.summary: This is a simple tomb inscription for Madelena, likely from late antiquity or the early medieval period.

EDCS-09302854.summary: This is a dedication or tomb inscription for Iulia Gratilla, possibly from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09302855.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantinus, Pious, Most Noble Caesar, son of the deified Constantius.
EDCS-09302855.summary: This is a formal inscription honoring Emperor Constantine the Great, dating to the early 4th century CE.

EDCS-09302856.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, Viventius, his foster-son.
EDCS-09302856.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Viventius by his foster-son, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09302862.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, Lucius Censorins Severus, who lived seven years and twenty-one days. Lucius Censorins Severinus and Careia Felicissima set up this monument to their most dutiful son.
EDCS-09302862.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a young boy named Lucius Censorins Severus, set up by his parents, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09302863.translation: He ordered a monument to be set up to Lucius Aemilius Valentinus to the spirits of the underworld.
EDCS-09302863.summary: This inscription records a posthumous commission for a monument to Lucius Aemilius Valentinus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09302864.text_edition: \n Escingillus Valtaci Parcabus votum solvit libens animo\n
EDCS-09302864.translation: Escingillus paid his vow to the Parcæ willingly.
EDCS-09302864.summary: This votive inscription records an individual named Escingillus fulfilling a vow to the Parcæ (Fates).

EDCS-09302872.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, Lucius Baebius Eucles, Augustalis of the IIIIvirate, a student of law. Lucius Baebius Tertius to his patron.
