EDCS-09302872.summary: This is a funerary inscription from a patron to his client, who was an Augustalis and a student of law, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09302873.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, Titus Geminius Tatianus to his most excellent parents, Titus Geminius Zethus and Titia Martial, daughter of Martialis.
EDCS-09302873.summary: This is a funerary inscription from a son to his parents, one of whom was an Augustalis of the IIIIvirate, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09302881.translation: To the spirits of the father Quintus Aurelius. To the spirits of Sextus Aurelius, the goldsmith.
EDCS-09302881.summary: This inscription appears to be a double funerary dedication, one to a father and another to a goldsmith, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-09302882.translation: To Adiutor, our patron, from the freedwomen.
EDCS-09302882.summary: This inscription is a dedication to a patron named Adiutor by freedwomen.

EDCS-09302884.translation: Balbus, a freedman, placed this in honor of the Divine Shades of Caius Antonius Paullus.
EDCS-09302884.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a freedman named Balbus for Caius Antonius Paullus.

EDCS-09302886.translation: To Quintina, from Atia Valeria, her daughter.
EDCS-09302886.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Quintina by her daughter Atia Valeria.

EDCS-09302889.translation: To Casuria, from Cornelia Primula, his wife.
EDCS-09302889.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Casuria by his wife Cornelia Primula.

EDCS-09302892.summary: This is a simple name inscription, likely for Titus Domitius Crispinus.

EDCS-09302893.translation: In honor of the Divine Shades of Erotus, a most excellent slave, placed by Iulia Advena.
EDCS-09302893.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Iulia Advena for her excellent slave, Erotus.

EDCS-09302896.translation: To the Divine Shades of Fuficia Trophima, his most devoted wife.
EDCS-09302896.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Fuficia Trophima, described as a devoted wife.

EDCS-09302897.translation: To the Divine Shades of Fuscus Arcessus.
EDCS-09302897.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Fuscus Arcessus.

EDCS-09302898.translation: Albucia Dubitata, wife of Lucius Iulius Successus, placed this in honor of the Divine Shades.
EDCS-09302898.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Albucia Dubitata for her husband Lucius Iulius Successus.

EDCS-09302899.translation: Iulia Pusilla, from her own resources, to the Divine Shades of Quintus Terentius Massa.
EDCS-09302899.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by Iulia Pusilla for Quintus Terentius Massa, funded by herself.

EDCS-09302900.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Iustus, son of Etius, to his wife Secundina, daughter of Etius.
EDCS-09302900.summary: A funerary dedication by a husband to his wife.

EDCS-09302901.translation: To Marcus Magius, by his will.
EDCS-09302901.summary: A dedication made according to a will, likely funerary.

EDCS-09302902.translation: Octavia placed this for her most dutiful husband Maritimus and her grandson Marcianus.
EDCS-09302902.summary: A funerary monument set up by a wife and grandson for a husband and grandfather.

EDCS-09302903.summary: An epitaph identifying an individual by name and parentage.

EDCS-09302904.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcina, a most dutiful mother, to her daughter Maximia Marcellina.
EDCS-09302904.summary: A funerary dedication by a mother to her daughter.

EDCS-09302906.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Dubitata, daughter of Valeria Melissa, to her most dutiful mother.
EDCS-09302906.summary: A funerary dedication by a daughter to her mother.

EDCS-09302909.translation: To my father Peregrinus, whom Servatus of Illium and Calamus, freedmen of the Emperor, [placed this]; to Virillio.
EDCS-09302909.summary: A dedication to a father and another individual, possibly with imperial freedmen involved in the placement.

EDCS-09302911.summary: A dedication of an unspecified monument by Maternus to Severus.

EDCS-09302913.translation: To Successus and to those who are listed above, in accordance with the power given to Avillius Seranus, Decimus Iulius Iulius Cosmio, Publius Licinius Priscus, Titus Licinius.
EDCS-09302913.summary: A dedication or legal declaration naming several individuals, possibly related to inheritance or property.

EDCS-09302916.translation: Quintus Spurius Primulus, to his excellent wife Veriana, his freedman.
EDCS-09302916.summary: A funerary dedication by a freedman to his wife.

EDCS-09302917.translation: To Vettius Paris and Munatia Primigenia.
EDCS-09302917.summary: This is a dedication to Vettius Paris and Munatia Primigenia, likely a tombstone inscription.

EDCS-09302928.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Naus to Aemilia Iada, possibly on a tomb or monument.

EDCS-09302929.summary: This is a funerary inscription stating that Valerius Magnus is buried in this location.

EDCS-09302933.translation: Quintus Servaeus Reburrus willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Mercury.
EDCS-09302933.summary: This is a votive inscription by Quintus Servaeus Reburrus to the god Mercury.

EDCS-09302935.translation: To Nemausus, Augustus, and the divine powers of the gods, and likewise to the genius of the associations of the dyers and the tree-bearers, of the city...
EDCS-09302935.summary: This is a dedication to various deities and the genius of specific trade guilds, likely from a public building or monument.

EDCS-09302937.translation: Antonia Maria, daughter of Antonius Celeris, made this for herself while alive.
EDCS-09302937.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a woman for herself.

EDCS-09302938.translation: [...] and his brother, Campanus and Restutus [died?] in the water, and one [remains?]
EDCS-09302938.summary: This fragmented inscription appears to record a tragic drowning incident involving at least two brothers.

EDCS-09302940.translation: C. Turpio willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Belenus.
EDCS-09302940.summary: This is a votive inscription by C. Turpio to the deity Belenus.

EDCS-09302944.translation: From the colony Iulia Paterna, Martius Narbo, freedman of the Caesars, (erected this) while alive for himself (at his own expense).
EDCS-09302944.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Martius Narbo, a freedman, who erected his own tomb in the colony of Narbo.

EDCS-09302945.translation: Volumnius (?) Aurelius Cominus, a tuba player of the 13th Legion Gemina, aged 30 years, with 13 years of service.
EDCS-09302945.summary: This funerary epitaph records the name, rank (tuba player), legion, age, and service length of a soldier.

EDCS-09302949.translation: Lucius Rennius Pamphilus, a bath attendant (?).
EDCS-09302949.summary: This is a brief epitaph identifying an individual named Lucius Rennius Pamphilus, possibly a bath attendant.

EDCS-09302950.text_edition: \n Vivus Marcus Iulius Capito Foroiuliensis copo sibi et vivae Liciniae Luci filiae Primae uxori\n
EDCS-09302950.translation: While alive, Marcus Iulius Capito of Forum Iulii, a wine seller, [made this] for himself and for his wife, the living Licinia Prima, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-09302950.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a wine seller for himself and his wife.

EDCS-09302951.translation: Vivit. Lucius Tullius Felix, a rope maker, [dedicated this] for himself and his patron (?) and his wife Satulla.
EDCS-09302951.summary: This funerary inscription records a rope maker who set up the monument for himself, possibly his patron, and his wife.

EDCS-09302953.translation: To Lucius Silius, freedman of Lucius, named Sandro, merchant, freedman of [---] Ligur, [in] the territory, 15 feet [in front].
EDCS-09302953.summary: This is a funerary and boundary inscription, likely for a merchant named Sandro, indicating land ownership or a burial plot.

EDCS-09302954.translation: To Lucius Squeillanius Faustus, freedman of Lucius, the ship-owner, and to Flavia Venusta, freedwoman of Marcus, his wife, by the arbitration of Venusta, my wife.
EDCS-09302954.summary: This is a funerary monument set up for a ship-owner and his wife, with the inscription indicating it was arranged by the wife.

EDCS-09302955.translation: To [---]ius Fuscus [---] and to Annia Aucta, freedwoman of Titus, his wife. [---] Julius Priscus, merchant, cloth merchant, 15 feet in front.
EDCS-09302955.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a couple, likely commemorating a merchant and his wife, with a specified front dimension of the plot.

EDCS-09302958.translation: To Lucius Aemilius, son of Marcus, from the Veranius family.
EDCS-09302958.summary: This is a dedication, likely on a tomb, to Lucius Aemilius, son of Marcus.

EDCS-09302959.summary: This inscription likely indicates that M. Albinus lived together with Albina, possibly a marriage or cohabitation record.

EDCS-09302960.summary: This inscription simply lists the names Antiopa and Anchisa, possibly a dedication or tombstone.

EDCS-09302964.translation: To the Divine Manes. Decimus Attius Victor, his son, [erected this] to his most devoted father, Decimus Attius Victor.
EDCS-09302964.summary: This funerary inscription records a son dedicating a monument to his father.

EDCS-09302969.translation: Fabius Paternus [erected this] to Charis, his dearest wife, and to himself.
EDCS-09302969.summary: This funerary inscription records a husband dedicating a monument to his wife and himself.

EDCS-09302970.translation: Titus Comm [et al.] in the field, fifteen feet.
EDCS-09302970.summary: This inscription appears to record a land measurement of fifteen feet belonging to Titus Comm.

EDCS-09302972.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph stating that Aulus Licinius Erato is alive, likely indicating a false death report or a playful inscription.

EDCS-09302974.summary: This inscription records the names Festus and Receptus, possibly indicating they are alive or as part of a larger funerary context.

EDCS-09302975.translation: Lucius Fulvius Tertius is alive for himself, and for his patron Lucius Fulvius Bellonus, his wife Silenia Faustae, his freedwoman Fulvia Exoche, and his children Fulvia Amaryllis, Fortunatus, and Receptus.
EDCS-09302975.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Fulvius Tertius and several family members and dependents, including his patron.

EDCS-09302977.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph stating that Publius Gavius Alexander is alive, likely indicating a false death report or a playful inscription.

EDCS-09302978.translation: [Erected by] IO N CI L Iucundus F SI.
EDCS-09302978.summary: This fragmented inscription appears to record the name of a dedicator, possibly 'Iucundus', with some abbreviations.

EDCS-09302980.translation: Publius Iulius Tertullus [is alive] for Sextus Licinius Secundus.
EDCS-09302980.summary: This inscription records Publius Iulius Tertullus being alive in relation to Sextus Licinius Secundus.

EDCS-09302981.translation: To Lucius Lollius I, for himself and for his freedman Iucundus Ingenuus, in the front, ten feet.
EDCS-09302981.summary: This inscription records a land dedication or measurement of ten feet in front, for Lucius Lollius I and his freedman.

EDCS-09302982.translation: Lucius Lucaenius, freedman of Lucius, made this monument for himself and his wife, Titus, out of his own money while he was alive.
EDCS-09302982.summary: This funerary epitaph records a freedman's self-funded monument for himself and his wife.

EDCS-09302987.translation: Argentillus, freedman of Lucius, 15 feet in all directions.
EDCS-09302987.summary: This boundary marker specifies the dimensions of a plot of land belonging to Argentillus, a freedman.

EDCS-09302990.translation: Pompeius Rufus, son of Lucius, of the Fabia tribe, is alive.
EDCS-09302990.summary: This brief inscription records the vitality of Pompeius Rufus.

EDCS-09302991.summary: This inscription likely denotes a property boundary or a length of land owned by Primula.

EDCS-09302992.summary: This is a simple inscription identifying Primus, son of Marcus.

EDCS-09302994.translation: Papiria Ruga and Marcus Licinius, her mother.
EDCS-09302994.summary: This inscription seems to identify two individuals, Papiria Ruga and her mother Marcus Licinius.

EDCS-09302995.translation: Publius Sulpicius Potamo, while alive, and his freedwoman Hecale, while alive, for themselves and their patron Titus Atinas Crescens, and for Publius Sulpicius Lan. Died.
EDCS-09302995.summary: This funerary epitaph records a monument established by a man and his freedwoman for themselves and their patron, as well as another individual.

EDCS-09302997.translation: Eros, freedman of Caius, a place from the road to the road.
EDCS-09302997.summary: This inscription likely marks a path or access to a specific location belonging to Eros, a freedman.

EDCS-09302999.translation: Miorius Sextus. It is here. Buried.
EDCS-09302999.summary: This short epitaph marks the burial place of Miorius Sextus.

EDCS-09303026.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or ownership marker related to a person named Gallus.

EDCS-09303040.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Julius Messianus to his most dutiful mother, Coelia Messina.
EDCS-09303040.summary: A funerary dedication by a son to his mother, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09303041.translation: To the god Abianius, as he had promised, gladly and joyfully.
EDCS-09303041.summary: A votive inscription to a deity named Abianius, indicating a fulfillment of a vow, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09303042.summary: This is a simple dedication or ownership marker for Decimus Sintacius Temporis.

EDCS-09303043.translation: Servanda placed this for Sextus Paunus.
EDCS-09303043.summary: A funerary dedication by Servanda for Sextus Paunus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09303045.translation: In this tomb rests in peace, of good memory, Romanus, a subdeacon, who lived more or less 60 years, died in Christ on the Kalends of November, after the consulship of the very distinguished man Basilius, the consul.
EDCS-09303045.summary: A funerary inscription for Romanus, a subdeacon who died in November, dating the inscription to after the consulship of Basilius in the late Roman or early Byzantine period.

EDCS-09303047.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Antonia, sister, to her deserving wife Decia Amabilis. Cecilius [dedicates this] too.
EDCS-09303047.summary: A funerary dedication from Antonia to her wife Decia Amabilis, with a possible addition by Cecilius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09303048.translation: To Decimus Antistius Bassus. Chloe, his wife.
EDCS-09303048.summary: A funerary dedication by Chloe to her husband Decimus Antistius Bassus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09303049.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Servata to her daughter Marcia, daughter of Marcus, Secundilla.
EDCS-09303049.summary: A funerary dedication by Servata to her daughter Marcia Secundilla, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09401113.translation: Eutropus, may peace remain with you.
EDCS-09401113.summary: A funerary greeting or epitaph for Eutropus, likely from the late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-09401114.translation: On the seventeenth day before the Kalends of April [March 16th], Marcia Romania Celsa, a most distinguished woman, who lived 38 years, 2 months, and 10 days, will rest here in peace; Flavius Ianuarinus, a most distinguished man, former ordinary consul, placed [this] for his well-deserving wife.
EDCS-09401114.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcia Romania Celsa, detailing her lifespan and placed by her husband, Flavius Ianuarinus, a former ordinary consul, dating it to after his consulship in the late Roman period.

EDCS-09401117.translation: Laevinus and Aquinus, sons, made [this] for Rufus, son of Solitius, and for Axsedus, wife of Casidannus.
EDCS-09401117.summary: A funerary monument or dedication erected by two sons, Laevinus and Aquinus, for their father Rufus and mother Axsedus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09401463.summary: A very brief inscription, possibly a funerary epitaph or a personal note, listing a name and numbers, dating is uncertain.

EDCS-09500170.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augg(ustus) Pius Felix Parthicus maximus Britannicus maximus tribunicia potestate XVI consul IIII pater patriae proconsul viam vetustate collabsam restituit curam agente Iulio Hono rato procuratore Augusti ex primipilo XI\n
EDCS-09500170.translation: The Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Pius Felix, conqueror of Parthia, conqueror of Britannia, with tribunician power for the 16th time, consul for the 4th time, father of the country, proconsul, restored the road which had collapsed from age, with the care of Julius Honoratus, procurator of Augustus, a former centurion of the 11th legion.
EDCS-09500170.summary: This imperial rescript records Emperor Marcus Aurelius restoring a road, with details of the procurator in charge of the project, likely from the late 2nd century AD.

EDCS-09500186.translation: Tiberius Caesar, son of the divine Augustus, Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 33rd year, rebuilt the road.
EDCS-09500186.summary: This inscription records Emperor Tiberius rebuilding a road, dating to his 33rd year of tribunician power (AD 32).

EDCS-09500187.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantinus Pius Felix [---]
EDCS-09500187.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Constantine, part of a larger inscription that is now incomplete.

EDCS-09500191.translation: To our Lords, the Emperors Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantinus, Pious, Fortunate, Augustus, grandson of Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maximianus Augustus, son of the deified Constantius Augustus Pious, [our Lords] Valentinianus and Valens and Gratianus, Augustuses, born for the good of the republic.
EDCS-09500191.summary: A dedication to the emperors Valentinianus, Valens, and Gratianus, referencing their imperial lineage, likely from the late 4th century CE.

EDCS-09500193.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the country, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 8th time, emperor for the 2nd time, consul for the 4th time. [---] 7
EDCS-09500193.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperor Antoninus Pius, listing his titles and powers, likely from around AD 145.

EDCS-09500194.translation: To the Restorer of the world, to the Emperor Caesar Lucius Domitius Aurelianus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, chief priest, conqueror of the Germans, conqueror of the Goths, conqueror of Parthia, with tribunician power for the 4th time, consul for the 3rd time, father of the country, proconsul. 5
EDCS-09500194.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Aurelian, praising his military victories and imperial titles, likely from the late 3rd century AD.

EDCS-09500195.translation: To our lord Flavius Claudius Constantinus, father, grandfather, and ancestor among the emperors, born a Caesar, most noble, forever to benefit the world.
EDCS-09500195.summary: This inscription is a dedicatory text honoring Emperor Constantine, likely from the 4th century CE.

EDCS-09500199.translation: Emperor Caesar Augustus, Imperator for the 10th time, holding tribunician power for the 11th time.
EDCS-09500199.summary: This inscription records the titles and powers of an emperor, likely Augustus, dating to the early Roman Empire.

EDCS-09500202.translation: Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the fatherland, chief priest, holding tribunician power for the 8th time, Imperator for the 2nd time, Consul for the 4th time.
EDCS-09500202.summary: This inscription lists the titles and offices of Emperor Antoninus Pius, likely from the mid-2nd century CE.

EDCS-09500207.translation: Nero Claudius, son of the deified Claudius, grandson of Germanicus Caesar, great-grandson of Tiberius Caesar Augustus, great-great-grandson of the deified Augustus, Caesar Augustus Germanicus, chief priest, holding tribunician power for the 4th time, Imperator for the 4th time, Consul for the 3rd time, father of the fatherland, restored (this).
EDCS-09500207.summary: This inscription details the full titulature of Emperor Nero, likely from the mid-1st century CE.

EDCS-09500208.translation: Nero Claudius, son of the deified Claudius, grandson of Germanicus Caesar, great-grandson of Tiberius Caesar Augustus, great-great-grandson of the deified Augustus, Caesar Augustus Germanicus, chief priest, holding tribunician power for the 4th time, Imperator for the 4th time, Consul for the 3rd time, father of the fatherland, restored (this).
EDCS-09500208.summary: This inscription details the full titulature of Emperor Nero, likely from the mid-1st century CE.

EDCS-09500211.translation: Nero Claudius, son of the deified Claudius, grandson of Germanicus Caesar, great-grandson of Tiberius Caesar Augustus, descendant of the deified Augustus, Caesar Augustus Germanicus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the fourth time, imperator for the fourth time, consul for the third time, father of the country, restored [this].
EDCS-09500211.summary: An inscription detailing the imperial titulature and achievements of Emperor Nero, likely dating to his early reign (c. 54-58 CE).

EDCS-09500212.translation: Nero Claudius, son of the deified Claudius, grandson of Germanicus Caesar, great-grandson of Tiberius Caesar Augustus, great-great-grandson of the deified Augustus, Caesar Augustus Germanicus, chief priest, holding tribunician power for the 4th time, Imperator for the 4th time, Consul for the 3rd time, father of the fatherland, restored (this).
EDCS-09500212.summary: This inscription details the full titulature of Emperor Nero, likely from the mid-1st century CE.

EDCS-09500214.translation: Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, son of Drusus, chief priest, holding tribunician power for the 3rd time, Consul for the 3rd time, Imperator for the 5th time, father of the fatherland, repaired (this).
EDCS-09500214.summary: This inscription records the titles and restoration work by Emperor Claudius, likely from the mid-1st century CE.

EDCS-09500215.translation: Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, chief priest, holding tribunician power for the 9th time, Imperator for the 2nd time, Consul for the 4th time, father of the fatherland, restored (this).
EDCS-09500215.summary: This inscription lists the titles and offices of Emperor Antoninus Pius, likely from the mid-2nd century CE.

EDCS-09500216.translation: Under our Lords Theodosius and Valentinianus, Pious, Fortunate, Victorious, and Triumphant, always Augustuses, in their fifteenth and fourth consulships respectively, the illustrious man Auxiliaris, praetorian prefect of the Gauls, ordered milestones to be set up from Arelate to Massilia, one mile.
EDCS-09500216.summary: An inscription recording the placement of a milestone by Auxiliaris, praetorian prefect of the Gauls, under the emperors Theodosius and Valentinianus, dating to the mid-5th century CE.

EDCS-09500218.translation: Tiberius Caesar Augustus, son of the deified Augustus, chief priest, holding tribunician power for the 22nd time, repaired and restored (this).
EDCS-09500218.summary: This inscription records the restoration work by Emperor Tiberius, likely from the early 1st century CE.

EDCS-09500228.translation: Father of the fatherland, Emperor Caesar Augustus, son of the divine, chief priest, consul for the 12th time, consul designate for the 13th time, imperator for the 14th time, holder of tribunician power for the 21st time, [year] XI.
EDCS-09500228.summary: This inscription is a titulature of Emperor Augustus, likely from a public monument, recording his many honors and offices.

EDCS-09500231.translation: Father of the fatherland, Emperor Caesar Augustus, son of the divine, chief priest, consul designate for the 13th time, imperator for the 14th time, [year] VII, [tribunician power] XI.
EDCS-09500231.summary: This inscription is a titulature of Emperor Augustus, likely from a public monument, recording his many honors and offices.

EDCS-09500232.translation: Tiberius Caesar Augustus, son of the divine Augustus, chief priest, holder of tribunician power for the 33rd time, restored and rebuilt.
EDCS-09500232.summary: This inscription records Tiberius Caesar Augustus restoring and rebuilding something, likely a public building, and indicates his 33rd year of tribunician power.

EDCS-09500235.translation: Tiberius Caesar Augustus, son of the divine Augustus, chief priest, holder of tribunician power for the 33rd time, restored and rebuilt.
EDCS-09500235.summary: This inscription records Tiberius Caesar Augustus restoring and rebuilding something, likely a public building, and indicates his 33rd year of tribunician power.

EDCS-09500240.translation: Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the fatherland, chief priest, holder of tribunician power for the 8th time, consul for the 4th time, XXXVI.
EDCS-09500240.summary: This inscription is a titulature of Emperor Antoninus Pius, likely from a public monument, recording his honors and offices.

EDCS-09500242.translation: Emperor Caesar Lucius Domitius Aurelianus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, chief priest, holder of tribunician power for the 6th time, consul for the 3rd time, father of the fatherland, proconsul, restorer of the world, repaired and restored, XV.
EDCS-09500242.summary: This inscription is a titulature of Emperor Aurelian, likely from a public monument, recording his titles and the restoration of something.

EDCS-09500244.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Carus Pius Felix Invictus, chief priest, holder of tribunician power for the 2nd time, consul for the 2nd time, father of the fatherland, proconsul.
EDCS-09500244.summary: This inscription is a titulature of Emperor Carus, likely from a public monument, recording his titles and offices.

EDCS-09500245.summary: A simple patronymic inscription, likely a funerary epitaph or a boundary marker, dating is uncertain.

EDCS-09500246.translation: Father of the fatherland, Emperor Caesar Augustus, son of the divine, chief priest, consul for the 12th time, consul designate for the 13th time, imperator for the 14th time, holder of tribunician power for the 21st time.
EDCS-09500246.summary: This inscription is a titulature of Emperor Augustus, likely from a public monument, recording his many honors and offices.

EDCS-09500248.translation: Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the fatherland, holder of tribunician power for the 7th time, consul for the 3rd time.
EDCS-09500248.summary: This inscription is a titulature of Emperor Antoninus Pius, likely from a public monument, recording his honors and offices.

EDCS-09500251.translation: To Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, with his seventh tribunician power, and third consulship.
EDCS-09500251.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Antoninus Pius, likely recording his seventh tribunician power and third consulship.

EDCS-09500252.translation: To Emperor Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantinus, pious, most noble Caesar, son of the divine Constantius Pius Augustus.
EDCS-09500252.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Constantine the Great, identifying him as the son of Constantius I and noting his status as Caesar.

EDCS-09500255.translation: Constantius Augustus, Pious, Fortunate, 9 miles. To our Lords, the Emperors Caesar Augustus, born for the good of the republic, 9 miles. To our Lord Flavius Valentinianus and Flavius Theodosius and Flavius Arcadius, Augustuses, born for the good of the republic, 9 miles. Flavius Dalmatius, 9.
EDCS-09500255.summary: A complex inscription detailing road mileages associated with several emperors including Constantius, Valentinianus, Theodosius, Arcadius, and Dalmatius, likely dating to the late 4th century CE.

EDCS-09500256.translation: To our Lord Flavius Crispus, the noblest Caesar, born of emperors, father and grandfather, 9 miles.
EDCS-09500256.summary: An inscription honoring Flavius Crispus as a noble Caesar, likely referring to a road marker, dating to the early 4th century CE.

EDCS-09500257.translation: To our lord Flavius Julius Constantius, most blessed Caesar, 12 miles.
EDCS-09500257.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Constantius I, likely indicating a distance of 12 miles, possibly related to a road or boundary.

EDCS-09500258.text_edition: \n Domini nostri Flavio Crispo patre avo maioribus Inpperatoribus sic nato nobilissimo Ceesari sic milia VIII Piissimis principibus Caio Valerio Constantio et Caio Valeriano Maximiano nobilissimis Caesaribus VIII\n
EDCS-09500258.translation: To our lords, Flavius Crispus, father, grandfather, and ancestor emperors, thus born most noble Caesar, 8 miles. To the most pious princes, Gaius Valerius Constantius and Gaius Valerianus Maximianus, most noble Caesars, 8.
EDCS-09500258.summary: This inscription honors multiple emperors, including Crispus and the Caesars Constantius II and Galerius Maximianus, indicating distances of 8 miles.

EDCS-09500260.translation: To our Lord Flavius Dalmatius, the noblest Caesar.
EDCS-09500260.summary: An inscription dedicated to Flavius Dalmatius, described as the noblest Caesar, likely from the early 4th century CE.

EDCS-09500264.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Flavio Valerio Constantino Pio Felici Augusto divi Constanti Augusti Pii filio\n
EDCS-09500264.translation: To Emperor Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantinus, pious, happy, unconquered Augustus, son of the divine Constantius Augustus Pius.
EDCS-09500264.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Constantine the Great, emphasizing his titles and parentage.

EDCS-09500271.translation: To Emperor Caesar Galerius Valerius Maximianus, pious, happy, unconquered Augustus, and to Maximinus, most noble Caesar.
EDCS-09500271.summary: This inscription honors Emperors Galerius Maximianus and Maximinus, likely as co-rulers or in recognition of their imperial titles.

EDCS-09500301.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar divi Magni Antonini Pii filius divi Severi nepos [Marcus Aurelius] [Antoninus] Pius Felix Augustus pontifex maximus tribunicia potestate II consul II pater patriae proconsul milia passuum III\n
EDCS-09500301.translation: To Emperor Caesar, son of the divine Antoninus Pius, grandson of the divine Severus, Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, with his second tribunician power, twice consul, father of the country, proconsul, 3 miles.
EDCS-09500301.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Marcus Aurelius (likely Commodus), detailing his numerous titles and a distance of 3 miles.

EDCS-09500302.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar Caius Iulius Maximinus Pius Felix Augustus et Caius Iulius Maximus nobilissimus Caesar pontes et vias vetustate conlabsas sic restituerunt colonia Equestri milia passuum III\n
EDCS-09500302.translation: Emperor Caesar Gaius Julius Maximinus Pius Felix Augustus and Gaius Julius Maximus, most noble Caesar, restored bridges and roads worn out by age, Colony of Equestri, 3 miles.
EDCS-09500302.summary: This inscription records the restoration of bridges and roads by Emperors Maximinus Thrax and his son, Caesar Gaius Julius Maximus, in the colony of Equestri.

EDCS-09500303.translation: To Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus Arabicus Adiabenicus Parthicus Maximus, chief priest, with his ninth tribunician power, emperor for the eleventh time, consul for the second time, designated for the third, father of the country, and to Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, with his fourth tribunician power, designated consul, and to Publius Septimius Geta, most noble Caesar.
EDCS-09500303.summary: This inscription honors Emperors Septimius Severus, Caracalla, and Geta, detailing their extensive titles and powers.

EDCS-09500306.translation: To Emperor Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantinus, pious, happy, unconquered Augustus, and to Severus, most noble Caesar, 7.
EDCS-09500306.summary: This inscription honors Emperors Constantine the Great and Severus, likely noting a distance of 7 miles or a seventh designation.

EDCS-09500315.translation: To Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, son of Drusus, chief priest, holding tribunician power for the 3rd time, acclaimed imperator for the 3rd time, consul for the 3rd time, father of the country. (Measurement) 7 [miles].
EDCS-09500315.summary: This is a milestone inscription from the reign of Claudius, indicating a distance of 7 miles, likely related to a road construction or maintenance project.

EDCS-09500318.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the country, chief priest, holding tribunician power for the 7th time, consul for the 4th time. (Measurement) 3 [miles].
EDCS-09500318.summary: This is a milestone inscription from the reign of Antoninus Pius, indicating a distance of 3 miles, likely related to a road construction or maintenance project.

EDCS-09500321.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the country, chief priest, holding tribunician power for the 7th time, consul for the 4th time. (Measurement) 14 [miles].
EDCS-09500321.summary: This is a milestone inscription from the reign of Antoninus Pius, indicating a distance of 14 miles, likely related to a road construction or maintenance project.

EDCS-09500322.translation: To Emperor Caesar Gaius Julius Verus Maximinus Pius Felix Augustus Germanicus Sarmaticus Dacicus Maximus and Gaius Julius Verus Maximus, most noble Caesar. (Measurement) 30 [miles].
EDCS-09500322.summary: This is a milestone inscription from the reign of Maximinus Thrax and his son Gaius Julius Verus Maximus, indicating a distance of 30 miles, likely related to a road construction or maintenance project.

EDCS-09500323.translation: To Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, son of Drusus, chief priest, holding tribunician power for the 3rd time, acclaimed imperator for the 3rd time, consul for the 3rd time, father of the country. (Measurement) 25 [miles].
EDCS-09500323.summary: This is a milestone inscription from the reign of Claudius, indicating a distance of 25 miles, likely related to a road construction or maintenance project.

EDCS-09500324.translation: Emperor Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantius, Pious, Fortunate, Augustus; Flavius Valerius Severus, the noblest Caesar; 30 miles. Valentinianus, our Lord, always Augustus, born for the good of the republic.
EDCS-09500324.summary: An inscription referencing Emperor Constantius, the Caesar Severus, and Emperor Valentinianus, possibly related to road construction or milestones, dating to the early 4th century CE.

EDCS-09500325.translation: To Emperor Caesar Lucius Domitius Aurelianus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, chief priest, greatest German, greatest Goth, greatest Carpus, holding tribunician power for the 5th time, acclaimed imperator for the 3rd time, consul, father of the country. (Measurement) 39 [miles].
EDCS-09500325.summary: This is a milestone inscription from the reign of Aurelian, indicating a distance of 39 miles, likely related to a road construction or maintenance project.

EDCS-09500326.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Claudius Pius Augustus Felix, chief priest, greatest Goth, holding tribunician power for the 3rd time, consul for the 2nd time, father of the country, proconsul.
EDCS-09500326.summary: This is a fragmented milestone inscription from the reign of Claudius Gothicus, likely indicating a distance and administrative titles.

EDCS-09500330.translation: To Emperor Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantinus Pius Felix Augustus, son of the divine Augustus Pius Constantine. [Text missing].
EDCS-09500330.summary: This is a milestone inscription from the reign of Constantine the Great, honoring him and his father, with a missing indication of distance or further dedication.

EDCS-09500331.translation: To our lords Dalmatins, most noble Caesar. [Text missing].
EDCS-09500331.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely dedicated to a Caesar, possibly Dalmatins, with missing context and date.

EDCS-09500332.translation: To Emperor Caesar Lucius Domitius Aurelianus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, chief priest, greatest German, greatest Goth. [Text missing].
EDCS-09500332.summary: This is a fragmented milestone inscription from the reign of Aurelian, honoring him with several titles, with a missing indication of distance or further dedication.

EDCS-09500333.translation: Tiberius Caesar Augustus, son of the deified Augustus, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power for the 33rd time, rebuilt and restored.
EDCS-09500333.summary: This is a dedication by Emperor Tiberius, likely for a public building or infrastructure, indicating his restoration work.

EDCS-09500334.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantinus, pious, fortunate, unconquered Augustus, grandson of the deified Constantius Augustus Pius, son of [---].
EDCS-09500334.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Constantine the Great, possibly on a monument commemorating his lineage and titles.

EDCS-09500335.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantinus, pious, most noble Caesar, son of the deified Constantius Pius Augustus. [---]
EDCS-09500335.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Constantine the Great as Caesar, likely from an earlier period of his rule, before he became Augustus.

EDCS-09500336.translation: Tiberius Caesar Augustus, son of the deified Augustus, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power for the 33rd time, rebuilt and restored.
EDCS-09500336.summary: This is a dedication by Emperor Tiberius, likely for a public building or infrastructure, indicating his restoration work (variant of EDCS-09500333).

EDCS-09500339.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Flavius Claudius Constantius, Pious, the noblest Caesar, grandson of the deified Constantius Augustus Pious, 13 miles.
EDCS-09500339.summary: A dedication to Emperor Constantius, son of the deified Constantius, likely related to a road marker, dating to the mid-4th century CE.

EDCS-09500340.translation: To the restorer and peacemaker of the world, the Emperor Caesar Lucius Domitius Aurelianus, pious, fortunate, unconquered Augustus, Germanicus maximus, Gothicus maximus, Carpicus maximus, Persicus maximus, pontifex maximus. [---]
EDCS-09500340.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Aurelian, listing his numerous honorific titles and acknowledging his military victories and role as a peacemaker.

EDCS-09500341.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Valerius Diocletianus, pious, fortunate, Augustus, 31 miles. // To the Emperor Caesar Licinius Licinius, 31 miles.
EDCS-09500341.summary: This inscription records milestones for roads dedicated to Emperors Diocletian and Licinius, indicating distances in Roman miles.

EDCS-09500343.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the fatherland, holding tribunician power for the 7th time, consul for the 4th time, 17 miles.
EDCS-09500343.summary: This is a milestone inscription for Emperor Antoninus Pius, noting road distances and his consular and tribunician powers.

EDCS-09500344.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Pius, father of the fatherland, holding tribunician power for the 7th time, consul for the 4th time, 16 miles.
EDCS-09500344.summary: This is a milestone inscription for Emperor Antoninus Pius, noting road distances and his consular and tribunician powers.

EDCS-09500345.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Pius, father of the fatherland, holding tribunician power for the 7th time, consul for the 4th time, 14 miles.
EDCS-09500345.summary: This is a milestone inscription for Emperor Antoninus Pius, noting road distances and his consular and tribunician powers.

EDCS-09500346.translation: To our Lord Flavius Valerius Constantinus, most noble Caesar, Alba, 14 miles.
EDCS-09500346.summary: This is a milestone inscription likely dedicated to Constantine the Great, noting a distance from Alba.

EDCS-09500348.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Pius, father of the country, holding the tribunician power for the 7th time, consul for the 4th time; 9 miles.
EDCS-09500348.summary: This is a milestone inscription dedicated to Emperor Antoninus Pius, recording a distance of 9 miles and dating to his 7th tribunician power and 4th consulship.

EDCS-09500350.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Pius, father of the country, holding the tribunician power for the 7th time, consul for the 4th time; 6 miles.
EDCS-09500350.summary: This is a milestone inscription dedicated to Emperor Antoninus Pius, recording a distance of 6 miles and dating to his 7th tribunician power and 4th consulship.

EDCS-09500351.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Pius, father of the country, holding the tribunician power for the 7th time, consul for the 4th time; 4 miles.
EDCS-09500351.summary: This is a milestone inscription dedicated to Emperor Antoninus Pius, recording a distance of 4 miles and dating to his 7th tribunician power and 4th consulship.

EDCS-09500352.translation: To the deified Constantius our lord Valerius Licinianus Licinius the Younger, most noble Caesar, son of our lords Constantine the Great and perpetual Augustus, brother-in-law of the prince, born for the good of the state.
EDCS-09500352.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the deified Emperor Constantius, likely from the early 4th century.

EDCS-09500354.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Valerianus Pius Felix Augustus, father of the country, holding the tribunician power for the 3rd time, consul for the 3rd time; 14 miles.
EDCS-09500354.summary: This is a milestone inscription dedicated to Emperor Valerian, recording a distance of 14 miles and dating to his 3rd tribunician power and 3rd consulship.

EDCS-09500357.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maximianus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, pontifex maximus, holder of tribunician power, father of the country, consul, proconsul; Alba, 17 miles.
EDCS-09500357.summary: This is a milestone inscription dedicated to Emperor Maximian, recording a distance of 17 miles and mentioning the location Alba.

EDCS-09500360.translation: Under Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the country, holding the tribunician power for the 7th time, consul for the 4th time; 10 miles.
EDCS-09500360.summary: This is a milestone inscription dedicated to Emperor Antoninus Pius, recording a distance of 10 miles and dating to his 7th tribunician power and 4th consulship.

EDCS-09500361.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantinus, noble Caesar, son of the divine Augustus Constantine, good for the state, born.
EDCS-09500361.summary: This inscription honors Constantine the Great's son, the Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantinus.

EDCS-09500362.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the country, holding the tribunician power for the 7th time, consul for the 4th time; 13 miles (?).
EDCS-09500362.summary: This is a milestone inscription dedicated to Emperor Antoninus Pius, recording an uncertain distance of 13 miles and dating to his 7th tribunician power and 4th consulship.

EDCS-09500363.translation: To the Emperor Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the country, holding the tribunician power for the 7th time, consul for the 4th time; 17 miles.
EDCS-09500363.summary: This is a milestone inscription dedicated to Emperor Antoninus Pius, recording a distance of 17 miles and dating to his 7th tribunician power and 4th consulship.

EDCS-09500364.translation: To the Emperor Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the country, holding the tribunician power for the 7th time, consul for the 4th time; 20 miles.
EDCS-09500364.summary: This is a milestone inscription dedicated to Emperor Antoninus Pius, recording a distance of 20 miles and dating to his 7th tribunician power and 4th consulship.

EDCS-09500365.translation: To the Emperor Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the fatherland, holding tribunician power for the 7th time, consul for the 4th, 21 miles.

EDCS-09500366.translation: To the Emperor Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the fatherland, holding tribunician power for the 7th time, consul for the 4th, 22 miles.

EDCS-09500368.translation: To the Emperor Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the fatherland, holding tribunician power for the 7th time, consul for the 4th, [---] [6 characters illegible].

EDCS-09500371.translation: [To the Emperor Titus] / [Aelius Hadrianus] / [Antoninus] / Augustus Pius, father of the fatherland, holding tribunician power for the 7th time, consul for the 4th, 30 miles.

EDCS-09700189.translation: Sextus, son of Anlisius, son of Quintus.

EDCS-09700190.translation: To Lucius Appius Pristinus, son of Quartus, a pious son.

EDCS-09700194.translation: Consors, son of Nigrus, to his wife Tertulla, daughter of Commius.

EDCS-09700195.translation: To Divecillus, son of Cario, pious sons.

EDCS-09700201.translation: To Gaius Julius Fuscus, the trumpeter.

EDCS-09800549.translation: Tiberius Caesar Augustus, son of the deified Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 33rd time, repaired and restored it [the building/structure]; 63 [paces/units].
EDCS-09800549.summary: This inscription records the repair and restoration of a building or structure by Emperor Tiberius, with a measurement of 63 units.

EDCS-09800551.translation: Tiberius Caesar Augustus, son of the deified Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 33rd time, repaired and restored it [the building/structure]; 62 [paces/units].
EDCS-09800551.summary: This inscription records the repair and restoration of a building or structure by Emperor Tiberius, with a measurement of 62 units.

EDCS-09800555.text_edition: \n Caesari a Nemauso milia passuum XXXI\n
EDCS-09800555.summary: This inscription records a distance of 31 miles from Nemausus, likely a milestone or directional marker.

EDCS-09800558.translation: Tiberius Caesar Augustus, son of the deified Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 33rd time, repaired [the building/structure].
EDCS-09800558.summary: This inscription records the repair of a structure by Emperor Tiberius, dating to his 33rd year of tribunician power.

EDCS-09800559.translation: To our lord Gaius Pius Esuvius Tetricus, most noble Caesar, son of Emperor Gaius Pius Esuvius Tetricus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 2nd time, consul.
EDCS-09800559.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the usurper emperor Tetricus I or his son Tetricus II, likely from the late 3rd century CE.

EDCS-09800560.translation: Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, chief priest, greatest, with tribunician power for the 7th time, imperator for the 14th time, father of the country, consul for the 4th time, censor, repaired [the building/structure]; 3 (?) units.
EDCS-09800560.summary: This inscription records the repair of a structure by Emperor Claudius, likely dating to around 47-48 CE.

EDCS-09800564.translation: The Emperor Caesar Augustus, son of the deified [father], father of the country, chief priest, greatest, consul for the 13th time, with tribunician power for the 22nd time, imperator for the 14th time; 16 [paces/units]; Forum Julii 917 [paces/units]; the civitas of the Vasionenses of the Vocontii 898 [paces/units]; the kingdom of the Cotti [?] [lacuna].
EDCS-09800564.summary: This inscription, likely from the reign of Augustus, records distances in paces to Forum Julii and a civitas of the Vocontii, and possibly refers to the regnum of the Cotti.

EDCS-09800569.text_edition: \n Flavio Valerio Constantino nobilissimo Caesari milia p(assuum) XXXIIII\n
EDCS-09800569.translation: To Flavius Valerius Constantinus, most noble Caesar; 34 miles.
EDCS-09800569.summary: This inscription records a distance of 34 miles to Flavius Valerius Constantinus (Constantine the Great), likely a milestone.

EDCS-09800570.translation: To Marcus Numerius Numerianus, most noble Caesar, prince of the youth; from Narbo, 1 mile.
EDCS-09800570.summary: This inscription records a distance of 1 mile from Narbo to Marcus Numerius Numerianus, likely a milestone.

EDCS-09800573.translation: To Gaius Pius Tetricus, most noble Caesar, prince of the youth, consul; 29 [units].
EDCS-09800573.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Gaius Pius Tetricus (Tetricus II), likely from the late 3rd century CE.

EDCS-09800577.translation: To our Lord Galerius Valerius Maximianus Pius Felix Invictus Semper Augustus Caesar. 15 miles. To our Lord Flavius Julius Dalmatius, most noble Caesar. 15 miles. Emperor Caesar Gaius Julius Verus Maximinus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, Pontifex Maximus, holder of tribunician power for the [X]th time, consul for the second time, father of the country, proconsul, restored [this road]. 15 miles.
EDCS-09800577.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a road by Emperor Maximinus, likely dating to the early 4th century CE.

EDCS-09800578.translation: To Emperor Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantinus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, grandson of Marcus [Aurelius] Valerius Maximinus Augustus, son of the divine Constantius Augustus. 16 miles. To our Lords Magnus Maximus and Flavius Victor. 16 miles. To our Lords Flavius Valentinianus and Flavius Theodosius and Flavius Arcadius, born for the good of the state. 16 miles.
EDCS-09800578.summary: This inscription marks milestones for several emperors, including Constantine, Magnus Maximus, Flavius Victor, Valentinian, Theodosius, and Arcadius, spanning the late 4th century CE.

EDCS-09800579.translation: Three Roman miles to our lord Flavius Decentius, most noble Caesar.
EDCS-09800579.summary: This milestone indicates a distance of three Roman miles to a monument dedicated to Flavius Decentius, likely in the 4th century CE.

EDCS-09800584.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maximinus Pius [Felix Invictus] Augustus.
EDCS-09800584.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription dedicated to Emperor Maximinus, likely from the early 4th century CE.

EDCS-10400172.translation: To the divine spirits. Marcus Valerius Iustus to his most holy wife, Iulia Paulina, daughter of Sergius.
EDCS-10400172.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Marcus Valerius Iustus to his wife Iulia Paulina, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-10501387.summary: This is a funerary inscription for someone named Clarin, likely from late antiquity.

EDCS-10502259.translation: [Nero] Claudius, son of the divine Claudius, grandson of Germanicus Caesar, great-grandson of Tiberius Caesar Augustus, great-great-grandson of the divine Augustus, Caesar Augustus Germanicus, Pontifex Maximus.
EDCS-10502259.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription naming Emperor Nero Claudius, likely dating to the mid-1st century CE.

EDCS-10701803.translation: Iulia Avita, daughter of Sextus, to Elausia, according to her vow.
EDCS-10701803.summary: This is a votive inscription by Iulia Avita to the deity Elausia, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11501882.translation: To Castor Augustus, Gaius Caprilius Sparsus from the votive offerings of the year of the consulship of Mani Acilius Glabrio and Marcus Ulpius Traianus, during which he was priest.
EDCS-11501882.summary: This is a dedication to the god Castor from the year 117 CE, made by Gaius Caprilius Sparsus who was serving as priest.

EDCS-11501885.translation: To the Divine Manes, Marcus Iulius Marcianus, father [of the deceased].
EDCS-11501885.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Iulia Optata, made by her father.

EDCS-11501888.translation: Lucius P. Amoenus willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Mercury.
EDCS-11501888.summary: This is a votive dedication to Mercury by Lucius P. Amoenus, who fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-11501894.summary: This is an isolated name, likely indicating a tomb or memorial.

EDCS-11501895.translation: Lucius Valerius Amabilis, priest, [dedicated this] to Mars.
EDCS-11501895.summary: This is a dedication to Mars by Lucius Valerius Amabilis, who held the office of priest.

EDCS-11501896.summary: This inscription records a monetary donation of 10,000 sesterces by Procula.

EDCS-11700306.translation: To Gaius Lucceius, son of Lucius, of the Aniensis tribe, veteran of the First Cohort of Marines, Sertorianus Sertoris, son of Sertor, [dedicates this] along with his wife and daughters.
EDCS-11700306.summary: This is a dedication to Gaius Lucceius, a veteran of the First Cohort of Marines, made by his relative Sertorianus Sertoris and his family.

EDCS-11700308.translation: Salviae, his freedwoman, the goldsmith Nicias, deservedly, and to himself.
EDCS-11700308.summary: This inscription records Nicias, a goldsmith, dedicating something to his freedwoman Salvia and possibly to himself as well.

EDCS-11700309.translation: Niger made [this] for P. and for his Cleopatra, his midwife.
EDCS-11700309.summary: This inscription records Niger dedicating something to P. and his wife Cleopatra, who was a midwife.

EDCS-11700313.translation: To Anicetus, freedman of Ca., his fellow freedmen and household.
EDCS-11700313.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Anicetus, a freedman, made by his fellow freedmen and household.

EDCS-11700314.translation: To Dionysius, son of Democratis; his heir [made this].
EDCS-11700314.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Dionysius, son of Democratis, by his heir, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11700317.translation: Theodorus, son of Moschus, made this for his wife Hortensia Chrotarion.
EDCS-11700317.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Theodorus for his wife, Hortensia Chrotarion, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11700318.translation: To Arguria and Safronia Fortunata, in memory of the deserving Laelius Martinus.
EDCS-11700318.summary: This inscription records a memorial for Laelius Martinus, set up by Arguria and Safronia Fortunata, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11700319.translation: Clodea made this for Lucretia Marcia, according to the will.
EDCS-11700319.summary: This funerary inscription indicates that Clodea erected a monument for Lucretia Marcia as stipulated in a will, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11700321.translation: Quintus Pescennius made this, while alive, for his brother Titus Pescennius Gracchus, son of Pescennius, and for his sister Silvina, daughter of Caius, and for Vera, daughter of Lucius, wife of Gavia, daughter of Lucius Silvinus.
EDCS-11700321.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Quintus Pescennius for his brother and sisters, indicating family relationships and likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11700323.translation: To Valerius Calitus, son of Caius.
EDCS-11700323.summary: This is a dedication to Valerius Calitus, son of Caius, likely a funerary or honorific inscription dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11700324.translation: To the Divine Shades: for Valeria, his wife, Briganticus.
EDCS-11700324.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Briganticus to the Divine Shades in memory of his wife Valeria, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11700325.translation: To Victor, son of Onesimus, son of F(---) O F V, his son, in front 3 feet, in the field 3 feet.
EDCS-11700325.summary: This inscription records a funerary dedication to Victor, son of Onesimus, specifying plot dimensions, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11700326.translation: To the Divine Shades: for Vigellia Isis, his dearest freedwoman, by Vigellia.
EDCS-11700326.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Vigellia to her dearest freedwoman, Vigellia Isis, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11700336.summary: This fragmentary inscription mentions a son of Lucius and possibly an indication of birth or status, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11700350.text_edition: \n Caius Iulius Dionysius Caius Iulius Apolinaris\n
EDCS-11700350.translation: Gaius Julius Dionysius, Gaius Julius Apollinaris.
EDCS-11700350.summary: This is a very brief inscription likely recording the names of two individuals, possibly related or associated.

EDCS-11700352.translation: To Caia V. Severa, daughter of Marcus, of the tribe Oniissio, wife of Numerius Tessieleus, from Postumia Quarta.
EDCS-11700352.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Caia V. Severa, likely set up by her relative Postumia Quarta.

EDCS-11700353.translation: To Lucius Aconius, son of Lucius, of the tribe Aniensis, of the 21st and 4th legions, husband.
EDCS-11700353.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Lucius Aconius, a soldier of two legions.

EDCS-11700354.translation: The monument of Titus Exomnius, son of Cuo, and his living son Lucius.
EDCS-11700354.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Titus Exomnius for himself and his living son Lucius.

EDCS-11700355.translation: To Primus Rufus, son of his son, sister.
EDCS-11700355.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely a funerary dedication from a sister to Primus Rufus.

EDCS-11700356.text_edition: \n Caio Novellio Quinti filio Aniensi veterano legionis VIIII\n
EDCS-11700356.translation: To Gaius Novellius, son of Quintus, of the Aniensis tribe, a veteran of the Ninth Legion.
EDCS-11700356.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Gaius Novellius, a veteran of the Ninth Legion, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11700357.translation: To Gaius Coelius Severus, freedman of Gaius, Vivirus, to his wife Iucunda, freedwoman of Gaius.
EDCS-11700357.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Gaius Coelius Severus to his wife Iucunda.

EDCS-11700358.translation: Marcus Octavius, son of Catullus, set this up while alive for himself and for Lucius, son of his brother.
EDCS-11700358.summary: This is a funerary dedication erected by Marcus Octavius for himself and his nephew Lucius.

EDCS-11700360.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription indicating that 'Anus Molici' is buried here.

EDCS-11700361.translation: To Lucius Casinius, soldier of the 8th legion, a scout, who died at the age of 28.
EDCS-11700361.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Lucius Casinius, a soldier and scout in the 8th legion.

EDCS-11700362.translation: To the divine spirits of Ursa, a most innocent soul, aged 20. Statia Lupa, mother.
EDCS-11700362.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Ursa, erected by her mother Statia Lupa.

EDCS-11700363.translation: Marcus Satrius, son of Marcus, of the tribe Teretina, a soldier, a scout, is buried here.
EDCS-11700363.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Satrius, a soldier and scout.

EDCS-11700365.text_edition: \n Sextae Satiae Sexti filiae Maxsumae sic coniugi Quintus Masonius Kari libertus Alco\n
EDCS-11700365.translation: To Sextae Satiae, daughter of Sextus, Maxsuma, as his wife. Quintus Masonius Alco, freedman of Kari.
EDCS-11700365.summary: This inscription is a dedication from Quintus Masonius Alco to his wife Sextae Satias, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11700366.translation: Roquetus, freedman of Primus Caius Julius, gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11700366.summary: This is a votive inscription recording a freedman fulfilling a vow to an unknown deity.

EDCS-11700372.translation: Augustus Germanicus, son of the deified Claudius, grandson of Germanicus Caesar, great-grandson of Tiberius Caesar Augustus, great-great-grandson of the deified Augustus, Emperor, Pontifex Maximus, with tribunician power for the fourth time, Imperator for the fourth time, Consul for the third time, Father of the Fatherland, restored this.
EDCS-11700372.summary: This is a lengthy imperial dedication by Emperor Nero, listing his titles and ancestry, recording a restoration.

EDCS-11700378.translation: To Lucius Matucius Maximus, decemvir for adjudicating lawsuits, military tribune of the Legio II Adiutrix, quaestor of the province Macedonia, patron, by decree of the local councillors.
EDCS-11700378.summary: This is an honorific inscription dedicated to Lucius Matucius Maximus, detailing his career and public honors.

EDCS-11700380.translation: To Gaius Verginus, son of Verginus, magistrate of the four-man board, and son of the four-man magistrate.
EDCS-11700380.summary: This is a dedication to Gaius Verginus, mentioning his role as a magistrate and his father's similar position.

EDCS-11700381.translation: To Marcella, priestess of Minerva and Diana, in honor of her husband Calpurnius Hermes, by the Augustales corporati of Antipolis.
EDCS-11700381.summary: This is a dedication to Marcella, a priestess, made by a collegium in her honor and in honor of her husband.

EDCS-11700382.summary: This is a dedication to Marcus Veturius, identifying him as a member of a collegium.

EDCS-11700386.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Vincentius to his deserving friend Aurelius Bubalus.
EDCS-11700386.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating a monument to Aurelius Bubalus by his friend Vincentius.

EDCS-11700387.text_edition: \n Caius Cornelius Carpophorus sibi vivus fecit\n
EDCS-11700387.translation: Gaius Cornelius Carpophorus made this for himself while alive.
EDCS-11700387.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording that Gaius Cornelius Carpophorus commissioned his own monument during his lifetime, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11700390.summary: This is a funerary inscription from a son dedicating something to his beloved mother, Marcella.

EDCS-11700399.summary: This is a very brief inscription identifying Marcus, son of Marcus.

EDCS-11700401.summary: This is a dedication to Valentina, identifying her parentage.

EDCS-11700402.translation: Hail Gaius Valerius Valerianus; may you be well; farewell. Gaius Valerius Paternus and Valeria Valeriana.
EDCS-11700402.summary: This is a private dedication, likely a tombstone or epitaph, by Gaius Valerius Paternus and Valeria Valeriana for Gaius Valerius Valerianus.

EDCS-11700403.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Gaius Valerius Valerianus, by his most devoted father Gaius Valerius Classicus, who lived 18 years.
EDCS-11700403.summary: This is a tombstone set up by a father for his son, Gaius Valerius Valerianus, who died at the age of 18.

EDCS-11700404.summary: This is a dedication, likely a tombstone, for Lucius Valerius Germanus.

EDCS-11700406.translation: To the spirits of the departed: for Quintus Aemilius Secundus, decurion, a most deserving parent, from his son Marcus Aemilius Nepos.
EDCS-11700406.summary: This is a tombstone set up by a son for his deserving father, Quintus Aemilius Secundus, who held the rank of decurion.

EDCS-11700407.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Lucius Abicelius Hermias made this for his most excellent wife Abicelia Ania.
EDCS-11700407.summary: This is a tombstone set up by a husband for his wife, Abicelia Ania.

EDCS-11700410.summary: This is a dedication, likely a tombstone, for Lucius Abicelius Fim[---].

EDCS-11700411.translation: Lucius Hilarius Quartus and Caricia Optata and his sister Hilaria Frontina made this for their incomparable son Lucius Hilario Paternus.
EDCS-11700411.summary: This is a tombstone set up by parents and a sister for their beloved son, Lucius Hilario Paternus.

EDCS-11700412.summary: This is a dedication, likely a tombstone, from Pompeia Lasciva for an individual whose name is incomplete.

EDCS-11700413.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Verginius Hilarus made this for himself and his family while alive.
EDCS-11700413.summary: This is a funerary monument that Verginius Hilarus commissioned for himself and his family during his lifetime.

EDCS-11700414.summary: This is a dedication, likely a tombstone or a commemorative monument, made by Publius Carfinius Quartus.

EDCS-11700421.translation: To Caius Venusius, son of Caius, Andron, duovir.
EDCS-11700421.summary: This inscription records the dedication to Caius Venusius by Andron, who held the office of duovir.

EDCS-11700422.translation: Lucius Amaenius Fronto and his wife Vilbia Marcella, and their sons Marcus Amaenius Maturus and Marcus Amaenius Optatianus, erected this statue of Arbugio and also the pagus.
EDCS-11700422.summary: This inscription records a family, the Amaenii, dedicating a statue and a pagus (village or district) to Arbugio.

EDCS-11700423.translation: To the Divine Shades. Caius Nemasunius and Rufina, parents, made this for their most dutiful son Lucius Nemas L. Nemasunius, and for themselves and their descendants, while they were alive.
EDCS-11700423.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by parents for their son Lucius Nemas L. Nemasunius, and also for themselves and their descendants.

EDCS-11700429.translation: To the Divine Shades, sacred. Severina made this for her most sweet mother Viria Melpomenes, and for herself. Severina made this for her most sweet mother Viria Melpomenes, and for herself.
EDCS-11700429.summary: This funerary inscription records Severina dedicating a memorial to her mother Viria Melpomenes and for herself.

EDCS-11700430.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Tullius [dedicated this].
EDCS-11700430.summary: This is a fragmentary dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, likely made by an individual named Tullius.

EDCS-11700431.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Viator has dedicated.
EDCS-11700431.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Viator.

EDCS-11700433.translation: Valerius, son of Lati, willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Mercury.
EDCS-11700433.summary: This inscription records Valerius, son of Lati, fulfilling a vow to Mercury.

EDCS-11700434.text_edition: \n Reiuniis Marcus Iulius Iustus hastatus primus legionis IIII Macedonicae votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11700434.translation: Marcus Julius Justus, hastatus primus of the Fourth Macedonian Legion, freed from vows willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-11700434.summary: This inscription records Marcus Julius Justus, a soldier of the Fourth Macedonian Legion, fulfilling a vow, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11700435.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or dedication to Heusychas, son of Sotericus.

EDCS-11700436.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the departed spirits.

EDCS-11700437.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Marco Iulio Grato Iulia Grata patri pientissimo viva fecit\n
EDCS-11700437.translation: To the departed spirits. Iulia Grata made this for her most dutiful father, Marcus Iulius Gratus, while she was alive.
EDCS-11700437.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Iulia Grata for her father, Marcus Iulius Gratus.

EDCS-11700438.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Nero, a Batavian citizen, he made this memorial for himself for eternity while alive.
EDCS-11700438.summary: This funerary inscription records Nero, a Batavian citizen, making a memorial for himself.

EDCS-11700439.text_edition: \n ------ A]rausiensis Secundus filio mo vivos sic fecit\n
EDCS-11700439.translation: Secundus of Arausio made this for his sons while he was alive.
EDCS-11700439.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Secundus of Arausio for his sons.

EDCS-11700448.translation: To the Divine Shades. Severina and Deuter set this up for Fortunatus, their most sweet freedman, who lived for X years.
EDCS-11700448.summary: This funerary inscription records Severina and Deuter dedicating a memorial to their freedman Fortunatus.

EDCS-11700454.translation: Under Gaius Bruttius Crispinus and Lucius Roscio Aelianus, consuls, on the tenth day before the Kalends of March. By decree of the decurions of the municipium of Dinium and Bodionticum, having been summoned to the curia, the scribes who wrote this decree were: Marcus Messius Serenus, flamen of the civitas; Gaius Beiuclus Sequens; Lucius Maculius Severus; Gaius Valerius Victor; Marcus Marini. And Valerius Licinianus, Marcus [---], duumviri, [---] and quaestors, it was decided that [---] should be provided by them and those [---]. Titus Veranius L[---]nia because [---] Veranius [---] justice [---] it is lawful [---] Sextus Sa[---] Satu[---] qua[---]
EDCS-11700454.summary: This inscription records a municipal decree from Dinium and Bodionticum, detailing financial matters and appointments of officials, dated to February 21st under consuls Gaius Bruttius Crispinus and Lucius Roscio Aelianus.

EDCS-11700455.translation: Pompeia Antiopa paid her vow to Borbanus.
EDCS-11700455.summary: This inscription records Pompeia Antiopa fulfilling a vow to Borbanus.

EDCS-11700457.translation: Anilla gladly paid her vow to Minerva, as deserved.
EDCS-11700457.summary: This is a votive inscription by Anilla to Minerva, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11700458.translation: Priamus gladly paid his vow to the Nymphs, as deserved.
EDCS-11700458.summary: This is a votive inscription by Priamus to the Nymphs, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11700459.translation: Priamus gladly paid his vow to the Nymphs, as deserved.
EDCS-11700459.summary: This is a votive inscription by Priamus to the Nymphs, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11700462.translation: Gaius Pompeius Hospes gladly paid his vow, as deserved.
EDCS-11700462.summary: This is a votive inscription by Gaius Pompeius Hospes, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11700464.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Cnaei Licini Marci Licinia Veneria marito incomparabili et dendrophori Aquenses\n
EDCS-11700464.translation: To the departed spirits. Licinia Veneria and the dendrophori of Aquae for their incomparable husband, Cnaeus Licinius Marcu.
EDCS-11700464.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Licinia Veneria and the dendrophori of Aquae for Cnaeus Licinius Marcu.

EDCS-11700465.translation: Marcus Vitellius Celsus [erected this] for Lucius Antonius Rufus.
EDCS-11700465.summary: This is a dedication by Marcus Vitellius Celsus to Lucius Antonius Rufus, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11700466.summary: This is a dedication to Atilius Dionysius, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11700467.translation: Aulus Volumnius [dedicated this] to Cornelia F. Fausta.
EDCS-11700467.summary: This is a dedication by Aulus Volumnius to Cornelia F. Fausta, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11700469.translation: To the Divine Shades: Gaius Iulius Carus [erected this] for Lucius Cr[---].
EDCS-11700469.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Iulius Carus for Luci Cr[---], likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11700470.translation: Marcus Flavius Artemidorus [erected this] for his incomparable wife, Elpis.
EDCS-11700470.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Marcus Flavius Artemidorus for his wife Elpis, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11700471.translation: To the Divine Shades: Euhodus, fellow soldier [of?] Frontonia Sabina.
EDCS-11700471.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Euhodus, a contubernalis, for Frontonia Sabina, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11700473.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Publicia Terticia, aged 50, [erected this].
EDCS-11700473.summary: A funerary dedication by Publicia Terticia to the Manes, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-11700474.translation: Quintus Cornelius Pietas erected this memorial to Terentia Primula and Quintus Terentius Miccio, his fellow slaves/lovers.
EDCS-11700474.summary: A funerary monument erected by Quintus Cornelius Pietas for his partners, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-11700505.translation: Varus gladly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-11700505.summary: A votive inscription by Varus, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-11700509.translation: To Quintus Licinius Trocus, who lived 25 years. A worthy father to his son.
EDCS-11700509.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Licinius Trocus, noting his age and paternal qualities, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-11700510.text_edition: \n Fausta Herculi votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11700510.translation: Fausta willingly and deservedly paid her vow to Hercules.
EDCS-11700510.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Fausta fulfilling a vow to Hercules.

EDCS-11700512.translation: Placidus, son of Advetisso, gladly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-11700512.summary: A votive inscription by Placidus, son of Advetisso, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-11700514.translation: To Gaius Marillus Tyrannus, this monument in accordance with his will.
EDCS-11700514.summary: A funerary monument commissioned by testament for Gaius Marillus Tyrannus, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-11700517.summary: The name inscription of Pinaria Primigenia, likely a funerary marker or dedicant, dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-11700518.translation: Sextius Coinn paid his vow gladly and deservedly to Jupiter the Horned.
EDCS-11700518.summary: A votive inscription by Sextius Coinn to Jupiter Corniger, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-11700519.translation: Regillus dedicated the temple from its foundation.
EDCS-11700519.summary: An inscription recording the dedication of a temple from its foundation by Regillus, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11700526.translation: Quartus for himself and his family to Belinus.
EDCS-11700526.summary: A dedication by Quartus to the god Belinus for himself and his family, possibly from Roman Britain, dating to the 2nd-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-11700531.translation: To Liber Pater, from Bacchylus, freedman of Sextus Iulius Sereni.
EDCS-11700531.summary: This is a dedication to the god Liber Pater by a freedman named Bacchylus.

EDCS-11700535.translation: To Silvanus, from Titus Cornelius Maternus.
EDCS-11700535.summary: This is a dedication to the god Silvanus by Titus Cornelius Maternus.

EDCS-11700536.summary: This is a dedication to the 'Pagani' (villagers or rural community) by Petronia.

EDCS-11700539.translation: To the Nymphs, Servatus willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-11700539.summary: This records a votive offering to the Nymphs by Servatus.

EDCS-11700540.translation: To the Parcae (Fates), Materna willingly and deservedly paid her vow.
EDCS-11700540.summary: This records a votive offering to the Parcae (Fates) by Materna.

EDCS-11700541.translation: Valeria, daughter of Caius, to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, for the health and safety of the emperor.
EDCS-11700541.summary: This inscription likely records a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Valeria, possibly related to the well-being of the emperor.

EDCS-11700542.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead, for Cornelia Felicula.
EDCS-11700542.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Cornelia Felicula.

EDCS-11700544.translation: To Dexiva, ORARP willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-11700544.summary: This records a votive offering to a deity named Dexiva by a person whose name is partially illegible.

EDCS-11700545.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Cordius willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-11700545.summary: This records a votive offering to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Cordius.

EDCS-11700546.translation: To Lanovius, Sextus Celtilius Senecio willingly and deservedly paid his vow on behalf of Sextus Veratius.
EDCS-11700546.summary: This is a votive offering to the god Lanovius, made by Sextus Celtilius Senecio for Sextus Veratius.

EDCS-11700548.translation: To the god Divannus, Lucius Octavius Div [dedicated this].
EDCS-11700548.summary: A dedication to the god Divannus by Lucius Octavius Div.

EDCS-11700549.translation: Verus, son of Gesatus, gladly and deservedly paid his vow to Silvanus.
EDCS-11700549.summary: A votive dedication to the god Silvanus by Verus, son of Gesatus.

EDCS-11700550.translation: To Iulius Ratus, my most dutiful brother.
EDCS-11700550.summary: A dedication or memorial inscription for Iulius Ratus.

EDCS-11700551.translation: Verax, son of Antenor, and Potissuma, daughter of Olluna, [dedicated this] for the Uroices and AII in the months of [---].
EDCS-11700551.summary: A dedication by Verax and Potissuma, possibly for a local community or deities, with a date.

EDCS-11700553.translation: Decimus Domitius, son of Lucius, of the Voltinia tribe, Celer, military tribune, and praefectus fabrum, made this himself while alive.
EDCS-11700553.summary: A funerary monument or dedication by Decimus Domitius Celer, a military tribune and engineer, who made it during his lifetime.

EDCS-11700554.translation: Lucius Domitius, son of Lucius, of the Volinia tribe; Magu Domitia, daughter of Sextus, his mother.
EDCS-11700554.summary: A familial inscription noting Lucius Domitius and his mother, Magu Domitia.

EDCS-11700555.translation: Domitius, son of Lucius, of the Voltinia tribe, Macer, military tribune and pontifex, made this himself while alive.

EDCS-11700756.translation: To Hippodamia, his own, whom he set up as a perpetual memorial, born at one birth to his mother, alas too soon left by her beloved husband, Apolaustus. You, who are passing by, I pray you, pause your steps a moment and read: anxious fates once bound me, when life remained in flourishing youth, but contrary to my wishes, my parent died in grief for her beloved husband, and always for her husband. Your beauty, blessed one, also departed, fleeing the turning spheres. She left me behind. Together we were seen on the shores. Why was I born? I die. Life prepared death for me, for the one born from birth delivered me to the shades. Hippodamia was my name when life remained. This much, however, to you, my beloved wife, and to my country, where life was given to me. Alas, for the one born, this is sad for me, beloved spouse, P...
