EDCS-12100286.text_edition: \n Tito Statilio Tauro Lucio Cassio Longino consulibus X Kalendas Octobres numini Augusti votum susceptum a plebe Narbonensium in perpetuom sic quod bonum faustum felixque sit Imperatori Caesari Divi filio Augusto patri patriae pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate XXXIIII coniugi liberis gentique eius senatui populoque Romano et colonis incolisque coloniae Iuliae Paternae Narbonis Marti qui se numini eius in perpetuum colendo obligaverunt pleps sic Narbonensium aram Narbone in foro posuit ad quam quot annis VIIII Kalendas Octobres qua die eum saeculi felicitas orbi terrarum rectorem edidit tres equites Romani a plebe et tres libertini hostias singulas inmolent et colonis et incolis ad supplicandum numini eius thus et vinum de suo ea die praestent et VIII Kalendas Octobres thus vinum colonis et incolis item praestent Kalendis quoque Ianuariis thus et vinum colonis et incolis praestent VII quoque Idus Ianuarias qua die primum imperium orbis terrarum auspicatus est thure vino supplicent et hostias singulas inmolent et colonis incolisque thus vinum ea die praestent et pridie Kalendas Iunias quod ea die Tito Statilio Tauro Manio Aemilio Lepido consulibus iudicia plebis decurionibus coniunxit hostias singulas inmolent et thus et vinum ad supplicandum numini eius colonis et incolis praestent exque iis tribus equitibus Romanis tribusve libertinis unu[s ------ Pleps Narbonensis aram numinis Augusti dedicavit [] legibus iis quae infra scriptae sunt numen Caesaris Augusti patris patriae quando tibi hodie hanc aram dabo dedicaboque his legibus hisque regionibus dabo dedicabo quas hic hodie palam dixero uti infimum solum huiusque arae titulorumque est si quis tergere ornare reficere volet quod beneficii causa fiat ius fasque esto sive quis hostia sacrum faxit qui magmentum nec protollat idcirco tamen probe factum esto si quis huic arae donum dare augereque volet liceto eademque lex ei dono esto quae arae est ceterae leges huic arae titulisque eadem sunto quae sunt arae Dianae in Aventino hisce legibus hisque regionibus sicuti dixi hanc tibi aram pro Imperatore Caesare Augusto patre patriae pontifice maximo tribunicia potestate XXXV coniuge liberis genteque eius senatu populoque Romano colonis incolisque coloniae Iuliae Paternae Narbonis Marti qui se numini eius in perpetuum colendo obligaverunt doque dedicoque uti sies volens propitium\n
EDCS-12100286.translation: In the consulship of Titus Statilius Taurus and Lucius Cassius Longinus, on the 8th day before the Kalends of October, a vow undertaken by the people of Narbonensium for eternity to the divine Augustus, Father of the Fatherland, Pontifex Maximus, with tribunician power for the 34th time, to his wife, children, family, the Senate, and the Roman People, and to the colonists and inhabitants of the colony of Iulia Paternensis Narbonis Martis who have bound themselves to worship his divinity forever: thus the people of Narbonensium have placed an altar to his divinity in the forum at Narbo, to which every year on the 8th day before the Kalends of October, the day on which the good fortune of the age gave him as ruler to the world, three Roman knights chosen by the people and three freedmen shall each sacrifice one victim, and shall provide from their own means oil and wine on that day for the colonists and inhabitants for supplicating his divinity, and on the 9th day before the Kalends of October, they shall likewise provide oil and wine for the colonists and inhabitants; also on the Kalends of January, they shall provide oil and wine for the colonists and inhabitants; and on the 7th day before the Ides of January, on which day he first began his rule over the world, they shall supplicate with incense and wine and sacrifice one victim each, and shall provide oil and wine for the colonists and inhabitants on that day; and on the day before the Kalends of June, because on that day, in the consulship of Titus Statilius Taurus and Manius Aemilius Lepidus, he joined the judgments of the people with the decurions, they shall sacrifice one victim each, and provide incense and wine for supplicating his divinity for the colonists and inhabitants. And from these, three Roman knights and three freedmen [---]. The People of Narbonensium dedicated the altar to the divinity of Augustus, Father of the Fatherland, according to the laws written below: When I will give and dedicate this altar to you today, O divinity of Caesar Augustus, Father of the Fatherland, Pontifex Maximus, with tribunician power for the 35th time, to his wife, children, family, the Senate, and the Roman People, and to the colonists and inhabitants of the colony of Iulia Paternensis Narbonis Martis who have bound themselves to worship his divinity forever, I will give and dedicate it according to these laws and these boundaries which I will declare here today in public, just as the lowest ground of this altar and its inscriptions are: if anyone wishes to clean, adorn, or repair it, let it be lawful and right for it to be done for the sake of kindness. If anyone sacrifices a victim and does not prolong the offering, nevertheless let it be considered properly done. If anyone wishes to give or add to this altar, let it be permitted, and let the same law apply to that gift as to the altar itself. Let the other laws for this altar and its inscriptions be the same as those for the altar of Diana on the Aventine. According to these laws and these boundaries, as I have said, I give and dedicate this altar to you, for Emperor Caesar Augustus, Father of the Fatherland, Pontifex Maximus, with tribunician power for the 35th time, to his wife, children, family, the Senate, and the Roman People, and to the colonists and inhabitants of the colony of Iulia Paternensis Narbonis Martis who have bound themselves to worship his divinity forever, and I give and dedicate it, so that you may be willing and propitious.
EDCS-12100286.summary: This is a lengthy public inscription from Narbo, dated to 11 BCE, detailing the dedication of an altar to the divine Augustus by the local populace and establishing complex rules for its maintenance, sacrifices, and offerings, with specific provisions for Roman knights and freedmen.

EDCS-13301740.summary: This is a dedication to the god Silvanus by Anthillus.

EDCS-13301741.translation: To Silvanus. A vow for himself.
EDCS-13301741.summary: This is a dedication to the god Silvanus, recording a vow made by the dedicator for himself.

EDCS-13301742.translation: Sacred to Tiberius Augustus. Sextus Aelianus Pisinus dedicated it from his own funds.
EDCS-13301742.summary: This is an imperial dedication to Tiberius Augustus, funded by Sextus Aelianus Pisinus.

EDCS-13301743.translation: To Caesar Germanicus, holder of tribunician power and thrice consul, Sextus Aelianus Pisinus, Augustalis, dedicated this from his own funds.
EDCS-13301743.summary: This is a dedication by Sextus Aelianus Pisinus to Caesar Germanicus, likely dating to the period of Germanicus's tribunician power.

EDCS-13301745.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Antiochus and Barytimus, parents, for their most dutiful son, who died at the age of 17 years and 8 months.
EDCS-13301745.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by parents for their deceased son, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13301746.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Expentanius Lucritianus placed this for Expentania Ermoninis, his freedwoman or wife, incomparable.
EDCS-13301746.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Expentanius Lucritianus for his freedwoman or wife, Expentania Ermoninis.

EDCS-13301748.summary: This is a funerary epitaph identifying a woman by her name and filiation, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13301749.summary: This is a funerary epitaph identifying a woman by her name and filiation, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13301752.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Vinicius Euprepes made this for himself and his descendants while alive.
EDCS-13301752.summary: This is a funerary epitaph where the deceased dedicates a tomb for himself and his family, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13301754.translation: For Avita, daughter of Marcus, most dutiful, aged 25.
EDCS-13301754.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young woman named Avita, providing her name, father, and age, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13301755.translation: Here, in peace, for more or less [X] years with his sons. October, by the mercy of God, lived faithfully.
EDCS-13301755.summary: This is a fragmented funerary epitaph that records a person named October who lived for a period with his sons, likely from the late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-13301759.translation: Marcus Aurelius Priscus, a distinguished former centurion, supply officer, gatekeeper, and usher for the most eminent Praetorian Prefects, and first scribe of the Praetorian camp; Marcus Iulius Eutyches, a Roman knight, granted this place for his incomparable friend, by decree of the decurions, because of his services to him.
EDCS-13301759.summary: This inscription records the grant of a burial place to Marcus Aurelius Priscus, a prominent military and administrative official, by a Roman knight named Marcus Iulius Eutyches, reflecting social relationships and honors in the Roman military and bureaucracy, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-13301764.translation: The judgment of Atleades, the judgment of a mad man.
EDCS-13301764.summary: This inscription is a short, possibly personal or critical, statement about someone named Atleades, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13301765.summary: This is a simple maker's inscription by a craftsman named Philiscus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13301766.translation: Marcus Aurelius Vo, the ship-owner, made [this].
EDCS-13301766.summary: This is a maker's inscription by a ship-owner named Marcus Aurelius Vo, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13301767.translation: For Quintus Aemilius Epitynchanus: Practicus and Chresimus, his fellow freedmen.
EDCS-13301767.summary: This is a funerary dedication by fellow freedmen for Quintus Aemilius Epitynchanus, indicating social relationships within the freedman class, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13301768.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Attia, the most holy woman, rests here; Encolupus and Antonilla, her heirs, [set this up] for their patroness.
EDCS-13301768.summary: This funerary inscription honors Attia, a woman of high status, and was erected by her heirs.

EDCS-13301769.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Caecilia Decumilla, aged 8 years. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-13301769.summary: This is a child's tombstone for Caecilia Decumilla, recording her age and a common epitaph.

EDCS-13301770.summary: This is a brief funerary marker, possibly a reminder of a mother's resting place.

EDCS-13301771.translation: Cornelia Faebianes, who lived 47 years and 6 months.
EDCS-13301771.summary: This inscription records the name and lifespan of Cornelia Faebianes.

EDCS-13301772.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Lucius Cornelius Quintio.
EDCS-13301772.summary: This is a simple funerary dedication to Lucius Cornelius Quintio.

EDCS-13301775.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Hermionenus, freedwoman, and for Julia Juliana, her most sweet nurse.
EDCS-13301775.summary: This funerary inscription honors two individuals: a freedwoman named Hermionenus and her nurse, Julia Juliana.

EDCS-13301776.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. He lives forever. Who first found the letters, lest I should not know who lay in this tomb. But the inscription speaks and does not know how to deceive. For Attius Mios Soproniscus. Pray, Eutycianus and Titus Junius Centurio and Perseus, to their most excellent friend.
EDCS-13301776.summary: This complex funerary inscription, possibly from the 2nd century AD, dedicates a tomb to Attius Mios Soproniscus, with an unusual preamble about the inscription itself and mentions multiple dedicators who were friends.

EDCS-13301777.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Caecilius Antiochus, most excellent friend. Antonius Olympiodorus placed this.
EDCS-13301777.summary: This funerary inscription records that Antonius Olympiodorus dedicated a monument to his excellent friend, Caecilius Antiochus.

EDCS-13301779.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Zosima, the very rare wife. Annius Achilleus to his dearest wife, 30 years.
EDCS-13301779.summary: This funerary inscription from an unknown date records Annius Achilleus dedicating a tomb to his wife Zosima, noting their 30 years of marriage.

EDCS-13301781.translation: Mara Secunda made this for herself while alive, and for Gnaeus Cornelius Maelo, and for Quintus Licinius, and for Lucius Licinius.
EDCS-13301781.summary: This is a funerary inscription commissioned during the lifetime of Mara Secunda, who made provision for herself and three other individuals.

EDCS-13301784.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For Pompeia Eutychis, who died at the age of nine years. Eutyches and Apollonia, her parents.
EDCS-13301784.summary: A funerary epitaph for a child, set up by her parents.

EDCS-13301785.translation: Here in peace rests Antonina of good memory, who lived for more or less 19 years and died on the fourth day before the Ides of January, when Probus the Younger was consul, in the third indiction.
EDCS-13301785.summary: A funerary epitaph for Antonina, recording her age, death date, and the consulship of Probus the Younger.

EDCS-13301787.translation: Here in peace rests Laurentius of good memory, who lived for more or less 14 years and died on the Kalends of February, in the sixth indiction.
EDCS-13301787.summary: A funerary epitaph for Laurentius, recording his age and death date.

EDCS-13301801.summary: An inscription dedicating a monument to Quintus Licinius Mento.

EDCS-13301802.summary: A woman's name and her father's name, likely an epitaph or a dedication.

EDCS-13301804.translation: Lucius Valerius Voco [dedicated this] to Silvanus.
EDCS-13301804.summary: A dedication to the god Silvanus by Lucius Valerius Voco.

EDCS-13301808.translation: Quintus Melius Voltinia Flavus [dedicated this] to his parents, Touto, son of Melius, and Maliccona, daughter of Mulius.
EDCS-13301808.summary: A funerary epitaph for Touto and Maliccona, set up by their son Quintus Melius Voltinia Flavus.

EDCS-13301809.translation: Boudilla, daughter of Vindos, made [this] for herself and for her son Dometius, son of Caranticcon, while alive.
EDCS-13301809.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Boudilla for herself and her son during her lifetime.

EDCS-13301810.summary: A dedication to a personal Genius by his slave Amphio.

EDCS-13301813.translation: Titus T. Optatus placed [this] for the god Mars.
EDCS-13301813.summary: A dedication to the god Mars by Titus T. Optatus.

EDCS-13301816.translation: To the god Silvanus, Exuperius, freedman of Caesar, willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-13301816.summary: This is a dedication to the god Silvanus by Exuperius, likely a freedman, who fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-13301822.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Flavia, daughter of Graecinus, wishing her well.

EDCS-13301823.translation: Here rests in peace, of good memory, Priscus, who lived approximately 46 years, died on the third day before the Ides of September, in the fourth indiction.
EDCS-13301823.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription recording the death of Priscus, including his approximate age and date of death.

EDCS-13301824.translation: Lucius Sennius Tertiolus, to his own relatives.
EDCS-13301824.summary: This is a dedication or memorial by Lucius Sennius Tertiolus to his relatives.

EDCS-13301826.translation: Sacred to the departed shades. Caecinia Euporia, who lived 36 years, 3 months, and 23 days, Gallius Marcellinus made for his well-deserving wife.
EDCS-13301826.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caecinia Euporia, dedicated by her husband Gallius Marcellinus.

EDCS-13301829.summary: This is a very short inscription, likely a name from a funerary monument or ownership mark.

EDCS-13301832.translation: On the Ides of April, Constantia died.
EDCS-13301832.summary: This inscription records the death of Constantia on the Ides of April.

EDCS-13301834.translation: To the goddess, Titus Petius, priest, 10 pounds.
EDCS-13301834.summary: This inscription records a dedication to a goddess by Titus Petius, who held a priestly office and possibly refers to a donation of 10 pounds.

EDCS-13301837.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Mario Ermiano, who lived for...
EDCS-13301837.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Mario Ermiano, with the text cut off before stating his lifespan.

EDCS-13301838.translation: To his incomparable wife, Terialia, Cresconius made this.
EDCS-13301838.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Cresconius to his beloved wife, Terialia.

EDCS-13301850.translation: To Mercury, Gaius Birrius Fuscus willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-13301850.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Mercury by Gaius Birrius Fuscus, who fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-13301851.translation: Sacred to Mercury. Seranus, willingly and deservedly, [fulfilled his vow].
EDCS-13301851.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Mercury by Seranus.

EDCS-13301852.summary: This is a dedication to Minerva, likely by Coelius.

EDCS-13301853.translation: Titus Atilius Felix, [having made] a vow to Proximus, [fulfilled it].
EDCS-13301853.summary: This is a votive inscription by Titus Atilius Felix to a deity named Proximus.

EDCS-13301854.translation: Gaius Cornelius Tarentinus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Proximus.
EDCS-13301854.summary: This is a votive inscription by Gaius Cornelius Tarentinus to Proximus.

EDCS-13301857.translation: Gaius Birrius Fuscus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Vasion.
EDCS-13301857.summary: This is a votive inscription by Gaius Birrius Fuscus to the deity Vasion.

EDCS-13301858.translation: Lucius Messius Rhodinus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Vasion.
EDCS-13301858.summary: This is a votive inscription by Lucius Messius Rhodinus to the deity Vasion.

EDCS-13301859.translation: The brothers M. V. [and?] Us Mansuetus fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-13301859.summary: This is a votive inscription by two brothers, identified by initials and the name Mansuetus.

EDCS-13301860.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription possibly dedicating something to a deified figure, perhaps Claudius.

EDCS-13301862.translation: The people of Vasio [dedicate this] to Lucius Messius, son of Vocontius.
EDCS-13301862.summary: This is a dedication by the people of Vasio to Lucius Messius, son of Vocontius.

EDCS-13301864.translation: Quintus Esmerius, aged 8 years, 2 months, and 10 days, to his dearest son.
EDCS-13301864.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Quintus Esmerius, who died at a young age, set up by his parents.

EDCS-13301865.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Valerius Severinus to his mother, Magia Auretilia.
EDCS-13301865.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Valerius Severinus to his mother, Magia Auretilia.

EDCS-13301866.translation: To Messia Alpina, daughter of Gaius Domitius Rufus, (honoring) Apronius Atilinus Iulianus.
EDCS-13301866.summary: This inscription honors Messia Alpina, daughter of Gaius Domitius Rufus, with a dedication to Apronius Atilinus Iulianus.

EDCS-13301867.translation: Lucius Minnius Nivatus and Tertius, his freedman, made (this) while alive for Sextus Minnius Parcus and Gaius Minnius Taurus.
EDCS-13301867.summary: This is a funerary monument made by Lucius Minnius Nivatus and his freedman Tertius for Sextus Minnius Parcus and Gaius Minnius Taurus.

EDCS-13301868.summary: This is a brief dedication to a mother by Pretenius.

EDCS-13301869.summary: This is a very fragmented inscription that seems to refer to a person named Molus.

EDCS-13301870.translation: Tiberius Iulius Valens and Tiberius Iulius Verus fulfilled their vow to Mars willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-13301870.summary: This is a votive inscription to Mars by Tiberius Iulius Valens and Tiberius Iulius Verus.

EDCS-13301873.translation: Siccius Secundus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mars Bruatus.
EDCS-13301873.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Mars Bruatus by Siccius Secundus.

EDCS-13301874.translation: Gaius Silonius Frequens willingly and deservedly (dedicated this) to Mars Nabelcus.
EDCS-13301874.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Mars Nabelcus by Gaius Silonius Frequens.

EDCS-13301875.translation: Lucius Coelius Apella, son of Lamo, slave of Gaius Coelius Catus.
EDCS-13301875.summary: This inscription likely marks the burial place or honors Lucius Coelius Apella, the son of Lamo and slave of Gaius Coelius Catus.

EDCS-13301876.translation: Pefirus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Silvanus.
EDCS-13301876.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Silvanus by Pefirus.

EDCS-13301877.translation: Publius Romanius Socrates willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the Goddess Victory.
EDCS-13301877.summary: This is a votive inscription to the Goddess Victory by Publius Romanius Socrates.

EDCS-13301879.translation: Calventius and Birro made this for their father and mother from their own peculium, sons of Silvanus.
EDCS-13301879.summary: This is a dedication by Calventius and Birro to their parents, made from their own peculium, with the sons identified as belonging to Silvanus.

EDCS-13301880.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Campanus, son of Cursus, made this from a will for himself, for Venimara, daughter of Mocianti, his mother, and for Certo, son of Cursus.
EDCS-13301880.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Campanus, son of Cursus, made from a will for himself, his mother Venimara, and Certo, son of Cursus.

EDCS-13301881.translation: Titus Iulius Titullus arranged for this to be made for Dometia, daughter of Capito.
EDCS-13301881.summary: This records that Titus Iulius Titullus commissioned a monument for Dometia, daughter of Capito.

EDCS-13301882.translation: Quintus Amiteius, the architect, made this.
EDCS-13301882.summary: This is a simple dedication by Quintus Amiteius, identified as an architect.

EDCS-13301884.translation: For the Great Mother of the Gods, for the health of Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, and Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, and [Publius Septimius Geta Caesar], and Julia Augusta, the public community of the Vocontii performed a taurobolium, with Talusius Appianus presiding publicly.
EDCS-13301884.summary: This inscription records a taurobolium, a ritual sacrifice, performed by the public community of the Vocontii for the health of the imperial family, including emperors Septimius Severus, Caracalla, and Geta, and empress Julia Domna.

EDCS-13301885.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Avita, daughter of Avitus, to her dearest son.
EDCS-13301885.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Avita, daughter of Avitus, to her son.

EDCS-13301886.translation: From Avitus, son of Servatus. Roudus, his wife Iulia Potiti, and his daughter Avita.
EDCS-13301886.summary: This inscription lists members of a family: Avitus, son of Servatus, his wife Iulia Potiti, and his daughter Avita.

EDCS-13301888.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Calvisia Secundilla made this monument while alive for her freedman Publius Calvisius Trophimus, and for herself.
EDCS-13301888.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Calvisia Secundilla, made during her lifetime for her freedman Publius Calvisius Trophimus and for herself.

EDCS-13301890.translation: Occius Eutyches to his wife Fortunatia, daughter of Veratius.
EDCS-13301890.summary: This is a dedication by Occius Eutyches to his wife Fortunatia, daughter of Veratius.

EDCS-13301893.translation: Messinus, a slave, to his dearest wife Gratiana, freedwoman of Maximinius, from the Vocontii.
EDCS-13301893.summary: This is a dedication by Messinus, a slave, to his wife Gratiana, a freedwoman of Maximinius, likely from the region of the Vocontii.

EDCS-13301894.translation: After Ernianus died, Victoria Maternus made this monument, not lasting because of its condition, and her daughter as heir by my command. I, Victoria Maternus, while alive, subscribed the place.
EDCS-13301894.summary: This is a funerary monument inscription by Victoria Maternus for her deceased husband Ernianus, acknowledging her heir and her own living subscription to the plot.

EDCS-13301895.translation: Carina, wife of Quintus Pompeius Filonius.
EDCS-13301895.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Carina, wife of Quintus Pompeius Filonius.

EDCS-13301897.translation: To the spirits of the underworld; the heirs of Repentina, daughter of Repentinus.
EDCS-13301897.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the spirits of the underworld by the heirs of Repentina.

EDCS-13301898.translation: To the spirits of the underworld; Decimus Romanius Silvester, heir, for Valeria, daughter of Valentinus.
EDCS-13301898.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the spirits of the underworld by Decimus Romanius Silvester for Valeria.

EDCS-13301903.translation: Felix, son of Smerus, willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Bagius and Baginatiabus.
EDCS-13301903.summary: This inscription records a vow paid by Felix, son of Smerus, to Bagius and Baginatiabus.

EDCS-13301905.translation: Sacred to the god Volcano; Valeria Sextia and Iccius Cration, by order.
EDCS-13301905.summary: This inscription is a sacred dedication to the god Volcano by Valeria Sextia and Iccius Cration.

EDCS-13301906.translation: To the spirits of the underworld; P. Heraclius dedicated to his most beloved wife, Iulia Marciana, under the axe.
EDCS-13301906.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by P. Heraclius to his wife Iulia Marciana, indicating a 'sub ascia' burial.

EDCS-13301907.translation: To the spirits of the underworld; her father made this for his most beloved daughter who lived 17 years, 8 months. [Text illegible].
EDCS-13301907.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by a father to his daughter, specifying her age at death.

EDCS-13301908.translation: Aulus Lampas made this for himself and his family while alive.
EDCS-13301908.summary: This is a dedication made by Aulus Lampas for himself and his family, indicating a living commission.

EDCS-13301909.translation: Niger, cellarius of Caius Satrius Silius of Anaria, willingly and deservedly paid his vow to the victorious mothers from his own property.
EDCS-13301909.summary: This inscription records a vow paid by Niger to the Matres Victrices (victorious mothers).

EDCS-13301910.summary: This is a dedication to the Matres Victrices (victorious mothers).

EDCS-13301912.translation: Niger dedicated [this] to the Victorious Mother.
EDCS-13301912.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Niger to the "Victorious Mother".

EDCS-13301914.summary: This inscription appears to be a simple name and filiation.

EDCS-13301915.translation: Niger, son of Caius Satrius, gives from his own property.
EDCS-13301915.summary: This inscription records a donation by Niger, son of Caius Satrius, from his personal funds.

EDCS-13301919.translation: Sextus Cabirius Iullinus of the Cautians.
EDCS-13301919.summary: This inscription appears to be a name and ethnic affiliation.

EDCS-13301920.translation: In this tomb rests in good peace Genesius, who lived for [X] years.
EDCS-13301920.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Genesius, providing his name and the duration of his life.

EDCS-13301921.translation: Here rests in good memory Constantinus, the subdeacon, whose burial was on the 4th day before the Nones of August, after the consulship of Justinus Augustus.
EDCS-13301921.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Constantinus, a subdeacon, with his burial date given relative to a consulship.

EDCS-13301932.translation: To the divine shades: Caius Iulius Calemerus and Valeria Domitia arranged for this to be set up for their most dutiful mother; Caius Iulius Hermes, freedman of the colony, [arranged this] for his most holy wife.
EDCS-13301932.summary: This funerary inscription records the erection of a monument by Caius Iulius Calemerus and Valeria Domitia for their mother, and also by Caius Iulius Hermes for his wife.

EDCS-13301933.translation: [3]E[3] of Lucius Cominius [3], their sons. Lucius Cominius Paulinus [dedicated this] to his most excellent parents and his most devoted brother.
EDCS-13301933.summary: This is a dedication by Lucius Cominius Paulinus to his parents and brother.

EDCS-13301934.translation: To Decimus Dannius Capito of the Voltinia tribe.
EDCS-13301934.summary: This is a dedication to Decimus Dannius Capito.

EDCS-13301935.translation: To the divine shades: Marcus Domitius Sequanus arranged for this to be set up for his most reverent and dutiful brother Tiberius Sabineus Ingenuus and for his dearest wife Vireia Vaena.
EDCS-13301935.summary: This funerary inscription records the erection of a monument by Marcus Domitius Sequanus for his brother and his wife.

EDCS-13301936.translation: His father [erected this] for Marcus Sextius Maternus, son of Marcus.
EDCS-13301936.summary: This inscription records a monument erected by a father for his son, Marcus Sextius Maternus.

EDCS-13301937.translation: To the divine shades, for eternal rest and perpetual security: Aulus Terentius Myrismus [erected this] for his very rare friend Marcus Valerius Hilario.
EDCS-13301937.summary: This funerary inscription records the erection of a monument by Aulus Terentius Myrismus for his friend Marcus Valerius Hilario.

EDCS-13301940.translation: To the blessed daughter of Optatus, Phorus and his sons, his sons.
EDCS-13301940.summary: This is a fragmented dedication possibly for a daughter of Optatus, mentioning dedicants Phorus and his sons, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13301944.summary: This is a fragmented funerary inscription, likely a dedication to Niceros, son of Caelus, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13301951.translation: To the divine, of Oanion, son of Iova.
EDCS-13301951.summary: This is a fragmented inscription, possibly a dedication to a deity or an individual named Oanion, son of Iova, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13301955.translation: Here rests in good memory in peace Peleger, who lived for III months and IIII days, died on the 3rd of the Nones of January, in the consulship of Avienus the Younger.
EDCS-13301955.summary: This is a tomb inscription recording the death and burial of Peleger, mentioning her longevity and the consul Avienus the Younger, likely from the Late Roman period.

EDCS-13301956.translation: In this tomb rests in good memory Ananthailda, a nun, to whom may the Lord grant eternal rest, always devoted to the poor, generous, died on the 8th of the Kalends of May, after the consulship of Venantius, to rise again in peace.
EDCS-13301956.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Ananthailda, a devout nun, specifying her death date and her charitable nature, likely from the Late Roman period.

EDCS-13301961.translation: Matrona, clever, simple, modest, formerly of noble parents, who lived for X years, died on the 6th of the Kalends of March, after the consulship of Opilio.
EDCS-13301961.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Matrona, noting her noble lineage, virtues, and lifespan, with a death date after the consulship of Opilio, likely from the Late Roman period.

EDCS-13301967.translation: Here rest the tender innocent limbs of Sanctus, holy in name, holy in innocence, of three years of age and months, whom blessed rest holds among the stars. Do not grieve, father and mother, nor cease weeping, the offspring has joys of eternal life. Died in peace on the 8th of the Ides of October, in the 14th indiction.
EDCS-13301967.summary: This is a tomb inscription for a young child named Sanctus, consoling his parents and noting his death date and peaceful afterlife, likely from the Late Roman period.

EDCS-13301968.translation: Here rests in peace the good-memoried Maurolenus, whom envious death snatched away, whose infancy was good, who lived for more or less 23 years, died on the Kalends of May, in the 3rd indiction, in the 3rd year of the reign of our lord Clother.
EDCS-13301968.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Maurolenus, a young man who died at approximately 23 years old, specifying the date and the reign of King Clother, likely from the Early Medieval period.

EDCS-13301972.translation: Here rests in peace the good-memoried Bonosa, a nun, and God-fearing, who lived for X years.
EDCS-13301972.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Bonosa, a devout nun, mentioning her piety and a partial lifespan, likely from the Late Roman or Early Medieval period.

EDCS-13301973.translation: Here rests in peace the good-memoried Eufemia, consecrated to God, adorned with every spiritual grace, who was first in charity, bright in virginity, piety in her 23rd year. Death took her away, but she found life because she loved the author of life alone on earth; with Him she is joined in heaven. Died in Christ, to rise again in glory. Burial on the Kalends of [March?].
EDCS-13301973.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Eufemia, a consecrated virgin and nun, detailing her virtues, death at 23, and her heavenly union, likely from the Late Roman or Early Medieval period.

EDCS-13301974.translation: Galla, devout woman, of good memory.
EDCS-13301974.summary: This inscription is a short epitaph for a pious woman named Galla, likely dating to the late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-13301975.translation: Here rests in peace Ingerosa, who lived more or less 50 years.
EDCS-13301975.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Ingerosa, who lived approximately 50 years, and dates to the early Christian period.

EDCS-13301976.translation: Here rests in peace Iovenales, who lived approximately 80 years and passed away on the fourth day before the Kalends of January.
EDCS-13301976.summary: This epitaph records the death of Iovenales, who lived about 80 years, and provides a specific date (likely in the 4th century AD) with consular dating elements.

EDCS-13301990.summary: This is a very brief inscription likely marking a burial, possibly of an individual named Boclar.

EDCS-13301998.translation: Caius Attius Atticus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Maia.
EDCS-13301998.summary: This dedication records Caius Attius Atticus fulfilling a vow made to the goddess Maia.

EDCS-13301999.translation: Here rests in peace, of good memory, Claudianus the presbyter, who lived 56 years and died on the 4th day before the Nonas of November, in the consulship of the most illustrious Rusticianus and Vitalianus.
EDCS-13301999.summary: This epitaph records the death of Claudianus, a presbyter, who lived 56 years, and provides a precise date in the early 6th century AD based on consular dating.

EDCS-13302002.translation: In this tomb rests in peace, of good memory, Sacrata, a handmaid of God devoted to God, a maiden, Populunia, in hope of resurrection and the mercy of Christ, who lived 25 years and died on the Ides of October, in the twelfth indiction.
EDCS-13302002.summary: This epitaph records the death of Populunia, a young consecrated servant of God, who lived 25 years and died in the early 6th century AD, based on the indiction and context.

EDCS-13302004.summary: This is a simple funerary marker indicating a tomb belonging to or associated with the Aveorum family.

EDCS-13302007.translation: Caius Virrius Quartio ordered this base to be set up by his will from the contributions.
EDCS-13302007.summary: This inscription records Caius Virrius Quartio's posthumous dedication of a base, funded by voluntary contributions, likely in honor of the Emperor Victoria Augustus.

EDCS-13302008.translation: Marcus Verrius Mansuetus, in his own name and that of his brother Manso, ordered this to be set up by his will to the divine will of Augustus.
EDCS-13302008.summary: This dedication records Marcus Verrius Mansuetus establishing a monument by his will to honor the numen (divine spirit) of Augustus, also on behalf of his brother.

EDCS-13302010.translation: Octavius Caesar Actius, having fulfilled his vow, approved the weight of 212 [pounds].
EDCS-13302010.summary: This inscription records the approval of a weight by Octavius Caesar Actius, likely related to a votive offering.

EDCS-13302016.translation: Aurelia Firmina, daughter of Marcus, ordered this to be set up by her will at Augusta of the Allobroges.
EDCS-13302016.summary: This inscription records Aurelia Firmina's posthumous dedication of a monument at Genava (modern Geneva), commissioned in her will.

EDCS-13302017.translation: Quintus Servilius Severus also dedicated a temple and porticoes in fulfillment of a vow to Maia.
EDCS-13302017.summary: This inscription records a votive dedication of a temple and porticoes by Quintus Servilius Severus to the goddess Maia.

EDCS-13302018.translation: To Mercury Augustus, Marcus and his son Linus, in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-13302018.summary: This inscription is a votive dedication to Mercury Augustus by Marcus and his son Linus.

EDCS-13302019.translation: Virilis paid what he had vowed, gladly and deservedly.
EDCS-13302019.summary: This inscription records Virilis fulfilling a vow he had made.

EDCS-13302020.translation: To Quintus Decius Alpinus, magistrate of the nauclarii (boatmen) of Lake Geneva.
EDCS-13302020.summary: This inscription honors Quintus Decius Alpinus, who served as a magistrate for the boatmen of Lake Geneva.

EDCS-13302021.translation: Titus Nonnius Ianuarius, twice aedile, gave these at his own expense.
EDCS-13302021.summary: This inscription records a donation by Titus Nonnius Ianuarius, who served as aedile twice, using his own funds.

EDCS-13302023.translation: To the Divine Manes. Urittii Graecus and Rusticus arranged for this to be made for their excellent father, Coius Astutus.
EDCS-13302023.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording Urittii Graecus and Rusticus dedicating a monument to their father, Coius Astutus.

EDCS-13302025.translation: Caius Labienus Bassus dedicated this to his daughter, Labiena Montica, Flaminica Augustalis, daughter of Caius, by the father of the daughter. The site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-13302025.summary: This inscription records Caius Labienus Bassus dedicating a monument and burial plot to his daughter, Labiena Montica, who held the priesthood of the Augustales, with the space granted by local officials.

EDCS-13302029.translation: To Servilia Sabina, [from] Catia Sabinula, her dearest mother.
EDCS-13302029.summary: This inscription is a dedication from Catia Sabinula to her mother, Servilia Sabina.

EDCS-13302030.translation: To the Divine Spirits and to his own memory, Marcus Veratius Macrinus [dedicated this] to his dearest wife.
EDCS-13302030.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Marcus Veratius Macrinus to his wife Severa.

EDCS-13302031.summary: This is a funerary dedication, likely a continuation of EDCS-13302030, to a daughter named Sevva Verecunda.

EDCS-13302033.translation: Lucius Valerius Tertius established and consecrated this place to Jupiter Best and Greatest.
EDCS-13302033.summary: This inscription records the establishment and consecration of a place to Jupiter by Lucius Valerius Tertius.

EDCS-13302035.translation: Albanus, a public slave, lived 40 years.
EDCS-13302035.summary: This is a brief epitaph recording the name, status, and age at death of Albanus.

EDCS-13302037.translation: To the Divine Spirits, Atius Amoenus and Connia Honorata [dedicated this] to their most dutiful daughter, Connia Amatia.
EDCS-13302037.summary: This is a funerary dedication by parents Atius Amoenus and Connia Honorata to their daughter Connia Amatia.

EDCS-13302042.translation: Lucius Granius Optatus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Apollo.
EDCS-13302042.summary: This is a votive inscription by Lucius Granius Optatus to Apollo.

EDCS-13302043.translation: To the Divine Spirits, [dedicated by her] mother to her most dutiful daughter Quintilla.
EDCS-13302043.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a mother to her daughter Quintilla.

EDCS-13302045.translation: Gellius [made this] to Jupiter, in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-13302045.summary: This is a votive inscription by Gellius to Jupiter.

EDCS-13302047.summary: This is a dedication by Eppia Iullina to the goddess Minerva.

EDCS-13302048.translation: To the Divine Spirits, Antonia Primigenia, freedwoman. To the Divine Spirits, Optatus, freedman of Antonius Aescunus.
EDCS-13302048.summary: This inscription records two separate funerary dedications by freedpersons, Antonia Primigenia and Optatus.

EDCS-13302049.summary: This is a dedication to Quartio Uppiritus, likely an individual or a deity, with no further context provided.

EDCS-13302050.translation: To the Divine Shades. Marcus Valerius Pudens, father, to his most devoted son, Marcus Valerius Marcellinus.
EDCS-13302050.summary: This funerary inscription records a father's dedication to his deceased son, Marcus Valerius Marcellinus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13302051.translation: To the Divine Shades of Lucius Valerius Optatus.
EDCS-13302051.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Lucius Valerius Optatus, typical of Roman burial contexts from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13302054.translation: Tertius, son of Tincoris, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Segomannus.
EDCS-13302054.summary: This inscription records Tertius, son of Tincoris, fulfilling a vow to Segomannus, suggesting a votive offering potentially in a Romano-Celtic context.

EDCS-13302055.translation: Gaius Baebius Felix willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mars Magius.
EDCS-13302055.summary: This inscription records Gaius Baebius Felix fulfilling a vow to the god Mars Magius, indicating a votive offering.

EDCS-13302056.translation: To the Divine Shades of Carantius Valentinus.
EDCS-13302056.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Carantius Valentinus, common in Roman burial inscriptions from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13302057.translation: To the Divine Shades of Titus Solius, son of Dumnia, of Privatus.
EDCS-13302057.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Titus Solius, son of Dumnia and Privatus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-13302058.translation: The guild of carpenters of Nemausus, to Porcius Filetus.
EDCS-13302058.summary: This inscription records a dedication from the guild of carpenters of Nemausus to Porcius Filetus, likely a patron or honored member.

EDCS-13302059.translation: To the Divine Shades. Tyche, wife of Quintus Anicius Verecundus.
EDCS-13302059.summary: This funerary inscription records Tyche, the wife of Quintus Anicius Verecundus, dedicated to the deceased.

EDCS-13302061.translation: To the Divine Shades of Tertia, daughter of Kallos.
EDCS-13302061.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Tertia, daughter of Kallos, typical of Roman burial inscriptions from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13302062.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Primi, son of Maxsimus.

EDCS-13302063.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Primae, daughter of Atullus.

EDCS-13302065.translation: To the Genius of Lucius Licinius Prophetes, by Pinite, freedwoman, and Pannychis, slave.
EDCS-13302065.summary: This is a dedication to the Genius of Lucius Licinius Prophetes, made by his freedwoman and slave.

EDCS-13302067.translation: Lais Lucretia willingly and deservedly paid her vow to Mercury the Displacer.
EDCS-13302067.summary: This is a votive inscription to Mercury, dedicated by Lais Lucretia.

EDCS-13302069.translation: Ianuaria for her own people, aged 18.
EDCS-13302069.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age of Ianuaria.

EDCS-13302070.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Restitutus and his family.

EDCS-13302071.translation: Viria Agathe for her own people.
EDCS-13302071.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Viria Agathe and her family.

EDCS-13302074.summary: This is a dedication of a sacred offering by Lucius Valerius Karus.

EDCS-13302076.translation: Marcus Agrippa, son of Lucius, consul for the third time, imperator, with tribunician power for the third time, gives to the colony of Augusta Nemauso.
EDCS-13302076.summary: This inscription records a gift by Marcus Agrippa to the colony of Augusta Nemauso, likely from the late 1st century BCE.

EDCS-13302083.translation: To Annius Rusticus, member of the board of four for the treasury, pontiff, and prefect of the watch and armories.
EDCS-13302083.summary: This is a dedication, possibly honorary, to Annius Rusticus, who held several important public offices, likely from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-13302086.translation: To Servilius Excingomarus, quaestor of the colony.
EDCS-13302086.summary: This inscription honors Servilius Excingomarus, the quaestor of a colony, likely on a public monument.

EDCS-13302088.translation: To the Divine Manes of Sextus Iccius Cosmicus, high priest of the synod.
EDCS-13302088.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Sextus Iccius Cosmicus, identified as a high priest of a synod.

EDCS-13302089.translation: To the Divine Manes of Terentia Marcella, daughter of Marcus, Augustan priestess of the colony of Narbo; by decree of the colony of Nemausus, the public granted the place of burial for her funeral and erected a statue at public expense.
EDCS-13302089.summary: This funerary inscription records a public grant of burial space and a statue for Terentia Marcella, an Augustan priestess in Narbonne, by the colony of Nemausus.

EDCS-13302090.translation: To the Divine Manes of Gaius Julius Chrysio, a member of the IIII viri Augustales, the corporati; by his heirs.
EDCS-13302090.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Gaius Julius Chrysio, a member of the IIII viri Augustales, by his heirs.

EDCS-13302092.translation: To the Divine Manes of Gaius Terentius Atticus, physician; erected by himself during his lifetime with his own money.
EDCS-13302092.summary: This funerary inscription is a self-funded dedication by Gaius Terentius Atticus, a physician.

EDCS-13302093.translation: Thraex Ametystus in the ludus [school/training ground] [XXI] In AtaiEX.
EDCS-13302093.summary: This inscription likely records the gladiator Thraex Ametystus and potentially his record or location within a gladiatorial school.

EDCS-13302094.translation: Calistus, the murmillo, [won] XX [bouts]; his associate erected [this].
EDCS-13302094.summary: This inscription commemorates the gladiator Calistus, a murmillo, who won twenty bouts, and was set up by his associate.

EDCS-13302095.translation: Thraex Orpheus, is buried here; Julia Fusca placed [this] for her well-deserving companion.
EDCS-13302095.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of the gladiator Orpheus, a Thraex, dedicated by Julia Fusca to her companion.

EDCS-13302096.translation: Urso of Lugdunum, the murmillo contraretiarius, [won] XIIII [bouts]; Cascellius, his associate, [erected this].
EDCS-13302096.summary: This inscription records the gladiator Ursio of Lugdunum, a murmillo contraretiarius, who won fourteen bouts, and was set up by his associate Cascellius.

EDCS-13302098.translation: To the Divine Manes of Abudia Phlegusa; [dedicated by] Gellius, her freedman.
EDCS-13302098.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Abudia Phlegusa, dedicated by her freedman Gellius.

EDCS-13302099.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Sextus Adcenno Solimarus.

EDCS-13302100.translation: Sextus Aemilius Flamma to his father, Sant, and mother, Rigo, and brother, Quintus.
EDCS-13302100.summary: This funerary inscription records Sextus Aemilius Flamma dedicating a monument to his parents and brother.

EDCS-13302101.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Marcus Aponius Laetus.

EDCS-13302102.translation: To the Divine Manes of Attia Philenis, their most excellent patroness, her heirs have set this up.
EDCS-13302102.summary: This funerary inscription records heirs setting up a monument to their patroness, Attia Philenis.

EDCS-13302103.translation: To the Divine Manes of Quintus Aurelius Abascantus.
EDCS-13302103.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Quintus Aurelius Abascantus.

EDCS-13302104.translation: To the Divine Manes of Auxesis.
EDCS-13302104.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Auxesis.

EDCS-13302105.translation: To Baebius Draco, by Thais Alleticciae, his freedwoman, for herself and her husband.
EDCS-13302105.summary: This funerary inscription records Thais Alleticciae, a freedwoman, setting up a monument for her husband, Baebius Draco, and herself.

EDCS-13302107.translation: Gaius Caesius Rufus, Juventia, daughter of Publius, Pipia.
EDCS-13302107.summary: This inscription likely records the names of Gaius Caesius Rufus and Juventia, daughter of Publius, also known as Pipia, possibly in a funerary context.

EDCS-13302109.translation: To the Manes of Calybis of Julianus, by Repentinus and Nymphe, fellow slaves.
EDCS-13302109.summary: This funerary inscription records fellow slaves Repentinus and Nymphe setting up a monument to Calybis of Julianus.

EDCS-13302110.translation: Carisia, daughter of Lucius Servata, ordered this to be made for herself and her husband, Gaius Terentius, by her will.
EDCS-13302110.summary: This inscription records Carisia Servata, through her will, ordering a monument to be made for herself and her husband, Gaius Terentius.

EDCS-13302111.translation: To Catulla, his wife, Catullus [erected this] to his parents.
EDCS-13302111.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by Catullus to his wife and parents.

EDCS-13302112.translation: Caius Chrysius, Philargus, freedman of Caius, sends greetings to you also.
EDCS-13302112.summary: This is a funerary greeting inscription from a freedman, Philargus, to an unknown recipient.

EDCS-13302113.translation: To the shades of Quinti Cirrati Secundini.
EDCS-13302113.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Quinti Cirrati Secundini.

EDCS-13302114.translation: To the shades of Cominia Successa. V.
EDCS-13302114.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Cominia Successa.

EDCS-13302115.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription likely mentioning Marcus Connius Optatus and his lineage.

EDCS-13302116.translation: To the shades of Titi Corneli Cerialis.
EDCS-13302116.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Titi Corneli Cerialis.

EDCS-13302117.translation: To the shades of Aulus Cornelius Euhodus. Cornelia, his wife, [dedicated this].
EDCS-13302117.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Aulus Cornelius Euhodus by his wife Cornelia.

EDCS-13302118.translation: To Cornelius Niger, to his wife Cornelia. Cornelius Nigrinus, son. Cornelius Capito, son.
EDCS-13302118.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by two sons, Cornelius Nigrinus and Cornelius Capito, to their father Cornelius Niger and mother Cornelia.

EDCS-13302119.translation: To the shades of Publius Cornelius Valerianus. Aelius Cornelius Hermes to his most dutiful son.
EDCS-13302119.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Aelius Cornelius Hermes to his son, Publius Cornelius Valerianus.

EDCS-13302120.translation: To the shades of Decumia, daughter of Titus, named Titulla.
EDCS-13302120.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Decumia Titulla, daughter of Titus.

EDCS-13302121.translation: To Domitius Catilo Segomarus, freedman of Cassius.
EDCS-13302121.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Domitius Catilo Segomarus, a freedman.

EDCS-13302122.translation: To the Divine Manes. Faventina and Avitus, children of Festus Faventinus, and Sabinus, son of Silvinus, to their most devoted parents; and to their most pious brother.
EDCS-13302122.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by children and a sibling to their deceased parents and brother.

EDCS-13302123.translation: To the Divine Manes. Lucius Iulius Trophimus to his comrade.
EDCS-13302123.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Lucius Iulius Trophimus to his comrade.

EDCS-13302124.translation: To the Divine Manes. Caius Fulvius Ceniter to his brother, Caius Fulvius Maior.
EDCS-13302124.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Caius Fulvius Ceniter to his brother, Caius Fulvius Maior.

EDCS-13302126.translation: To the Divine Manes. Aelia Amabilis and Marcus to their brother Gratius Gratinus.
EDCS-13302126.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Aelia Amabilis and Marcus to their brother, Gratius Gratinus.

EDCS-13302127.translation: Gaius Iulius Onesimus and Gaius Iulius Aurelius Iulianus, the heirs, made this for the most devoted Julia Aprulla, and set it up for themselves and their families while alive.
EDCS-13302127.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by heirs to Julia Aprulla, and also intended for the erectors and their families.

EDCS-13302128.translation: To Caius Iulius Dionysias, freedman of Sandyce.
EDCS-13302128.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Caius Iulius Dionysias, a freedman.

EDCS-13302130.translation: To Julia C. Gaius Iulius Cu. Gaius Iulius G. Secu, most devoted.
EDCS-13302130.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Julia C. and Gaius Iulius Cu. Gaius Iulius G. Secu, likely for their devotion.

EDCS-13302132.translation: Marcus Iulius Onesimus set this up for his most rare wife.
EDCS-13302132.summary: This funerary inscription records Marcus Iulius Onesimus setting up a monument for his wife.

EDCS-13302133.translation: To the Divine Manes. Vettonianus Crysis and Sergianus the patron to Marcus Iulius Severinus.
EDCS-13302133.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication by Vettonianus Crysis and his patron Sergianus to Marcus Iulius Severinus.

EDCS-13302134.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Iulia Crysis to her most dutiful husband, Marcus Julius Vethonianus.
EDCS-13302134.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by Iulia Crysis to her husband, Marcus Julius Vethonianus.

EDCS-13302135.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Cerialis to his wife, Iulia Pannychis.
EDCS-13302135.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by Cerialis to his wife, Iulia Pannychis.

EDCS-13302136.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Lutatia.

EDCS-13302137.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Plutia Primigenia placed this for her husband, Quintus Marius Severus, and for herself while alive.
EDCS-13302137.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Plutia Primigenia for herself and her husband, Quintus Marius Severus, likely in the Imperial period.

EDCS-13302138.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Tasgia Titulla placed this for Messina, daughter of Messinus.
EDCS-13302138.summary: A funerary epitaph erected by Tasgia Titulla for Messia, daughter of Messinus.

EDCS-13302141.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Priscus to his most dutiful brother, Paullus Pacatus, son of Paullus, and to his wife, Valentia, daughter of Verina.
EDCS-13302141.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by Priscus to his brother, Paullus Pacatus, and his wife, Valentia.

EDCS-13302144.translation: Secunda Pompeia dedicates this to her Pompeia Cantharis while alive.
EDCS-13302144.summary: An epitaph set up by Secunda Pompeia for Pompeia Cantharis, indicating it was prepared during the lifetime of the deceased.

EDCS-13302145.summary: A funerary epitaph honoring Primullia as a devoted mother.

EDCS-13302147.translation: For Quintus Satrius Aster and his sons, the Ianuaris.
EDCS-13302147.summary: An epitaph intended for Quintus Satrius Aster and his sons, possibly a family tomb inscription.

EDCS-13302148.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Serana, daughter of Seranus, son of Laticcius.
EDCS-13302148.summary: A funerary epitaph for Serana, daughter of Seranus Laticcius.

EDCS-13302149.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Setuleia Ga, of Caius Pacius Stephanus.
EDCS-13302149.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication to the departed spirits for Setuleia Ga, likely by her husband Caius Pacius Stephanus.

EDCS-13302150.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Severus, son of Quintus, father, and for Pompeia Virilis, daughter, mother.
EDCS-13302150.summary: This funerary inscription dedicates the monument to the spirits of the departed, honoring Severus (father) and Pompeia Virilis (mother).

EDCS-13302151.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Serania Severa, mother, for her most dutiful son Severus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-13302151.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Serania Severa to her devoted son, Severus, son of Lucius.

EDCS-13302152.translation: For Severa, daughter of Silvinus, and for Valentina, daughter of Vennius. Silvinus, son of Septumius, to his most dutiful daughter and best wife.
EDCS-13302152.summary: This funerary inscription is set up by Silvinus, son of Septumius, to honor his daughter Severa and his wife Valentina.

EDCS-13302153.summary: This brief inscription records the name Sextus, son of Paetus, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-13302154.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Erotis, of Quintus Tacitus, who lived 11 years and 11 months. To Quintus Tacitius Annianus, his most fortunate pupil.
EDCS-13302154.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the memory of Erotis, a pupil of Quintus Tacitius Annianus, who died at the age of 11 years and 11 months.

EDCS-13302155.translation: Terentia Irene, freedwoman of Maximi, made this for herself and for her daughter Cara, while alive, in her own burial plot.
EDCS-13302155.summary: This funerary inscription is a self-dedication made by Terentia Irene, freedwoman of Maximi, for herself and her daughter Cara.

EDCS-13302156.translation: Teucidia, daughter of Lucius Sabinus, is buried here. She lived 25 years.
EDCS-13302156.summary: This inscription records the burial and lifespan of Teucidia, daughter of Lucius Sabinus.

EDCS-13302158.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Valeria Hellas. Gaius Valerius Cosmus, to his most dutiful mother.
EDCS-13302158.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Gaius Valerius Cosmus to his mother, Valeria Hellas.

EDCS-13302159.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Valeria Nigrina. Valerius Nigrinus and her mother Severina, to their most dutiful daughter and to themselves, most deserving.
EDCS-13302159.summary: This funerary inscription is set up by Valerius Nigrinus and Severina, the parents, for their daughter Valeria Nigrina and for themselves.

EDCS-13302160.translation: For Gaius Venius Serre and his wife Annita Exorata, and for Gratula, their freedwoman.
EDCS-13302160.summary: This inscription is a dedication, likely funerary, to Gaius Venius Serre, his wife Annita Exorata, and their freedwoman Gratula.

EDCS-13302161.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Vetulia Amabilis. By Crescens, her companion.
EDCS-13302161.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Vetulia Amabilis by her companion Crescens.

EDCS-13302162.summary: This inscription records the age of a person named Victor.

EDCS-13302181.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Sextia.
EDCS-13302181.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Sextia.

EDCS-13302185.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or perhaps a funerary mention related to 'Aspiration' and Martial, possibly by Iulia.

EDCS-13302190.translation: Vegeta willingly and deservedly paid her vow to Minerva.
EDCS-13302190.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made by Vegeta to the goddess Minerva.

EDCS-13302192.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Masclus, son of Cornelius Capito, and for Iulia Verula, daughter of Quintus. By Cornelia Avita, daughter of Masclus, for her parents.
EDCS-13302192.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Cornelia Avita to her parents Masclus and Iulia Verula.

EDCS-13302193.translation: Gaius L. H. willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.
EDCS-13302193.summary: This inscription records Gaius L. H. paying a votive offering to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.

EDCS-13302194.translation: For Jupiter and Silvanus. Gaius Octavius Pedo.
EDCS-13302194.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Gaius Octavius Pedo to the gods Jupiter and Silvanus.

EDCS-13302195.translation: To our Genius. Primigenius, his freedman.
EDCS-13302195.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Genius of an unnamed person, made by his freedman Primigenius.

EDCS-13302199.translation: To Frequens, son of Messius, and Marcellus, son of Martius, and Servata, daughter of Frequens, from her parents.
EDCS-13302199.summary: This inscription is a dedication made by parents to their children, Frequens, Marcellus, and Servata.

EDCS-13302200.translation: To the divine spirits of Quintus Fronto, son of Quintus, of the Voltinian tribe, former official of the four, judge, priest, prefect of the watch, and armourer, and to his wife, Craxia Secundina, from Craxia Secundina to her excellent husband.
EDCS-13302200.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Craxia Secundina to her husband, Quintus Fronto, who held several important public and military offices.

EDCS-13302202.translation: To the divine spirits of Hortensia Phillis, by Atilia Homonea.
EDCS-13302202.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Hortensia Phillis by Atilia Homonea.

EDCS-13302203.translation: To the divine spirits of Titus Julius Festus, from his mother Dubitata and his sister Iulia Valeria.
EDCS-13302203.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Titus Julius Festus by his mother and sister.

EDCS-13302204.translation: To the divine spirits of Cnaeus Lucretius Euctemon, placed here at her own expense by Primula Licinilla.
EDCS-13302204.summary: This funerary dedication for Cnaeus Lucretius Euctemon was set up by Primula Licinilla.

EDCS-13302205.translation: To the divine spirits of Quintus Messius Severus, from his brother Messius Seranus.
EDCS-13302205.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Quintus Messius Severus by his brother, Messius Seranus.

EDCS-13302206.translation: To the divine spirits of Marcus Rec Paternus, from Caius Pat[---].
EDCS-13302206.summary: This is a partial funerary dedication to Marcus Rec Paternus by Caius Pat[---].

EDCS-13302207.translation: To the divine spirits of Saedius Communis and Crispia Euc[---], from Crispius Primu[---].
EDCS-13302207.summary: This is a partial funerary dedication to Saedius Communis and Crispia Euc[---] by Crispius Primu[---].

EDCS-13302209.translation: To Seranus, son of Quintus, of the Voltinian tribe.
EDCS-13302209.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Seranus, son of Quintus, likely a funerary monument.

EDCS-13302210.translation: To Servatus, son of Sabinus, and to Primula, daughter of Quintus.
EDCS-13302210.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Servatus and Primula, likely a funerary monument.

EDCS-13302211.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Bouda, sister of Marcus Servilius Secundus, made this at her own expense.
EDCS-13302211.summary: A funerary dedication by a sister for her deceased brother, Marcus Servilius Secundus.

EDCS-13302212.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Gaius Cestius Apelles, to his most devoted wife Servilia Messina, his sister, his mother Albina, and his brother Messorius.
EDCS-13302212.summary: A funerary dedication by Gaius Cestius Apelles to his wife, sister, mother, and brother.

EDCS-13302213.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Tertius. His mother Secundina.
EDCS-13302213.summary: A funerary dedication by a mother, Secundina, for her son, Tertius.

EDCS-13302216.translation: Titus Vossaticius Vinitor made this for himself and his wife Dubia Senilis, while alive.
EDCS-13302216.summary: A funerary monument erected by Titus Vossaticius Vinitor for himself and his wife during their lifetime.

EDCS-13302218.translation: In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Here rests Ranilo, servant of God, who died the day before the Nones of January. May she live in Christ. Amen.
EDCS-13302218.summary: A Christian funerary inscription recording the death of Ranilo, a servant of God, on January 4th.

EDCS-13302220.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Cornelia Tertulla, mother of Annius Annianus.
EDCS-13302220.summary: A funerary dedication by Cornelia Tertulla for her deceased son, Annius Annianus.

EDCS-13302221.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Publius Caecilius, son of Publius, aged 4 years and 5 months, and to Viricia Samnagensis, his most beloved.
EDCS-13302221.summary: A funerary inscription for a young boy, Publius Caecilius, and Viricia Samnagensis, possibly his mother or another close relative.

EDCS-13302222.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Titia Cominia, to her most devoted father Titus Cominius Valerianus.
EDCS-13302222.summary: A funerary dedication by Titia Cominia to her father, Titus Cominius Valerianus.

EDCS-13302223.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Cai Cluvi Silani Cluvia Sina Cai liberta coniugi kariss<i=E>mo viva posuit \n
EDCS-13302223.translation: To the departed shades. Cluvia Sina, freedwoman of Caius, placed this for her most beloved husband, Caius Cluvius Silanus, while she was alive.
EDCS-13302223.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Cluvius Silanus, dedicated by his wife Cluvia Sina.

EDCS-13302224.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Domitia Amabilis, freedwoman of Publius, her most indulgent patroness Domitia Fortunata.
EDCS-13302224.summary: A funerary dedication by the freedwoman Domitia Amabilis to her patroness Domitia Fortunata.

EDCS-13302225.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Gravata, daughter of Gallicus. Camulatia, daughter of Quintus, Pa...
EDCS-13302225.summary: A funerary dedication possibly by Camulatia, daughter of Quintus, to Gravata, daughter of Gallicus.

EDCS-13302226.translation: To the Divine Shades. Gaius Julius Firminus. Titus Tavius.
EDCS-13302226.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Gaius Julius Firminus by Titus Tavius.

EDCS-13302227.translation: To the Divine Shades. Of Titus Paternus Martinus. Licinia and Valerianus.
EDCS-13302227.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Titus Paternus Martinus by Licinia and Valerianus.

EDCS-13302228.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary dedication to Severus, son of Marcius.

EDCS-13302230.translation: Titus Romanius made this while alive.
EDCS-13302230.summary: This inscription records Titus Romanius making something during his lifetime.

EDCS-13302232.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription that mentions years and possibly a name, likely funerary.

EDCS-13302234.translation: To Lucius Aponius, cavalry prefect, tribune of soldiers of the Seventh Legion and the Twenty-second Legion, camp prefect, first Augustan priest of the city of Julia Baeterra, prefect, holding the office of duumvir for the second time, for Caius Caesar, son of Augustus, for his father, the Augustan priest of the city of Julia Baeterrensium, Cornelia Tertulla, for her pious father.
EDCS-13302234.summary: This is a dedication honoring Lucius Aponius for his numerous civic and military roles, likely a public monument from Julia Baeterra.

EDCS-13302235.translation: Gaius Gresius Domitus, son of Lucius, of the Pupinia tribe, quaestor of the colony of the city of Iulia Baeterris, aedile, prefect, holding the office of duumvir for the second time, flamen, for himself and for his father Lucius Gresius Domitus, son of Titus, of the Pupinia tribe, and for his mother Faltonia Maximilla, daughter of Faltonia, and for his wife Gresia, daughter of Gaius, and for his most pious daughter Priscilla, he ordered this to be made by his will, under the supervision of Gaius Gresius.
EDCS-13302235.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaius Gresius Domitus and his family, detailing his career and the construction of the monument by his will, from Iulia Baeterra.

EDCS-13302236.translation: [3] and for Publius Iulius, son of Publius, of the Pupinia tribe, [3] a quinquennial official, and for Publius Iulius Firmus, son of Publius, [3] his brother.
EDCS-13302236.summary: This fragmented inscription appears to record dedications or mentions related to members of the Iulius family, including a quinquennial official.

EDCS-13302237.translation: Gaius Cassius Venustus, master of the guild of pavement makers, gives a marble floor and two feet on the walls, at his own expense.
EDCS-13302237.summary: This is a dedication by Gaius Cassius Venustus, master of a trade guild, recording a donation of building materials.

EDCS-13302239.translation: To Calidia Aucta, freedwoman of Publius Calidius, mother of Calidia Felix, freedwoman of Publius Calidius; to Gaius Iulius Bassus, freedman; by the heirs according to the will.
EDCS-13302239.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by the heirs of several individuals, including freedmen and freedwomen, according to a will.

EDCS-13302240.translation: To the departed shades. To Zozimes, freedwoman of Caius, [his?] wife, most beloved.
EDCS-13302240.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Zozimes, possibly the wife of the person who erected the monument.

EDCS-13302241.translation: Iunius Quintus, son of Iunius, Quintus Iunius, son of Quintus Iunius.
EDCS-13302241.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription recording a lineage, likely a tombstone.

EDCS-13302244.translation: To Auctus, father, son of Publicius; to [3]llus, servant of Lucius Martius; who died aged 11.
EDCS-13302244.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for Auctus and a servant named [3]llus, likely from the early imperial period.

EDCS-13302249.translation: To Aponius Chereas, son of Lucius, of the Papiria tribe, augur, quaestor of Narbo Martius, honored with the ornaments of an aedile; for which service he endowed the public treasury of Narbo with 150,000 sesterces. Also honored with the ornaments of an aedile, duovir, and flamen, and augur in Sicily, in the Thermis of Syracuse, and in Panormus. Honored with the ornaments of an aedile, duovir, and flamen, and augur. Aponius Blastus, to his excellent patron. A place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-13302249.summary: This is a dedication honoring Aponius Chereas, a prominent citizen of Narbo, who was also honored for his public services in Sicily, and includes a grant of land by the local senate.

EDCS-13302250.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Gaius AI, likely by an associate.

EDCS-13302251.text_edition: \n naviculario Cornelius Panegyricus et Cornelius Chryseros amico optimo\n
EDCS-13302251.translation: Cornelius Panegyricus, a shipowner, and Cornelius Chryseros, to their excellent friend.
EDCS-13302251.summary: This is a funerary dedication from two shipowners to their friend.

EDCS-13302253.translation: Lived: Titus Felix, freedman of Titus, holder of the quaestorship four times, Augustalis.
EDCS-13302253.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Titus Felix, who held multiple civic and religious offices.

EDCS-13302255.translation: To the Augustal priests, 33 sesterces. Syntrophus, father. Birthday (celebrated) with whom wealth.
EDCS-13302255.summary: This inscription records a payment of 33 sesterces to the Augustal priests, possibly related to a birthday celebration, with Syntrophus identified as the father.

EDCS-13302257.translation: Lived: Titus Attius Quartus, stonemason. 15 feet in all directions.
EDCS-13302257.summary: This tombstone marks the burial plot of Titus Attius Quartus, a stonemason, specifying the dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-13302258.translation: While alive, Quintus Aurelius Exsoratus made (this) for himself and for his wife Veratia, who had died. Gaius Aurelius and Lucius Aurelius Cupitus.
EDCS-13302258.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Quintus Aurelius Exsoratus for himself and his deceased wife, with Gaius Aurelius and Lucius Aurelius Cupitus also mentioned.

EDCS-13302259.translation: To the Divine Spirits of Auruncaea Umidia.
EDCS-13302259.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the deified spirit of Auruncaea Umidia.

EDCS-13302260.translation: Marcus Careieus, freedman of Marcus, a baker, made (this) while alive for himself and for Careia Nigella and for Careia Tertia, daughter of Marcus, aged VI. The mother, with her child, lies here, struck by a pitiable fate, whom purity and unity brought to the ashes together.
EDCS-13302260.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Careieus, a baker, and his daughter Careia Tertia, made by himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-13302261.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Coelia Chrysis made (this) for her most beloved son, Mago. Mangon, grandfather.
EDCS-13302261.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Coelia Chrysis to her son Mago, with Mago's grandfather also mentioned.

EDCS-13302263.text_edition: \n Marco Fabio MMMarcorum liberto GI mercatori Cordubensi \n
EDCS-13302263.translation: To Marcus Fabius, freedman of M. Marcus, merchant of Corduba.
EDCS-13302263.summary: This is a dedication to Marcus Fabius, a freedman and merchant from Corduba.

EDCS-13302264.translation: For Fadia Domestica, 18 feet in front.
EDCS-13302264.summary: This inscription indicates the funerary plot size for Fadia Domestica.

EDCS-13302265.text_edition: \n Vivus Quintus Flavius Quinti libertus Primus lardarius [] []\n
EDCS-13302265.translation: Alive: Quintus Flavius Primus, freedman of Quintus, pork butcher.
EDCS-13302265.summary: This inscription indicates that Quintus Flavius Primus, a pork butcher, made his own tomb in advance.

EDCS-13302266.translation: For Quintus Julius Rufus, son of Quintus, who lived 24 years. Iulia Primigenia, mother, and Gaius Valerius Crescens, for their most dutiful son and for themselves.
EDCS-13302266.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Julius Rufus, set up by his mother Iulia Primigenia and Gaius Valerius Crescens.

EDCS-13302267.translation: Lucius Crypianus, freedman, made (this) for his altars and for Iulia Stacte, freedwoman, and for Aegle.
EDCS-13302267.summary: This inscription records the construction of altars by Lucius Crypianus, a freedman, for himself, his freedwoman Iulia Stacte, and Aegle.

EDCS-13302268.translation: Sextus Karius Rufus, son of Marcus, a retiarius, while alive. Sextus Karius Felix, freedman of Sextus, a retiarius, 15 feet in every direction.
EDCS-13302268.summary: This funerary epitaph for Sextus Karius Rufus, a retiarius, was made by himself and his freedman Sextus Karius Felix, also a retiarius.

EDCS-13302269.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Claudia Marcella made this in memory of her most dutiful son, who lived 35 years, 4 months, and 8 days.
EDCS-13302269.summary: A funerary dedication by Claudia Marcella for her son, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-13302270.translation: Menander, freedman of Philoxsinus, for his patron Marcus Livius Alexas, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-13302270.summary: A funerary dedication for the patron Marcus Livius Alexas by his freedman Menander.

EDCS-13302271.translation: For Lucius Mirmus Lepidus, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-13302271.summary: A funerary dedication for Lucius Mirmus Lepidus, freedman of Lucius.

EDCS-13302272.translation: Lagge, my son, may you rest well; your mother asks that you receive her to yourself. Farewell. 15 feet in every direction.
EDCS-13302272.summary: A tombstone epitaph from a mother to her son, requesting he welcome her spirit upon her death, with funerary plot dimensions.

EDCS-13302273.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For Publius Olidius Peregrinus. The matrona and Campister, freedman, [dedicate this] for their patron.
EDCS-13302273.summary: A funerary dedication for Publius Olidius Peregrinus by his freedman and a woman identified as 'matrona'.

EDCS-13302274.translation: For Titus Paconius, son of Titus, of Quinctius.
EDCS-13302274.summary: A funerary dedication for Titus Paconius, son of Titus, possibly indicating a gentile affiliation.

EDCS-13302275.translation: Marcus Planius Maxsumus, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-13302275.summary: A funerary dedication for Marcus Planius Maxsumus, freedman of Marcus.

EDCS-13302276.translation: [...]tius, freedman of Marcus Papus, repaired [this] at his own expense for Chelidonius.
EDCS-13302276.summary: A dedication recording a repair made by a freedman named Papus for Chelidonius, likely on a public or funerary structure.

EDCS-13302278.translation: For Publius Titius Phileros, freedman of Publius. 12 feet in front.
EDCS-13302278.summary: A funerary dedication for Publius Titius Phileros, freedman of Publius, with funerary plot dimensions.

EDCS-13302279.translation: For Sextus Voltilius Saturnus. Quintus Iulius [dedicates this].
EDCS-13302279.summary: A funerary dedication by Quintus Iulius for Sextus Voltilius Saturnus.

EDCS-13302282.translation: Here rests in good memory Valeriana, who lived more or less 40 years and died on the seventh day before the Ides of September in the fourth indiction.
EDCS-13302282.summary: A funerary epitaph for Valeriana, noting her age at death and burial date, likely from the 4th century CE.

EDCS-13302283.translation: Here rests in good memory Genesius, who lived more or less 40 years and passed away on the third day before the Kalends of February during the consulship of Decius Longinus.
EDCS-13302283.summary: A funerary epitaph for Genesius, noting his age at death and burial date, with a specific consular dating to 266 CE.

EDCS-13302284.translation: Here rests in good memory Venantius, who lived more or less 35 years and 1 month, after the consulship of Probus.
EDCS-13302284.summary: A funerary epitaph for Venantius, noting his age at death and burial date, likely from the late 3rd century CE.

EDCS-13302286.translation: All of you who come to the church, pray for Adroarius, a sinful priest, so that the Lord may have mercy on you on the day of judgment. Amen.
EDCS-13302286.summary: A devotional plea inscribed in or near a church, asking for prayers for a priest named Adroarius.

EDCS-13302287.translation: Flavius Cassius placed this in peace for Agroecia, his well-deserving wife, resting in the sign of Christ, who lived 17 years, 4 months, and 5 days.
EDCS-13302287.summary: A funerary epitaph for Agroecia, dedicated by her husband Flavius Cassius, mentioning her age at death and dedication in Christ.

EDCS-13302309.translation: To Maxumus, tribune of the II Praetorian cohort, twice a primus pilus, procurator of Emperor Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, twice prefect of the V Praetorian cohort, and to the EMPEROR...
EDCS-13302309.summary: A fragmentary inscription honoring a military officer, Maxumus, who held several high-ranking positions in the Praetorian Guard and imperial service.

EDCS-13302314.translation: To Marcus Julius Quintillus, son of [---], of the Voltinian tribe, from the colony Julia Ruscino.
EDCS-13302314.summary: A dedication or funerary inscription for Marcus Julius Quintillus, noting his tribal affiliation and origin from Colonia Julia Ruscino.

EDCS-13302316.translation: Severus ordered this to be made by his will, for 1,000,000 sesterces.
EDCS-13302316.summary: A funerary inscription indicating that Severus commissioned his own tomb and allocated a sum of money for its construction.

EDCS-13302322.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Quelia Victrix for her most dutiful son, Gaius Quelius Marcianus.
