EDCS-13302322.summary: A dedication to the 'Dis Manibus' (Spirits of the Underworld) by Quelia Victrix for her son, Gaius Quelius Marcianus.

EDCS-13302323.translation: Marcus Atilius Labeo willingly fulfilled his vow, as deserved, on the boundary.
EDCS-13302323.summary: An inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow by Marcus Atilius Labeo, possibly related to a boundary marker or property dispute.

EDCS-13302325.translation: To Marcus Julius, son of Marcus, Contessus; to Domitia, daughter of Lucius; and to Julius, son of Marcus, of the Voltinia tribe.
EDCS-13302325.summary: This is a funerary inscription listing several individuals, possibly family members, with their names and tribal affiliations.

EDCS-13302326.translation: A sad task of a mother, she placed the bones of her two sons here; she ought to have placed [her own] here. Memmia Paramone, daughter of Marcus, while alive, for herself and for her sons Lucius Memmius Celer and Memmia Vegeta.
EDCS-13302326.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a mother for herself and her deceased sons, indicating she wished to be buried with them.

EDCS-13302328.translation: Satyrus, freedman, son of [---]; Secundilla, freedwoman, wife of [---]; Apollinaris, freedman, son of [---]; Castina, freedwoman, wife of [---]; Maximus, freedman, son of [---]; Cara, freedwoman, wife of [---]; Severus, freedman, son of [---]; Maturus, freedman, son of [---]; Sedulus, freedman, son of [---].
EDCS-13302328.summary: This inscription appears to be a list of freedmen and freedwomen, possibly from a tomb, with their names and some familial relationships indicated, dating to the late Roman period.

EDCS-13302329.translation: To [---], son of Titus, and to his brother [---]. [---] made this for [---] and his brother [---], while alive. [---] made this.
EDCS-13302329.summary: This is a dedication for a living person and their brother, likely for a tomb, with the dedicant identified by patronymics.

EDCS-13302331.translation: Quintus Tadius Carus gives [this] to Silvanus.
EDCS-13302331.summary: This is a dedication of an offering or object to the god Silvanus by Quintus Tadius Carus.

EDCS-13302332.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, from Cinnamis, mother of Paulinus and Callistenus.
EDCS-13302332.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the 'Dis Manibus' (spirits of the underworld) by a mother for her sons.

EDCS-13302333.translation: Nigrinus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Abianius and Mercurius.
EDCS-13302333.summary: This is an inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow made to the deities Abianius and Mercurius by Nigrinus.

EDCS-13302577.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantinus, pious, most noble Caesar, son of the deified Constantius Pius Augustus, for the third time.
EDCS-13302577.summary: This is an honorific inscription for Emperor Constantine the Great, likely recording his third consulship or other high office.

EDCS-13302588.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying Marcus Alphius as an oil merchant.

EDCS-13302589.translation: The public mine in the name of Primulus Silonis, 297, procurator of the colony of Onobensis.
EDCS-13302589.summary: This inscription records the management of a public mine by Primulus Silonis, identified as a procurator of the colony of Onobensis, likely in the late Roman period.

EDCS-13302592.summary: This is a simple funerary or identification marker for Sextus Arrius, son of Marcus.

EDCS-13302593.summary: This is a dedication made by Caius Piraius Cerdo, likely on a tomb or monument.

EDCS-13302594.summary: This is a dedication made by Caius Piranus Felix, likely on a tomb or monument.

EDCS-13302597.translation: Quintus Caecilius Cornutus fulfilled his vow to Matris Mageis.
EDCS-13302597.summary: This inscription records Quintus Caecilius Cornutus fulfilling a vow to the deity Matris Mageis.

EDCS-13302598.summary: This is a dedication to the god Mercury, possibly by a person named Vicinia or referring to a local aspect of Mercury.

EDCS-13302671.summary: This inscription identifies Marci Natti as being from the Arverni tribe, possibly on a funerary or public monument.

EDCS-13302676.summary: This inscription simply names Caius Acilius Acisius, likely appearing on a tomb or official marker.

EDCS-13302678.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Quintus Licinius Surus vivos sic sibi et Quinto Licinio Repentino patrono\n
EDCS-13302678.translation: To the Divine Shades. Quintus Licinius Surus, while alive, to himself and to Quintus Licinius Repentinus, his patron.
EDCS-13302678.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Quintus Licinius Surus for himself and his patron, Quintus Licinius Repentinus.

EDCS-13302679.translation: Flavius Meterius and Iulia Peganius to their dearest son Victorio Optato.
EDCS-13302679.summary: This is a dedication by Flavius Meterius and Iulia Peganius to their beloved son, Victorio Optato, likely on a tomb.

EDCS-13302686.translation: Staia Saturnina made this for her own family while alive.
EDCS-13302686.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Staia Saturnina for her family during her lifetime.

EDCS-13302708.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Quintus Parucius to the goddess Isis.

EDCS-13302717.translation: Lucius Senecius Martialis and Lucius Senecius Maternus willingly and deservedly fulfilled their vow to Mars Melovius.
EDCS-13302717.summary: This inscription records Lucius Senecius Martialis and Lucius Senecius Maternus fulfilling a vow to the deity Mars Melovius.

EDCS-13302718.translation: Varius Gentinus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Castor.
EDCS-13302718.summary: This is a votive inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow to the god Castor.

EDCS-13303398.translation: Quintus Cassius's diapsoricum for clarity, Quintus Cassius's diasmyrnes for Quintus Cassius's mixture, against all things, Quintus Cassius's diamisus.
EDCS-13303398.summary: This inscription lists various preparations or remedies associated with Quintus Cassius, likely for medicinal purposes.

EDCS-13400056.summary: This is a dedication, likely on a tombstone or monument, to Lucius Tettius Crito.

EDCS-13400061.translation: Maternianus and Maternus, from a vow.
EDCS-13400061.summary: This inscription records that Maternianus and Maternus fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-13400062.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Publius Annius Euschemon to his wife Annia Diophantis.
EDCS-13400062.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Publius Annius Euschemon to his deceased wife, Annia Diophantis.

EDCS-13400063.translation: To Antistia Pia, daughter of Quintus, priestess of the Flavian Colony of Tricastini, an excellent patroness. Philocrates, her freedman.
EDCS-13400063.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a freedman, Philocrates, to his patroness, Antistia Pia, who held a significant religious and civic role.

EDCS-13400081.summary: This inscription likely records the name of Ianuarius Voconius, possibly on a tomb or monument.

EDCS-13400094.translation: Quintus Valerius Cassianus, aged 27, son of Maternus, of the Voltinia tribe. A Vossaticcian.
EDCS-13400094.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Quintus Valerius Cassianus, providing his age, parentage, tribal affiliation, and a possible ethnic or regional identifier.

EDCS-13400197.translation: To the Unconquered God. Marcus Iccius.
EDCS-13400197.summary: This is a dedication to the Unconquered God by Marcus Iccius.

EDCS-13400200.translation: Decimus Domitius Celer, son of Lucius, of the Voltinia tribe, military tribune, officer of the engineers, made this while alive. Lucius Domitius, son of Lucius, of the Voltinia tribe. Domitia Mater, daughter of Sextus, of the Voltinia tribe. Lucius Domitius Macer, son of Lucius, of the Voltinia tribe. Lucius Tontus.
EDCS-13400200.summary: This is a funerary monument commissioned by Decimus Domitius Celer, a military officer, and includes dedications to other family members, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-13400201.translation: Decimus Domitius Celer, son of Lucius, of the Voltinia tribe, military tribune and prefect of engineers, made this in his lifetime.
EDCS-13400201.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Decimus Domitius Celer, a military officer, in his own lifetime.

EDCS-13400202.translation: Lucius Domitius Magun, son of Lucius, of the Voltinia tribe, and Domitia, daughter of Sextus, his mother.
EDCS-13400202.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or statement of family relation involving Lucius Domitius Magun and his mother Domitia.

EDCS-13400203.translation: Domitius Macer, son of Lucius, of the Voltinia tribe, military tribune and priest.
EDCS-13400203.summary: This inscription records the titles of Domitius Macer, a military tribune and priest.

EDCS-13400204.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely records the name of Gaius Valerius Hermetis, possibly as a dedication or ownership mark.

EDCS-13500185.translation: Drink, slave, I am not free for you.
EDCS-13500185.summary: This is a short, informal inscription, possibly a graffito, with a direct address to a slave.

EDCS-13500186.translation: I am a thief from Tibur, beware of evil.
EDCS-13500186.summary: This is a short, informal inscription, possibly a graffito, warning others about a thief from Tibur.

EDCS-13500314.translation: Duvia paid her vow freely and deservedly to her Mercury.
EDCS-13500314.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made by Duvia to Mercury.

EDCS-13500315.summary: This is a dedication to Auribus Loreia Pia, identified as a minister.

EDCS-13500316.translation: Peregrina paid her vow freely and deservedly to the Iunones.
EDCS-13500316.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made by Peregrina to the Iunones.

EDCS-13500318.translation: To the holy divine power of Silvanus, Titus Quadrinius Valerianus paid his vow freely and deservedly.
EDCS-13500318.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made by Titus Quadrinius Valerianus to the deity Silvanus.

EDCS-13600211.translation: Magia Pastoris, daughter of Pastor, paid her vow freely and deservedly.
EDCS-13600211.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made by Magia Pastoris.

EDCS-13600399.translation: Valerius Logicus, freedman of Bassus, for the six-member priesthood.
EDCS-13600399.summary: This is a dedication by Valerius Logicus for a priesthood, likely a funerary or honorific monument.

EDCS-13700350.translation: Julius Boudus, the aedile, from his many possessions.
EDCS-13700350.summary: This inscription records an offering or expenditure by Julius Boudus in his capacity as aedile.

EDCS-13700351.summary: This is a dedication or votive offering to health by Marcus Agrippa, possibly for himself or another.

EDCS-13800108.translation: Marcus Decumius Marcellinus willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Hercules.
EDCS-13800108.summary: This is a votive inscription by Marcus Decumius Marcellinus to the god Hercules, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-13800109.translation: Marcus Vinicius paid his vow to Hercules.
EDCS-13800109.summary: This is a votive inscription by Marcus Vinicius to the god Hercules, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-13800110.translation: Marcellinus willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Hercules.
EDCS-13800110.summary: This is a votive inscription by Marcellinus to the god Hercules, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-13800113.translation: Marcus U Zmaragdus willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Hercules.
EDCS-13800113.summary: This is a votive inscription by Marcus U Zmaragdus to the god Hercules, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-13800114.translation: The vow undertaken for Hercules Victor for the health and safe return of Gaius Licinius Macr, tribune, and the centurions and soldiers of the Glanici, who were under the standard, was willingly and deservedly paid by Gnaeus Pompeius Cornutus, optio, from his pay and a bonus which had been established for him as a gift.
EDCS-13800114.summary: This inscription records a soldier's vow fulfilled to Hercules Victor for the well-being of himself and his military unit, likely from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-13800115.translation: Marcus Licinius Claudia Verecundus, a veteran of the XXI Rapax legion, willingly and deservedly paid his vow to the Glani, the Glanicae, and Fortuna Redux.
EDCS-13800115.summary: This is a votive inscription by a veteran of the XXI Rapax legion to local deities and Fortuna Redux, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-13800183.summary: This is a simple funerary or ownership inscription identifying Lucius Titius, son of Caius.

EDCS-13800184.translation: Of Marcus, son of Caius, of the family of Lasius.
EDCS-13800184.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragment of a funerary monument or a dedicatory label, possibly identifying a person or a family.

EDCS-13800219.text_edition: \n Senatus populusque Romanus Imperatori Caesari Divi filio Augusto consuli VIII dedit clupeum virtutis clementiae iustitiae pietatis erga deos patriamque\n
EDCS-13800219.translation: The Senate and the Roman people gave to the Emperor Caesar, son of the Divine one, Augustus, in his eighth consulship, a shield for his valor, clemency, justice, piety towards the gods, and fatherland.
EDCS-13800219.summary: This inscription records the Roman Senate and people presenting Emperor Augustus with a shield in recognition of his virtues and service.

EDCS-13900376.translation: Gnaeus Domitius Ahenobarbus, son of Gnaeus, imperator for the 20th time.
EDCS-13900376.summary: This inscription records the high military rank and achievements of Gnaeus Domitius Ahenobarbus, likely from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-13900386.translation: To the departed spirits. Annia Terentia, from the public records office, placed this for her dearest husband and for herself while alive, and dedicated it under the axe.
EDCS-13900386.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Annia Terentia for her husband and herself, indicating a 'sub ascia' dedication for a property or burial plot.

EDCS-13900387.summary: This is likely a name inscription, possibly for a tombstone, statue base, or other dedicatory monument.

EDCS-13900433.translation: To the father of the fatherland, consul for the 11th time, imperator for the 14th time.
EDCS-13900433.summary: This inscription lists honorific titles, likely for an emperor or a highly distinguished Roman official, referring to consulships and imperatorial acclamations.

EDCS-13900436.translation: By decree of the decurions, for his merits in public affairs: to Julius, son of Titus, of the Teretina tribe, first-rank centurion twice, military tribune twice, cavalry prefect twice, camp prefect, naval prefect, from the college of Honor and Virtue, duovir twice, augur, flamen of Rome and Caesar Augustus.
EDCS-13900436.summary: This is a lengthy honorary inscription honoring Julius, son of Titus, detailing his extensive military and civil career and his participation in various religious and collegial offices, likely erected by a town council.

EDCS-14000029.text_edition: \n SD I VK XXIII insulae Furianae coloniae iugera XX et nova VII praestant aera IV |(denarii) I|(bes) |(semuncia) solvunt heredes Firmi Secundi SD I VK XXII coloniae iugera XCVII|(bes) Quinto Curtio Rufo IIviro et inventore nova iugera XV|(dodrans) praestant aera III |(denarii) III|(dodrans) |(semuncia) TAI solvunt heredes Firmi Secundi\n
EDCS-14000029.translation: The twenty-third cohort of volunteers from the Furian estate of the colony provide twenty jugera of land and seven new ones, they pay four asses. The heirs of Firminus Secundus provide ninety-seven jugera of land and fifteen new ones, they pay three asses. Quinto Curtio Rufo, duovir and overseer, provides fifteen new jugera. The heirs of Firminus Secundus pay three asses.
EDCS-14000029.summary: This inscription records land distribution and payments made by the heirs of Firminus Secundus for the twenty-third cohort of volunteers of the colony of Vienna.

EDCS-14100201.translation: orius inus V ounce, semiobolus, S... kardinem VIII III Cornelius Sacratus, the decumanus on the right.
EDCS-14100201.summary: This inscription appears to be related to land surveying or division, possibly indicating measurements or boundaries with specific terms and names.

EDCS-14800020.text_edition: \n Titus Pompeius Titi libertus Palatina Phrixus Longus sevir Firmo Iulio et Copia Munatia Luguduni vivos sibi fecit Regini eius libertus ex sacroviri gente qui decessit Romae nnorum XVII\n
EDCS-14800020.translation: Titus Pompeius Phrixus Longus, freedman of Titus, of the Palatine tribe, a sevir, made this for himself while alive, with Reginus, his freedman, of the Sacroviri clan, who died in Rome at the age of seventeen.
EDCS-14800020.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Titus Pompeius Phrixus Longus, a freedman and sevir, by his freedman Reginus, who died young.

EDCS-15000083.translation: Iucundus, son of Covertina, donated the wall around the altar of Vulcan through his magistracy to the order of the Diensians.
EDCS-15000083.summary: This inscription records a donation of a wall around an altar by Iucundus to his community, likely as part of his duties as a local magistrate.

EDCS-15000126.text_edition: \n Teucer hic fuit ante diem IV Kalendas Apriles Cnaeo Domitio Caio Sossio consulibus\n
EDCS-15000126.translation: Teucer was here four days before the Kalends of April, in the consulship of Gnaeus Domitius and Gaius Sossius.
EDCS-15000126.summary: This is an epitaph or marker recording the presence of Teucer on a specific date in 49 BC.

EDCS-15200122.translation: Here lies buried Tolosanus, a Briton by nation, the sorrow of the proconsul.
EDCS-15200122.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a man named Tolosanus, noting his origin and perceived impact on a proconsul.

EDCS-15200124.translation: Lucius Mut Vitalis made this from Vasio.
EDCS-15200124.summary: This is a dedicatory or construction inscription stating that Lucius Mut Vitalis created something originating from Vasio.

EDCS-15300367.summary: This inscription likely records names, possibly related to a funerary context or an official list.

EDCS-15300369.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription honoring Caius Atilius Atticus.

EDCS-15300371.translation: By the prompting of Hippona, Lucius C Viator, the temple attendant, to all the gods.
EDCS-15300371.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Lucius C Viator, a temple attendant, prompted by Hippona, to all the gods.

EDCS-15300372.translation: Sextus Tiberius Ver, a messenger, placed a golden image of Mars on the altar at the first light.
EDCS-15300372.summary: This dedication records Sextus Tiberius Ver, a messenger, placing a golden image of Mars on an altar.

EDCS-15300373.translation: Attia Musa, servant of the Lady, placed this.
EDCS-15300373.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Attia Musa, a servant, to a female deity.

EDCS-15300374.translation: Vinicia Eutychia to the Good Goddess.
EDCS-15300374.summary: This is a dedication by Vinicia Eutychia to the Bona Dea (Good Goddess).

EDCS-15300375.summary: This inscription identifies a group, likely associated with the town of Glanum, possibly in a dedicatory or guild context.

EDCS-15300376.translation: Opibus Optata willingly fulfilled her vow, deservedly.
EDCS-15300376.summary: This inscription records Opibus Optata fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-15300378.translation: Silanus, son of Lutevus, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-15300378.summary: A dedication by Silanus fulfilling a vow to an unspecified deity, likely from the late Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-15300379.translation: Caecilius Firmus gladly fulfilled his vow to Abianus as deserved.
EDCS-15300379.summary: A votive inscription by Caecilius Firmus to Abianus, dating likely to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15500016.translation: Marcus Staius Achilleus, one of the six leaders of the Augustales, for his patroness, to the Divine Spirits of Sextus Sammius Firminus.
EDCS-15500016.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Marcus Staius Achilleus to his patroness, Sextus Sammius Firminus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15500042.translation: Pope Lazarus, who lived in the fear of God for more or less 70 years, rests here in peace on the day before the Kalends of September in the 105th year.
EDCS-15500042.summary: A tombstone for Pope Lazarus, recording his lifespan and death date, likely from the Late Roman or early Byzantine period.

EDCS-15700071.summary: A very brief inscription possibly related to a measure or tribute of grain, origin and date uncertain.

EDCS-15700073.translation: Titus Iulius Licinianus gladly fulfilled his vow to Vulcan as deserved.
EDCS-15700073.summary: A votive inscription dedicated to Vulcan by Titus Iulius Licinianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15700074.translation: Veratianus gladly fulfilled his vow to Fortuna as deserved.
EDCS-15700074.summary: A votive inscription dedicated to Fortuna by Veratianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15700157.translation: Procellus Curmisso Albarino fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-15700157.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Procellus Curmisso Albarino fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-15700158.translation: Aulus, son of A. C., for the Carinian Nymphs, fulfilled his vow gladly and deservedly.
EDCS-15700158.summary: A votive inscription to the Carinian Nymphs by Aulus, son of A. C., likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15700160.translation: Dula set up an altar to Father Dis [Pluto] by vow.
EDCS-15700160.summary: A dedication of an altar to Dis Pater by Dula, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15700161.translation: Anteremius Afer set up an altar to Jupiter.
EDCS-15700161.summary: An altar dedicated to Jupiter by Anteremius Afer, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15700166.translation: May you fare well, Genius, from your inheritance of fifty-nine (items).
EDCS-15700166.summary: This is a dedication to the Genius, possibly from an inheritance or a gift, dated to the 59th year (of an unspecified reign or period).

EDCS-15700167.translation: Marcia Donata, daughter of Marcius, of the Oufentina tribe, from Milan, while still alive, together with Quintus Pescennius, son of Quintus, and Titullus, son of Titus Valerius, for her third part.
EDCS-15700167.summary: This inscription records a property division or inheritance involving Marcia Donata and two other individuals, likely from Milan, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15800460.text_edition: \n Vivont sic dei Manes sacrum humane Titus Vettius Publi filius Papiria Loripes summae sic rudis Publius Vettius Titi filius Papiria Martialis duas sic Vettias sic Titi liberti Suavis et Utilis\n
EDCS-15800460.translation: The divine Manes (rest in peace). Titus Vettius, son of Publius, of the Papirian tribe, called Loripes (clubfoot), and his son Publius Vettius Martialis, son of Titus, of the Papirian tribe, and two slaves of Titus, freedmen, Suavis and Utilis (rest in peace).
EDCS-15800460.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication for Titus Vettius, his son Publius Vettius Martialis, and two freedmen, Suavis and Utilis, likely related to a family tomb.

EDCS-15900097.translation: To the Tutela of Charsitas, whether god or goddess.
EDCS-15900097.summary: This is a dedication to a local deity named Tutela of Charsitas, possibly a protective spirit of a place, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15900098.translation: Prima, daughter of Philemas, willingly fulfilled her vow deservedly.
EDCS-15900098.summary: This is a votive inscription by Prima, daughter of Philemas, indicating the fulfillment of a vow, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15900138.text_edition: \n Viamae deae Craxo votum solvit libens merito voto excepto\n
EDCS-15900138.translation: To the goddess Viama, Crax willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow, with the exception of the vow.
EDCS-15900138.summary: This is a votive inscription by Crax to the goddess Viama, acknowledging the fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-15900402.translation: To the Nymphs. He willingly fulfilled his vow deservedly.
EDCS-15900402.summary: This is a votive inscription to the Nymphs by an anonymous male dedicator, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15900403.translation: Temporinius Cerialis, chief scribe, and his brother Secundinus, for their parents.
EDCS-15900403.summary: This inscription records a dedication or memorial for parents by Temporinius Cerialis, a chief scribe, and his brother Secundinus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-15900404.summary: This inscription records a dedication or memorial by Domitius Verres for his close family members, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16000036.translation: For Apollo Augustus, for the well-being of Marcia Taurina, daughter of Titus. Epicifius, his freedman, according to his vow.
EDCS-16000036.summary: This is a votive inscription by Epicifius, a freedman, to Apollo Augustus for the health of Marcia Taurina, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16000553.translation: The elected officials of the landowners of Aqui donated the grove with its vineyard to the villagers of Aqui for the celebration of games for the safety of the Emperor Augustus. Zmertuccius Titianus, patron of the village, dedicated the altar at his own expense.
EDCS-16000553.summary: This inscription records the donation of a grove and vineyard by local landowners to villagers for games celebrating the Emperor's safety, with a further dedication of an altar by the village patron, Zmertuccius Titianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16000555.translation: Aulus Adius Aurelianus and Nummularia, daughter of Titus, to his wife.
EDCS-16000555.summary: This inscription records a dedication or memorial by Aulus Adius Aurelianus and Nummularia to Aurelianus' wife, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16100377.translation: Our governor, Marcus Iulius Severus, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his sacred vow to the legion I.
EDCS-16100377.summary: This inscription records a governor, Marcus Iulius Severus, fulfilling a vow to the first legion, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-16200062.translation: Crinas, of the tribe Sidus, son of Tullus.
EDCS-16200062.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, possibly a funerary dedication or ownership mark, for a person named Crinas.

EDCS-16200064.translation: Cotutos, from Acitabli, made 1400 mortaria (mixing bowls) and 120 seats for the paraschista (performers/assistants) at the paraschista (tent/stage).
EDCS-16200064.summary: This inscription records the production of 1400 mortaria and 120 seats by Cotutos, likely for a theatrical or performance context.

EDCS-16200970.summary: This is a maker's signature on a stone object, indicating Philiscus was a stonemason.

EDCS-16201049.summary: This is a dedication to the god Silvanus, made by a person also named Silvanus.

EDCS-16201642.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Aurelius Eutyches, freedman, and his heirs Eventius, dedicated this for Aurelius Valens, freedman of the emperor, superintendent of the forty-percent tax office at Genava.
EDCS-16201642.summary: This funerary inscription honors Aurelius Valens, an imperial freedman and tax official, and was set up by his freedmen.

EDCS-16400089.summary: This is a possessive or dedicatory inscription, likely for a tomb or object belonging to Lucius Statius Epitynchus.

EDCS-16500078.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, possibly part of a longer text or a curse, mentioning Hercules.

EDCS-16700014.translation: He fulfilled it willingly and deservedly, as he had vowed.
EDCS-16700014.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow, likely a votive offering.

EDCS-16800195.translation: Anchialus, slave of Lucius Sirtius, looks at the coins in the month of February, when Marcus Tullius and Gaius Antonius were consuls.
EDCS-16800195.summary: This inscription records a slave, Anchialus, observing coins during the consulship of Marcus Tullius and Gaius Antonius (likely 30 BCE).

EDCS-17700134.translation: Thraex Campanus gives 20 crowns from his own property.
EDCS-17700134.summary: This inscription records a dedication by a gladiator named Thraex Campanus.

EDCS-18300301.translation: Sextius Flavius Basilius' myrrh for blemishes, Sextius Flavius Basilius' lamp for the eyes, Sextius Flavius Basilius' amethyst for scars, Sextius Flavius Basilius' trigonum for dryness.
EDCS-18300301.summary: This inscription lists various medicinal preparations or cosmetic items belonging to Sextius Flavius Basilius.

EDCS-18500151.translation: Quintus Lucius Dionysius' dialibanum from an egg for eye inflammation, Quintus Lucius Dionysius' penicillum from an egg for the onset of eye inflammation, Quintus Lucius Dionysius' diaglaucium from an egg for eye inflammation, Quintus Lucius Dionysius' chloron from an egg for eye inflammation.
EDCS-18500151.summary: This inscription records several eye remedies or treatments prepared by Quintus Lucius Dionysius, possibly from an egg base.

EDCS-20000134.summary: This is a very brief inscription indicating that Senecio and Matuso were the makers of the object.

EDCS-20000135.summary: This is a very brief inscription indicating that Senecio and Matuso were the makers of the object.

EDCS-20000136.translation: Gaius Sextus Eutyches made [this] in Vienna.
EDCS-20000136.summary: This inscription records that Gaius Sextus Eutyches was the maker of the object in Vienna.

EDCS-20000137.translation: Cnaeus Tal Hermes made [this] in Vienna.
EDCS-20000137.summary: This inscription records that Cnaeus Tal Hermes was the maker of the object in Vienna.

EDCS-20000138.summary: This inscription records that Tat Pop was the maker of the object in Vienna.

EDCS-20000139.summary: This inscription records that Tat Pop was the maker of the object in Vienna.

EDCS-20500239.text_edition: \n Lucius Lucius C Lucius V Quintus \n
EDCS-20500239.translation: Lucius Lucius C Lucius V Quintus
EDCS-20500239.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely containing names, possibly a funerary or ownership marker.

EDCS-20500244.translation: To the Matres Baginienses, Sextia, daughter of Rusticus, her vow, willingly, deservedly.
EDCS-20500244.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the Matres Baginienses by Sextia, daughter of Rusticus.

EDCS-20500245.translation: To the Matres Baginienses, Firmus, son of Sio, willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-20500245.summary: This votive inscription records a vow paid to the Matres Baginienses by Firmus.

EDCS-20500246.translation: To the Baginiates, Caius Girubius Cato willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-20500246.summary: This votive inscription records a vow paid to the Baginiates by Caius Girubius Cato.

EDCS-20500247.translation: To the Baginiates, Primula, daughter of Quintus, willingly and deservedly paid her vow.
EDCS-20500247.summary: This votive inscription records a vow paid to the Baginiates by Primula.

EDCS-20500248.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Vetinia Nereis fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-20500249.translation: To the Baginiates, Ioventius, son of Lemiso, willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-20500249.summary: This votive inscription records a vow paid to the Baginiates by Ioventius.

EDCS-20500251.translation: To Jupiter, Iubrus willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-20500251.summary: This votive inscription records a vow paid to Jupiter by Iubrus.

EDCS-20500252.translation: Vini Viventiaes, a pultarius (a type of vessel or possibly a person's name/nickname).
EDCS-20500252.summary: This inscription possibly records names or a designation related to a vessel, possibly of funerary context.

EDCS-20500256.text_edition: \n Cornelio Gabiniani filio Gabiniano Voltinia quaestori colonia Vienna flamini Iuventutis IIviro [iure dicundo ------\n
EDCS-20500256.translation: To Cornelius Gabinianus, son of Gabinianus, of the Voltinian tribe, quaestor, to Gabinianus, of the colony of Vienna, flamen of Youth, duovir [judiciary...].
EDCS-20500256.summary: This is a dedication to Cornelius Gabinianus, listing his various civic and religious offices in the colony of Vienna.

EDCS-20500257.translation: Titus Domitius Mansuetus made this at Vienna.
EDCS-20500257.summary: This is a dedication of a monument or object made by Titus Domitius Mansuetus at Vienna.

EDCS-20500260.summary: This is a name inscription, likely for a tomb or dedication, belonging to Sextilanus Porcius.

EDCS-20500266.text_edition: \n Marcus Iulius Magnus Marti ut voverat solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-20500266.translation: Marcus Iulius Magnus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mars.
EDCS-20500266.summary: A private votive inscription from Marcus Iulius Magnus to Mars, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-23900154.translation: Abascantus willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Avianus for the bees.
EDCS-23900154.summary: This votive inscription records a vow paid to Avianus by Abascantus concerning bees.

EDCS-23900155.text_edition: \n Quintus Ateius Calventius Lucius Ateius Rufus Mercurio votum solverunt libentes merito quod vovit Calventius Capitonis filius\n
EDCS-23900155.translation: Quintus Ateius Calventius and Lucius Ateius Rufus willingly and deservedly fulfilled their vow to Mercury, which Calventius, son of Capito, had vowed.
EDCS-23900155.summary: A private votive inscription by Quintus Ateius Calventius and Lucius Ateius Rufus to Mercury, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-23900161.translation: In this tomb rests in peace, of good memory, Constantia, who lived more or less 60 years, died in peace on the 11th day before the Kalends of the month, after the consulship of the most excellent consul Basil, in the indictione.
EDCS-23900161.summary: This epitaph records the death of Constantia, providing her age, date of death relative to a consul, and mentions her husband Basil, likely from the 4th or 5th century CE.

EDCS-23900165.translation: Marcus Iulius Primulus dedicated [this] to the goddess Coriotana.
EDCS-23900165.summary: This votive inscription records a dedication to the goddess Coriotana by Marcus Iulius Primulus.

EDCS-23900166.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Papiriae Luci filiae Tertull\n
EDCS-23900166.translation: To the Divine Shades of Papiria, daughter of Lucius, called Tertulla.
EDCS-23900166.summary: A funerary inscription honoring Papiria Tertulla, daughter of Lucius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23900168.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Cornelius, son of Cornelia.
EDCS-23900168.summary: This is a funerary dedication for a man named Cornelius, son of Cornelia, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23900170.text_edition: \n Mansuetae Mansueti filiae heredes faciendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-23900170.translation: Her heirs had this made for Mansueta, daughter of Mansuetus.
EDCS-23900170.summary: A funerary inscription commissioned by the heirs for Mansueta, daughter of Mansuetus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23900171.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Macrini Tatia Macrina filio piissimo\n
EDCS-23900171.translation: To the Divine Shades of Macrina, to her most devoted son.
EDCS-23900171.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to Macrina, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23900173.translation: Modesta fulfilled her vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-23900173.summary: This inscription records a woman named Modesta fulfilling a vow, likely to a deity, during the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24200263.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Viventia O filiae pientissimae vixit annos XVII mensis sic VI\n
EDCS-24200263.translation: To the Divine Shades of Viventia, daughter of O, most devoted, who lived 17 years and 6 months.
EDCS-24200263.summary: A funerary inscription for Viventia, daughter of O, detailing her age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24200266.summary: This is a personal identification of Minicia Tertulla, daughter of Marcus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24200267.summary: This inscription records a man named Abianus fulfilling a vow, likely to a deity, during the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-24400405.translation: For mother Paulla, by the decision of her daughter Attia.
EDCS-24400405.summary: This inscription is a dedication to a mother named Paulla, arranged by her daughter Attia, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-25800631.translation: Proclus, husband of Rufina, lies here. By the will of the Fates, leaving life and me a widow, I made for you a great tomb in a prominent place, a wonder to all, and I placed shining doors and set up a likeness of you, just as you shone among the distinguished Romans, and among the consuls themselves you won outstanding glory. But I shall never be parted from you, just as our home was joined together while we were alive, so one tomb will cover us even in death.
EDCS-25800631.summary: This is a Greek funerary epigram from the Roman Imperial period, set up by a widow for her distinguished husband, Proclus, commemorating his public career and their inseparable union.

EDCS-30200092.translation: Whoever, seeing this honorable tomb and the sorrowful honor, you will weep for Avitus, enclosed in this earth, and if you are troubled with sad cares from your heart, for he whom full faith, whom lofty glory, whom piety, whom a ready hand, whom perpetual fame proclaims, holds nothing with death, but look at the deeds of this holy man, how great they were in his blooming disposition, when he disdained the fasces having rejected his ancient lineage, when he offered his mature spirit while still in tender years, and, by the virtue of the world's vow, he banished what was permitted. Nor did delay allow him to assume the worthy insignia of a pontiff, as was accustomed to increase the happy undertakings of his labor; sweetness does not obstruct the summit of rigor; the great man is subjected, the highest keeps moderate things, the generous distributes, the fasting feeds; he mixes the most indulgent with the austere. He aided the hesitant with persuasion, the sad with solace; he ended quarrels, joined the quarreling with a treaty. He subdued discordant doctrines which the true law fashions, by his exhortation, genius, counsel, and merits. He was alone in the citadel in any order of speaking; no orator was his equal, nor any poet. They cry out that his books are scattered through many volumes. Who lived, lives, and will live through all ages.
EDCS-30200092.summary: This epitaph praises a holy man named Avitus, detailing his virtuous life as a pontiff, orator, and poet, and assuring his eternal life through his merits and faith, likely from the Merovingian period given the names and context.

EDCS-30200094.translation: Posterity greatly desires to see the lives of the saints recorded, after the courses of the age have passed, so that it may be able to stand on sure truths and to reach afar, to live after death. Therefore, the limbs of the holy Pantagathus, a father and pious pontiff, are laid in this tomb, whose life was exalted with a twofold honor, distinguished by fasces, powerful in religion. He assumed the cingula of the quaestorship by the authority of kings, preeminent in lineage, more known for his integrity, giving feasts to the nobles and lavish gifts, and giving to the poor, seeking the heavenly kingdoms. He shone with keen intellect and great doctrine; he was also a great orator and poet. Therefore, in these studies, in the prime flower of his youth, he strove to be foremost among the greatest. Fortunate in his offspring, he saw the gift divided: one part consecrated to God, the other remains to be born. After his mature life passed with time, holy faith conferred upon him the apostolic summit, thus leaving the world, he possesses the heavenly citadel. Who is this, Vienna, your protection? He completed sixty years of life along the path and saw more than five years beyond our ages, contemplating the rewards of eternal life in which he deserved perpetual light.
EDCS-30200094.summary: This epitaph commemorates Pantagathus, a holy father and pontiff, who was distinguished by secular honors (fasces, quaestorship) and religious devotion, and who is celebrated for his intellect, generosity, and seeking heavenly reward; it also mentions his connection to Vienna and his attainment of the apostolic summit.

EDCS-30200095.translation: The pontiff Avitus, bound by the ties of death, is covered in this tomb. He who once shone with pontifical honor and, having completed worldly titles, was a capable and benevolent quaestor and ruler, finally chose to dwell in sacred buildings, wisely devoted to the worship of Christ, a patron of peace, who strove to make warring citizens peaceful with a special vow of a friendly mind. A measurer of times, discerning numbers by his calculation, and a strenuous teacher, he therefore gladly taught the fraternal companies in the temples, not yet completing seven double-year periods. Yet he placed his body in this blessed see, dwelling with the just and shining with eternal light. His sister Marcella, grieving that he died last, shedding tears, provides this small epitaph and inscription with a lament.
EDCS-30200095.summary: This epitaph honors Avitus, a former pontiff, quaestor, and ruler, who became a devout worshipper of Christ, a peacemaker, and a teacher, and who died before completing 14 years in religious service; his sister Marcella inscribed this epitaph for him.

EDCS-30200096.translation: Whoever, trembling, groans at human fortunes under your breast, and surveys tombs with a flowing eye, and revolves in your mind with excessive grief that cruel death devours all, that shadow covers them, never to release them from eternal joys, turn your gaze here, bend your eyes here, and receive solace, most sorrowful one, by ceasing your weeping, because man lives eternally if he follows justice and willingly carries out Christ's commands. As he did, Namatius, placed in this tomb, who, while he dispensed laws to the many cities entrusted to him with justice and in all ways, decreed most just things, called a patrician, and ruler of the homeland. Hence, having rejected the riches and titles of the world, he pleased to submit himself to the eternal King and to obey all God's commands, being perfectly suited. Thus, after he received the highest duties of a pontiff through merits and divine law, he will add rewards. The poor man departs happy, the naked departs covered, the captive rejoices that he is redeemed; he gives thanks and rejoices in such a prelate. He repressed the adversaries among themselves in broad peace. He was a refuge for the wretched and a protection for the kindly, noble in his eloquence and high in lineage, more noble in merits and brighter in the actions of his life. May he live eternally and rejoice in Christ's love. If you ask his age and the end of his salvation, he had completed seventy-three years. Symmachus Junior and the fifteenth, when the world arose, when he placed the fasces or cingula, sent his abundant soul to the highest heavens, commending his body to the earth, leaving earthly things behind.
EDCS-30200096.summary: This extensive epitaph commemorates Namatius, a patrician and ruler who became a devout pontiff, lauded for his justice, piety, generosity, eloquence, and noble lineage; it details his virtuous life, his service to God and man, and assures his eternal life, noting he lived seventy-three years and died when Symmachus Junior and the fifteenth year of his consulship occurred.

EDCS-30200097.translation: Whoever is allotted the century by the light-bringing god, is rather brought forth by his setting; and all things accomplished in the course of the worldly time, whether good or bad, all sing of death. Phoebus indeed shines forth, produced by his rising; if he has closed the day with a bright circle, he sets. Here, descended from ancestral consuls, Silvia left her earthly body, seeking the heavenly kingdoms. She shone, distinguished by the twofold star of life, by the highest honors of the century, by religion, by God, powerful in the splendor of her offspring, strengthened by her vigor, she rejoiced in having renewed her parents through childbirth. Hence, endowed with the clear honor of the priesthood, and deserved to see the patrician rank three times. The swift times were turning the fifth lustrum, and three years were added besides. The 9th day of Mars, shining with the golden star of spring, brought such great rewards. This is the supreme day, the first on the heavenly threshold, which the end of life took from this world and gave to the heavens. Let the pledges cease to be burdened with tears and weeping; it is not pleasing to groan, but to celebrate. Whose deposition is the 7th day before the Ides of March, thirty-nine years after the consulship of Basilius, most illustrious man, consul, the twelfth indiction.
EDCS-30200097.summary: This inscription commemorates Silvia, a woman of noble birth (descended from consuls), who held high status through her offspring, priesthood, and patrician rank, and who died on March 8th, 39 years after Basilius' consulship during the 12th indiction, having earned eternal rewards.

EDCS-32900125.inscription_type: tituli honorarii, tituli operum, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-32900125.text_edition: \n Lucio Terentio filio Pupinia Potito filio agenti annos XXVII decurioni ornamentario Claudia Luteva quaestori IIviro decurioni coloniae urbis Iuliae Baeterrensium Lucio Terentio Potito\n
EDCS-32900125.translation: To Lucius Terentius Potitus, son of Lucius Terentius, of the Pupinia tribe, who served as a decurion with ornamental rank, and Claudia Luteva, quaestor, twice duumvir, and decurion of the colony of the city of Julia Baeterrensis, [this was set up by] Lucius Terentius Potitus.
EDCS-32900125.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Lucius Terentius Potitus, likely set up by his father, who held several civic and military offices in Baeterrae.

EDCS-33400004.text_edition: \n Caio Oppio Voltinia Secundo militi cohortis III praetoriae centuria Luci Baebi Sabini militavit annos XVI optio annos III vixsit sic annos XL testamento fieri iussit\n
EDCS-33400004.translation: To Gaius Oppius Secundus, soldier of the 3rd Praetorian cohort, centuria of Lucius Baebius Sabinus. He served as a soldier for 16 years and as an optio for 3 years. He lived for 40 years. He ordered this to be made by his will.
EDCS-33400004.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaius Oppius Secundus, a soldier in the Praetorian Guard, who served for 19 years and died at the age of 40.

EDCS-33400005.summary: This is a funerary inscription stating that Esta rests in this place.

EDCS-33400010.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Sammiae Placentinae collibertae et coniugi piissimae Sammius Primitivus vivus et sibi fecit et sub ascia dedicavit\n
EDCS-33400010.translation: To the Divine Shades. Sammia Placentina, freedwoman and most devoted wife. Sammius Primitivus, alive, made this for himself and dedicated it under the axe.
EDCS-33400010.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Sammius Primitivus for his wife Sammia Placentina and himself, indicating it was consecrated and intended to be burned in a pyre.

EDCS-33500301.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Cai Comini Cominiani Comini Connius et Connianus et Conniola filii patri pientissimo posuerunt et sub ascia dedicaverunt\n
EDCS-33500301.translation: To the Divine Shades. Cai Cominius Cominianus, his sons Cominius and Connianus and Conniola, to their most dutiful father, placed [this] and dedicated it under the axe.
EDCS-33500301.summary: A funerary dedication by three sons, Cominius, Connianus, and Conniola, to their very dutiful father, Cai Cominius Cominianus.

EDCS-33500339.text_edition: \n Publice ex decreto decurionum Marco Carisio Sexti filio Voltinia Alpino praefecto fabrum tribuno militum legionis XXI\n
EDCS-33500339.translation: By public decree of the decurions, [this monument was erected] to Marcus Carisius Alpinius, son of Sextus, of the Voltinia tribe, prefect of engineers, tribune of the soldiers of the legion XXI.
EDCS-33500339.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Carisius Alpinius, a military officer and prefect of engineers, with a public dedication by the town council.

EDCS-33600012.translation: Marcus Verrius Mansuetus, in his own name and that of his brother Manso, ordered this to be set up by his will to the divine spirit of Augustus.
EDCS-33600012.summary: This inscription records an order made in a will by Marcus Verrius Mansuetus to set up a monument to the divine spirit of Augustus, also in honor of his brother.

EDCS-33600013.translation: Marcus Verrius Mansuetus, in his own name and that of his brother Manso, ordered this to be set up by his will to the divine spirit of Augustus.
EDCS-33600013.summary: This inscription records an order made in a will by Marcus Verrius Mansuetus to set up a monument to the divine spirit of Augustus, also in honor of his brother.

EDCS-33600014.translation: Titus Flaminius Secundus, son of Titus, and Cnaeus F. Romanus, son of Cnaeus, from their own resources, took care that this be erected to Victoria Augusta.
EDCS-33600014.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument to Victoria Augusta by Titus Flaminius Secundus and Cnaeus F. Romanus.

EDCS-33600017.translation: Marcus Rufius Marcianus made this while alive.
EDCS-33600017.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Marcus Rufius Marcianus during his lifetime.

EDCS-33600018.translation: Publius Attius Firmus made this vow to Mercury as soon as good fortune smiled upon me here, a dedication from profanity through [---] and with piety.
EDCS-33600018.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Mercury by Publius Attius Firmus.

EDCS-33600021.translation: Our Lords Emperors Caesar Gaius Aurelius Valerius Diocletian Pius Felix Invictus Augustus and Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maximian Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, by their providence, having established and completed the walls of Cularo with the inner buildings, ordered the Roman Gate to be called Jovian. Our Lords Emperors Caesar Gaius Aurelius Valerius Diocletian Pius Felix Invictus Augustus and Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maximian Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, by their providence, having established and completed the walls of Cularo with the inner buildings, ordered the Viennese Gate to be called Herculean.
EDCS-33600021.summary: This inscription records an imperial edict by Diocletian and Maximian dedicating and naming two gates, Porta Romana (Jovian) and Porta Viennensis (Herculean), of the city of Cularo (Grenoble).

EDCS-33600449.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely a tombstone, simply identifying Lucius Vibius, son of Caius.

EDCS-33600450.summary: This inscription identifies Iulianos as a patron.

EDCS-33700001.translation: To Lucius Pompeius Campanus, son of Lucius Pompeius and Sentia, dedicated by Lucius Pompeius Campanus, still living, to his father Lucius Pompeius, son of Caius, from his paternal grandfather Caius Pompeius Campanus; to his paternal grandmother Catia Secundina; to his paternal aunt Pompeia Maxima; to his paternal brother Pompeius Campanus; to his paternal uncle Decimus Valerius Gratus, son of Iaeus; to his paternal aunt Pompeia Secunda, daughter of Lucius; to his brother Caius Pompeius Justus; and to his parents: to his maternal grandmother Voluntilia Censa, daughter of Caius; to his maternal grandfather Caius Sentius Justus; and to Lucius Pompeius Campanus, son of Caius and Sentia.
EDCS-33700001.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication of a monument by Lucius Pompeius Campanus to his extensive family, including parents, grandparents, siblings, and an uncle.

EDCS-33700616.translation: To Amatia Marcella, her most devoted husband Staio Eudromus made this.
EDCS-33700616.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by a husband to his devoted wife, Amatia Marcella.

EDCS-33800047.translation: To Emperor Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantinus Pius Felix Augustus, grandson of Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maximianus Augustus, son of the deified Constantius Augustus Pius, Emperor Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantinus Pius Felix Augustus, son of the deified Constantius Augustus Pius.
EDCS-33800047.summary: This inscription is a titulary of Emperor Constantine the Great, emphasizing his lineage and imperial titles.

EDCS-33800049.translation: To Sextus, son of Sextus, father; to Titus Riccius Niva, brother.
EDCS-33800049.summary: This fragmented inscription appears to be a dedication to a father and a brother.

EDCS-33800054.translation: Gaius Clodius, praefectus iure dicundo, made this for himself and Secundina while still living.
EDCS-33800054.summary: This is a dedication made by Gaius Clodius, who held the office of praefectus iure dicundo, for himself and Secundina during his lifetime.

EDCS-33800094.translation: Secunda, daughter of Laebus [or Baius], willingly set this up.
EDCS-33800094.summary: This short inscription records Secunda setting up a monument, possibly indicating a funerary context.

EDCS-33800096.text_edition: \n Iovi Salutari Marcus Aurelius Maximianus monitus posuit libens merito\n
EDCS-33800096.translation: To Jupiter the Healer, Marcus Aurelius Maximianus placed [this] willingly, as deserved.
EDCS-33800096.summary: A dedication to the healing aspect of Jupiter, set up by Marcus Aurelius Maximianus.

EDCS-33800097.text_edition: \n Flavio Valerio Constantino nobilissimo Caesari milia passuum L\n
EDCS-33800097.translation: To Flavius Valerius Constantinus, most noble Caesar, 50 miles.
EDCS-33800097.summary: This inscription appears to mark a distance of 50 miles, likely on a road, dedicated to Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantinus.

EDCS-33800098.translation: Titus Julius Paternus, son of Titus Julius Paternus.
EDCS-33800098.summary: This inscription likely commemorates Titus Julius Paternus, possibly by his father of the same name, or is a self-dedication.

EDCS-33800621.translation: Decimus Aprius Vastus ordered this to be made by will for himself and his brother, to Titus Aprius Voltinia, son of Titus Voltinius Vastus, and to Decimus Aprius Voltinia.
EDCS-33800621.summary: This funerary inscription records the posthumous commission of a monument by Decimus Aprius Vastus for himself and his brother, mentioning relatives.

EDCS-33900042.translation: This noble urn covers Eutropius, your proven servant in Christ, embraced by the body. Although he displayed great signs through frequent miracles, a few words about the tomb are fitting. He indeed embraced the clear and conspicuous signs of Christ, who chose him. My humble faith led me to seek Christ. This man, conquered, had thin walls and hard beds of bristly hair for his clothing. If only the great sorrow, the tears, and the people who see him buried in this tomb knew what wonders he performed. [---]
EDCS-33900042.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription praising the deceased Eutropius for his virtues and miracles, dated to late antiquity.

EDCS-33900045.translation: The death of Titus Julius Servatus.
EDCS-33900045.summary: This very brief inscription records the death of Titus Julius Servatus.

EDCS-33900046.translation: In the name of Christ, in this place rest in peace the faithful servants of God Ampelius and Singenia, who lived in conjugal affection and mutual charity for about 60 years, or remained faithful in the Lord's peace for continuous years. Their life was such that the wife, leaving her husband and exceeding 20 years, would remain in perpetual chastity. Ampelius, of venerable memory, died on the 16th day before the Kalends of December, during the consulship of Festus and Flavius Marcianus. Singenia, of good recollection, departed on the 8th day before the Kalends of January, after the consulship of Viator. In the name of Christ.
EDCS-33900046.summary: This is a Christian epitaph commemorating Ampelius and Singenia, a married couple who lived long and faithfully, with their death dates given in relation to specific consulates and within a Christian context.

EDCS-34000162.translation: To Augusta, daughter of Titus Ecimarius, Apula.
EDCS-34000162.summary: This is a dedication to Augusta by Apula, daughter of Titus Ecimarius, likely a funerary dedication.

EDCS-34000311.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Titus Atilius Heliodorus et Atilia Vitalis Tito Atilio \n
EDCS-34000311.translation: To the Divine Shades. Titus Atilius Heliodorus and Atilia Vitalis [set this up] to Titus Atilius.
EDCS-34000311.summary: A funerary dedication to Titus Atilius, set up by Titus Atilius Heliodorus and Atilia Vitalis.

EDCS-34000317.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Flaviae Uliadis Titus Flavius Lucilianus matri pientissimae\n
EDCS-34000317.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Titus Flavius Lucilianus to his most dutiful mother, Flavia Uliadis.
EDCS-34000317.summary: A funerary dedication by Titus Flavius Lucilianus to his mother, Flavia Uliadis.

EDCS-34000318.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Marci Silvi Sabini Silvius Sabinianus CO\n
EDCS-34000318.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Silvius Sabinianus to Marcus Silvius Sabinus.
EDCS-34000318.summary: A funerary dedication by Silvius Sabinianus to Marcus Silvius Sabinus.

EDCS-34000319.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Caio Iulio Alexandro Iulia Tryphosa coniugi\n
EDCS-34000319.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Iulia Tryphosa to her husband, Gaius Iulius Alexander.
EDCS-34000319.summary: A funerary dedication by Iulia Tryphosa to her husband, Gaius Iulius Alexander.

EDCS-34000320.translation: To the Divine Manes. Helpis erected this for her most dutiful son, Titus Domitius Helpisson.
EDCS-34000320.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up by Helpis for her pious son, Titus Domitius Helpisson.

EDCS-34000321.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Synoridi libertae piissimae Myrria Hedyle\n
EDCS-34000321.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Myrria Hedyle to her most dutiful freedwoman, Synoris.
EDCS-34000321.summary: A funerary dedication by Myrria Hedyle to her freedwoman, Synoris.

EDCS-34000322.translation: To the Divine Manes. Valeria Eutychia made this for Blaesus Valerius Cupitus, her most sweet and incomparable husband.
EDCS-34000322.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Valeria Eutychia for her beloved husband, Blaesus Valerius Cupitus.

EDCS-34000323.text_edition: \n Manibus Flaviae Fortunatae Flavius Phosphorus et Flavia Mansueta filiae suae\n
EDCS-34000323.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Flavius Phosphorus and Flavia Mansueta to their daughter, Flavia Fortunata.
EDCS-34000323.summary: A funerary dedication by Flavius Phosphorus and Flavia Mansueta to their daughter, Flavia Fortunata.

EDCS-34000324.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Arruntius to Arruntia Phita.
EDCS-34000324.summary: A funerary dedication by Arruntius to Arruntia Phita.

EDCS-34000330.translation: To the Divine Manes. Verecundus Cestius for Julia Epaphra.
EDCS-34000330.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Verecundus Cestius for Julia Epaphra.

EDCS-34000331.translation: Cossutia Nicee for her most dutiful husband, Sextus Annius Chaso.
EDCS-34000331.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Cossutia Nicee for her pious husband, Sextus Annius Chaso.

EDCS-34000332.translation: To the Divine Manes. Servilius for Ennia Agathemeris, his deserving wife.
EDCS-34000332.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Servilius for his deserving wife, Ennia Agathemeris.

EDCS-34000333.text_edition: \n Cestiae Chresimae Aulus Cestius Nestor et Valeria Pallas libertae pientissimae\n
EDCS-34000333.translation: To Cestia Chresima. Aulus Cestius Nestor and Valeria Pallas to their most dutiful freedwoman.
EDCS-34000333.summary: A funerary dedication by Aulus Cestius Nestor and Valeria Pallas to their freedwoman, Cestia Chresima.

EDCS-34000336.translation: In this tomb lies Abbess Tilisiola, who will preserve the glory of her name through her life and deeds, and having followed Christ-born Mary in mind and practice, she presided over sacred virgins for 40 years. She lived 70 years. Her deposition was on the 7th day before the Ides of April, in the 8th indiction.
EDCS-34000336.summary: This is a Christian epitaph for Abbess Tilisiola, detailing her pious life, her leadership of virgins, her age at death, and the date of her repose, likely from the 6th century or later due to the indiction.

EDCS-34000339.text_edition: \n mirae innocentiae E TIMIE CONSOR E C F quae \n
EDCS-34000339.translation: Of wonderful innocence. To Eutimia, wife of [---], daughter of the divine Claudius, who...
EDCS-34000339.summary: An epitaph honoring Eutimia, emphasizing her innocence and likely her connection to the imperial family.

EDCS-34000357.translation: Here rests in peace, of good memory, Istefanus, who lived more or less 17 years. He departed on the 7th day before the Kalends of October, in the ninth indiction.
EDCS-34000357.summary: This is a Christian epitaph for Istefanus, stating his age at death and the date of his passing, likely from the 6th century or later due to the indiction.

EDCS-34500058.translation: In the consulship of Apro(nianus) and Paet(inus). [---] of Marcus Fabius Licymnus.
EDCS-34500058.summary: A dedication or marker associated with Marcus Fabius Licymnus, dated to the consulship of Aproianus and Paetinus.

EDCS-36100272.translation: Successus, of Domitia Lucilla, daughter of Publius. Slaves.
EDCS-36100272.summary: This inscription records the names of Successus and Domitia Lucilla, the daughter of Publius, and identifies them as slaves, likely a funerary marker for enslaved individuals or property.

EDCS-36100352.translation: The pottery works of Primitius for Domitia Lucilla.
EDCS-36100352.summary: This is a maker's mark on pottery, identifying the producer Primitius and owner Domitia Lucilla, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-36100385.translation: Abascantus, slave of Gnaeus Domitius Trophimus, in the consulship of Paetinus and Apronianus.
EDCS-36100385.summary: An inscription mentioning Abascantus, a slave of Gnaeus Domitius Trophimus, dated to the consulship of Paetinus and Apronianus.

EDCS-36100397.translation: The pottery works of Primitius for Domitia Lucilla.
EDCS-36100397.summary: This is a maker's mark on pottery, identifying the producer Primitius and owner Domitia Lucilla, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-36400146.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Solliae Sexti filiae Maternae\n
EDCS-36400146.translation: To the divine shades of Sollia Matern a, daughter of Sextus.
EDCS-36400146.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Sollia Materna.

EDCS-36400148.summary: This inscription likely records ownership of a tomb or property belonging to Lucius Titius Rufianus, possibly from the 1st century CE.

EDCS-36400152.summary: This inscription likely records ownership of a tomb or property belonging to Gaius Ennius Paeon, possibly from the 1st century CE.

EDCS-36400153.summary: This inscription likely records ownership of a tomb or property belonging to Gaius Ennius Chrysipus, possibly from the 1st century CE.

EDCS-36400154.summary: This inscription likely records the name of an owner or deceased individual, possibly Silvinus Focia, with an incomplete or otherwise damaged context.

EDCS-36400156.summary: This inscription likely records ownership of a tomb or property belonging to Lucius Cornelius Comicus, possibly from the 1st century CE.

EDCS-36400157.summary: This inscription likely records ownership of a tomb or property belonging to Gaius Albucius Silanus, possibly from the 1st century CE.

EDCS-36400158.translation: Lucius Cornelius Sabinianus sculpted this at Narbo for Tiberius Aurelius Deuteri.
EDCS-36400158.summary: This is a sculptor's signature for a work created by Lucius Cornelius Sabinianus for Tiberius Aurelius Deuteri at Narbo, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-36400159.summary: This inscription is likely a dedication on a tomb or monument for Fabricia Quieta, possibly from the 1st century CE.

EDCS-36400161.translation: Our lord Theodosius, Pious, Fortunate, Augustus, the Wonderful, to Agroecius.
EDCS-36400161.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Theodosius I, likely from the late 4th century CE, honoring Agroecius.

EDCS-36400175.summary: This inscription records the name Sextus Pompeius Iustus, likely as an owner or deceased.

EDCS-36400178.translation: Titus Carisius, son of Titus, praetor of the Volcae, dedicates.
EDCS-36400178.summary: A dedication by Titus Carisius, son of Titus, who held the office of praetor among the Volcae, likely on a public monument.

EDCS-37700204.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, Iulius Sa[---].
EDCS-37700204.summary: A funerary dedication to the Dis Manes, with the name of the deceased incompletely preserved.

EDCS-37700205.summary: This inscription appears to refer to a specific item, possibly a hooded cloak belonging to someone named Norbillius.

EDCS-37700206.summary: This inscription records the name Caius Carinus and a quantity of seven segestriae, which could refer to objects or measures.

EDCS-37700207.summary: An ownership or dedication inscription naming Marcus Cotisius Bubalus.

EDCS-37700208.translation: To Quintus Vallius, son of Lucius, called Reperatus, his heir by will.
EDCS-37700208.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to Quintus Vallius Reperatus by his heir according to his will.

EDCS-38000209.translation: Ioustos, son of Seilos, lived 102 years.
EDCS-38000209.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Ioustos, son of Seilos.

EDCS-39200679.translation: Ioustos, son of Seilos, lived 102 years.
EDCS-39200679.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Ioustos, son of Seilos, identical to EDCS-38000209.

EDCS-39200683.translation: To Titus Porkios Aelianus, son of Porkios Aelianus, a most distinguished man and prophet, [and] to Kyreina Corneliana, priestess of Leucothea, chiliarch of the 15th Apollinaris Legion, chiliarch of the 9th Cohort of Batavians, prefect of the 2nd Ulpian Cohort, prefect of the 4th Cohort of Gauls, prefect of the Cohort of Dardani, prefect of the exploratores of Germania, curator and administrator for Flaminia Aemilia Liguria, curator and governor of the coastal Alps.
EDCS-39200683.summary: A complex dedication honoring multiple individuals, likely a father and son, detailing extensive military and administrative careers, possibly on a public monument or honorary base.

EDCS-39200684.translation: Athenades, son of Dioskourides, Roman scribe.
EDCS-39200684.summary: An inscription identifying Athenades, son of Dioskourides, as a Roman scribe.

EDCS-39200685.translation: Apollodoros, freedman, and his wife Primigenia, to their daughter and freedwoman, for the sake of memory.
EDCS-39200685.summary: A funerary dedication by a freedman and his wife to their daughter, who was also a freedwoman.

EDCS-39200686.translation: To the Chthonic Gods. Aurelius Dioklides, who lived 17 years and fifteen days. Aurelius Diokles and Aurelia Tertia, parents, set this up for the sake of memory. He was born in Veneris, where Hercules was taken up by the gods called Pythians on the day of Aphrodite.
EDCS-39200686.summary: A funerary epitaph for Aurelius Dioklides, who died at 17 years and 15 days, set up by his parents, with a complex and possibly symbolic description of his birth and death.

EDCS-39200688.translation: Tios, Derkylos, and Aktios, his foster-sons.
EDCS-39200688.summary: This inscription identifies Tios and records Derkylos and Aktios as his foster-sons.

EDCS-39200689.translation: To Diognetus, good and without sorrow. Farewell. You lived 8 years, 5 months.
EDCS-39200689.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Diognetus, recording his age at death and expressing good wishes.

EDCS-39200690.translation: Dionysios, to his mother Sida, for remembrance.
EDCS-39200690.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Dionysios to his mother, Sida, for remembrance.

EDCS-39200691.translation: Lucius Herennius Secundus and Decria Pomponia [dedicate this] to Lucius Herennius Praesent, their son, and to themselves, while alive.
EDCS-39200691.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Lucius Herennius Secundus and Decria Pomponia for their son and for themselves during their lifetime.

EDCS-39200692.summary: This is a simple greeting or epitaph for Zosimus.

EDCS-39200695.translation: Kleudemos, son of Dionysios, senior, victorious among the ephebes for good discipline and having served as gymnasiarch twice.
EDCS-39200695.summary: This inscription honors Kleudemos for his achievements as a senior ephebe and his two terms as gymnasiarch.

EDCS-39200696.summary: This is a dedication to Korynthos, who was the freedman of Theumedon.

EDCS-39200697.summary: This is a simple greeting or epitaph for Lenaïs.

EDCS-39200698.translation: Libas, son of Parmenon. Paramone, his daughter, for remembrance.
EDCS-39200698.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Paramone to her father, Libas, for remembrance.

EDCS-39200700.translation: Of Mariske, daughter of Parmenon. A(ugustus) Y(per) G(loria).
EDCS-39200700.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Mariske, daughter of Parmenon, with an accompanying acclamation.

EDCS-39200701.summary: A tombstone inscription wishing well-being to Makella.

EDCS-39200702.translation: To the Muse, Astycritys, son of Hymnis.
EDCS-39200702.summary: An inscription dedicating something to the Muse, with the name of the dedicator.

EDCS-39200703.translation: Parmeno, of the family of Reius, to Syrisca, daughter of Nitro.
EDCS-39200703.summary: An epitaph for Syrisca, daughter of Nitro, possibly erected by Parmeno.

EDCS-39200704.translation: Titus Pomponius Apollonides in memory of Titus Flavius Nicostratus, his teacher.
EDCS-39200704.summary: A memorial dedication by Titus Pomponius Apollonides for his teacher, Titus Flavius Nicostratus.

EDCS-39200705.translation: Rogatus for Ursola, his wife, in memory. She lived 27 years.
EDCS-39200705.summary: A memorial epitaph for Ursola, wife of Rogatus, noting her lifespan.

EDCS-39200706.translation: Titius Gemellus made this bust for himself in memory, so that he might be buried here.
EDCS-39200706.summary: A self-funded epitaph by Titius Gemellus for a bust to be placed with his burial.

EDCS-39200707.summary: A simple memorial dedication for Philatiades.

EDCS-39200708.translation: To Flavius Statius Surianus, most dutiful father, Statius Statianus.
EDCS-39200708.summary: A dedication by Statius Statianus to his father, Flavius Statius Surianus.

EDCS-39200709.translation: Fulvius Anthos, Fulvia Cytheris. Good people, farewell.
EDCS-39200709.summary: An epitaph for Fulvius Anthos and Fulvia Cytheris, wishing farewell to passersby.

EDCS-39200710.translation: To Charmolaus, son of Thraso, who was also Menos, by Charis, his freedman.
EDCS-39200710.summary: An inscription dedicating something to Charmolaus (also known as Menos), son of Thraso, by his freedman Charis.

EDCS-39200711.translation: I, formerly a mortal youth, now call myself a friend of the god, no longer subject to death. Like the Amyclaean gods, saviors of sailors, I too, being a sailor, found my rest in the sea's waves. Having received this tomb through piety, I have ceased from sickness and toil, from burden and labor. For these things are harsh for the flesh while alive, but when dead, there are two companies; one is carried on earth, the other dances with the heavenly ones. Of this company, I am one, having received a god as my leader. [He made this] from his own funds.
EDCS-39200711.summary: This is a funerary epigram from an unknown date, likely Roman Imperial period, for a sailor who became a cult hero after his death, possibly associated with the Dioscuri (Amyclaean gods).

EDCS-39200712.translation: Cal[---] for himself and for his whole household.
EDCS-39200712.summary: This is a short inscription from an unknown date, likely Roman Imperial period, indicating a dedication or offering made by a person named Cal[---] for his family.

EDCS-39200714.summary: This is a fragmented inscription from an unknown date, likely Roman Imperial period, possibly recording a name or a place related to a person named Paio.

EDCS-39200717.summary: This is a tombstone inscription from an unknown date, likely Roman Imperial period, recording the name and age of the deceased.

EDCS-39200720.summary: This is a funerary inscription from an unknown date, likely Roman Imperial period, a simple epitaph for a woman named Euthymia.

EDCS-39200722.translation: Ioses from the village of Epikion, upper [or lower?], lies here.
EDCS-39200722.summary: This is a tombstone inscription from an unknown date, likely Roman Imperial period, identifying the deceased as Ioses from the village of Epikion and indicating his burial location.

EDCS-39200727.translation: [May you] have a good life, Akontiō.
EDCS-39200727.summary: This is a short, potentially funerary, inscription from an unknown date, likely Roman Imperial period, wishing a good life to Akontiō.

EDCS-39200728.summary: This is an artist's signature or maker's mark from an unknown date, likely Roman Imperial period, indicating that Eibykos Praxiteles was the creator of the object.

EDCS-39200748.translation: Philon, son of Sotades, the Mosean orator, to Artemidoros, his brother, the orator.
EDCS-39200748.summary: This is a dedication or memorial inscription from an unknown date, likely Roman Imperial period, honoring Artemidoros, an orator, by his brother Philon.

EDCS-39200750.translation: Arethousa, Leukas, Xanthippe, Genios, the Sikeliote, Panopae, Boreios, Thetis, Triton, Dorothea, Nymphogenes, Glaukos, Palaemon, Ino.
EDCS-39200750.summary: This is a list of names from an unknown date, likely Roman Imperial period, possibly marking attendees at an event, members of a group, or names inscribed on a monument.

EDCS-39300196.translation: The partnership of Lucius Gargilius, son of Titus, and Marcus Laetilius, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-39300196.summary: This inscription records the formation of a business partnership between Lucius Gargilius and Marcus Laetilius.

EDCS-39501374.summary: This is a dedicatory or ownership inscription for Procopius, a high-ranking official.

EDCS-39501498.translation: Kosmos's small vessel; Kosmos's same-day; Kosmos's lentil-shaped vessel.
EDCS-39501498.summary: This inscription lists items, possibly vessels, belonging to someone named Kosmos.

EDCS-40100149.translation: For Primigenia, daughter of Domitia, wife of Publius Lucillus.
EDCS-40100149.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Primigenia, daughter of Domitia and wife of Publius Lucillus.

EDCS-40700002.summary: This inscription likely records ownership or a dedication by Lucius Arlenius Iapis.

EDCS-41100019.translation: Our brother Fulco Aldemarus lies here, who died in Christ.
EDCS-41100019.summary: This is a Christian epitaph commemorating the deceased brother Fulco Aldemarus.

EDCS-41100020.translation: Aulus Cornelius, son of Gallonius, for himself and his family; in front 15 feet, in the field 25 feet.
EDCS-41100020.summary: This inscription records a land purchase or allocation by Aulus Cornelius for his family, specifying dimensions.
